Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 1:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿Alif, Lam, Ra. A Book whose verses have been made firm, then elaborated, from One who is Wise and Aware﴾ (1)

Abu Ja'far said: We have already mentioned the differences of the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) concerning the interpretation of His saying: ﴿Alif, Lam, Ra﴾, and the correct view on that matter according to us, with its evidences, has been given in a way that makes repeating it in this place unnecessary. [[See what preceded: 1: 205-224 / 6: 149 / 12: 293, 294 / 15: 7.]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿A Book whose verses have been made firm﴾, it means: this Book which Allah sent down to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), and it is the Qur'an.

* *

The word "kitab" (Book) is in the nominative case by the intention of: "This is a Book."

As for the view of those who claim that His saying ﴿Alif, Lam, Ra﴾ refers to all the letters of the alphabet with which the Qur'an was revealed, and these letters are taken as an indication of all of them, and that the meaning of the speech is: "These letters are a Book whose verses have been made firm" — then, according to their view, "kitab" should be in the nominative case governed by His saying ﴿Alif, Lam, Ra﴾.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿whose verses have been made firm, then elaborated﴾, the people of interpretation differed concerning its meaning. Some of them said: its meaning is: its verses were made firm by command and prohibition, then elaborated by reward and punishment.

Mention of those who said that:

17915 - Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Abu Muhammad al-Thaqafi informed me, from al-Hasan, concerning His saying: ﴿A Book whose verses have been made firm, then elaborated﴾, he said: made firm by command and prohibition, and elaborated by reward and punishment. [[The report 17915: "Abu Muhammad al-Thaqafi", the narrator from al-Hasan, I do not know who he is.]]

17916 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Karim ibn Muhammad al-Jurjani narrated to us, from Abu Bakr al-Hudhali, from al-Hasan: ﴿Alif, Lam, Ra. A Book whose verses have been made firm﴾, he said: made firm in command and prohibition, and elaborated by threat. [[The report 17916: "Abd al-Karim ibn Muhammad al-Jurjani", judge of Jurjan, narrated from Qays ibn al-Rabi', Abu Hanifa, Zuhayr ibn Mu'awiya, Ibn Jurayj and others. Abu Yusuf the judge and Ibn Uyayna narrated from him, though both were older than him, as did al-Shafi'i and others. He died in about the seventies after 100 AH, so I do not know whether Muhammad ibn Humayd lived to narrate from him or not. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib.]]

17917 - al-Mathanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr narrated to us, from Ibn Uyayna, from a man, from al-Hasan: ﴿Alif, Lam, Ra. A Book whose verses have been made firm﴾, he said: by command and prohibition = ﴿then elaborated﴾, he said: by reward and punishment.

* *

A different view from al-Hasan has also been transmitted, namely:

17918 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Abu Bakr, from al-Hasan, he said= and Abbad ibn al-Awwam narrated to us, from a man, from al-Hasan, he said: ﴿made firm﴾ by reward and punishment = ﴿then elaborated﴾ by command and prohibition.

* *

Others said: the meaning of that is: ﴿its verses were made firm﴾ from falsehood, then elaborated, so that the lawful and the unlawful were made clear from them.

Mention of those who said that:

17919 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada concerning His saying: ﴿Alif, Lam, Ra. A Book whose verses have been made firm, then elaborated, from One who is Wise and Aware﴾, Allah made them firm against falsehood, then elaborated them with His knowledge, so that their lawful and unlawful, and their obedience and disobedience, were made clear.

* *

17920 - Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada: ﴿its verses were made firm, then elaborated﴾, he said: Allah made them firm against falsehood, then elaborated them, made them clear.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two views is the view of the one who said: its meaning is that Allah made its verses firm against corruption, defect and falsehood, then elaborated them by command and prohibition.

This is because "ihkam al-shay'" means its reform and perfection, and "ihkam the verses of the Qur'an" means making them firm against any defect in them, or any falsehood that a person of deviation could attack them with.

As for "tafsil of its verses," it is distinguishing some of them from others, by explaining what in them is lawful and unlawful, and command and prohibition.

* *

Some exegetes interpreted His saying ﴿elaborated﴾ to mean "explained" (fussirat), which is similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

17921 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Najih narrated to us, from Mujahid concerning Allah's saying: ﴿then elaborated﴾, he said: explained.

17922 - Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿elaborated﴾, he said: explained.

17923 - ... said: Muhammad ibn Bakr narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: it reached me from Mujahid: ﴿then elaborated﴾, he said: explained.

17924 - al-Mathanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

17925 - ... said: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abd Allah narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

17926 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, similarly.

* *

Qatada said: its meaning is: "made clear" (bayyinat), and we have already mentioned the report to that effect earlier, and it is close in meaning to the view of Mujahid.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿from One who is Wise and Aware﴾, its meaning is: ﴿Wise﴾ in the arranging and measuring of things, ﴿Aware﴾ of what their consequences will come to. [[See the treatment of "hakim" and "khabir" in the earlier linguistic indexes under (h-k-m) and (kh-b-r).]]

17927 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, concerning His saying: ﴿from One who is Wise and Aware﴾, he says: from the presence of One who is Wise and Aware. [[See the treatment of "min ladun" in the earlier volume 6: 362.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 2:

The explanation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿That you worship none but Allah. Indeed, I am to you from Him a warner and a bringer of good tidings﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, exalted is His remembrance, says: "Then it has been made detailed, [so that] you worship none but Allah alone, having no partner, and that you renounce the false gods and rivals."

Then Allah, exalted is His remembrance, said to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "Say, O Muhammad, to the people: ﴿Indeed, I am to you﴾ from Allah's side ﴿a warner﴾ warning you of His punishment for your disobedience and for worshipping idols, ﴿and a bringer of good tidings﴾, giving you good tidings of abundant reward for obeying Him and sincerely devoting worship and divinity to Him."

[[See the explanation of "warner" (nadhir) above, p. 215, note 2, and the references there.

And the explanation of "bringer of good tidings" (bashir) in the word-index of language above, under (b-sh-r).]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 3:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿And that you ask your Lord for forgiveness, then turn to Him in repentance; He will let you enjoy a good provision until an appointed term, and will give every doer of virtue his virtue. But if you turn away, then indeed I fear for you the punishment of a great day﴾ (3)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: His, the Exalted's, words mean: Then His verses were made distinct, that you should worship none but Allah, and that you should ask your Lord for forgiveness. By His words ﴿and that you ask your Lord for forgiveness﴾ He means: and that you, O people, do those deeds which please your Lord with regard to you, so that He will cover over for you the great sins you have committed by worshipping idols and images, and by associating gods and rivals with Him in worship. [[See the explanation of "istighfar" (seeking forgiveness) in the earlier word indexes of language (gh-f-r).]]

His words ﴿then turn to Him in repentance﴾ mean: then return to your Lord, sincerely devoting worship to Him alone, apart from anything else of all that you worship besides Him, after you have renounced rivals and disowned their worship. [[See the explanation of "tawbah" (repentance) in the earlier word indexes of language (t-w-b).]]

That is why it was said: ﴿And that you ask your Lord for forgiveness then turn to Him in repentance﴾, and it was not said "and turn to Him in repentance" alone, because "tawbah" means returning to acting in obedience to Allah, while "istighfar" is seeking forgiveness from the polytheism in which they were persisting; and action for Allah is not action for Him unless it follows abandoning association with Him. As for polytheism, its action is only for Satan. Therefore He, the Exalted, commanded them to repent to Him after seeking forgiveness from polytheism, because the people of polytheism used to think that they obeyed Allah in many of their deeds, while they remained persistent in their polytheism.

His words ﴿He will let you enjoy a good provision until an appointed term﴾ mean: Allah, the Exalted, says to the polytheists whom these verses address: Ask your Lord for forgiveness and turn to Him in repentance, for if you do that, He will extend to you of the world and provide you with its adornment, and He will lengthen your lifespans until the time at which death has been decreed for you. [[See the explanation of "matā'" (enjoyment) in the earlier word indexes of language (m-t-').

And the explanation of "al-ajal al-musamma" (the appointed term) in the earlier word indexes of language (a-j-l).]]

* *

The people of interpretation have said something similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

17928- Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿He will let you enjoy a good provision until an appointed term﴾: you are in that enjoyment, so take up obedience to Allah and knowledge of His right, for Allah is the Bestower who loves the grateful, and the people of gratitude are in increase from Allah, and that is His decree which He has decreed.

* *

As for His words ﴿until an appointed term﴾, it means death.

17929- Al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, he said: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿until an appointed term﴾, he said: death.

17930- Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding His words ﴿until an appointed term﴾, that it is death.

17931- Al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah: ﴿until an appointed term﴾, he said: death.

* *

As for His words ﴿and will give every doer of virtue his virtue﴾, it means: He will reward abundantly, in the Hereafter, every person who bestows favour from his wealth, his strength or his kindness upon others, seeking reward for it and intending thereby the Face of Allah, as:

17932- Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu Asim narrated to us, he said: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿and will give every doer of virtue his virtue﴾, he said: what one seeks reward for from his wealth, or from work done with his hand or foot, or a word, or whatever voluntary act he does in all his affairs.

17933- Al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, he said: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, he said=

17934-... And Ishaq narrated to us, he said: Abd Allah narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly= except that he said: or work with his hands or feet and his speech, and whatever he gives of himself in all his affairs.

17935- Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, similarly= except that he said: and whatever he speaks of in all his affairs.

17936- Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿and will give every doer of virtue his virtue﴾, i.e., in the Hereafter.

* *

It has been reported from Ibn Mas'ud that he used to say regarding the interpretation of this:

17937- I was told by Al-Musayyib ibn Sharik, from Abu Bakr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Mas'ud, regarding His words ﴿and will give every doer of virtue his virtue﴾, he said: Whoever does an evil deed, one evil deed is written against him, and whoever does a good deed, ten good deeds are written for him. If he is punished for the evil deed he committed in this world, ten good deeds remain for him; and if he is not punished for it in this world, one of the ten good deeds is taken and nine good deeds remain for him. Then he says: Destroyed is the one whose units overcome his tens!!

* *

As for His words ﴿But if you turn away, then indeed I fear for you the punishment of a great day﴾, the Exalted says: But if they turn away from what I have called them to, namely sincerely devoting worship to Allah, abandoning the worship of idols, and refusing to seek forgiveness from Allah and to repent to Him, and they turn their backs and withdraw from that, [[See the explanation of "tawalli" (turning away) in the earlier word indexes of language (w-l-y).]] ﴿then indeed I﴾, O people, ﴿fear for you the punishment of a great day﴾, whose matter is grave and whose terror is immense, which is the day on which every soul will be recompensed for what it earned, and they will not be wronged.

* *

His, the Exalted's, words ﴿But if you turn away, then indeed I fear for you the punishment of a great day﴾ are a case where a speech has preceded: the Arabs, when they put a statement before a speech, address the audience, then return to report about the absent party, then return again to address. We have explained this in more than one place, in a way that makes repeating it here unnecessary. [[See what preceded at 13:314, note, and 3; and the references there.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 4:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿To Allah is your return, and He is Able to do all things﴾

Abu Ja'far said: His saying, may He be remembered, means: ﴿To Allah﴾, O people, is your return (ma'ab) and your destination (masir). [[See the explanation of "al-marji'" (return) above, p. 146, note 5, and the references there.]]

So beware of His punishment if you turn away from what I call you to, namely repentance to Him from your worship of gods and idols, for He will make you abide in the Fire of Hell if you perish in your polytheism before repenting to Him. ﴿And He is Able to do all things﴾: that is, He is capable of bringing you back to life after your death, and of punishing you for associating idols with Him, and of whatever else He wills concerning you and others. [[See the explanation of "qadir" (able) in the earlier lexical indexes, under the root (q-d-r).]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 5:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿Verily they fold up their breasts to hide from Him. Yet when they cover themselves with their garments, He knows what they conceal and what they reveal. Indeed, He is Knowing of what is in the breasts.﴾ (5)

Abu Ja'far said: The reciters differed in their recitation of His words: ﴿Verily they fold up their breasts﴾. The reciters of the major cities generally read: ﴿أَلا إِنَّهُمْ يَثْنُونَ صُدُورَهُمْ﴾, as a form of "yaf'aluna" from "thaniya" (to fold), with "al-sudur" in the accusative.

Those who read it thus also differed in its interpretation. Some said: this was the action of some of the hypocrites. When one of them passed by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he would cover his face and bend his back.

Mention of those who said this:

17938. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi 'Adiy narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from Husayn, from Abdullah ibn Shaddad, regarding His words: ﴿Verily they fold up their breasts to hide from Him. Yet when they cover themselves with their garments﴾, he said: When one of them passed by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he would draw his garment over his face and bend his back. [[His words "qala bi-thawbihi 'ala wajhihi" mean: he took his garment and tried to cover his face with it so that he would not see the Prophet (ﷺ). "Qala" is a word of the language used with many meanings, and here it is meant to depict the movement.

See what has preceded: 2:546, 547 / the report 5796, vol. 5, p. 400, note 1 / the report 12523, vol. 10, p. 572, note 1 / the report 17429, vol. 14, p. 541, note 2.]]

17939. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Husayn informed us, from Abdullah ibn Shaddad ibn al-Hadi, regarding His words: ﴿Verily they fold up their breasts to hide from Him﴾, he said: "from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." He said: When the hypocrites passed by him, one of them would fold his chest and lower his head. So Allah said: ﴿Verily they fold up their breasts﴾, the verse.

17940. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Amr ibn Awn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Husayn, who said: I heard Abdullah ibn Shaddad say regarding His words: ﴿they fold up their breasts﴾: When one of them passed by the Prophet (ﷺ), he would fold his chest and cover himself with his garment, so that the Prophet (ﷺ) would not see him.

* *

Others said: Rather, they did this out of ignorance of Allah and their supposition that Allah would be unaware of what their breasts harbor when they did so.

Mention of those who said this:

17941. Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿they fold up their breasts﴾, he said: doubt and uncertainty regarding the truth, so that they might hide from Allah, if they were able.

17942. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿they fold up their breasts﴾, doubt and uncertainty regarding the truth. ﴿so that they might hide from Him﴾, he said: from Allah, if they were able.

17943. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿they fold up their breasts﴾, he said: they become constricted through doubt.

17944. Al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abdullah narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿they fold up their breasts﴾, he said: they become constricted through doubt and uncertainty regarding the truth. He said: ﴿so that they might hide from Him﴾, he said: from Allah, if they were able.

17945. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, with a similar report.

17946. Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Hawdhah narrated to us, saying: Awf narrated to us, from al-Hasan regarding His words: ﴿Verily they fold up their breasts to hide from Him. Yet when they cover themselves with their garments﴾, he said: out of their ignorance of Him. Allah said: ﴿Yet when they cover themselves with their garments﴾, in the darkness of the night, within the inner parts of their houses= ﴿He knows﴾ at that hour ﴿what they conceal and what they reveal. Indeed, He is Knowing of what is in the breasts﴾.

17947. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Abu Razin: ﴿Verily they fold up their breasts to hide from Him. Yet when they cover themselves with their garments﴾, he said: One of them would bend his back and cover himself with his garment.

* *

Others said: They only did this so that they would not hear the Book of Allah. [[In the printed edition: "the speech of Allah, exalted is He," and I have confirmed what is in the manuscript.]]

Mention of those who said this:

17948. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿Verily they fold up their breasts﴾, the verse, he said: [They would bend their breasts so that they would not hear the Book of Allah. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Yet when] they cover themselves with their garments, He knows what they conceal and what they reveal﴾, and that is the most hidden state of the son of Adam, when he bends his chest and covers himself with his garment, and conceals his intention within himself, for Allah does not hide that from Him. [[What is between the brackets is missing from the manuscript.]]

17949. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿they cover themselves with their garments﴾, he said: It is the most hidden state of a person when he conceals something within himself and covers himself with his garment; that is the most hidden state, and Allah knows what is in their souls, and Allah knows what they conceal and what they reveal.

* *

Others said: This is only a report from Allah to His Prophet (ﷺ) about the hypocrites who harbored enmity and hatred toward him while showing him love and affection, that they were with him and upon his religion. He, may His praise be glorified, says: Verily they conceal their breasts upon disbelief to hide from Allah. Then He, may His praise be glorified, informed that He does not hide from Him their secrets and their openness. [[In the printed edition: "wa-annahum" with a waw, whereas what is in the manuscript is good and correct.]]

* *

Others said: They used to do this when some of them conferred privately with one another.

Mention of those who said this:

17950. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: ﴿Verily they fold up their breasts to hide from Him﴾, he said: This is when some of them confer privately with others. And he recited: ﴿Yet when they cover themselves with their garments﴾, the verse.

* *

It is related from Ibn Abbas that he used to recite it: ﴿أَلا إِنَّهُمْ تَثْنَونِي صُدُورُهُمْ﴾, on the pattern of "tahlawli al-thamarah" (the fruit became sweet), "taf'awal".

17951. Narrated to us ... saying: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah who said: I heard Ibn Abbas recite ﴿أَلا إِنَّهُمْ تَثْنَوْنِي صُدُورُهُمْ﴾, and he said: They would not approach women or relieve themselves except that they had covered themselves with their garments, out of aversion to exposing their private parts to the sky. [[Report 17951: in the printed edition: "Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Abu Usamah narrated to us," which is not in the manuscript; rather, what is in it is what I have recorded: "narrated to us ... saying: Abu Usamah narrated to us," with a blank space between the two statements, and above it is written "kadha," meaning the blank is so in the original.]]

17952. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj who said: I heard Muhammad ibn Abbad ibn Ja'far say: I heard Ibn Abbas recite it: ﴿أَلا إِنَّهُمْ تَثْنَوْنِي صُدُورُهُمْ﴾, and he said: I asked him about it, and he said: Some people were ashamed to relieve themselves so that they would expose themselves to the sky, and to have intercourse so that they would expose themselves to the sky.

* *

It is related from Ibn Abbas another interpretation of that, which is:

17953. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us with it, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar who said: I was informed, from Ikrimah, that Ibn Abbas recited ﴿أَلا إِنَّهُمْ تَثْنَوْنِي صُدُورُهُمْ﴾, and Ibn Abbas said: "Tathnawni sudurahum" is doubt about Allah and the doing of evil deeds= ﴿yastaghshuna thiyabahum﴾: they act arrogantly, or they hide from Allah, while He sees them, He knows what they conceal and what they reveal.

17954. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from a man, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas that he recited: ﴿أَلا إِنَّهُمْ تَثْنَونِي صُدُورُهُمْ﴾. Ikrimah said: "Tathnawni sudurahum": doubt about Allah and the doing of evil deeds, so he covers his garment and hides from Allah, while Allah sees him and knows what they conceal and what they reveal.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct reading in this matter, in our view, is what the reciters of the major cities read, which is: ﴿أَلا إِنَّهُمْ يَثْنُونَ صُدُورَهُمْ﴾, on the pattern of "yaf'aluna", with "al-sudur" in the accusative, meaning: they bend their breasts and conceal them, as:

17955. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas regarding His words: ﴿yathnuna sudurahum﴾, he said: they conceal.

17956. Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas regarding His words: ﴿Verily they fold up their breasts﴾, he said: they conceal what is in their hearts= ﴿Yet when they cover themselves with their garments﴾, He knows what they did by night and by day.

17957. It was related to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words: ﴿Verily they fold up their breasts﴾, he said: ﴿tathnawni sudurahum﴾.

Abu Ja'far said: This interpretation which al-Dahhak gave follows the reading of Ibn Abbas, except that what was narrated to us mentions the reading in the transmission in this form.

* *

Since the reading we mentioned is the preferable of the two readings in this matter, due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters upon it, then the most preferable interpretation of it is the interpretation of those who said: They did this out of ignorance of Allah, supposing that He would not know what their souls conceal or what they confide among themselves.

We said this is the most preferable interpretation of the verse because His words ﴿so that they might hide from Him﴾ mean: so that they might hide from Allah, and the pronoun in His words ﴿from Him﴾ refers to the name of Allah, and no mention of Muhammad has preceded it, so it cannot be taken as referring to his (ﷺ) mention, while it is within the context of the report about Allah. When this is so, it is more fitting that it refers to the mention of Allah. And when this is established, it is known that they did not imagine that they could hide from Allah except through their ignorance of Him. So He, may His praise be glorified, informed them that the secret of their affairs and their openness is not hidden from Him, in whatever state they were, whether they covered themselves with garments or appeared in the open [[al-barraz (with a fatha on the ba'): a wide open space, with no trees or cover.]],

and He said: ﴿Yet when they cover themselves with their garments﴾, meaning: they wrap their garments around themselves, covering and clothing themselves.

* *

It is said from this: "istaghsha thawbahu wa-taghashshahu" (he covered himself with his garment). Allah said: ﴿And they cover themselves with their garments﴾ [Surah Nuh: 7], and al-Khansa' said:

"I watch the stars, though I was not charged with watching them... and at times I cover myself with the surplus of my worn garments." [[Her Diwan: 109, from her elegies for her brother Sakhr. She says before it: "I was sleepless, so I spent the night awake, as if my eyes had been anointed with 'iwar." "Iwar" is dust/speck. Her words "I watch the stars" mean she observes them, from the dominance of grief over her at night; she is awake, finding comfort in gazing at the heavens. "Atmar" are worn-out garments. She says: her mourning and sorrow have lasted long, and she does not care whether she has new clothes; she is in her worn garments, and when her vigil lengthens and what overcomes her overcomes her, she covers herself with her worn garments as a grieving person does, and weeps or withdraws into her sorrows.]]

* *

= ﴿He knows what they conceal﴾: He, may His praise be glorified, says: He knows what these ignorant people about their Lord conceal, those who suppose that Allah is unaware of what their breasts harbor when they bend them over what is in them and fold them, and what they confide among themselves and keep secret= ﴿and what they reveal﴾, the secrets of His servants and their openness are equal to Him= ﴿Indeed, He is Knowing of what is in the breasts﴾. He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Indeed Allah has knowledge of all that the breasts of His creatures conceal, of faith and disbelief, truth and falsehood, good and evil, and what they hide that they have not yet concealed, [[See the explanation of "dhat al-sudur" above, vol. 13, p. 570, note 2, and the references there.]] as:

17958. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿Yet when they cover themselves with their garments﴾, he says: they cover their heads.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: Beware lest your Lord notice you while you harbor in your breasts doubt about any part of His oneness, His command or His prohibition, or about what He has obligated you to believe in and affirm, and so you perish through holding that belief.

**Commentary on the words of the Exalted: ﴿And there is no creature (dabba) on the earth but that upon Allah is its provision, and He knows its place of settlement and its place of storage. All of it is in a clear Record.﴾ (11:6)**

Abu Ja'far said: By His words ﴿And there is no creature on the earth but that upon Allah is its provision﴾, the Exalted means: and there is no creature that crawls on the earth.

* *

The word "dabba" (creature) is the active form (al-fa'ila), from "dabba," so one says "he crawls (yadubbu), so he is a crawler (dabbun), and she is a creature (dabba)." [[See the explanation of "al-dabba" above, 14:21, note 1, and the references there.]]

* *

﴿Except upon Allah is its provision﴾ means: there is no creature except that its provision, which reaches it, comes from Allah, who has undertaken it. That provision is its food, its nourishment, and that by which its life is sustained.

* *

Some of the people of interpretation (ta'wil) said something similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

17959. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Mujahid said, concerning His words ﴿And there is no creature on the earth but that upon Allah is its provision﴾: "Whatever provision comes to it is from Allah, though perhaps it is not provided for until it dies of hunger, but whatever provision there is, is from Allah."

17960. Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His words: ﴿And there is no creature on the earth but that upon Allah is its provision﴾, he said: "Every creature."

17961. It was reported to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, concerning His words ﴿And there is no creature on the earth but that upon Allah is its provision﴾: "That is, every creature, and people are among them."

* *

Some scholars of the Arabic language from Basra claimed that every property (mal) is "dabba" [[In the printed edition: "every walking thing is a dabba," but what I have established is the text of the manuscript. "Mal" among the Arabs means camels and livestock, and all other animals that are kept. This is a valid view. However, what is in Majaz al-Qur'an, and this is the text of his words, is "every eater," and I have no ability to decide on the correctness of what Abu 'Ubayda said, because the printed copy of Majaz may differ from what is transmitted from Abu 'Ubayda in other books.]] = and that the meaning of the statement is: "and there is no dabba on the earth" = and that "min" is superfluous. [[This is the text of Abu 'Ubayda in Majaz al-Qur'an 1:285.]]

* *

As for His words ﴿And He knows its place of settlement﴾, that is the place where it settles, which is its abode to which it returns by night or by day. ﴿And its place of storage﴾ is the place where it is deposited, either by its death there or by its burial. [[See the explanation of "al-mustaqarr" and "al-mustawda'" above, 1:539 / 11:434, 562–572 / 12:358, 359.]]

* *

Some of the people of interpretation said something similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

17962. al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ibn al-Taymi informed us, from Layth, from al-Hakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: ﴿Its place of settlement﴾ is where it takes shelter, and ﴿its place of storage﴾ is where it dies.

17963. al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His words ﴿And He knows its place of settlement﴾, he says: where it takes shelter. ﴿And its place of storage﴾, he says: when it dies.

17964. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Layth, from al-Hakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿He knows its place of settlement and its place of storage﴾, he said: "The settlement" is where it takes shelter, and "the storage" is where it dies.

* *

Others said: ﴿Its place of settlement﴾ is in the womb, and ﴿its place of storage﴾ is in the loins.

Mention of those who said that:

17965. al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿And He knows its place of settlement﴾, in the womb, ﴿and its place of storage﴾, in the loins, like what is in "al-An'am." [[See the commentary on Surat al-An'am, 11:562–572, and the reports there.]]

17966. Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His words: ﴿And He knows its place of settlement and its place of storage﴾: "The settlement" is what is in the womb, and "the storage" is what is in the loins.

17967. It was reported to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, concerning His words ﴿And He knows its place of settlement﴾, he says: in the womb, ﴿and its place of storage﴾, in the loins.

* *

Others said: "The settlement" is in the womb, and "the storage" is where it dies.

Mention of those who said that:

17968. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: my father and Ya'la, and Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Isma'il, from Ibrahim, from 'Abd Allah: ﴿And He knows its place of settlement and its place of storage﴾, he said: "Its settlement" is the wombs, and "its storage" is the earth in which it dies.

17969. . . . narrated to us, saying: 'Ubayd Allah narrated to us, from Isra'il, from al-Suddi, from Murra, from 'Abd Allah: ﴿And He knows its place of settlement and its place of storage﴾: "The settlement" is the womb, and "the storage" is the place where it dies.

* *

Others said: ﴿Its place of settlement﴾ is its days of life, and ﴿its place of storage﴾ is where it dies in it.

Mention of those who said that:

17970. al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Sa'd narrated to us, saying: Abu Ja'far informed us, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, concerning His words: ﴿And He knows its place of settlement and its place of storage﴾, he said: ﴿Its place of settlement﴾ is its days of life, and ﴿its place of storage﴾ is where it dies and from where it is raised.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: We chose the view that we chose only because the Exalted informed us that whatever provision the creatures receive is from Him. It is therefore more fitting that this be followed by knowing their abode and their settlement, rather than informing us of His knowledge of what is contained in the loins and the wombs.

* *

By His words ﴿all of it is in a Record﴾, [clear], He means: the number of every creature, the amount of its provision, the measure of its settlement in its place of settlement, and the length of its stay in its place of storage. All of that is in a Record with Allah, recorded and written down. ﴿Clear﴾ means it makes clear to whoever reads it that this is recorded and written before He creates it and brings it into existence. [[See the explanation of "mubin" above in the language indexes under (b-y-n).]]

This is information from Allah, the Exalted, to those who used to fold their chests (to conceal themselves) in order to hide from Him: that He has known all things and recorded them in a Record with Him before He creates them and brings them into existence. The Exalted says to them: whoever among them He has known before bringing them into existence, how could what their souls conceal be hidden from Him when they fold their chests over it and cover their garments over themselves?

The commentary of Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) on surah 11, verse 7 (part 1 of 2):

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And it is He who created the heavens and the earth in six days, and His Throne was upon the water, that He may test you as to which of you is best in deed. And if you, [O Muhammad], say, "Indeed, you will be resurrected after death," those who disbelieve will surely say, "This is not but obvious magic."﴾ (7)

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: God, to whom you will return, O people, all of you, ﴿And it is He who created the heavens and the earth in six days﴾. That is, will He who created that from nothing be unable to restore you alive after He causes you to die?
* *
It has been said: God, exalted is His remembrance, created the heavens and the earth and what is in them during the six days, and so mention of the creation of the heavens and the earth is sufficient in this place, without mention of the creation of what is in them.

1797l. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Isma'il ibn Umayyah informed me, from Ayyub ibn Khalid, from Abdullah ibn Rafi', mawla (freedman) of Umm Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) took my hand and said: "God created the clay on Saturday, and created the mountains in it on Sunday, and created the trees in it on Monday, and created the disliked things on Tuesday, and created the light on Wednesday, and dispersed in it every kind of creature on Thursday, and created Adam after the 'Asr prayer on Friday, at the last of creation, in the last hours of Friday, between the 'Asr and the night."

[Note on the report 1797l: This is a sound hadith. Muslim related it in his Sahih (17:123), and Ahmad related it in his Musnad (2:327, no. 8323 in the numbering of my brother, may God have mercy on him, in the part of the Musnad that has not been printed). Abu Ja'far related it in his Tarikh (1:28, 29, 32), all through the route of al-Qasim ibn Bashir ibn Ma'ruf and al-Husayn ibn Ali al-Sada'i, from Hajjaj. It is therefore the beginning of another isnad (chain of narration) other than this isnad, even though the rest of it agrees. Some people have arisen who wish to nullify this kind of hadith by opinion, and then by attacking the noble Companion Abu Hurayrah. Some of them took a path that is blameworthy in the eyes of the scholars, by bringing together various fabrications, intending thereby to disparage a man from the Companions of the Messenger of God, without verifying the foundation on which the matter is built. O God, protect Your religion from our desires, for nothing has destroyed religion and worldly life except the desire that dominates our minds and souls. This matter calls for a discussion that is not appropriate to this place.]

1797m. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His words, ﴿in six days﴾, he said: The creation of the earth began in two days, and He determined its sustenance in two days.

1797n. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Ka'b, who said: God began the creation of the heavens and the earth on Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday, and finished with them on Friday, so He created Adam in the last hour of Friday. He said: So He made each day equal to a thousand years.

1797o. It was narrated to me, from al-Musayyab ibn Shurayk, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, regarding ﴿And it is He who created the heavens and the earth in six days﴾, he said: "Of the days of the Hereafter, each day equal to a thousand years. He began the creation on Sunday and concluded the creation on Friday, and so it was named 'Friday' (al-jum'ah). He rested on Saturday (sabt) and created nothing."
* *
As for His words, ﴿and His Throne was upon the water﴾, he means: His Throne was upon the water before He created the heavens and the earth and what is in them. [See the explanation of "the Throne" (al-'arsh) above: 12:482; 14:587; 15:18.] As follows:

1797p. Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of God: ﴿and His Throne was upon the water﴾, before He had created anything.

1797q. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

1797r. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abdullah narrated to us, from Waqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

1797s. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿and His Throne was upon the water﴾, "Your Lord, blessed and exalted, informs you how the beginning of His creation was before He created the heavens and the earth."

1797t. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿and His Throne was upon the water﴾, he said: "This is the beginning of His creation, before He created the heaven and the earth."

1797u. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: al-Hajjaj narrated to us, saying: Hammad narrated to us, from Ya'la ibn Ata, from Waki' ibn Hudus, from his paternal uncle Abu Razin al-Uqayli, who said: I said, "O Messenger of God, where was our Lord before He created the heavens and the earth?" He said: "In 'ama'. [The word "'ama'" in the language of the Arabs means cloud. Abu Ubayd al-Qasim ibn Salam said: 'We have interpreted this hadith according to the sense in which the Arabs understood it, and we do not know how that 'ama' was.' This is the statement of a scholar who understands from his Lord and does not reject the report of His Messenger who conveyed it from Him, who knows His attributes, and by analogy with it, the like of what is reported in hadiths on the beginning of creation and similar matters, provided the isnad of the report from the Prophet of God, may my father and mother be his ransom, is sound. Al-Tirmidhi, in his Sunan, transmitted from Ahmad, from Yazid ibn Harun: "'Ama': that is, there was nothing with Him."]
Above it was air, and below it was air, then He created His Throne upon the water." [Report 1797u: "Hammad" is Hammad ibn Salamah, who has passed many times. "Ya'la ibn Ata al-Amiri al-Ta'ifi" is trustworthy; he has passed under nos. 2858, 11527, 11529, 16579. "Waki' ibn Hudus", or "ibn Uds", Abu Mus'ab al-Uqayli al-Ta'ifi, was mentioned by Ibn Hibban in al-Thiqat. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir (4/2/178) and Ibn Abi Hatim (4/2/36). "Abu Razin al-Uqayli" is Laqit ibn Amir ibn al-Muntafiq, or Laqit ibn Sabrah, who narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ); he has passed under no. 3223, where the distinction between him and Laqit ibn Sabrah was made. This report was also transmitted by al-Tabari in his Tarikh (1:19) through this same route. Ahmad related it in his Musnad (4:11) through Yazid ibn Harun from Hammad, and (p. 12) through Bahz, from Hammad. Al-Tirmidhi related it in his Tafsir, through Yazid ibn Harun, and said: "This is a hasan hadith." Ibn Majah related it in his Sunan (1:64, no. 182) through Yazid. See the next report, no. 17981.]

1797v. Ibn Waki' and Muhammad ibn Harun al-Qattan al-Razigi narrated to us, both saying: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, from Hammad ibn Salamah, from Ya'la ibn Ata, from Waki' ibn Hudus, from his paternal uncle Abu Razin, who said: I said, "O Messenger of God, where was our Lord before He created His creation?" He said: "He was in 'ama', with air above it and air below it, then He created His Throne upon the water." [Report 1797v: It is a repetition of the preceding report, and its takhrij (sourcing) has passed there. "Muhammad ibn Harun al-Qattan al-Razigi", a teacher of al-Tabari, is thus written in the manuscript too, and similarly in the Tarikh without "al-Razigi"; I have not found that in the books available to me. The teacher of al-Tabari who has passed many times is "Muhammad ibn Harun ibn Ibrahim al-Rab'i al-Harbi al-Bazzaz, Abu Nushayt", and it is possible that "al-Qattan" was put in place of "al-Bazzaz", since the two are close in meaning. As for "al-Razigi", this is problematic. He is only called "al-Harbi" or "al-Rab'i", and "Abu Nushayt" has passed under nos. 9511, 10371, 14294.]

1797w. Khallad ibn Aslam narrated to us, saying: al-Nadr ibn Shumayl informed us, saying: al-Mas'udi informed us, saying: Jami' ibn Shaddad informed us, from Safwan ibn Muhriz, from Ibn Husayn, who was one of the Companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), who said: Some people came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), entered upon him, and he began giving them glad tidings, and they kept saying, "Give us!" until that upset the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and then they left from his presence. Then other people came, entered upon him, and said, "We came to greet the Messenger of God (ﷺ), to gain understanding of the religion, and to ask him about the beginning of this matter." He said: "Accept the glad tidings, since those who left did not accept them!" They said, "We have accepted." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "God was, and nothing was with Him, and His Throne was upon the water, and He wrote in the Reminder (al-dhikr) before everything, then He created the seven heavens. Then a caller came to me and said: 'Your she-camel has gone.' So I went out, and the mirage (al-sarab) hid her from my sight, and I wished I had left her."
[Report 1797w: "Khallad ibn Aslam", Abu Bakr al-Saffar, a teacher of al-Tabari, has passed under nos. 3004, 11512. "Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl al-Mazini al-Nahwi" is trustworthy; the group narrated from him; he has passed under nos. 11512, 16767. "Al-Mas'udi" is Abd al-Rahman ibn Abdullah ibn Utbah, who has passed many times, the last under no. 15349. "Jami' ibn Shaddad al-Muharibi" is trustworthy; the group narrated from him; he has passed under no. 8289. "Safwan ibn Muhriz ibn Ziyad al-Mazini" is trustworthy; the five narrated from him; he has passed under nos. 6496, 12866. "Ibn Husayn" is Imran ibn Husayn al-Khuza'i, a Companion. This report was transmitted by al-Tabari in his Tarikh (1:19) with this same isnad. Al-Bukhari transmitted it at length through al-A'mash, from Jami' ibn Shaddad, and transmitted it in brief through Sufyan, from Jami' ibn Shaddad (al-Fath 6:205-207), and through Sufyan (al-Fath 8:76). Ahmad transmitted it in his Musnad through several routes: through Sufyan from Jami', in brief (4:426, 436), and through al-A'mash, from Jami', at length (4:431, 432), which is the isnad of al-Bukhari with almost the same wording. Its transmission through these sound routes confirms the report of al-Mas'udi, because the scholars spoke about al-Mas'udi, that he became confused towards the end of his life, and the accepted part of his narrations is what the early ones heard from him. It seems that al-Nadr ibn Shumayl narrated from him in early times. Al-Hakim transmitted it in al-Mustadrak (2:341) through Rawh ibn Ubadah from al-Mas'udi himself, from Jami' ibn Shaddad, from Safwan ibn Muhriz, from Buraydah al-Aslami, the Companion, with its wording, and said: "This is a hadith with a sound isnad, but they did not transmit it," and al-Dhahabi agreed with him. I do not know when Rawh ibn Ubadah heard from al-Mas'udi. The difference regarding "Buraydah" and "Imran ibn Husayn" requires further careful verification.]

1797x. Muhammad ibn Mansur narrated to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: Amr ibn Abi Qays narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Layla, from al-Minhal ibn Amr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying, ﴿and His Throne was upon the water﴾, he said: "The Throne of God was upon the water, then He made for Himself a garden, then He made another beneath it, then He closed them with a single pearl." He said: ﴿And beneath them are two gardens﴾ [Surah al-Rahman: 62]. He said: "And they are those which ﴿no soul knows﴾ = or he said: 'and they are those which no soul knows' ﴿what has been hidden for them of comfort for the eyes, as reward for what they used to do﴾ [Surah al-Sajdah: 17]." He said: "And they are those which the creatures do not know what is in them = or: what is in them both = there comes to them every day from them = or: from them both = a gift."

1797y. Muhammad ibn Wakee' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-A'mash, from al-Minhal, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: Ibn Abbas was asked about the saying of God, ﴿and His Throne was upon the water﴾. He said: "Upon what was the water?" He said: "Upon the back of the wind." [Report 1797y: al-Hakim transmitted it in al-Mustadrak (2:341) through al-A'mash, from al-Minhal ibn Amr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and said: "This is a sound hadith according to the condition of the two Shaykhs, though they did not transmit it," and al-Dhahabi agreed with him. It will come in the next one through al-A'mash, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, without an intermediary. Al-A'mash narrates from Sa'id ibn Jubayr. al-Tabari also transmitted it in his Tarikh through this same route (1:20, 21).]

1797z. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-A'mash, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: Ibn Abbas was asked about His saying, ﴿and His Throne was upon the water﴾, "Upon what was the water?" He said: "Upon the back of the wind." [Report 1797z: It is a repetition of the two preceding reports, through al-A'mash, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, without an intermediary. al-Tabari transmitted it with this route in his Tarikh (1:21).]

1797aa. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Sa'id, from Ibn Abbas, the same.
[Report 1797aa: It is a repetition of the preceding reports. al-Tabari transmitted it in his Tarikh (1:21).]

1797bb. ... [the isnad begins with a gap] ... said: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Mubashshir al-Halabi narrated to us, from Artah ibn al-Mundhir, who said: I heard Damrah say: "God's Throne was upon the water, and He created the heavens and the earth with truth, and He created the pen and it wrote with it whatever He would create and whatever would occur of His creation. Then that Book glorified God and extolled Him for a thousand years before He created anything of creation." [Report 1797bb: "Mubashshir al-Halabi" is Mubashshir ibn Isma'il al-Halabi, whom the group narrated from, and who has passed under no. 17001. In the printed edition it was "Maysar", which is an error. "Artah ibn al-Mundhir al-Sakuni" is trustworthy, one of the Successors of the Successors, biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir (1/2/58) and Ibn Abi Hatim (1/1/326). "Damrah ibn Habib ibn Sahib al-Zubaydi" is trustworthy, biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir (2/2/338) and Ibn Abi Hatim (2/1/467). Abu Ja'far transmitted this report in his Tarikh (1:21) through this same route.]

1797cc. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ismail ibn Abd al-Karim narrated to me, saying: Abd al-Samad ibn Ma'qil narrated to me, who said: I heard Wahb ibn Munabbih say: "The Throne was before God created the heavens and the earth. Then He took a handful (qabdah) from the clear (saffah) water, and then He opened the handful, and it rose up as smoke, then He decreed them as seven heavens in two days. Then He took a clay (tinah) from the water and placed it where the House is, then He spread out the earth from it. Then He created the sustenance in two days, the heavens in two days, and created the earth in two days, then He finished the last of creation on the seventh day." [Report 1797cc: al-Tabari transmitted it in his Tarikh (1:20) through Muhammad ibn Sahl ibn Askar, from Ismail ibn Abd al-Karim, in brief. On the phrase "saffah al-ma'": in the printed edition it was "ثم قبض قبضة من صفاء الماء", which misread what is in the manuscript, so it was changed. I have added "qabdah" between brackets from the transmission of this report by another isnad in al-Tabari's Tarikh. As for "saffat al-ma'", it seems he meant by it "the white foam" mentioned in the reports nos. 2044, 7428, and in al-Durr al-Manthur (3:322), from the hadith of al-Rabi' ibn Anas: "His Throne was upon the water. When He created the heavens and the earth, He divided that water into two parts, and He made the clear part (saffa'/saffah) beneath the Throne, and it is the Sea that is kindled (al-bahr al-masjur), so not a drop falls from it until the Trumpet is blown, then something like dew descends from it, and bodies grow from it."]

* *
As for His words, ﴿that He may test you as to which of you is best in deed﴾, He, exalted is His remembrance, says: And He is the One who created the heavens and the earth, O people, and created you in six days = ﴿that He may test you﴾, he says: that He may examine you [See the explanation of "trial" (al-bala') above: 13:448, note 3, and the references there] = ﴿as to which of you is best in deed﴾, he says: as to which of you is best in obedience to Him, as follows:

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 7 (part 2 of 2):**

17989 - Narrated to us by Dawud ibn al-Muhabbar, who said: Abd al-Wahid ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Kulayb ibn Wa'il, from Abd Allah ibn Umar, from the Prophet (ﷺ): that he recited this verse: ﴿That He may test you as to which of you is best in deed﴾, and said: "Which of you is best in intellect, most scrupulous regarding the prohibitions of Allah, and quickest in obedience to Allah?" [[The report 17989: Dawud ibn al-Muhabbar al-Ta'i al-Thaqafi, the author of "Kitab al-Aql" (The Book of Intellect), is "like nothing" (shabbah la shay'), as Ahmad ibn Hanbal said; he did not know what hadith was. He is weak and narrates munkar reports. The critics mentioned the Kitab al-Aql, and al-Daraqutni said: "The Kitab al-Aql was composed by four men. The first of them was Maysara ibn Abd Rabbih; then Dawud ibn al-Muhabbar stole it from him and reconstructed it with chains different from those of Maysara. Abd al-Aziz ibn Abi Rija stole it from him and reconstructed it with yet other chains. Then Sulayman ibn Isa al-Sijzi stole it and brought other chains." al-Hakim said: "They related to us from al-Harith ibn Abi Usama, from him, the Kitab al-Aql, and most of what was deposited in that book is fabricated hadith upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 2/1/223, and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/2/424. And Abd al-Wahid ibn Yazid al-Basri, the storyteller, shaykh of the Sufis, a munkar al-hadith, entirely weak; biographed in Ta'jil al-Manfa'a p. 266, Mizan al-I'tidal 2:157, and Ibn Abi Hatim 3/1/20. And Kulayb ibn Wa'il ibn Habbar al-Taymi al-Yashkuri, who narrated from Ibn Umar: reliable, though Abu Zur'a declared him weak; biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 4/1/229, and Ibn Abi Hatim 3/2/167. Thus this hadith is entirely weak, and has no basis.]]

17990 - Narrated to us by al-Qasim, who said: al-Husayn narrated to us, who said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His words: ﴿That He may test you as to which of you is best in deed﴾, meaning: the two weighty things (al-thaqalan, i.e., humankind and jinn).

* *

As for His words: ﴿And if you say, "Indeed you will be resurrected after death," those who disbelieve will surely say, "This is not but obvious magic."﴾ — Exalted is He, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): And if you say to these polytheists of your people, "Indeed you will be resurrected alive after your death!" and you recite to them this, My revelation and My inspiration, ﴿they will surely say, "This is not but obvious magic,"﴾ meaning: what you recite to us of what you say is nothing but magic to its hearer, made clear to its hearer as to its reality, that it is magic.

[[In the printed edition: "إلا سحر لسامعه مبين حقيقته أنه سحر", and in the manuscript: "إلا سحر لسامعه عن حقيقته أنه سحر", and between "سحر" and "لسامعه" there is the letter "ط" indicating an error. The correct phrasing is what I have established, God willing. And see the explanation of "magic" above, p. 159, note 1, and the references there.
And the explanation of "obvious" (mubin) in the lexical indexes (bayn) above.]]

* *

This is according to the reading of those who recite: ﴿Inna hadha illa sihrun mubin﴾ (this is nothing but obvious magic).

* *

As for those who read: ﴿Inna hadha illa sahirun mubin﴾ (this is nothing but an obvious magician), then this directs the report about them to the meaning that they described the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) as being, regarding what he brought them, an obvious magician.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: We have already explained the correct reading in this matter in its parallels, previously, with what suffices without repeating it here. [[See what has passed: 11:216, 217, 265.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 8:

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And if We defer the punishment from them for a counted number of days, they will surely say, "What is it that holds it back?" Unquestionably, on the day it comes to them, it will not be turned away from them, and what they used to mock will encompass them.﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: His words, mighty and majestic is He, mean: And if We defer from these polytheists of your people, O Muhammad, the punishment, not hastening it for them, and extend their terms until ﴿a counted number of days﴾, a fixed time and known years.

* *

The root meaning of "ummah" (community, period) is what we have already explained earlier in this book: it is a group of people gathered upon one creed and religion. It is then used in many meanings that return to the original sense I have mentioned. [[See the explanation of "ummah" above, 13:285, note 3, and the references there.]] The years and the period in this place and similar places are called "ummah" only because within them a community comes to be. [[See the explanation of "ma'dudah" (counted) above, 3:417 / 4:208, and what follows.]]

* *

The meaning of the statement is: And if We defer the punishment from them until the coming of one community and the passing of another before it.

* *

Consistent with what we have said, that the meaning of "ummah" in this place is term and period, were the people of interpretation.

Those who said so:

17991. Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us. And al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, saying: Sufyan al-Thawri narrated to us, from 'Asim, from Abu Razin, from Ibn 'Abbas. And al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from 'Asim, from Abu Razin, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning ﴿And if We defer the punishment from them until a counted number of days﴾: he said, "Until a fixed term."

17992. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from 'Asim, from Abu Razin, from Ibn 'Abbas, similarly.

17994. Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿until a counted number of days﴾: he said, "A counted term."

17995. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, who said: "Until a counted term."

17996. Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning ﴿until a counted number of days﴾: he said, "Until a time."

17997. al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

17998. ... narrated to us, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

17999. al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, concerning ﴿And if We defer from them the punishment until a counted number of days﴾, meaning: We withhold the punishment from them ﴿until a counted number of days﴾. Ibn Jurayj said: Mujahid said, "Until a time."

18000. Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His words: ﴿And if We defer from them the punishment until a counted number of days﴾, meaning: until a known term. [[In the numbering I skipped No. 18001 by mistake.]]

* *

As for His words: ﴿They will surely say, "What is it that holds it back?"﴾, meaning: "They will surely say," these polytheists, "What holds it back?" That is, what prevents it from hastening the punishment with which He threatens us? [[See the explanation of "al-habs" (holding back) above, 11:172.]] This is in denial of it, and their assumption that it was delayed from them only because the one threatening was lying, as:

18002. al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said concerning His words: ﴿They will surely say, "What holds it back?"﴾: "In denial of it, or that it is nothing."

* *

As for His words: ﴿Unquestionably, on the day it comes to them, it will not be turned away from them﴾, meaning, His mention, exalted is He, confirming His threat and verifying His report: ﴿on the day it comes to them﴾, the punishment they deny, ﴿it will not be turned away from them﴾, meaning: no one turns it away from them, and no one repels it from them; rather it will descend upon them and destroy them. [[See the explanation of "al-sarf" (turning away) above, 11:286 / 13:112 / 14:582 / 15:84.]] ﴿And what they used to mock will encompass them﴾, meaning: what they used to ridicule of God's punishment will descend upon them and befall them. [[See the explanation of "haqq" (encompass) above, 11:172, and the explanation of "al-istihza'" (mockery) above in the lexical indices under (h-z-').]] Their mockery of it that God mentioned was their saying before its descent: ﴿What holds it back?﴾ and "Why does it not come to us?" [[In the printed edition: "naqalan bi-anbiya'ihi" (transmitting with His prophets), which is a meaningless confusion. In the manuscript: "wa-na'alan bi-anbiya'ihi," the first word poorly written with the remaining letters unpointed; this is the correct reading, God willing.]]

* *

Consistent with what we have said regarding this, some of the people of interpretation said.

Those who said so:

18003. al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning ﴿And what they used to mock will encompass them﴾: "What their prophets brought of the truth."

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if We let man taste mercy from Us, then take it away from him, indeed he is despairing and ungrateful﴾ (11:9).

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: And if We let man taste from Us ease and abundance in provision and livelihood, and We extend to him of the world [[See the explanation of "al-dhawq" (tasting) above, p. 146, note 6, and the references there.]] — and it is this "mercy" which He, exalted is His remembrance, mentioned in this place — ﴿then take it away from him﴾, meaning: then We strip him of that, so calamities strike him that wipe it out and carry it away [[See the explanation of "al-naz'" (taking away) above, 12:437 / 13:17.]] — ﴿indeed he is despairing and ungrateful﴾, meaning: he remains despondent of the mercy of Allah, hopeless of good.

* *

As for His saying, "ya'us" (despairing), it is a pattern of "fa'ul" (intensive form), from the saying of the speaker, "So-and-so despaired of such-and-such, so he is ya'us," when that becomes a characteristic of him. [[See the explanation of "al-ya's" (despair) above, 9:516.]]

As for His saying, "kafur" (ungrateful), it means: he is ungrateful toward the one who bestowed favour upon him, little thankful to his Lord who graced him with what He had granted him of His blessing. [[See the explanation of "al-kufr" (ingratitude/disbelief) in the language indexes above under (k-f-r).]]

* *

The people of interpretation have said things similar to what we have said.

Those who said this:

18004 – Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding ﴿And if We let man taste mercy from Us, then take it away from him, indeed he is despairing and ungrateful﴾, he said: O son of Adam, when you have a blessing from Allah of abundance, safety and well-being, you are ungrateful for what you have of it; and when it is taken from you, [the devil] seeks to restrain your self-restraint and your intellect [[In the printed edition: "yabtaghi lak farighak, fa-yu'us..." which differs from the manuscript; the manuscript reads: "yas'a far'aka wa-'aqlaka fa-yu'us," and the correct reading is what is given here. "Al-qad'" means restraint and prevention.]], so he despairs of the spirit of Allah, despondent of His mercy, as is the hypocrite and the disbeliever.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 10–11:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if We let him taste ease after hardship has touched him, he will surely say, "The evils have gone from me." Indeed, he is exultant and boastful.﴾ (10) ﴿Except for those who are patient and do righteous deeds; those will have forgiveness and great reward.﴾ (11)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: His mention, exalted is He, says: "And if We spread out for man in his worldly life, grant him ease in his living, and expand his provision for him" — and these are the blessings (al-ni'ma) of which Allah, mighty is His praise, said: ﴿And if We let him taste blessing (in the Arabic: ni'ma' - see the explanation of "al-na'ma'" in the earlier lexical indexes under the root n-‘-m) ﴾ [[See the explanation of "al-na'maa'" in the earlier lexical indexes (root n-‘-m).]] And His saying: ﴿after hardship has touched him﴾ means: after a narrowing of living that he had been in, and a difficulty that he was dealing with [[See the explanation of "al-mass" earlier, p. 219, note 2, and the references there. And the explanation of "al-durra'" earlier, p. 49, note 1, and the references there.]] ﴿he will surely say, "The evils have gone from me"﴾ — His mention, exalted is He, says: he will surely say at that time: "The narrowness and difficulty have gone from me, and the hardships and adversities have passed." ﴿Indeed, he is exultant and boastful﴾ — His mention, exalted is He, says: indeed man is exultant at the blessings that are given to him, rejoicing in them [[See the explanation of "farih" earlier, vol. 14, p. 289.]]

﴿Boastful﴾ means: possessing pride in what he has attained of abundance in the world, and what has been spread out for him of living in it, and he forgets its vicissitudes and the adversity of its calamities, and abandons seeking the lasting bliss and the joy that endures and does not pass away. [[In the printed edition: "nakad al-'awarid", differing from the manuscript; "al-'awa'is" is the plural of "ha'is" or "ha'isa", and similarly "al-'awsa'", and all of it means: hardship, difficulty and need.]]

Hadith 18005 — Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His saying: ﴿The evils have gone from me﴾ — out of delusion regarding Allah and audacity against Him. ﴿Indeed, he is exultant﴾ — and Allah does not love the exultant. ﴿Boastful﴾ — after he has been given, and he does not thank Allah.

* *

Then Allah, mighty is His praise, made an exception from the man whom He described with these two attributes: "those who are patient and do righteous deeds." The exception of them from him is permissible because "man" carries the sense of a genus and the sense of a plural. It is like His saying: ﴿By time, indeed mankind is in loss, except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ [Surah al-'Asr: 1–3] [[See the Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' in the interpretation of the verse. From here I will refer to the manuscript copy of Ma'ani al-Qur'an, because the rest of the book has not yet been printed. The copy I refer to is the manuscript at the Dar al-Kutub al-Misriyya under number: B 24986, a photograph of a copy of the "Baghdadli Wahbi" library at the Suleymaniye Library in Istanbul.]]

So He, exalted is He, said: ﴿except those who are patient and do righteous deeds﴾ — for if a hardship from the world and difficulty in it come upon them, that does not turn them from the obedience of Allah; rather, they are patient with His command and decree. And if they attain in it ease and abundance, they thank Him and fulfill His rights with what He has given them of it. Allah says: ﴿those will have forgiveness﴾ — He will forgive it for them, and will not disgrace them with it on their return — ﴿and great reward﴾ — meaning: they will have from Allah, along with the forgiveness of their sins, a reward for their righteous deeds that they did in the abode of the world, abundant and magnificent.

Hadith 18006 — Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj: ﴿except those who are patient﴾ — at the time of trial — ﴿and do righteous deeds﴾ — at the time of blessing — ﴿those will have forgiveness﴾ — for their sins — ﴿and great reward﴾ — he said: Paradise.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if We let him taste ease after hardship has touched him, he will surely say, "The evils have gone from me." Indeed, he is exultant and boastful.﴾ (10) ﴿Except for those who are patient and do righteous deeds; those will have forgiveness and great reward.﴾ (11)
