Hadith 18006 — Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj: ﴿except those who are patient﴾ — at the time of trial — ﴿and do righteous deeds﴾ — at the time of blessing — ﴿those will have forgiveness﴾ — for their sins — ﴿and great reward﴾ — he said: Paradise.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 12:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿So perhaps you will leave some of what is revealed to you, and your breast will be constricted by it, lest they say, "Why has a treasure not been sent down to him, or an angel not come with him?" You are only a warner, and Allah is Disposer of all things.﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: Allah, the Exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "So perhaps you, O Muhammad, will leave some of what your Lord reveals to you, [failing] to convey from His command that you should deliver it, and your breast will be constricted by what is revealed to you, so that you do not convey it to them, for fear that ﴿they will say, 'Why has a treasure not been sent down to him, or an angel not come with him?'﴾ [while] he has no one to confirm that he is truly a Messenger of Allah!" Allah, the Exalted, says: "Then convey to them what I have revealed to you, for you are only a warner, warning them of My punishment and cautioning them of My might because of their disbelief in Me. The signs they ask of you are with Me and within My authority; I send them down when I wish, and it is not incumbent upon you except conveying and warning." ﴿And Allah is Disposer of all things﴾, meaning: Allah is the Sustainer of everything, and its management is in His hand. So carry out what I have commanded you, and let their demand of you for signs not prevent you from conveying My revelation and carrying out My command. [[See the explanation of the terms of this verse in the lexical indexes of what has preceded.]]

* *

Similar to what we have said on this, some of the people of interpretation have said.

Those who said that:

18007- Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, who said: Allah said to His Prophet: "So perhaps you will leave some of what is revealed to you," [meaning] that you would not act upon what you were commanded and call to it as you were sent. They said: ﴿Why has a treasure not been sent down to him?﴾ We do not see wealth with him; where is the wealth? ﴿Or an angel not come with him?﴾ to warn with him? ﴿You are only a warner﴾, so convey what you were commanded.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 13:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"? Say, "Then bring ten surahs like it, invented, and call upon whomever you can besides Allah, if you should be truthful."﴾ (11:13)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: Almighty Allah says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "This Qur'an is sufficient for you as proof of the truth of what you have brought them, and as an indication of the soundness of your prophethood, above all other signs, since signs are only given as evidence of the truth of the one to whom they are given, because all of creation is unable to bring forth the like of them. This Qur'an, all of creation is incapable of bringing forth its like." [[In the printed edition: "all of creation has been unable," which differs from what is in the manuscript, and it corrupts the meaning considerably.]] "If they say, 'He has invented it'," meaning: they have fabricated it and called it a lie. [[See the explanation of "al-iftira' (invention)" in the language indexes earlier (root f-r-y).]]

* *

= This is what shows that the meaning of the speech is what we have mentioned: His saying, ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"﴾ to the end of the verse. By His saying, ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"﴾, He means: "Do they say, 'He has invented it'?"

* *

= We have already explained the reason the Arabs use "am" (or) in such a position. [[See the explanation of "am" earlier at 2:492, 3:97, and then 14:165, note 1, and the references there.]]

* *

= So say to them: "Bring ten surahs like this Qur'an, invented (muftarayat)," meaning: fabricated and made up, "if what I have brought you of this Qur'an is an invention and not a miraculous sign like the other signs you have asked of me, such as the treasure you said, 'Why was it not sent down to him?' or the angel you said, 'Why did he not come with him as a warner and confirmer?' For you are my people, you are of my tongue, and I am a man from among you. It is impossible that I alone could fabricate a hundred and fourteen surahs, while none of you together could invent and make up ten surahs like it, especially if you seek help in that from whomever you wish of creation."

He, may His praise be exalted, says: "Say to them: 'Call upon whomever you are able to call upon besides Allah'," meaning: other than Allah, for the invention and fabrication of that from among the gods. "If you are unable to invent ten surahs like it, then it has become clear to you that you are liars in your saying, ﴿He has invented it﴾, and the reality of what I have brought you has been established for you, that it is from Allah. It was not for you to choose the signs against your Lord, when there has come to you, as proof of the reality of what you deny, that it is from Allah, the like of what you ask for as proof and desire, claiming that you would believe upon its arrival."

* *

As for His saying, ﴿if you should be truthful﴾, it relates to His saying, ﴿Then bring ten surahs like it﴾. The full meaning is: "Say: Then bring ten surahs like it, invented, if you are truthful that Muhammad has invented this Qur'an, and call upon whomever you can besides Allah to help you in that, from among the gods and rivals."

18008 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"﴾: "They have indeed said it. ﴿Say: Then bring ten surahs like it, invented. And call upon your witnesses﴾," he said: "They testify that it is like it." This is what al-Qasim said in his narration. [[That is, he said "and call upon your witnesses," though this is not in this verse; rather it is in another verse, the verse of Surat al-Baqarah 2:23: "And if you are in doubt about what We have sent down upon Our servant, then bring a surah like it and call upon your witnesses other than Allah, if you should be truthful."]]

**The interpretation of His words, may He be exalted: ﴿Then if they do not respond to you, know that it was sent down with the knowledge of God, and that there is no god but Him. Will you then submit?﴾ (11:14)**

Abu Ja'far said: God, may He be remembered, says to His Prophet: "Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists: If those whom you call upon besides God do not answer you, [when you challenge them] to produce ten surahs like this Qur'an, fabricated, and neither you nor they are able to produce such, then know and be certain that it was sent down from heaven upon Muhammad ﷺ with the knowledge and permission of God, and that Muhammad did not fabricate it, nor is he able to fabricate it." ﴿And that there is no god but Him﴾ means: "And be certain also that there is no deity deserving of worship over creation except God, to whom belong the creation and the command. So cast off the rivals and false gods, and devote worship to Him alone."

* *

It has been said that His words ﴿Then if they do not respond to you﴾ are an address from God to His Prophet, as if He had said: "If these disbelievers do not respond to you, O Muhammad, then know, O polytheists, that it was sent down with the knowledge of God." But that interpretation is far from the apparent meaning.

* *

As for His words ﴿Will you then submit?﴾, the meaning is: "Will you then submit to God in obedience and devote worship sincerely to Him, after the proof has been established against you?"

* *

Mujahid used to say: "By this statement is meant the companions of Muhammad ﷺ."

18009: Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿Will you then submit?﴾ He said: "[It is addressed] to the companions of Muhammad ﷺ."

18010: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said —

18010: And Ishaq narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His words: ﴿And that there is no god but Him, will you then submit?﴾ He said: "[It is addressed] to the companions of Muhammad ﷺ."

18011: Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.

* *

It has also been said: "﴿Then if they do not respond to you﴾, and the address at the beginning of the speech was directed to a single person, namely His words ﴿Say, then bring﴾, and He did not say 'if they do not respond to you [singular]', in accordance with what we have already explained earlier regarding the address to the leader of a people and their chief: the Arabs sometimes give his address the form of the plural when his address is also to his followers and soldiers, and sometimes the form of the singular when he is alone in himself." [See what has passed: 12:298, 549, note 1, and the references there.]

The Interpretation of His Words, the Exalted: ﴿Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornment, We will pay them in full for their deeds therein, and they will not be deprived therein.﴾ (11:15)

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Whoever intends by his deed the life of this world, seeking by it only the world and its adornment,[[In the printed edition: "and its furnishings and its adornment he seeks by it," which corrupts and disorders the sense. It is correct in the manuscript as I have recorded it.]] We will pay them in full the rewards of their deeds therein and their recompense = ﴿and they therein﴾, meaning: in this world, ﴿will not be deprived﴾, meaning: their reward will not be diminished, but they will receive it in full in this world.[[For the explanation of "adornment," see what has preceded at p. 177, notes 2 and 5, and the references there. For the explanation of "tawfiyah" (paying in full), see the language indexes (w-f-y) earlier.]][[For the explanation of "bakhs" (deprivation/diminishing), see what has preceded at 6:56 and 12:555.]]

* *

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said what we have said regarding its interpretation.

Those who said so:

18012. Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornment﴾ to the end of the verse: It is what Allah gives them of the world in return for their good deeds, because they will not be wronged even a speck (naqir). He says: whoever performs a righteous deed seeking the world, fasting, praying, or performing night prayer, and does not do it except to seek the world, Allah says: I will pay him in full what he sought in this world of reward, and his deed which he performed seeking the world will be nullified, and he will be among the losers in the Hereafter.

18013. Ibn Wakf' related to us, saying: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: ﴿Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornment, We will pay them in full for their deeds therein﴾. He said: the reward for what they did in the world of good, they are given in this world, and they have in the Hereafter nothing but the Fire, and what they did therein is nullified.

* *

18014. Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr regarding His words: ﴿Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornment, We will pay them in full for their deeds therein﴾. He said: the equivalent of the good they did is given to them in this world, and they have in the Hereafter nothing but the Fire, and what they did therein is nullified. He said: this is like the verse in Surat al-Rum: ﴿And what you give in usury to increase within the wealth of people does not increase with Allah﴾ [Surat al-Rum: 39].[[In the printed edition: "and perhaps they did of good what they were given in this world," which is a garbled statement without meaning. In the manuscript it is what I have recorded, except that it has "wa-rubba ma" written without dots, and the correct reading is what I have given.]]

18015. Ibn Wakf' related to us, saying: my father related to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: ﴿Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornment﴾. He said: whoever works for the world, it is paid to him in this world.

18016. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornment﴾. He said: whoever performs a deed of what Allah has commanded, such as prayer or charity, not seeking thereby the Face of Allah, Allah gives him in this world the reward of that, like what he spent. That is His words: ﴿We will pay them in full their deeds therein﴾, in this world, ﴿and they therein will not be deprived﴾, the reward of what they did therein, ﴿those are the ones for whom there is nothing in the Hereafter but the Fire, and what they did therein is nullified﴾, to the end of the verse.

18017. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from 'Isa, meaning Ibn Maymun, from Mujahid regarding His words: ﴿Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornment﴾. He said: of those whose deeds are not accepted; he is recompensed for it, given its reward.

18018. Ibn Wakf' related to us, saying: Ibn Yaman related to us, from Sufyan, from 'Isa al-Jurashi, from Mujahid: ﴿Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornment, We will pay them in full for their deeds therein﴾. He said: of those whose deeds are not accepted; it is hastened for him in this world.[[The report 18018: "'Isa al-Jurashi" is "'Isa ibn Maymun al-Jurashi al-Makki," mentioned in the preceding report. It has passed several times before, the last being number 14677.]]

18019. Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah regarding His words: ﴿Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornment, We will pay them in full for their deeds therein and they therein will not be deprived﴾. That is: they will not be wronged. He says: whoever has the world as his concern and his preoccupation (sadam),[["Al-sadam" (with two fathas): being infatuated with a thing and persisting in it, grieving over its pursuit, and regretting its loss. In a hadith: "Whoever has the world as his concern and his sadam, Allah places his poverty between his eyes."]] and his aim and his intention, Allah repays him for his good deeds in this world, then he goes to the Hereafter, and he has no good deed for which he is given a reward. As for the believer, he is repaid for his good deeds in this world and is rewarded for them in the Hereafter = ﴿and they therein will not be deprived﴾, that is: in the Hereafter they will not be wronged.

18020. Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us = and al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us = all of them, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornment, We will pay them in full for their deeds therein﴾ to the end of the verse. He said: whoever's aspiration is only the world, seeking only it, Allah gives him wealth and gives him in it what sustains him, and that is a recompense for him for his deed. ﴿And they therein will not be deprived﴾. He said: they will not be wronged.

18021. ... He said: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi: that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever does good to a doer of good, his reward has fallen upon Allah in the swift world and the delayed Hereafter."[[The report 18021: this is a mursal report.]]

18022. It was related to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words: ﴿Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornment, We will pay them in full for their deeds therein﴾ to the end of the verse: He says: whoever does a righteous deed without piety = meaning from among the polytheists = is given a reward for that in this world: he keeps the ties of kinship, gives to the beggar, shows mercy to the distressed, and in similar acts of righteousness. Allah hastens for him the reward of his deed in this world, expands for him in livelihood and provision, gladdens his eye with what He has bestowed upon him, and wards off from him the hardships of the world, and similar things; and he has no share in the Hereafter.

18023. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Hafs ibn 'Umar Abu 'Umar al-Darir related to us, saying: Hammam related to us, from Qatadah, from Anas regarding His words: ﴿We will pay them in full their deeds therein, and they therein will not be deprived﴾. He said: it concerns the Jews and the Christians.

18024. ... He said: Hafs ibn 'Umar related to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zuray' related to us, from Abu Raja' al-Azdi, from al-Hasan: ﴿We will pay them in full their deeds therein﴾. He said: their good things.

18025. Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, from Abu Raja', from al-Hasan, the like of it.

18026. Ibn Wakf' related to us, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, from Abu Raja', from al-Hasan, the like of it.

18027. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Suwayd related to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Wuhayb: that it reached him that Mujahid used to say regarding this verse: they are the people of showing off (riya'), they are the people of showing off.

18028. ... He said: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Haywah ibn Shurayh, who said: al-Walid ibn Abi al-Walid Abu 'Uthman related to me, that 'Uqbah ibn Muslim related to him, that Shufayy ibn Matia al-Asbahi related to him: that he entered Medina, and there he saw a man around whom people had gathered. He asked: who is this? They said: Abu Hurayrah! So I drew near to him until I sat before him, while he was narrating to the people. When he fell silent and was alone,[[In the printed edition: "wa-khalla," the correct reading being what I have recorded, as in the manuscript.]] I said: I beseech you by the right of, and by the right of,[["By the right of, and by the right of": this is an oath upon him, meaning "by the right of such-and-such," and it is abbreviated.]] that you narrate to me a hadith you heard from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), which you understood and retained. He said: Abu Hurayrah said: I will do so, I will narrate to you a hadith the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) narrated to me! Then he gave a gasp (nashgha),[["Nashagha al-rajul": he gasped until he nearly fainted. Abu 'Ubaydah said: "A person only does that out of longing for his companion, or for a thing lost, grieving over it and loving to meet it."]] then recovered and said: I will narrate to you a hadith the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) narrated to me in this house, with no one present except me and him! Then Abu Hurayrah gave a severe gasp, then leaned forward, falling on his face, and remained so for a long time. Then he recovered and said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) narrated to me: when the Day of Resurrection comes, Allah, blessed and exalted, descends to the Judgment to decide among them, and every nation will be kneeling. The first to be called will be a man who gathered the Qur'an, a man who was killed in the way of Allah, and a man of abundant wealth. Allah will say to the reciter: Did I not teach you what I sent down upon My Messenger? He will say: Yes, O Lord! He will say: What did you do with what you were taught? He will say: I used to stand during the hours of the night and the hours of the day! Allah will say to him: You lie! And the angels will say: You lie! Allah will say to him: Rather, you wished that it be said: "So-and-so is a reciter," and that was said! Then the man of wealth will be brought, and Allah will say to him: Did I not widen your provision until I did not let you need anyone? He will say: Yes, O Lord! He will say: What did you do with what I gave you? He will say: I used to maintain the ties of kinship and give charity. Allah will say to him: You lie! And the angels will say: You lie! Allah will say to him: Rather, you wished that it be said: "So-and-so is generous," and that was said! Then the one who was killed in the way of Allah will be brought, and it will be said to him: For what were you killed? He will say: I was commanded to strive in Your way, so I fought until I was killed. Allah will say to him: You lie! And the angels will say to him: You lie! Allah will say to him: Rather, you wished that it be said: "So-and-so is brave," and that was said! Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) struck my knee and said: O Abu Hurayrah, those three are the first of Allah's creation whom the Fire will be kindled with on the Day of Resurrection.[[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "tusa''ar lahum" (kindled for them); the correct reading is what I have recorded from Sunan al-Tirmidhi.]]

= Abu 'Uthman al-Walid said: 'Uqbah informed me that it was Shufayy who entered upon Mu'awiyah, and informed him of this.

Abu 'Uthman said: al-'Ala' ibn Abi Hakim related to me that he was an executioner (sayyaf) for Mu'awiyah. He said: a man entered upon him and related this to him from Abu Hurayrah. Abu Hurayrah had said: this has been done to those, so how about whoever remains of the people! Then Mu'awiyah wept intensely until we thought he had died, and we said: [this man has brought us] evil news![[In the printed edition: "qalu: hadha al-rajul sharr," which is thoroughly corrupt. The manuscript is similar except it has "bisharr." The correct reading is what I have recorded from Sunan al-Tirmidhi, and I have placed the addition between brackets.]] Then Mu'awiyah recovered, wiped his face, and said: Allah and His Messenger have spoken truly: ﴿Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornment, We will pay them in full for their deeds therein﴾, and he recited to: ﴿and what they did was in vain, and what they used to do is false﴾.[[The report 18028: "Ibn al-Mubarak" is "'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak," the well-known imam. "Haywah ibn Shurayh al-Tujibi al-Misri" was narrated by the group (al-jama'ah) and has passed many times, the last being number 16382. "Al-Walid ibn Abi al-Walid al-Qurashi, Abu 'Uthman," is trustworthy, and has passed as number 5455. "'Uqbah ibn Muslim al-Tujibi al-Misri" is a trustworthy Successor (tabi'i), and has passed many times, the last being numbers 13240 and 13241. "Shufayy ibn Matia al-Asbahi al-Misri" is a trustworthy Successor, one of the trustworthy Egyptians, who was a learned and wise scholar. Ibn Jarir al-Tabari counted him among the Companions, but this hardly holds. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, Ibn Sa'd 7/2/201, al-Kabir 2/2/267, Ibn Abi Hatim 2/1/389, and al-Isabah in his biography in the fourth section of the letter shin. The Hafiz Ibn Hajar said: "Baqi ibn Makhlad also cited his hadith in his Musnad. I have not seen a narration of his from a Companion except from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As, and his hadith from him is in the Sunan. Al-Bukhari, Ibn Hibban, Abu Hatim al-Razi and others asserted that he was a Successor and that his hadith is mursal." This report was related by al-Tirmidhi in "The Book of Asceticism," in the chapter "Showing Off and Ostentation," and he said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith." Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah said: "When al-Tirmidhi says hasan gharib, he may mean that it is gharib from that path, but the text has supporting evidence that makes it part of the hasan category." I say: the strangeness of this hadith lies in Shufayy ibn Matia's narration from Abu Hurayrah, and no other well-known narration of Shufayy is known except from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As. Although his narration from Abu Hurayrah is good despite its strangeness, because it is plausible that he narrated from him, and plausible that he met him once in Medina, as this report indicates. It was also related in abridged form by al-Nasa'i in his Sunan 6:23, by another route, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la, from Khalid, from Juraij, from Yusuf ibn Yusuf, from Sulayman ibn Yasar, who said: The people dispersed from around Abu Hurayrah, and a speaker from the people of Syria said to him: O shaykh, narrate to me a hadith you heard from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)... the hadith. So this speaker from the people of Syria appears to be Shufayy ibn Matia, who had been in Syria before settling in Egypt. Shufayy is in the second generation of Egyptian Successors, as Ibn Sa'd counted him. Sulayman ibn Yasar al-Hilali is one of the seven jurists of Medina, and heard from Abu Hurayrah. So it seems this speaker, or Shufayy ibn Matia, was young at that time asking Abu Hurayrah in Medina. And the report of al-Nasa'i is the supporting evidence from the sound hadith which led al-Tirmidhi to describe the first report as "hasan gharib."]]

18029. Al-Harith related to me, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from 'Isa ibn Maymun, from Mujahid: ﴿Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornment﴾ to the end of the verse. He said: of those whose deeds are not accepted; who fasts and prays seeking the world, and the concern of the Hereafter is removed from him = ﴿and they therein will not be deprived﴾, meaning they will not be diminished.[[In the manuscript and the printed edition: "wa-yadfa'u 'anhu wahm al-akhirah" (and the illusion of the Hereafter is removed from him). This has no sense, and I think the correct reading is what I have recorded.]]

**The interpretation of His words, Exalted is He: ﴿Those are the ones for whom there is nothing in the Hereafter but the Fire, and what they did therein will come to nothing, and what they used to do is void.﴾ (11:16)**

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, Exalted is He, says: These are the ones I mentioned, to whom We pay the wages of their deeds in this world. ﴿For them there is nothing in the Hereafter but the Fire﴾, they will burn in it. ﴿And what they did therein will come to nothing﴾, meaning: what they did in this world will be gone. [[See the explanation of "ḥabaṭa" (to come to nothing) above, vol. 14, p. 344, note 1, and the references there.]] ﴿And what they used to do is void﴾, because they used to work for other than Allah, so Allah nullified it and rendered its doer's reward null.

* *

**The interpretation of His words, Exalted is He: ﴿Is one who has a clear proof from his Lord, and a witness from Him recites it, and before it the Book of Moses as a guide and mercy? Those believe in it﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, Exalted is He, says: ﴿Is one who has a clear proof from his Lord﴾, meaning: his religion has been made clear to him, so he has clarity about it. [[See the explanation of "bayyina" (clear proof) above in the lexical indexes, root (b-y-n).]] ﴿And a witness from Him recites it﴾. [[See the explanation of "yatlu" (recites) and "shāhid" (witness) above in the lexical indexes, roots (t-l-w) and (sh-h-d).]]

* *

The scholars of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed about the interpretation of this.

Some of them said: By His words ﴿Is one who has a clear proof from his Lord﴾ He means Muhammad (ﷺ).

Those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Khalaf narrated to me, saying: Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, saying: Shaybān narrated to us, from Qatādah, from ʿUrwah, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥanafiyyah, who said: I said to my father: O father, are you the one who recites in ﴿and a witness from Him recites it﴾? He said: No, by Allah, my son! I wish I were him, but it is his tongue.

18032. Ibn Bashshār narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abī ʿAdī narrated to us, from ʿAwf, from al-Ḥasan, regarding His words ﴿and a witness from Him recites it﴾, he said: his tongue.

18035. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazīd narrated to us, saying: Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatādah, regarding His words ﴿Is one who has a clear proof from his Lord﴾: he is Muhammad, who had a clear proof from his Lord.

18036. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazīd narrated to us, saying: Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatādah, from al-Ḥasan, regarding His words ﴿and a witness from Him recites it﴾: he said: his tongue.

18037. Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatādah: ﴿and a witness from Him recites it﴾, he said: his tongue is the witness.

18038. Ibn Wakīʿ narrated to us, saying: Abū Usāmah narrated to us, from Shuʿbah, from Abū Rajāʾ, from al-Ḥasan, the same.

18039. Ibn Wakīʿ narrated to us, saying: Ghundar narrated to us, from ʿAwf, from al-Ḥasan, the same.

* *

Others said: By His words ﴿and a witness from Him recites it﴾ He means Muhammad (ﷺ).

Those who said this:

18040. Muḥammad ibn Bashshār narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abī ʿAdī narrated to us, from ʿAwf, from Sulaymān al-ʿAllāf, from al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī, regarding His words ﴿and a witness from Him recites it﴾: he said: The witness is Muhammad (ﷺ). [[The report 18040: Sulaymān al-ʿAllāf is biographed in al-Kabīr (2/2/31) and Ibn Abī Ḥātim (2/1/153), and they mention no criticism of him; they said that a report reached him from al-Ḥasan, and ʿAwf narrated from him. al-Bukhārī said: mursal (a report with a missing link). Probably this is what he means by this report; see the following report. In the printed edition and manuscript it reads "from al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī," which is an error, as shown by what I have mentioned here, and see the following report and the one after it.]]

18041. Ibn Wakīʿ narrated to us, saying: Ghundar narrated to us, from ʿAwf, who said: Sulaymān al-ʿAllāf narrated to me, saying: It reached me that al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī said: ﴿and a witness from Him recites it﴾, he said: Muhammad (ﷺ).

18042. ... said: Abū Usāmah narrated to us, from ʿAwf, from Sulaymān al-ʿAllāf, who heard al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī: ﴿and a witness from Him recites it﴾, he says: Muhammad, he is the witness from Allah. [[The reports 18041 and 18042: see the note on Sulaymān al-ʿAllāf above. In both reports the manuscript and printed edition read "al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī," but the correct reading is what I have written, as already noted in the note on the previous report.]]

18043. Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words ﴿Is one who has a clear proof from his Lord and a witness from Him recites it﴾: he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had a clear proof from his Lord, and the Qur'an is recited by a witness also from Allah, that he is the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). [[In the printed edition: "a witness from Him also," and what is in the manuscript is the better reading.]]

18044. Ibn Wakīʿ narrated to us, saying: Jarīr narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujāhid: ﴿Is one who has a clear proof from his Lord﴾, he said: the Prophet (ﷺ).

18045. Ibn Wakīʿ narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from Naḍr ibn ʿArabī, from ʿIkrimah, the same.

18046. ... said: my father narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Manṣūr, from Ibrāhīm, the same.

18047. al-Ḥārith narrated to us, saying: Abū Khālid narrated to us, saying: I heard Sufyān say: ﴿Is one who has a clear proof from his Lord﴾, he said: Muhammad (ﷺ).

* *

Others said: It is ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib.

Those who said this:

18048. Muḥammad ibn ʿUmārah al-Asadī narrated to us, saying: Razīq ibn Marzūq narrated to us, saying: Ṣabbāḥ al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, from Jābir, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Najiyy, who said: ʿAlī (may Allah be pleased with him) said: There is no man of Quraysh but that a verse or two were revealed about him. A man said to him: And you, what was revealed about you? ʿAlī said: Do you not read the verse revealed about Hūd: ﴿and a witness from Him recites it﴾? [[The report 18048: Razīq ibn Marzūq al-Kūfī al-Muqriʾ al-Bajalī narrated from Abū al-Aḥwaṣ and Ibn ʿUyaynah, and Sahl ibn Shuʿayb; and Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā al-Ṣūfī and Abū Ḥātim al-Rāzī narrated from him, and Abū Ḥātim said: "ṣadūq" (truthful). Biographed in Ibn Abī Ḥātim (1/2/506). "Ṣabbāḥ al-Farrāʾ": I have not found him, and I fear he may be "Ṣabbāḥ ibn Yaḥyā al-Muzanī," the Shiʿi who was abandoned (matrūk), who was mentioned earlier under no. 16113. "Jābir" is al-Juʿfī, Jābir ibn Yazīd al-Juʿfī, who is weak, indeed what is said about him may be even harsher; he was beyond that a Rafidi (extreme Shiʿi) who reviled the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Ibn Ḥibbān said: "He was one of the companions of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Saba', and he used to say that ʿAlī would return to this world." Mentioned several times, the last being no. 14008. "ʿAbd Allāh ibn Najiyy ibn Salamah al-Kūfī al-Ḥaḍramī," is not strong; his father was the one who carried the water-skin (muṭahhara) of ʿAlī (may Allah be pleased with him). al-Bukhārī said: "fīhi naẓar" (there is problem with him). Biographed in al-Tahdhīb, Ibn Abī Ḥātim (2/2/184), and Mīzān al-Iʿtidāl (2:82). al-Dhahabī said: "Jābir al-Juʿfī narrated from him, and so his reports are unusual from Jābir." al-Nasāʾī declared him reliable (thiqah). In the printed edition it reads "ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yaḥyā," which means the editor did not read the manuscript well enough to recognise the name.]]

* *

Others said: It is Gabriel.

Those who said this:

18049. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazīd narrated to us, saying: Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatādah, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿and a witness from Him recites it﴾, that he used to say: Gabriel.

18050. Abū Kurayb and Ibn Wakīʿ narrated to us, both saying: Ibn Idrīs narrated to us, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿUbayd Allāh, from Ibrāhīm: ﴿and a witness from Him recites it﴾, he said: Gabriel.

18051. Abū Kurayb narrated to us again, with his chain from Ibrāhīm, and said: He said: They say "ʿAlī," but it is Gabriel.

18052. Abū Kurayb and Ibn Wakīʿ narrated to us, both saying: Ibn Idrīs narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujāhid, who said: He is Gabriel, who recited the Torah, the Gospel and the Qur'an, and he is the witness from Allah.

18053. Ibn Bashshār narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, saying: Sufyān narrated to us; and Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Mukhrimī narrated to us, saying: Jaʿfar ibn ʿAwn narrated to us, saying: Sufyān narrated to us; and al-Ḥasan ibn Yaḥyā narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, saying: al-Thawrī informed us; and al-Muthannā narrated to me, saying: Abū Nuʿaym narrated to us, saying: Sufyān narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Ibrāhīm: ﴿and a witness from Him recites it﴾, he said: Gabriel.

18054. Muḥammad ibn al-Muthannā narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, saying: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Ibrāhīm, the same.

18055. ... said: Sahl ibn Yūsuf narrated to us, saying: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Ibrāhīm, the same.

18056. Ibn Wakīʿ narrated to us, saying: Jarīr narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Ibrāhīm, the same.

18057. ... said: Jarīr narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujāhid, who said: Gabriel.

18058. ... said: ʿAbd Allāh narrated to us, from Isrāʾīl, from al-Suddī, from Abū Ṣāliḥ: ﴿and a witness from Him recites it﴾, he said: Gabriel.

18059. ... said: Abū Muʿāwiyah narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk: ﴿and a witness from Him recites it﴾, he said: Gabriel.

18060. ... It was reported from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abū Muʿādh say: ʿUbayd ibn Sulaymān informed us, saying: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say regarding His words ﴿Is one who has a clear proof from his Lord﴾: he means Muhammad, who has a clear proof from Allah; ﴿and a witness from Him recites it﴾: Gabriel, a witness from Allah, who recites to Muhammad what he was sent with.

18061. Ibn Wakīʿ narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from Abū Jaʿfar, from al-Rabīʿ, from Abū al-ʿĀliyah, who said: It is Gabriel.

18062. ... said: my father narrated to us, from Naḍr ibn ʿArabī, from ʿIkrimah, who said: It is Gabriel.

18063. ... said: my father narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Manṣūr, from Ibrāhīm, who said: Gabriel.

18064. ... Muḥammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His words: ﴿Is one who has a clear proof from his Lord﴾, meaning Muhammad, who has a clear proof from his Lord; ﴿and a witness from Him recites it﴾: he is Gabriel, a witness from Allah, by what he recites from the Book of Allah which was revealed to Muhammad. He said: It is also said: ﴿and a witness from Him recites it﴾, meaning: the angel who is with him protects it.

18065. al-Muthannā narrated to me, saying: Abū al-Nuʿmān ʿĀrim narrated to us, saying: Ḥammād ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Ayyūb, who said: Mujāhid used to say regarding His words ﴿Is one who has a clear proof from his Lord﴾: he means Muhammad; ﴿and a witness from Him recites it﴾: he said: Gabriel.

* *

Others said: It is an angel who protects him.

Those who said this:

18066. Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abū ʿĀṣim narrated to us, saying: ʿĪsā narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid: ﴿and a witness from Him recites it﴾, he said: With him is a guardian from Allah, an angel.

18067. Ibn Wakīʿ narrated to us, saying: Yazīd ibn Hārūn and Suwayd ibn ʿAmr narrated to us, from Ḥammād ibn Salamah, from Ayyūb, from Mujāhid: ﴿and a witness from Him recites it﴾, he said: An angel who protects him.

18068. ... said: Muḥammad ibn Bakr narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from one who heard Mujāhid: ﴿and a witness from Him recites it﴾, he said: The angel.

18069. al-Muthannā narrated to me, saying: Abū Ḥudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid: ﴿and a witness from Him recites it﴾, he said: One who follows him, a guardian from Allah, an angel.

18070. al-Muthannā narrated to me, saying: al-Ḥajjāj ibn al-Minhāl narrated to us, saying: Ḥammād narrated to us, from Ayyūb, from Mujāhid: ﴿and a witness from Him recites it﴾, he said: The angel who protects him; ﴿they recite it as it should be recited﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 121], he said: they follow it as it should be followed.

18071. al-Qāsim narrated to us, saying: al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, saying: Ḥajjāj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujāhid: ﴿and a witness from Him recites it﴾, he said: A guardian from Allah, an angel.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these views that we have mentioned, in the interpretation of His words ﴿and a witness from Him recites it﴾, is the view of those who said: "It is Gabriel," because of the indication in His words ﴿and before it the Book of Moses as a guide and mercy﴾ confirming this. For the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) had not recited the Book of Moses before the Qur'an, so that would be evidence for the correctness of the view of those who said: "It refers to the tongue of Muhammad (ﷺ), or Muhammad himself, or ʿAlī" according to the view of those who said: "It refers to ʿAlī." And no one is known to have recited that before the Qur'an, or brought it, among those whom the scholars of interpretation mentioned as meant by His words ﴿and a witness from Him recites it﴾, other than Gabriel, peace be upon him.

* *

If someone says: If that is your evidence that the one meant is Gabriel, then the reading in His words ﴿and before it the Book of Moses﴾ should be in the accusative, because the meaning of the sentence according to your interpretation must be: "and a witness from Allah recites the Qur'an, and before the Qur'an the Book of Moses"?

It is said: The readers in the cities have unanimously agreed on reading it in the nominative, so no one has any dispute with it. And if the reading had come in the accusative, it would have been a correct reading and a correct meaning.

If he says: Then what is the reason for their reading "the Book" in the nominative, according to your claimed interpretation?

It is said: The reason for their nominative reading is that they began a statement about the coming of the Book of Moses before our Book revealed to Muhammad, so they put it in the nominative governed by "min" [and from Him]. [[In the printed edition: "so they put it in the nominative governed by 'min qablihi' (before it), and the reading is the same," which differs from what is in the manuscript because of this word which I have placed between brackets. I fear it may be an addition with no meaning, so I have kept it between brackets, as in the manuscript. See the explanation of this verse in al-Farrāʾ's Maʿānī al-Qurʾān.]] And the reading is likewise, and the meaning you mentioned of Gabriel's recitation before the Qur'an, and that its intended meaning is that, even if the statement is a new sentence as you described, relying on the indication of the sentence for its meaning.

* *

As for His words ﴿as a guide﴾ (imāman), it is in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier (qaṭʿ) of "the Book of Moses." [[The "qaṭʿ" here means the ḥāl (circumstantial accusative), as mentioned above, p. 76, note 4, and the references there.]] And His words ﴿and mercy﴾ are coordinated with "guide." It is as if it were said: And before it the Book of Moses as a guide for the Children of Israel whom they follow, and as a mercy from Allah which He recited to Moses, as:

18072. Ibn Wakīʿ narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from his father, from Manṣūr, from Ibrāhīm, regarding His words ﴿and before it the Book of Moses﴾, he said: Before it came the Book to Moses.

* *

There is an omitted element in the statement, whose mention has been left out, relying on the indication of what was mentioned, and it is: ﴿Is one who has a clear proof from his Lord and a witness from Him recites it, and before it the Book of Moses as a guide and mercy?﴾ = "like one who is in error, wavering, not guided to right conduct, not knowing truth from falsehood, and seeking by his deeds nothing but the life of this world and its adornment." This is similar to His words: ﴿Is one who is devoutly obedient during the hours of the night, prostrating and standing, fearing the Hereafter and hoping for the mercy of his Lord? Say: Are those who know equal to those who do not know?﴾ [Az-Zumar: 9] [[See the explanation of this verse in al-Farrāʾ's Maʿānī al-Qurʾān.]] And the evidence for the truth of what we have said in this matter is that this follows His words ﴿whoever desires the life of this world﴾, the verse, and then it is said: Is this better, or is one who has a clear proof from his Lord? The Arabs often do this when what has been mentioned indicates its meaning, despite the omission, like the saying of the poet: [[He is Imruʾ al-Qays.]]

*"By Him who swears, if a messenger of yours came to us other than you, but we would not find for you a way of refuge."*

[[His dīwān: 113; al-Khizānah 4:227; and others are many; it will come in the commentary 13:102 / 23:128 / 29:67 (Bulaq). This verse has been often cited as evidence for ellipsis, but al-Baghdādī made a good point, saying: "Their excuse for supposing the response is that this line is absent from most transmissions. al-Zajjājī mentioned it in his al-Amālī al-Ṣughrā and al-Kubrā among eight verses, which al-Mubarrad transmitted from a poem of Imruʾ al-Qays. We think it suffices to cite them, and they are:"*

*I sent to her while the stars were leaning, fearing that she would rise and listen.*
*So she came, walking slowly, fearing the journey, her two thighs pushing against four young women.*
*She is driven at the pace of one who has been wounded, while the drowsiness of sleep has flowed into his brain, so he stumbles.*
*She says, when I had stripped her of her garments, as you were frightened by the antelope with kohl-lined eyes, the long-necked one:*
*"Truly, if a messenger of yours came to us other than you, but we did not find a way of refuge for you."*
*Then we would have sent him back, even if he stayed long with us, but we are infatuated with your love."*
*So we spent the night turning the wild beasts away from us, as if we were two slain ones whose fall no one knew.*
*When the trembling of terror seized her, she held on to the shoulder of a bold man, who was valiant against terror.*

"This is what al-Baghdadi said, and in it there is a statement that this place cannot accommodate, but in it there is a beneficial point that is worth noting.]]

* *

And His saying: ﴿Those believe in it﴾. He says: these whom I mentioned affirm and acknowledge it, while these polytheists, who say that Muhammad invented it, disbelieve in it.

**The commentary on His words, the Exalted: ﴿And whoever among the factions disbelieves in it, then the Fire is his promised place. So be not in doubt about it. Indeed, it is the truth from your Lord, but most of the people do not believe﴾ (11:17)**

Abu Ja'far said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "Whoever disbelieves in this Qur'an, denying that it is from God," ﴿from the factions﴾, meaning those who band together in their creeds [[See the explanation of "hizb" (faction) above: 1:244 / 10:428.]], ﴿then the Fire is his promised place﴾, meaning that he will arrive at it in the Hereafter because of his denial. God says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿So be not in doubt about it﴾, meaning: do not be in doubt about it, [[See the explanation of "mirya" (doubt) above in the lexical indices under the root (m-r-y).]] concerning the fact that the promised place of those among the factions who disbelieve in the Qur'an is the Fire, and that this Qur'an which We have sent down to you is from God.

Then, may His praise be exalted, He began to give information about the Qur'an, saying: "Indeed, this Qur'an which We have sent down to you, O Muhammad, is the truth from your Lord, without any doubt in it, but most people do not affirm that this is so."

* *

If someone says: "Was the Prophet (ﷺ) in doubt that the Qur'an is from God and that it is true, such that it was said to him: 'So be not in doubt about it'?"

It is said: This is similar to His words: ﴿And if you are in doubt about what We have sent down to you﴾ [Surah Yunus: 94]. We have explained that there, [[See what has preceded shortly before, pp. 200–203.]]

* *

The people of ta'wil (interpretation, i.e., the exegetes) have said something similar to what we have said.

Those who said this:

18073. Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, saying: Ayyub narrated to us, saying: I was informed that Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "No report from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) has reached me in its correct form without my finding its confirmation in the Book of God, the Exalted, until he said: 'None of this nation hears of me, nor a Jew, nor a Christian, and then does not believe in what I was sent with, except that he enters the Fire.'" Sa'id said: "So I said: Where is this in the Book of God?" until I came upon this verse: ﴿And before it was the Book of Moses, as a guide and mercy. Those believe in it. And whoever disbelieves in it among the factions, the Fire is his promised place﴾. He said: "[The factions are] the people of all the religions."

18074. Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Makhrami and Ibn Waki' narrated to us, both saying: Ja'far ibn 'Awn narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, concerning His words: (And whoever disbelieves in it among the factions), he said: "[The factions are] all the religions."

18075. Ya'qub and Ibn Waki' narrated to me, both saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Ayyub narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: "I would not hear a report from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) in its correct form without finding its confirmation" — or he said "its affirmation" — "in the Qur'an. Then it reached me that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: 'None of this nation hears of me, nor a Jew, nor a Christian, and then does not believe in what I was sent with, except that he enters the Fire.' So I kept saying: 'Where is its confirmation?' until I came upon this: ﴿Is he who was upon clear evidence from his Lord﴾, up to His words ﴿then the Fire is his promised place﴾." He said: "So 'the factions' are all the religions."

18076. Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, saying: Ayyub narrated to me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "No one from this nation hears of me, nor a Jew, nor a Christian, and then does not believe in me, except that he enters the Fire." So I kept saying: "Where is its confirmation in the Book of God?" He said: "I rarely heard a report from the Prophet (ﷺ) without finding its confirmation in the Qur'an, until I found these verses: ﴿And whoever disbelieves in it among the factions, the Fire is his promised place﴾ — [the factions are] all the religions." [[The narrations 18073–18077 are from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, in which he related the report as a mursal (one lacking a companion in its chain). Al-Hakim transmitted it in al-Mustadrak 2:342, connected and traced back to the Prophet through Ibn 'Abbas. It is through the route of 'Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar, from Abu 'Amr al-Basri, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas. Al-Hakim said: "This is a sound hadith according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), though they did not record it," and al-Dhahabi agreed with him.

See the hadith of Abu Hurayrah in Sahih Muslim 2:186, and the hadith of Abu Musa below, number 18079.]]

18077. ... He said: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿And whoever disbelieves in it among the factions, the Fire is his promised place﴾. He said: "The disbelievers are factions, all of them united upon disbelief."

18078. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His words: ﴿And among the factions are those who deny part of it﴾ [Surah al-Ra'd: 36], meaning: they disbelieve in part of it, and they are the Jews and the Christians. He said: "It has reached us that the Prophet of God (ﷺ) used to say: 'None of this nation hears of me, nor a Jew, nor a Christian, and then dies before believing in me, except that he enters the Fire.'"

18079. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Yusuf ibn 'Adi al-Nadri narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Shu'bah, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari: that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever among my nation hears of me, or a Jew, or a Christian, and does not believe in me, will not enter Paradise." [[The report 18079: In the manuscript, "Yusuf ibn 'Adi al-Nasri" is written without diacritical points, while in the printed edition it is "al-Nadri"; I do not know where its diacritics came from. What passed earlier in the report number 10309, the narration of al-Muthanna from Yusuf ibn 'Adi from Ibn al-Mubarak, where I thought that it was "Yusuf ibn 'Adi ibn Razayq al-Taymi." I do not know what this nisba (attribution) here is, though I suspect it is "al-Misri," because Yusuf ibn 'Adi, although he was from Kufa, settled in Egypt and died there in the year 232 AH. This report was transmitted by Ahmad in his Musnad 4:396, through the route of Muhammad ibn Ja'far, from Shu'bah, from Abu Bishr, with this wording. Similarly 4:398, through the route of 'Affan, from Shu'bah.

Al-Haythami cited it in Majma' al-Zawa'id 8:261–262, at length, and in it is the statement of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari: "I said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) did not say anything except in the Book of God, the Mighty and Majestic. So I read and found: ﴿And whoever disbelieves in it among the factions, the Fire is his promised place﴾." This is similar to what Sa'id ibn Jubayr said in the earlier reports. Al-Haythami then said: "Al-Tabarani transmitted it, and the wording is his; Ahmad transmitted it similarly in the two narrations, and the narrators of Ahmad are the narrators of the Sahih; and al-Bazzar also transmitted it in abridged form."]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 18:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah? Those will be presented before their Lord, and the witnesses will say, "These are the ones who lied against their Lord. Unquestionably, the curse of Allah is upon the wrongdoers."﴾ (11:18)

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: And which of the people is more severe in punishment than one who invents a lie against Allah and then lies about Him? [[See the explanation of "iftara" (fabricated) in the previous lexical indices under (f-r-y).]] = ﴿Those will be presented before their Lord, and the witnesses will say, "These are the ones who lied against their Lord"﴾: they will be presented before their Lord on the Day of Resurrection, [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "yukadhdhibuna 'ala rabbihim" (they lie against their Lord), but the better reading is to keep it in line with the wording of the verse.]] and He will question them about what they used to do in the abode of the world, as:

18080- Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His saying: ﴿And who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah?﴾ He said: the disbeliever and the hypocrite. ﴿Those will be presented before their Lord﴾: He will question them about their deeds.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And the witnesses will say﴾, it means the angels and the prophets who witnessed them and preserved for them what they used to do. They are the plural of "shahid" (witness), like "al-asḥab," which is the plural of "sahib" (companion). ﴿These are the ones who lied against their Lord﴾: this means that these witnesses will testify in the Hereafter against these fabricators against Allah in the world, and they will say: "These are the ones who lied against their Lord in the world." Allah says: ﴿Unquestionably, the curse of Allah is upon the wrongdoers﴾, meaning: Unquestionably, the wrath of Allah is upon the transgressors who disbelieved in their Lord.

* *

Similar to what we have said regarding His saying ﴿And the witnesses will say﴾ is what the people of interpretation have said.

Mention of those who said that:

18081- Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And the witnesses will say﴾: he said, "the angels."

18082- Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: the angels.

18083- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: ﴿And the witnesses will say﴾; and the witnesses are the angels, who testify against the children of Adam for their deeds.

18084- Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada: ﴿al-ashhad﴾, he said: "the creation" = or he said: "the angels."

18085- al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, similarly.

18086- Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj: ﴿And the witnesses will say﴾: those who used to preserve their deeds against them in the world = ﴿These are the ones who lied against their Lord﴾: they preserved it and testified to it against them on the Day of Resurrection. = Ibn Jurayj said: Mujahid said: "al-Ashhad" are the angels.

18087- Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from Sufyan, who said: I asked al-A'mash about His saying: ﴿And the witnesses will say﴾, and he said: the angels.

18088- It was related to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: ﴿And the witnesses will say﴾: it means the prophets and messengers, and this is His saying: ﴿And the Day We raise up in every nation a witness against them from themselves, and We bring you as a witness against these﴾ [Surah an-Nahl: 89]. He said: and His saying: ﴿And the witnesses will say: These are the ones who lied against their Lord﴾, they say: "O our Lord, we conveyed to them the truth, but they disbelieved, so we bear witness against them that they lied against You, O our Lord."

18089- Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us, from Sa'id and Hisham, from Qatada, from Safwan ibn Muhriz al-Mazani, who said: While we were at the House with 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, and he was circumambulating, a man approached him and said: "O Ibn 'Umar, what did you hear the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say about the private conference (najwa)?" [[Mentioned in no. 6497 as: "Did you not hear"].] He said: I heard the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) say: "The believer will draw near to his Lord until He places His covering (kanaf) upon him and makes him acknowledge his sins, saying: 'Do you recognize such-and-such?' He will say: 'My Lord, I recognize it!' [[In no. 6497: "My Lord, forgive" in place of "My Lord, I recognize".]] twice, until when He has brought him to what Allah wills, He will say: 'Indeed I have concealed them for you in the world, and I forgive them for you today.' Then his record of good deeds will be given to him = or: his book, in his right hand. As for the disbelievers and the hypocrites, they will be called out against on the heads of the witnesses: 'Unquestionably, these are the ones who lied against their Lord. Unquestionably, the curse of Allah is upon the wrongdoers.'" [[The report 18089: this chain and its takhrij were previously given at no. 6497 (vol. 6: 119, 120).]]

18090- Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayya narrated to us, saying: Hisham narrated to us, from Qatada, from Safwan ibn Muhriz, from Ibn 'Umar, from the Prophet (ﷺ), similarly. [[The report 18090: this chain was previously given at no. 6497 as well.]]

18091- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: We used to be told that on that Day no one will be disgraced such that his disgrace is hidden from anyone among those created by Allah = or: the creation.

**The interpretation of the words of God, the Exalted: ﴿Those who bar from the way of God and seek to make it crooked, and they, in the Hereafter, are disbelievers﴾ (19)**

Abu Ja'far said: God, the Exalted, says: "Surely the curse of God is upon the wrongdoers ﴿who bar people from the way of God﴾," that is, who bar people from faith in Him, from acknowledging His lordship, and from devoting worship to Him alone, without the false gods and rivals. These are the polytheists of Quraysh, who would tempt those who had entered Islam away from it. [[See the explanation of "al-sadd" (barring) above, vol. 14, p. 216, note 3, and the references there.]]

﴿And seek to make it crooked﴾ means: they seek the way of God, which is Islam, to which Muhammad (ﷺ) called people, [[See the explanation of "baghā" (to seek) above, vol. 14, p. 283, note 1, and the references there.

And the explanation of "the way of God" in the lexical indexes above under (s-b-l).]] meaning: they seek to make it deviate and incline away from uprightness. [[See the explanation of "al-iwaj" (crookedness) above, vol. 7, pp. 53–54, and vol. 12, pp. 448, 559.]]

﴿And they, in the Hereafter, are disbelievers﴾ means: they, along with their barring from the way of God and their seeking to make it crooked, deny the resurrection after death. ﴿Are disbelievers﴾ means: they are those who deny that and reject it.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 20:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Those were not ones who could escape [Him] on earth, and they had no protectors besides Allah. Their punishment will be doubled. They could not bear to hear, and they used not to see.﴾ (11:20)

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, exalted is His remembrance, ﴿Those were not ones who could escape [Him] on earth﴾, He means: these, whom He, exalted is His praise, described as barring [people] from the way of Allah. He, exalted is His praise, says: They were not the kind who could defeat their Lord by fleeing from Him on earth when He wished to punish them and take vengeance on them. Rather, they were in His grip and His dominion. They could not escape Him when He wanted them, nor could they outrun Him in flight when He sought them. [See the explanation of "al-i'jaz" (inability to escape, lit. "making incapable") earlier, p. 102, note 4, and the references there.] ﴿And they had no protectors besides Allah﴾: that is, these polytheists had no helpers, besides Allah, to support them against Allah when He wished to punish them, and to come between them and Him when He punished them. Yet in this world they had a stronghold by which they protected themselves from whoever among the people wished them harm. [See the explanation of "al-wali" (protector) in the lexical indexes (w-l-y) earlier.] And His words ﴿Their punishment will be doubled﴾ mean, exalted is His remembrance: their punishment will be increased, so that for each one there will be two. [See the explanation of "al-mudā'afah" (doubling) earlier, vol. 12, pp. 417–419.]

* *

As for His words ﴿They could not bear to hear, and they used not to see﴾, the interpretation of them has been disputed.

Some said: By this, Allah described these polytheists as having had a seal set upon their hearing and their sight, so that they do not hear the truth nor see the proofs of Allah with the hearing of one who benefits, nor the sight of one who is guided.

Those who said this:

18092. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿They could not bear to hear, and they used not to see﴾: "Deaf to the truth, so they do not hear it; dumb, so they do not speak it; blind, so they do not see it, and they do not benefit from it."

18093. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿They could not bear to hear, and they used not to see﴾. He said: "They could not hear good so as to benefit from it, nor see good so as to take hold of it."

18094. al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Allah, glorified is He, informed that He placed a barrier between the people of shirk and obedience to Him in this world and in the Hereafter. As for this world, He said: ﴿They could not bear to hear﴾, which is His obedience, and ﴿nor did they see﴾. As for the Hereafter, He said: ﴿So they will not be able, with their eyes downcast﴾ [Surah al-Qalam: 42, 43].

* *

Others said: He meant by His words ﴿And they had no protectors besides Allah﴾ the gods that were worshipped and that barred [people] from the way of Allah. They said: the meaning of the speech is: "Those and their gods were not ones who could escape [Him] on earth. Their punishment will be doubled: they could not bear to hear, and they used not to see." That is, the gods had neither hearing nor sight. This is a view related from Ibn Abbas through a channel I dislike to mention because its chain is weak.

* *

Others said: The meaning is: their punishment is doubled because of what they could have heard but did not hear, and what they could have seen but did not look at with their eyes to ponder the proofs of Allah and take warning from them. They said: the particle "ba'" (bi, "because of") ought to have been used here, since He said ﴿And for them is a painful punishment because of [bi-ma] what they used to lie﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 10], meaning "because of their lying." In several places in the revelation the "ba'" is present, but its omission is permissible in speech, as when you say: "I will repay you for what you know" and "for what you know" [In the printed edition and the manuscript: "as you say in speech: la-hin bi-ma fika ma 'alimta wa-bi-ma 'alimta"; this is words that disown one another, and it is evident that the corruption is entirely from the copyist, because he wrote "la-hin" at the bottom of the page, then turned over and began the other page with "bi-ma fika ma 'amalta," which is strange. The correct reading that I have adopted is the actual wording of al-Farra's speech in Ma'ani al-Quran.] This is a view stated by some of the grammarians of Arabic.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this, in our opinion, is what Ibn Abbas and Qatadah said: that Allah, exalted is His remembrance, described them as being unable to hear the truth so as to benefit from it, and unable to see it so as to be guided by it, because they were occupied with the disbelief in which they persisted, which kept them from using their limbs in obedience to Allah. Yet they did have hearing and sight.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 11, verses 21–22:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those are the ones who have lost their souls, and what they used to fabricate has gone astray from them﴾ (21).

Abu Ja'far said: God, exalted is His remembrance, says: These people whose description is this are the ones who have cheated themselves of their portion of God's mercy [[See the explanation of "al-khusran" (loss) in the earlier word index (kh-s-r).]] = ﴿and what they used to fabricate has gone astray from them﴾, and their lie, their falsehood and their fabrication against God have been nullified, through their claim that He has partners. So what they used to worship as a god besides God has taken a course other than theirs and a path other than their path, and it has gone astray from them, because it led them to Hell, and their idols became nothing, nothing at all, since in the world they were stones, or wood, or copper. = Or [it is that] there was a friend of God, and He led him to Paradise; that too is a course other than theirs, and that too is a going astray from them.

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Without doubt, in the Hereafter they will be the greatest losers﴾ (22).

Abu Ja'far said: God, exalted is His remembrance, says: Truly, these people whose description is this, in the world and in the Hereafter, are the greatest losers, who have sold their dwellings in the gardens for the dwellings of the people of Hell in the Fire; and that is the manifest loss.

* *

We have already explained earlier that the meaning of their saying "jaramtu" is "I earned the sin," and "jarramtuhu" [is "I caused him to earn it"], [[See what preceded at 9:483–485 and 10:95. In the printed edition it read "jaramtu" and "ajramtuhu" with an alif, but the correct reading is what is in the manuscript, which matches what is in Ma'ani al-Qur'an.]] and that the Arabs frequently used it in the contexts of oaths, [[See what preceded at 9:483. However, I have not found there this detail that he mentions afterward, and I do not think any of it has passed, unless I failed to note it. I fear it may be an oversight by Abu Ja'far.]] and in the contexts of "la budda" (there is no escape), as in their saying "la jarama annaka dhahib," meaning "there is no escape that you are going," until they used it in contexts of affirmation, saying "la jarama lataqumanna," meaning: truly you will surely stand. [[See al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an on the interpretation of this verse; this is some of his speech.]] So the meaning of the statement is: there is no prevention regarding their [being the losers], and no turning away from it.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 23:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds and humbled themselves to their Lord—those are the companions of Paradise; they will abide therein eternally.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: His saying, exalted is His remembrance, means: Indeed, those who affirmed the truth of Allah and His Messenger and performed deeds of obedience to Allah in this world, and "humbled themselves to their Lord."

* *

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed regarding the meaning of "al-ikhbat" (humbling oneself, submission).

Some of them said: its meaning is: and turned penitently (anabu) to their Lord.

Mention of those who said that:

18095- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who believed and did righteous deeds and humbled themselves to their Lord﴾, he said: "al-ikhbat" is al-inabah (turning penitently).

18096- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿and humbled themselves to their Lord﴾, he says: and they turned penitently to their Lord.

* *

Others said: its meaning is: and they feared.

Mention of those who said that:

18097- al-Muthanna related to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿and humbled themselves to their Lord﴾, he says: they feared.

* *

Others said: its meaning is: they were at peace (tranquil).

Mention of those who said that:

18098- Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: 'Abd Allah related to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿and humbled themselves to their Lord﴾, he said: they were at peace.

18099- al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

18100- al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.

* *

Others said: its meaning is: they were humble (khasha'u).

Mention of those who said that:

18101- Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿and humbled themselves to their Lord﴾, "al-ikhbat" is al-takhashshu' (humility and lowliness) and al-tawadu' (modesty).

Abu Ja'far said: These sayings are close in meaning, even though their wording differs, because turning penitently to Allah stems from fear of Allah, and from humility and lowliness toward Allah through obedience, and tranquility toward Him stems from humility before Him. However, the essential meaning of "al-ikhbat" among the Arabs is humility and lowliness.

* *

He said: ﴿to their Lord﴾, and its meaning is: "and humbled themselves for their Lord." This is because the Arabs often place the preposition "li" (for) in the position of "ila" (to), and "ila" in the position of "li," as He, exalted, said: ﴿because your Lord has inspired her﴾ [Surah al-Zalzalah: 5], meaning: inspired to her. It is also possible that it was said in this way, because they were described as having aimed with their humility at Allah.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Those are the companions of Paradise; they will abide therein eternally﴾, He says: these whose description is this are the inhabitants of Paradise who will not leave it nor die therein, but they will remain therein without end. [[See the explanation of "ashab al-jannah" and "al-khulud" in the linguistic indexes (sahb), (khuld).]]

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 24:**

**On the interpretation (ta'wil) of His words, exalted is He:** ﴿The likeness of the two groups is like the blind and the deaf, and the seeing and the hearing. Are they equal in likeness? Will you not remember?﴾ (24)

Abu Ja'far said: His remembrance, exalted is He, says: The likeness of the two groups, the group of disbelief and the group of faith, is like the likeness of the blind man who sees nothing with his eye, and the deaf man who hears nothing. Likewise, the group of disbelief does not see the truth so as to follow it and act upon it, because it is preoccupied with its disbelief in God and overcome by God's abandonment of it. It does not hear the call of God to right guidance, so as to respond to it with guidance and be guided by it. It remains in its misguidance and wanders in its confusion. As for "the hearing and the seeing," that is the group of faith [[In the manuscript and the printed edition: "Likewise the group of faith," and the correct reading appears to be what I have adopted.]]. It saw the proofs of God and acknowledged what they indicate of the oneness of God, the disavowal of deities and rivals, and the prophethood of the prophets, peace be upon them. It heard the call of God, responded to it, and acted in obedience to God, as:

18102: Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn Abbas said: "The likeness of the two groups, like the blind and the deaf, and the seeing and the hearing." He said: "The blind and the deaf" is the disbeliever, and "the seeing" and "the hearing" is the believer.

18103: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, he said: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding: ﴿The likeness of the two groups, like the blind and the deaf, and the seeing and the hearing.﴾ "The two groups" are the two disbelievers and the two believers. As for "the blind and the deaf," they are the two disbelievers, and as for "the seeing and the hearing," they are the two believers.

18104: Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding: ﴿The likeness of the two groups, like the blind and the deaf, and the seeing and the hearing﴾, to the end of the verse: This is a likeness which God struck for the disbeliever and the believer. As for the disbeliever, he is deaf to the truth, so he does not hear it, and blind to it, so he does not see it. As for the believer, he heard the truth and benefited from it, saw it, grasped it, preserved it, and acted upon it.

* * *

God, exalted is He, says: ﴿Are they equal in likeness?﴾ He says: Are these two groups, despite the difference in their conditions in themselves, equal in your sight, O people? They are not equal in your sight. Likewise, the condition of the disbeliever and the believer are not equal in the sight of God. ﴿Will you not remember?﴾ His praise, exalted is He, says: Will you not take heed, O people, and reflect, so that you know the reality of the difference between their two states, and refrain from your misguidance toward guidance, and from disbelief toward faith?

* * *

The phrase "the blind and the deaf, and the seeing and the hearing" is four in wording, but two in meaning. That is why it was said: ﴿Are they equal in likeness?﴾

It was also said: "﴿Like the blind and the deaf﴾," meaning "like the blind-deaf," and likewise "﴿and the seeing and the hearing﴾," meaning "the seeing-hearing," like the speaker's saying "قام الظريف والعاقل" ("the witty one and the intelligent one stood up"), where he describes one person with both attributes.

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 11, verses 25–26:

The explanation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿And We certainly sent Noah to his people: "Indeed, I am a clear warner to you"﴾ ﴿"that you worship none but Allah. Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a painful day."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And We certainly sent Noah to his people: "Indeed, I am to you, O people, a warner from Allah, warning you of His punishment for your disbelief in Him. So believe in Him and obey His command."

By His saying ﴿mubin﴾ (clear), he means: he makes clear to you what he was sent with from Allah's command and prohibition. [[See the explanation of "nadhir" (warner) and "mubin" (clear) in the previous lexical indexes, under (n-dh-r) and (b-y-n).]]

* *

The reciters differed over the recitation of His saying ﴿inni﴾ (indeed I).

Most of the reciters of Kufa and some of the people of Medina recited it with a kasra on the "inna" (إنّ), as a fresh start (ibtida'), since in "sending" there is the meaning of "saying."

* *

Some of the reciters of Medina, Kufa and Basra recited it with a fatha on the "anna" (أنْ), with the verb "sending" governing it (i'mal al-irsal fiha). The meaning of the speech according to them is: We certainly sent Noah to his people with (bi-anni) "I am to you a clear warner."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this matter, in my opinion, is that both are two recitations with the same meaning. Each of them has been recited by a group of reciters, so whichever of them the reciter recites, he is correct.

* *

As for His saying ﴿an la ta'budu illa Allah﴾ (that you worship none but Allah): whoever recites the alif of ﴿inni﴾ with a kasra makes His saying ﴿arsalna﴾ (We sent) govern the "an" in His saying ﴿an la ta'budu illa Allah﴾, and the meaning then becomes: And We certainly sent Noah to his people, that you worship none but Allah, and say to them: "Indeed, I am to you a clear warner." Whoever recites it with a fatha makes the "an" in His saying ﴿an la ta'budu﴾ refer back to it, so the meaning then becomes: We certainly sent Noah to his people with (bi-anni) "I am to you a clear warner," on the basis that you worship none but Allah.

* *

By His saying [that you worship none but Allah, O people], he means the worship of gods and idols, [[Thus the sentence came in the manuscript and the printed edition, and the omission in it is clearly apparent. It seems the correct wording, God willing, is:

"By His saying (an la ta'budu illa Allah), i.e.: leave off worshipping the gods. . . "]]

and associating them in His worship. Single out Allah with monotheism and devote the worship sincerely to Him, for He has no partner in His creation.

* *

As for His saying ﴿Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a painful day﴾, he says: Indeed, I, O people, if you do not single out Allah in worship, and make Him one in monotheism, and cast off what is beneath Him of rivals and idols, I fear for you from Allah the punishment of a day whose punishment and chastisement are painful for whoever is punished in it.

* *

He made "painful" (alim) a description of "day" (yawm), while it is actually a description of the "punishment" (adhab), because the punishment occurs in it, as it is said: ﴿And He made the night a rest﴾ [Surah al-An'am: 96], whereas "rest" is actually a description of what rests in it, not of the night.

The explanation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿And We certainly sent Noah to his people: "Indeed, I am a clear warner to you"﴾ ﴿"that you worship none but Allah. Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a painful day."﴾
