Most of the reciters of Kufa and some of the people of Medina recited it with a kasra on the "inna" (إنّ), as a fresh start (ibtida'), since in "sending" there is the meaning of "saying."

* *

Some of the reciters of Medina, Kufa and Basra recited it with a fatha on the "anna" (أنْ), with the verb "sending" governing it (i'mal al-irsal fiha). The meaning of the speech according to them is: We certainly sent Noah to his people with (bi-anni) "I am to you a clear warner."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this matter, in my opinion, is that both are two recitations with the same meaning. Each of them has been recited by a group of reciters, so whichever of them the reciter recites, he is correct.

* *

As for His saying ﴿an la ta'budu illa Allah﴾ (that you worship none but Allah): whoever recites the alif of ﴿inni﴾ with a kasra makes His saying ﴿arsalna﴾ (We sent) govern the "an" in His saying ﴿an la ta'budu illa Allah﴾, and the meaning then becomes: And We certainly sent Noah to his people, that you worship none but Allah, and say to them: "Indeed, I am to you a clear warner." Whoever recites it with a fatha makes the "an" in His saying ﴿an la ta'budu﴾ refer back to it, so the meaning then becomes: We certainly sent Noah to his people with (bi-anni) "I am to you a clear warner," on the basis that you worship none but Allah.

* *

By His saying [that you worship none but Allah, O people], he means the worship of gods and idols, [[Thus the sentence came in the manuscript and the printed edition, and the omission in it is clearly apparent. It seems the correct wording, God willing, is:

"By His saying (an la ta'budu illa Allah), i.e.: leave off worshipping the gods. . . "]]

and associating them in His worship. Single out Allah with monotheism and devote the worship sincerely to Him, for He has no partner in His creation.

* *

As for His saying ﴿Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a painful day﴾, he says: Indeed, I, O people, if you do not single out Allah in worship, and make Him one in monotheism, and cast off what is beneath Him of rivals and idols, I fear for you from Allah the punishment of a day whose punishment and chastisement are painful for whoever is punished in it.

* *

He made "painful" (alim) a description of "day" (yawm), while it is actually a description of the "punishment" (adhab), because the punishment occurs in it, as it is said: ﴿And He made the night a rest﴾ [Surah al-An'am: 96], whereas "rest" is actually a description of what rests in it, not of the night.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 27:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then the chiefs of those among his people who disbelieved said, "We do not see you but a man like ourselves, and we do not see those who follow you except the lowest of us, at first thought. And we see not in you any merit over us; rather, we think you are liars."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: The great ones among the people of Noah and their nobles said — and they are "the chiefs" [[See the explanation of "al-mala'" (the chiefs, the notables) earlier, p. 177, note 1, and the references there.]] — those who disbelieved in God and denied the prophethood of their prophet Noah, peace be upon him: ﴿"We do not see you"﴾, O Noah, ﴿"but a man like ourselves"﴾. By this they mean that he is a human being like them in creation, form and kind, as though they were denying that God would send a messenger from among mankind to His creatures. [[See the explanation of "al-bashar" (human being) earlier, vol. 11, p. 521, note 1, and the references there.]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿"And we do not see those who follow you except the lowest of us"﴾, it means: And we do not see those who follow you except those who are our lowest people, rather than the great ones and nobles, in what we see and what appears to us.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿"at first thought"﴾ (bādiya al-ra'y), the reciters differed in its recitation.

The majority of the reciters of Medina and Iraq recited it: ﴿bādiya al-ra'y﴾, without a hamza on "bādī" and with a hamza on "al-ra'y", meaning: apparent opinion, from their saying "badā al-shay'u yabdū", when a thing appears, as the rajaz poet said: [[Abu Nukhayla al-Sa'di.]]

Adhā lī khālī shabahī bādī badī... wa ṣāra lil-faḥli lisānī wa yadī

[[This rajaz and the one following it are from the rajaz of Abu Nukhayla al-Sa'di. There is no doubt about the second verse of them; as for the first, I doubt the accuracy of its recitation in the form recited by al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Qur'an. Our friend and teacher 'Abd al-'Aziz al-Maymani al-Rajkuti has traced this rajaz in Simt al-La'ali: 293, 480; in Lisan (dhara'a); in Tahdhib Islah al-Mantiq 2: 32; Sibawayh 2: 54; Nawadir al-Yazidi: 128; al-Aghani (sasi) 18: 151; Tarikh Ibn 'Asakir 2: 321 = and Azid; Tarikh al-Tabari 9: 273; al-Ma'ani al-Kabir: 1223; al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Qur'an and Majaz al-Qur'an 1: 288; Lisan (bada). The verses are: "How is youthful pastime the deed of one who has not been guided, when a grey forelock has overtaken me, appearing at first thought..."

"And a dignified bearing that rises in my firmness after my youthful vigor was raised, and after what I recall of my bending, and after my walking and swinging of my hand, and my walking under the black crow..."

The author of Lisan mentioned it under (bada), and al-Tibrizi in Tahdhib Islah al-Mantiq, adding after "a dignified bearing that rises in my firmness": "and my tongue and hand became for the stallion." As for the first verse, I did not find it in any place, and I fear that "bādī badā" in it has been placed in the position of another word; and there is no doubt that the place of these two verses is not where the author of Lisan and al-Tibrizi placed one of them.]]

"Bādī badī" without hamza. Another said:

Wa qad 'alatnī dhur'atun bādī badī [[See the previous note. "Dhur'a" (with a dammah and then a sukun) means white hair at the front of the head.]]

* *

Some people of Basra recited it: ﴿bādi'a al-ra'y﴾, also with a hamza, meaning: the beginning of opinion, from their saying "I began with this matter" when one begins with it before anything else.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more preferable of the two readings in our view is the reading of the one who recites ﴿bādiya al-ra'y﴾ without a hamza on "bādī" and with a hamza on "al-ra'y", because the meaning of that statement is: "except those who are our lowest, in apparent opinion, and in what appears to us."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿"And we do not see in you any merit over us"﴾, it means: And we do not perceive for you any superiority over us that you have attained by your opposition to us in worshipping idols, turning to the worship of God and sincerely devoting worship to Him, so that we would follow you in seeking that superiority and in pursuing what you have gained by opposing us ﴿"rather, we think you are liars"﴾.

* *

This is an address from them to Noah, peace be upon him. They denied Noah only, not his followers, because his followers were not messengers. The address, though addressed to one person, takes the form of addressing all, as it is said: ﴿"O Prophet, when you divorce women"﴾ [Surah al-Talaq: 1].

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The interpretation of the statement is: "Rather, we think you, O Noah, in your claim that God has sent you to us as a messenger, to be a liar."

* *

The interpreters of the Qur'an have said what we have said regarding the interpretation of His saying ﴿at first thought﴾.

Those who said so:

18105 – Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ata' al-Khurasani, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿"And we do not see those who follow you except the lowest of us, at first thought"﴾, he said: "in what appeared to us."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 28:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿He said, "O my people, tell me, if I were upon clear evidence from my Lord and He had given me mercy from Himself, but it was obscured from you, would we compel you to accept it while you are averse to it?"﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says, relating what Noah said to his people when they denied him and rejected what had come to them from God of counsel: ﴿O my people, tell me, if I am upon clear evidence from my Lord﴾, upon knowledge, recognition and clarification from God of what is incumbent upon me concerning Him, and what is obligatory upon me of sincerely worshipping Him and abandoning the association of idols with Him in it, ﴿and He has given me mercy from Himself﴾, meaning: and He has granted me from Himself success, prophethood and wisdom, so I believed in Him and obeyed Him in what He commanded me and forbade me [[See the explanation of the words of the verse in the indices of language.]], ﴿but it was obscured from you﴾.

* *

The readers differed concerning the recitation of this.

The majority of the readers of Madina and some of the people of Basra and Kufa recited it: ﴿fa-'ummiyat﴾ with a fatha on the ʿayn and a light mim, meaning: the mercy was obscured from you, so you were not guided to it, so that you would not acknowledge it and affirm your messenger upon it.

The majority of the Kufan readers recited it: ﴿fa-ʿummiyat ʿalaykum﴾ with a damma on the ʿayn and a shadda on the mim, considering that reading to be that of ʿAbd Allah (Ibn Masʿud), for it is reported, in the recitation of ʿAbd Allah: ﴿fa-ʿammāhā ʿalaykum﴾.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two recitations in my view is the one who recited: ﴿fa-ʿummiyat ʿalaykum﴾ with a damma on the ʿayn and a shadda on the mim, because of the reason they mentioned for those who recite it, and because of its closeness to His saying: ﴿Tell me, if I am upon clear evidence from my Lord and He has given me mercy from Himself﴾, where He attributed the "mercy" to God; so likewise "its obscuring from others" is more fitting to attribute to Him.

* *

This is one of the words in which the Arabs shifted the verb from its place. The human being is the one who becomes blind to seeing the truth, since he is blinded from seeing it, and "the truth" is not described as blind except by the usage that has become established in speech. In its permissibility by the Arabs' usage it is like their saying: "The ring entered my hand, and the shoe my foot," whereas it is known that it is the foot that enters the shoe and the finger that enters the ring; but they used it in this way because the intended meaning was known. [[This is an abridgment of al-Farra's statement in Ma'ani al-Qur'an, on the interpretation of the verse.]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Would we compel you to accept it while you are averse to it?﴾, it means: Would we force you to enter Islam, when God has obscured it from you? ﴿while you are averse to it﴾ [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "upon you, averse to it", and the correct reading is what is established, with the addition of "you".]], meaning: while you are averse to our compelling you to it. "Averse" means: We do not do that, but we entrust your affair to God, so that He is the One who decides regarding your affair as He sees and wills. [[See the explanation of "al-kurh" in the indices of language earlier (k-r-h).]]

* *

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said.

Those who said that:

18106 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Noah said: ﴿O my people, if I am upon clear evidence from my Lord﴾, he said: "I have recognised it, and recognised by it His command, and that there is no god but Him" = ﴿and He has given me mercy from Himself﴾: Islam, guidance, faith, wisdom and prophethood.

18107 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, concerning His saying: ﴿Tell me, if I am upon clear evidence from my Lord﴾, to the end of the verse: "By God, if the Prophet of God (ﷺ) had been able, he would have compelled his people to it, but he was not able to do that and did not possess it."

18108 - Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Dawud, from Abu al-'Aliya, who said: In the recitation of Ubayy: ﴿Would we compel you to it from the side of our selves, while you are averse to it?﴾

18109 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zubayr narrated to us, from Ibn ʿUyayna, who said: Amr ibn Dinar informed us, who said: Ibn ʿAbbas recited: ﴿Would we compel you to it from the side of our selves﴾, he said: "'Abd Allah (Ibn ʿAbbas) said: 'from the side of our selves' means from our own accord."

18110 - Al-Harith narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd al-ʿAziz narrated to us, saying: Ibn ʿUyayna narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Dinar, from Ibn ʿAbbas, the like of it.

18111 - Al-Harith narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd al-ʿAziz narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Abu al-ʿAliya, from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb: ﴿Would we compel you to it from the side of our hearts, while you are averse to it?﴾ [[This recitation mentioned in the earlier reports, with the addition in the verse, is an irregular recitation (shadh) because it adds to the Mushaf; no one may recite it, and my opinion is that the phrase "from the side of our selves" or "from the side of our hearts" is an explanatory gloss inserted into the writing of the verse, and not a recitation.]]

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 29:**

**On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And O my people, I do not ask you for any wealth in return for it. My reward is only from Allah. And I will not drive away those who have believed. Indeed, they are to meet their Lord, but I see you as a people who are ignorant﴾**

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: This is also a report from Allah about what Nuh said to his people. He said to them: "O my people, I do not ask you for wealth as a payment for my advice to you and for calling you to the Oneness of Allah and to sincere worship of Him, so that you would accuse me regarding my advice and think that my action is a pursuit of some worldly gain." ﴿My reward is only from Allah﴾, meaning: the reward for my advice to you and my calling you to what I call you to is only from Allah, for it is He who will recompense me and reward me for it. ﴿And I will not drive away those who have believed﴾, meaning: I will not expel anyone who has believed in Allah, acknowledged His oneness, rejected the idols and disavowed them, even if they are not among your nobles and dignitaries. ﴿Indeed, they are to meet their Lord﴾, meaning: those whom you ask me to drive away will return to Allah, and Allah will question them about what they used to do in the world, not about their nobility and lineage.

* *

Nuh said this to his people because his people had said to him, as related:

18112 - al-Qasim told us, he said: al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, regarding His words: ﴿And I will not drive away those who have believed. Indeed, they are to meet their Lord﴾. He said: They said to him, "O Nuh, if you wish that we follow you, then drive them away; otherwise we will not accept that we and they be equal in the matter." So he said: ﴿I will not drive away those who have believed. Indeed, they are to meet their Lord﴾, meaning, He will question them about their deeds.

18113 - al-Qasim told us, he said: al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij; and Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, all of them, from Mujahid regarding His words: ﴿My reward is only from Allah﴾. He said: "My recompense."

18114 - al-Muthanna related to me, he said: Abu Hudhayfa told us, he said: Shibl told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

18115 - . . . he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abdullah told us, from Warqa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

* *

As for His words: ﴿But I see you as a people who are ignorant﴾, He means: "But I see you, O people, as a people who are ignorant of what is obligatory upon you regarding the right of Allah, and what is incumbent upon you of His obligations. And because of your ignorance, you have asked me to drive away those who have believed in Allah."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 30–31:

The explanation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿And O my people, who would help me against Allah if I drove them away? Will you not then be mindful?﴾ (30)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He means: ﴿O my people, who would help me﴾, that is, who would protect me from Allah if He punished me for driving away the believing monotheists? ﴿If I drove them away?⁠

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 30–31:

The explanation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿And O my people, who would help me against Allah if I drove them away? Will you not then be mindful?﴾ (30)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He means: ﴿O my people, who would help me﴾, that is, who would protect me from Allah if He punished me for driving away the believing monotheists? ﴿If I drove them away?⁠

**The interpretation of His words, exalted is He:** ﴿They said, "O Noah, you have disputed with us and multiplied our disputing, so bring us what you threaten us with, if you are among the truthful."﴾ (32)

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: The people of Noah said to Noah, peace be upon him: "You have argued with us and multiplied your arguing with us," [[See the explanation of "al-jidal" (dispute) above, 12:523, footnote 1, and the references there.]] "so bring us the punishment you threaten us with, if you are among the truthful in your threats and in your claim that you are the Messenger of God." He means by this that he would not be able to bring any of that.

* *

18117. Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿jadaltana﴾ (you have disputed with us), he said: "mariytana" (you have argued with us).

18118. al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

18119. And al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

18120. al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, who said: Mujahid said: ﴿They said, "O Noah, you have disputed with us"﴾, he said: "mariytana" (you have argued with us). ﴿And you have multiplied our disputing, so bring us what you threaten us with﴾. Ibn Juraij said: (meaning) denial of the punishment, and that it is false. ﴿And you have multiplied our disputing, so bring us what you threaten us with﴾. Ibn Juraij said: denial of the punishment, and that it is false.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 11, verses 33–34:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿He said, "Only Allah will bring it to you, if He wills, and you will not escape [Him].
And my advice will not benefit you, if I wished to advise you, if Allah intends to mislead you. He is your Lord, and to Him you will be returned."﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: Allah, exalted is His remembrance, says: Noah said to his people when they hastened him toward the punishment: "O my people, what you are seeking to hasten of the punishment is not up to me; it is only up to Allah, not to anyone else. It is He who will bring it to you, if He wills" = ﴿and you will not escape [Him]﴾ = meaning: and you will not, if He wills to punish you, be able to thwart Him, that is, to escape Him by fleeing from Him, for wherever you are, you are in His dominion, His authority and His power, and His judgment over you is in effect [see the explanation of "al-i'jaz" (inability/thwarting) earlier, p. 286, footnote 1, and the references there]. = ﴿And my advice will not benefit you﴾, meaning: my warning you of His punishment and the descent of His might upon you, given your disbelief in Him, will not benefit you = ﴿if I wished to advise you﴾, in my warning you of that, because my advice will not benefit you, since you will not accept it. [See the explanation of "nasahtu laka" (I advised you) earlier, 3:212.] = ﴿if Allah intends to mislead you﴾, meaning: if Allah intends to destroy you with His punishment = ﴿He is your Lord, and to Him you will be returned﴾, meaning: and to Him you will be sent back after destruction. [See the explanation of "al-marji'" (the return) earlier in the lexical indices, root (r-j-'), .]

* *

It is related from the tribe of Tayy that they say: "Such-and-such became ghawiyan," meaning: sick.

And it is related from others, by hearing from them: "I caused such-and-such to be ghawiya (misled/destroyed)," meaning: I destroyed him. And "ghawiya al-fasil" (the suckling camel colt went astray), when it lost milk and died.

And it is mentioned that the saying of Allah, ﴿So they will meet ghayy﴾ [Surah Maryam: 59], means: destruction. [See the explanation of "ghawa" earlier, 12:333, footnote 3, and the references there.]

And it is related from others, by hearing from them: "I caused such-and-such to be ghawiya (misled/destroyed)," meaning: I destroyed him. And "ghawiya al-fasil" (the suckling camel colt went astray), when it lost milk and died.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 35:

The explanation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it." Say, "If I have invented it, then upon me is my crime, and I am innocent of what you commit."﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The Exalted says: Do these polytheists of your people say, O Muhammad, "Muhammad has invented this Qur'an, and this report about Noah"? Say to them: If I have invented it, fabricated it and made it up [[See the explanation of "al-iftira'" (invention, fabrication), in the earlier language indexes under (f-r-y).]]

﴿Then upon me is my crime﴾ means: upon me is my sin in inventing what I have invented against my Lord, not against you. You will not be held accountable for my sin or my wrongdoing, and I will not be held accountable for your sin. ﴿And I am innocent of what you commit﴾ means: I am innocent of what you commit as sin and bear as wrongdoing against your Lord through your fabrication against Him.

* *

It is said from this root: "ajramtu ijraman" (I committed a crime), and "jaramtu ajrimu jarman" (I committed a crime), [[See the explanation of "al-ijram" (committing a crime) in the earlier language indexes under (j-r-m).]] as the poet said: [[He is al-Hayrdan ibn Khatar ibn Hafs al-Sa'di, the highwayman; his name is vocalized with a fatha on the ha', a sukun on the ya', and a damma on the ra'.]]

A fugitive from his tribe and a pledge held for a sin, for what my hand committed and what my tongue transgressed [[Majaz al-Qur'an by Abu 'Ubayda, 1:288, and Lisan al-'Arab (j-r-m).]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 36:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And it was revealed to Noah: "None of your people will believe except those who have already believed, so do not be distressed by what they have been doing."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: And Allah revealed to Noah, when the word had come due against his people and the command of Allah had overshadowed them, that he would not believe, O Noah, in Allah so that he would affirm His oneness and follow you in what you call them to, ﴿of your people except those who have already believed﴾, so they affirmed that and followed you. ﴿So do not be distressed﴾, meaning: do not feel humbled and do not grieve, ﴿by what they have been doing﴾, for I will destroy them and deliver you from them and from those who follow you. Allah revealed that to him after Noah had invoked destruction upon them, saying: ﴿My Lord, do not leave upon the earth from among the disbelievers a single dweller﴾ [Surah Nuh: 26].

* *

= It is from "tafta'ala" (the reflexive verb form) of "al-bu's" (misery, distress). It is said: "ibta'asa fulan bil-amr yabta'isu ibti'asan" (so-and-so was distressed by the matter), as Labid ibn Rabi'ah said:

In a mourning gathering like the she-goats of a herd, / who are distressed by what we have encountered

[His Diwan 2:46 (the poem: 35, the verse: 21), al-Lisan (y-'-s). A poem of his in which he mentions his daughter or wife and her condition after his death: "And I feared, after death, a day / when Asma' would blacken the brow..." / "Among gazelles of a herd, / who are distressed by what we encountered..." / "Stripped of their adornments, in coarse garments / of hair, virgins and matrons." This is poetry; enough for you as poetry!]

* *

And the people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

18121- Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿So do not be distressed﴾, he said: Do not grieve.

18122- al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid. And al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

18123- Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿So do not be distressed by what they have been doing﴾, meaning: do not grieve.

18124- Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿So do not be distressed by what they have been doing﴾, he said: Do not despair and do not grieve.

18125- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, his saying: ﴿And it was revealed to Noah: none of your people will believe except those who have already believed﴾, and that was when he invoked against them, saying ﴿My Lord, do not leave upon the earth from among the disbelievers a single dweller﴾ [Surah Nuh: 26]. His saying: ﴿So do not be distressed﴾, meaning: do not despair and do not grieve.

18126- It was related to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, concerning His saying: ﴿None of your people will believe except those who have already believed﴾: then he invoked destruction upon his people, when Allah had made clear to him that none of his people would believe except those who had already believed.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 37:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And build the ark under Our eyes and Our inspiration, and do not address Me concerning those who have wronged; indeed, they are to be drowned.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, mentioning Himself, says: "Inspire to him that none of your people will believe except those who have already believed, and that he should build the ark, which is the ship" [[See the explanation of "al-fulk" (the ark) above: 12:503 / 15:50, 153.]] as:

18127- Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "al-Fulk: the ship."

* *

As for His saying, ﴿bi-a'yunina﴾ (under Our eyes), it means: by the eye of God and His inspiration, as He commands you. As:

18127- Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿And build the ark under Our eyes and Our inspiration﴾. That was because he did not know how to build the ark, so God inspired him to build it in the shape of the breast of a bird. [[" Ju'ju' al-tair " (with a dammah on the jim, then a sukun, then a dammah on the jim): it is its breast.]]

18128- Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿And Our inspiration﴾, he said: as We command you.

18129- Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid. And al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abdullah narrated to us, from Warqa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿Under Our eyes and Our inspiration﴾, as We command you.

18130- Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ata al-Khurasani, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And build the ark under Our eyes and Our inspiration﴾, he said: by the eye of God. Ibn Jurayj said: Mujahid said: ﴿And Our inspiration﴾, he said: as We command you.

18131- Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah regarding His saying: ﴿Under Our eyes and Our inspiration﴾, he said: by the eye of God and His inspiration.

* *

As for His saying, ﴿And do not address Me concerning those who have wronged; indeed, they are to be drowned﴾, exalted is He, mentioning Himself, says: Do not ask Me to pardon those of your people who have wronged themselves, who have brought upon themselves, through their transgression against themselves by their disbelief in God, destruction by drowning; indeed, they are to be drowned by the flood. As:

18132- Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj: ﴿And do not address Me﴾, he said: it means: do not argue with Me. He said: it was decreed that he should not intercede for them with Him. [["Tuqaddama" (it was decreed), meaning His command concerning that.]]

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 11, verse 38:**

The explanation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And he was constructing the ark, and whenever a group of the chiefs of his people passed by him, they mocked him. He said, "If you mock us, then we mock you as you mock. And you are going to know,"﴾ (38)

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Noah was building the ship, and whenever a group of the leaders of his people passed by him [[See the explanation of "al-Mala'" (the chiefs) above, p. 295, note 1, and the references there.]] ﴿they mocked him﴾, meaning they ridiculed Noah, saying to him, "Have you turned into a carpenter after prophethood, and are you building a ship on dry land?" ﴿He said to them, "If you mock us"﴾, meaning if you ridicule us today, ﴿then we mock you in the Hereafter, as you mock us in the world"﴾ [[See the explanation of "sakhar" (mockery) above, vol. 14, p. 382, note 2.]] ﴿And you are going to know﴾, meaning when you witness the punishment of God, who among us was the one who had wronged himself.

* *

The making of the ship by Noah was as follows:

18133 - Al-Muthanna and Salih ibn Mismar narrated to me, saying: Ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, saying: Musa ibn Ya'qub informed us, saying: Fa'id, the freedman of Ubaydullah ibn Ali ibn Abi Rafi', narrated to me, that Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Rabi'ah informed him that A'ishah, the wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), informed him that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "If God had shown mercy to anyone of the people of Noah, He would have shown mercy to the mother of the child!" The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Noah remained among his people for a thousand years less fifty years, calling them to God. Until, at the end of his time, he planted a tree, and it grew tall and spread in every direction. Then he cut it down and began to make a ship. They would pass by and ask him, and he would say, 'I am making it a ship!' They would mock him and say, 'You are making a ship on dry land, how will it sail?' He would say, 'You will know.' When he finished it, the oven overflowed, and water increased in the streets. The mother of the child feared for him, for she loved him intensely, so she went out to the mountain until she reached a third of it. When the water reached her, she went out until she reached two-thirds of the mountain. When the water reached her, she went out until she stood upon the mountain. When the water reached her neck, she raised him between her hands until the water carried her away. So if God had shown mercy to any of them, He would have shown mercy to the mother of the child."

[[Hadith no. 18133: "Ibn Abi Maryam" is "Sa'id ibn Abi Maryam", a trustworthy narrator whom the group of compilers narrated from; he has appeared many times before, the last being no. 12771. "Musa ibn Ya'qub ibn Ya'qub al-Zam'i" is trustworthy, but his reliability has been questioned. His reliability was affirmed in nos. 9923, 15756 and 15822. Ali ibn al-Madini said: "weak in hadith, rejected in hadith." Al-Athram said: I asked Ahmad about him, and he seemed not to approve of him. "Fa'id, the freedman of Ubaydullah ibn Ali ibn Abi Rafi'", who is of the "Abadil", is "Fa'id, freedman of the Abadil", a trustworthy narrator with no problem. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 4/1/131, and Ibn Abi Hatim 3/2/84. "Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Rabi'ah al-Makhzumi" is "Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd Allah ibn Abi Rabi'ah", trustworthy, who narrated from his maternal aunt A'ishah. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 1/1/296, and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/1/111. This is a "hasan" (fair) isnad. Al-Tabari narrated it with this same isnad in his history 1:91. Al-Hakim also narrated it through this same chain in al-Mustadrak 2:342, 547, then said: "This hadith is sound in isnad, though they (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not include it." But al-Dhahabi said: "Its isnad is dark, and Musa is not of that standard," which is severe. Closer to the truth is what Ibn Kathir said in his tafsir 4:367-368, narrating it from this place in al-Tabari's tafsir and from the commentary of Ibn Abi Hatim, then said: "This is a strange hadith from this route. It has been narrated from Ka'b al-Ahbar and Mujahid ibn Jabr, the story of this child and his mother in similar terms." Al-Haythami recorded it in Majma' al-Zawa'id 8:200 and said: "Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Awsat, and in its chain is Musa ibn Ya'qub al-Zam'i, whom Ibn Ma'in and others declared trustworthy, while Ibn al-Madini declared him weak. The rest of its narrators are trustworthy."]]

18134 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: It was mentioned to us that the length of the ship was three hundred cubits, its width fifty cubits, and its height thirty cubits, and its door was at its side.

18135 - Al-Harith narrated to me, saying: Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, saying: Mubarak narrated to us, from al-Hasan, who said: The length of Noah's ship was one thousand two hundred cubits, and its width six hundred cubits.

18136 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Mufaddal ibn Fadalah, from Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an, from Yusuf ibn Mihran, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The disciples said to Jesus son of Mary: "If you would send to us a man who witnessed the ship, so that he could tell us about it!" He said: So he set out with them until he brought them to a mound of dirt. He took a handful of that dirt in his palm and said: "Do you know what this is?" They said: "God and His Messenger know best." He said: "This is the skull of Ham son of Noah." He said: Then he struck the mound with his staff and said: "Rise by God's permission!" And behold, he stood up, shaking the dust from his head, and he had gone grey. Jesus said to him: "Is this how you died?" He said: "No, but I died while young. But I thought it was the Hour, so for that reason I turned grey." He said: "Tell us about the ship of Noah." He said: "Its length was one thousand two hundred cubits, its width six hundred cubits, and it had three levels: one level for the beasts and wild animals, one level for humans, and one level for birds. When the dung of the beasts accumulated, God revealed to Noah: 'Rub the tail of the elephant,' so he rubbed it, and from it there fell a male pig and a female pig, and they went to the dung. When the mouse fell upon the sides [[In the printed edition: "bihabl al-safinah" (with the ship's rope). In the manuscript: "yahrur", undotted, and I considered reading it so. "al-Jarz" (with a fatha on the jim and zay) is the chest or middle part of a person, as they said of "al-Ju'ju'", which is the chest of a bird. In Tarikh al-Tabari it is "bikharz", as if the plural of "kharzah".]] and began to gnaw at it, God revealed to Noah: 'Strike between the eyes of the lion,' so from its nostril came out a male cat and a female cat, and they went to the mouse." Jesus said to him: "How did Noah know that the lands had been flooded?" He said: "He sent the raven to bring him news. It found a carcass and settled upon it, so he cursed it with fear, and for that reason it does not frequent houses." He said: "Then he sent the dove, and it came back with an olive leaf in its beak and mud on its feet, and he knew that the lands had been flooded." He said: "So he gave it a green collar on its neck, and prayed for it to be in comfort and safety, and for that reason it frequents houses." He said: "We said, 'O Messenger of God, shall we not take him to our families, so that he may sit with us and speak to us?' He said: 'How can he follow you when he has no provision?'" He said: "Then he said to him: 'Return by God's permission,' and he returned to dust."

[[Hadith no. 18136: "Al-Mufaddal ibn Fadalah ibn Abi Umayyah al-Qurashi" is "not of that standard", and it has been said that there is strangeness in his narrations. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 4/1/405, Ibn Abi Hatim 4/1/317, and Mizan al-I'tidal 3:195. "Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an" has appeared many times before, the last being no. 17861, and I mentioned there the declaration of trustworthiness by my brother Sayyid Ahmad, may God have mercy on him, and I mentioned the weakening of his hadith by the imams, and I preferred that his hadith be considered. This report is undoubtedly one of the remnants of the Israelite narratives and their like, and it does not reach the level of being anything. Al-Tabari narrated it in his history 1:91-92.]]

18137 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from one not accused of falsehood, from Ubayd ibn Umayr al-Laythi: that he used to narrate that it reached him that they used to attack him (meaning Noah's people), and they would choke him until he fainted. When he regained consciousness, he would say: "O God, forgive my people, for they do not know." Until, when they persisted in disobedience, and their sin grew great upon the earth, and the affair of him and them became prolonged, and the trial upon him from them intensified, and he waited for generation after generation, each generation was more wicked than the one before it, until one of the last of them would say: "This was with our fathers and our grandfathers, just like this, mad!" They did not accept anything from him. Until Noah complained of their affair to God, the Exalted, as God related to us in His Book: ﴿My Lord, I have called my people night and day, but my call has only increased them in flight﴾, up to the end of the story, until he said: ﴿My Lord, do not leave upon the earth from the disbelievers a single dweller. Indeed, if You leave them, they will mislead Your servants and will not beget except wicked disbelievers﴾, up to the end of the story [Surah Nuh: 5-27]. When Noah complained of them to God and sought His help against them, God revealed to him: ﴿Construct the ship under Our eyes and Our revelation, and do not address Me concerning those who have wronged; indeed, they are to be drowned﴾, meaning: after today. Noah then turned to building the ship, and he was occupied with it and neglected his people. He began to cut the wood, strike the iron, and prepare the equipment of the ship, including pitch and other materials that none but he could prepare. His people would pass by him while he was at his work, and they would mock him and ridicule him, and he would say: (If you mock us, then we mock you as you mock, and you are going to know who there will come upon him a punishment that will disgrace him, and upon whom will descend a lasting punishment). He said: They used to say, as it has reached me: "O Noah, you have become a carpenter after prophethood!" He said: God caused the wombs of the women to become barren, so they did not bear children. He said: The People of the Torah claim that God commanded him to make the ship from teak wood, and to make it "azwar" [[" Azwar", from "al-zawr" (with a fatha then sukun), which is the chest, and "al-zawr" (with two fathas), which is a bend in the chest, meaning that the breastplate is narrowed and the lower chest protrudes, as if it were squeezed from both sides.]], and to coat it with pitch inside and outside, and to make its length eighty cubits, and to make it three levels: lower, middle, and upper, and to make windows in it. Noah did as God commanded him, until when he finished it, and God had made a covenant with him: ﴿When Our command comes and the oven boils over, We said: Carry in it of each pair two, and your family, except those against whom the word has already gone forth, and whoever believes; and none believed with him except a few﴾. God had made the oven a sign between Him and him. He said: ﴿When Our command comes and the oven boils over, then load in it of each pair two﴾, and embark. When the oven boiled over, Noah carried in the ship, by God's command, those who were few, as God said. He carried in it of each pair two, of what has the spirit and of the trees, male and female. He carried in it his three sons: Sam, Ham and Japheth, and their wives, and six people who had believed in him, so they were ten individuals: Noah, his sons and their wives. Then he admitted what God had commanded him of the animals, and his son Yam, who was a disbeliever, stayed behind.

[[Hadith no. 18137: al-Tabari narrated it in his history 1:92-93.]]

18138 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from al-Hasan ibn Dinar, from Ali ibn Zayd, from Yusuf ibn Mihran, from Ibn Abbas, who said: I heard him say: The first thing Noah carried in the ship of animals was the ant, and the last he carried was the donkey. When the donkey was admitted and put its chest in, Iblis clung to its tail, so its two legs could not move. Noah began to say: "Woe to you, enter!" but it would rise and not be able to. Until Noah said: "Woe to you, enter, even if the devil is with you!" It was a word that slipped from his tongue. When Noah said it, the devil released his hold, and so it entered, and the devil entered with it. Noah said to him: "What brought you upon me, O enemy of God?" He said: "Did you not say, 'Enter, even if the devil is with you'?" He said: "Get out of my sight, O enemy of God!" He said: "You have no choice but to carry me!" So he was, as they claim, on the back of the ship. When Noah settled in the ship, and he admitted into it those who believed in him, and that was in the month... [[The number of the month that he mentioned has been dropped from both the manuscript and the printed edition, and the text proceeds in one continuous line. I have placed dots to indicate this omission, but the same appears in the history as well.]] of the year in which Noah entered, six hundred years after his birth, seventeen nights had passed of the month. When he entered and carried with him whom he carried, the springs of the Great Abyss [[" Al-Ghawt" (with a fatha then sukun) and "al-Ghait", the wide part of the earth from its depth, and here it means: the furthest depth of the earth.]] burst forth, and the gates of heaven were opened, as God said to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿So We opened the gates of heaven with water pouring forth, and We caused the earth to gush forth with springs, and the waters met for a matter already decreed﴾ [Surah al-Qamar: 11-12]. Noah and those with him entered the ship, and it was covered over them with its lid. [[" Al-Tabaq", the cover of everything. In the printed edition it was "bitabaqah", which is an error.]] Between the time God sent the water and the time the water bore up the ship was forty days and forty nights. Then the water bore it up, as the People of the Torah claim, and the water increased and became strong and rose, and God said to Muhammad: ﴿And We carried him on a vessel of planks and nails﴾ [Surah al-Qamar: 13], and "al-dusur" means nails, iron nails. So the ship began to sail with them and those with them in waves like mountains. Noah called to his son, who perished among those who perished, and he was apart when Noah saw from the truth of his Lord's promise what he saw, and he said: ﴿O my son, board with us and do not be with the disbelievers﴾. He was wretched and had concealed disbelief. ﴿He said, "I will take refuge on a mountain that will protect me from the water."﴾ He had known the mountains to be protection from rain when it fell, so he thought that it was as he knew it. Noah said: ﴿There is no protector today from the command of God, except for whom He grants mercy.﴾ And the waves came between them, and he was among the drowned [Surah Hud: 42-43]. The water increased until it overflowed and rose above the mountains, as the People of the Torah claim, by fifteen cubits. Every living thing upon the face of the earth perished, every creature that had a spirit or a tree, so nothing remained of creation except Noah and those with him in the ship, and Uj ibn Unuq, according to what the People of the Book claim. So between the time God sent the flood and the time the water receded was six months and ten nights.

[[Hadith no. 18138: al-Tabari narrated it in his history 1:93-94.]]

18139 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from al-Hasan ibn Dinar, from Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an. Ibn Humayd said: Salamah said: And Ali ibn Zayd narrated to me, from Yusuf ibn Mihran, who said: I heard him say: When the filth of people harmed Noah in the ship, he was commanded to rub the tail of the elephant, so he rubbed it, and two pigs came out of it, and that took care of it. And the mice multiplied in the ship, and when they harmed it, he was commanded to order the lion to sneeze, so it sneezed, and two cats came out of its nostrils, which ate the mice.

18140 - Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ali ibn Zayd, from Yusuf ibn Mihran, from Ibn Abbas, who said: When Noah was in the ship, the mouse gnawed at the ropes of the ship, and Noah complained, so God revealed to him, and he rubbed the tail of the lion, and two cats came out. There was filth in the ship, and he complained of that to his Lord, and God revealed to him, so he rubbed the tail of the elephant, and two pigs came out.

18141 - Ibrahim ibn Ya'qub al-Jawzajani narrated to us, saying: Al-Aswad ibn Amir narrated to us, saying: Sufyan ibn Sa'id informed us, from Ali ibn Zayd, from Yusuf ibn Mihran, from Ibn Abbas, with something similar.

[[Hadith no. 18141: "Ibrahim ibn Ya'qub ibn Ishaq al-Jawzajani al-Sa'di", the teacher of al-Tabari, was one of the memorizers of hadith. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/1/148. "Al-Aswad ibn Amir, Shadhan", is trustworthy, and has appeared before, no. 13927.]]

18142 - I was told, from al-Musayyib ibn Abi Rawq, from al-Dahhak, who said: Sulayman al-Qarasi said: Noah built the ship over four hundred years, and the teak took forty years to grow, until its length was four hundred cubits, and the cubit was measured to the shoulder.

[[Hadith no. 18142: "Al-Musayyib" is "al-Musayyib ibn Sharik al-Tamimi", who was abandoned, and has appeared before, no. 16806. "Sulayman al-Qarasi", I do not know who he is. In the manuscript and the printed edition it was "al-Musayyib ibn Abi Rawq", which is a plain error, and it will come later correctly as no. 18173. I say: These previous reports are all the fabrications of those who fabricated from the followers of the earlier scriptures, and there is no good in them. However, they may have recorded them in their books, because this is how it was transmitted. But none of the people of knowledge considers them proof of anything, or a basis for believing in their authenticity.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 11, verses 39–40:

**On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Whoever will receive a punishment that disgraces him, and upon whom will descend a lasting punishment﴾ (39) ﴿until when Our command came and the tannur (oven) boiled over, We said: Load into it two of every kind, a pair, and your family, except those against whom the word has already gone forth, and those who believe.﴾ And none believed with him except a few (40).**

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: Almighty Allah, mentioning the words of Noah to his people, says: ﴿So you will know﴾, O people, when the command of Allah comes, who is destroyed. ﴿Whoever will receive a punishment that disgraces him﴾ means: the one upon whom the punishment of Allah, from us and from you, comes, will be humiliated and debased [[See the explanation of "al-khizy (disgrace)" in the earlier lexical indices (kh-z-y).]] = ﴿and upon whom will descend a lasting punishment﴾ means: in addition to that, in the Hereafter, a punishment that is continuous and has no end will descend upon him, remaining upon him forever. [[See the explanation of "a lasting punishment" in earlier passages: 10:293 / 14:174, 340.]]

* *

His words: ﴿until when Our command came﴾ mean: "And Noah was making the ark" (until when Our command came), which We had promised, that his people would be overtaken by the flood that would drown them.

* *

His words: ﴿and the tannur boiled over﴾. The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of this.

Some of them said: its meaning is: water gushed forth from the surface of the earth. ﴿And the tannur boiled over﴾ refers to the surface of the earth.

Those who said this:

18143. Yaqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, he said: Hushaym narrated to us, he said: al-Awwam ibn Hawshab informed us, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas, that he said regarding His words ﴿and the tannur boiled over﴾: "The tannur is the surface of the earth." It was said to him: "When you see water on the surface of the earth, board the ship, you and those with you." He said: "The Arabs call the surface of the earth 'the tannur of the earth'."

18144. al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Amr ibn Awn narrated to us, he said: Hushaym informed us, from al-Awwam, from al-Dahhak, similarly.

18145. Abu Kurayb and Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to us, they both said: Ibn Idris narrated to us, he said: al-Shaybani informed us, from Ikrimah, regarding His words ﴿and the tannur boiled over﴾, he said: "The surface of the earth."

18146. Zakariya ibn Yahya ibn Abi Za'ida and Sufyan ibn Waki' narrated to us, they both said: Ibn Idris narrated to us, from al-Shaybani, from Ikrimah: ﴿and the tannur boiled over﴾, he said: "The surface of the earth."

* *

Others said: it is the dawning (tanwir) of the morning, from their saying: "The morning dawned (nawwara al-sabah) tanwiran."

Those who said this:

18147. Abu Hisham al-Rifa'i narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Fudayl narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq narrated to us, from Abbas, the freedman of Abu Juhayfa, from Abu Juhayfa, from Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), regarding his words: ﴿until when Our command came and the tannur boiled over﴾, he said: "It is the dawning of the morning."

18148. Ibn Waki' and Ishaq ibn Isra'il narrated to us, they both said: Muhammad ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq, from Ziyad, the freedman of Abu Juhayfa, from Abu Juhayfa, from Ali, regarding His words ﴿and the tannur boiled over﴾, he said: "The dawning of the morning."

18149. Hammad ibn Ya'qub narrated to us, he said: Ibn Fudayl informed us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq, from the freedman of Abu Juhayfa (I think he named him), from Abu Juhayfa, from Ali: ﴿and the tannur boiled over﴾, he said: "The dawning of the morning."

18150. Ishaq ibn Shahin narrated to me, he said: Hushaym narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from a man of Quraysh, from Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him): ﴿and the tannur boiled over﴾, he said: "The rising of dawn."

* *

18151. al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hushaym narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq informed us, from a man whom he named, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, his words: ﴿and the tannur boiled over﴾, he said: "When dawn rises."

* *

Others said: the meaning is: the highest part of the earth and its most elevated place boiled over with water. And he said: "The tannur" is the noblest part of the earth.

Those who said this:

18152. Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, his words: ﴿until when Our command came and the tannur boiled over﴾: "We used to narrate that it was the highest and noblest part of the earth, and it was a sign between Noah and his Lord."

18153. Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: Sulayman narrated to us, he said: Abu Hilal narrated to us, he said: I heard Qatadah, his words: ﴿and the tannur boiled over﴾, he said: "The noblest and highest part of the earth, from which the water boiled up."

* *

Others said: it is the oven in which bread is baked.

Those who said this:

18154. Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, he said: my paternal uncle narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, his words: ﴿until when Our command came and the tannur boiled over﴾, he said: "When you see the water gushing out of your family's oven, that is the destruction of your people."

18155. Yaqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, he said: Hushaym narrated to us, from Abu Muhammad, from al-Hasan, he said: "It was an oven of stone that belonged to Eve, until it came to Noah." He said: "It was said to him: When you see the water boiling up from the oven, board the ship, you and your companions."

18156. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, he said: Abu Usama narrated to us, from Shibl, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿and the tannur boiled over﴾, he said: "When the water burst forth, and Noah was commanded to board, he and those with him, into the ship."

18157. Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu Asim narrated to us, he said: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿and the tannur boiled over﴾, he said: "The water burst forth from it as a sign, that he should board with his family and those with him into the ship."

18158. al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, he said: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly, except that he said: "as a sign, that he should board his family and those with him into the ship."

18159. al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Ishaq narrated to us, he said: Abd Allah narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly, except that he said: "a sign that he should board with his family and those with them into the ship."

18160. al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: Khalaf ibn Khalifa narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, who said: "Water sprang up in the oven, and his wife became aware of it and informed him." He said: "And that was in the region of Kufa."

18161. ... He said: al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: Ali ibn Thabit narrated to us, from al-Sirri ibn Isma'il, from al-Sha'bi: that he used to swear by Allah that the tannur did not boil over except from the region of Kufa.

18162. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Hamid al-Himmani narrated to us, from al-Nadr Abu Umar al-Khazzaz, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿and the tannur boiled over﴾, he said: "The tannur boiled over in India."

18163. It was narrated to me on the authority of al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, he said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words: ﴿and the tannur boiled over﴾: "It was a sign for Noah. When water came out of it, the destruction and drowning had come upon the people."

* *

Ibn Abbas used to say, regarding the meaning of "fara (boiled over)": "it gushed forth."

18164. al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, he said: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, his words: ﴿and the tannur boiled over﴾, he said: "It gushed forth."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The "fawaran (boiling over) of water" is the surging of its rush. It is said of it: "The water boiled (fara al-ma' yafuru) fawran, and fu'uran and fawaran," [[His words "wa-fu'uran": omitted from the printed edition, but it is present in the manuscript.]] and that is when its rush flows.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The view most correct to us regarding the interpretation of His words ﴿the tannur﴾ is the view of the one who said: "It is the oven in which bread is baked," because that is the well-known usage of the Arabs, and the speech of Allah is only directed to the most prevalent and famous of its meanings among the Arabs, unless a proof is established regarding something of it that is contrary to that, in which case it is accepted. This is because He, majestic is His praise, addressed them only with what He addressed them with, to make its meaning understood by them.

* *

= ﴿We said﴾ to Noah, when Our punishment came to his people, the punishment with which We had promised Noah to punish them, and the tannur, whose boiling over with water We made a sign of the arrival of Our punishment between Us and him, for the destruction of his people = ﴿Load into it﴾, meaning into the ark, ﴿two of every kind, a pair﴾, meaning: a male and a female of every kind, as:

18165. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, he said: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿two of every kind, a pair﴾, he said: "A male and a female of every species."

18166. Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu Asim narrated to us, he said: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

18167. al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, he said: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿two of every kind, a pair﴾, "the single one is a 'zawj (mate)', and 'al-zawjayn (the pair)' is a male and a female of every species."

18168. ... he said: Ishaq narrated to us, he said: Abd Allah narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, his words: ﴿two of every kind, a pair﴾, he said: "A male and a female of every species."

18169. ... he said: al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the same.

18170. Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿We said: Load into it two of every kind, a pair﴾, he means: "two of every species."

18171. It was narrated to me on the authority of al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, he said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words: ﴿two of every kind, a pair﴾, he means by "the pair": "a male or a female."

* *

Some scholars of the Arabic language among the Kufans said: "al-zawjan (the pair)," in the speech of the Arabs, means "the two." He said: It is said: "He has two pairs of sandals (zawja n'al)" when he has two sandals on, and one does not say "he has a pair (zawj) of sandals"; and likewise: "he has two pairs of pigeons (zawja hamam)," and "he has two pairs of shackles (zawja qayd)." He said: Do you not hear His words: ﴿And that He created the pair, the male and the female﴾ [Surah al-Najm: 45], which means two. [[See the explanation of "al-zawjayn" in earlier passages: 12:183, 184.]]

* *

Some of the Basran grammarians said regarding His words: ﴿We said: Load into it two of every kind, a pair﴾: He made "al-zawjayn" mean "the two kinds (al-darbayn)," the males and the females. He said: Yunus claimed that the verse of the poet: [[I do not know who said it.]]

"You are a man who goes out on every heedless occasion, and so you err in it once and hit once,"

he meant by it the wolf. He said: This is even more anomalous than that.

* *

Another of them said: "al-zawj" means a color. He said: Every kind is called a "color," and he cited the verse of al-A'sha in this regard:

"And every zawj of brocade that he wears, Abu Qudama, adorned with it together."

[[Diwan: 86, al-Lisan (z-w-j), from his poem about "Hawdha ibn Ali al-Hanafi," and "Abu Qudama" is him. Before it: "Whoever meets Hawdha will prostrate, not refraining, when he wraps (the turban) above the crown or sets it down. For him are crowns of rubies, decorated by its goldsmiths, which you see without flaw or defect."]]

And Labid says:

"And one of brightness, whose herds covered its voice, and adorned it, the zawj (pairs) of a tinted blossom."

[[Diwan: poem 9, verse 25, describing a rain by which the earth became radiant. Before it he says: "And a rain that adorns its valleys with plants like a variegated embroidered garment." "Its clouds rained upon it, the dark-colored, heavy-rained ones, and when their downpour is exhausted, they pour..." (The Diwan's reading; the verse continues the description.) This is the Diwan's version; another narration reads: "colors of tinted light." "Al-dakdak" is what rises and levels off in the land, "al-wuhad" is what is low, "al-mukhallab" is the striped, describing the plant and its flower as if they were striped cloths spread over the hills and valleys. "Arabat" means remained, "al-wat'a" is the cloud close to the ground, "al-jawna" is the black, because of the abundance of its water, "hatuf" is one whose thunder calls out. "Anzafa al-shay'" means removed it. He says: this abundant cloud remained over it thundering; when the heavy rain was gone, it brought a pouring rain. "Al-bahja" is the splendor of plants, "kanna" means withheld and concealed, "al-maqanib" is groups of horses, "al-sawb" is rain, "mushrab" means tinted with colors of redness, yellowness and greenness. He says: the rain came and they took shelter in it because of its length and height. As for Abu Ja'far's version, its meaning is that the mounted groups prevented anyone other than themselves from grazing it, so no sound was heard from it.]]

* *

It was mentioned that al-Hasan said regarding His words: ﴿And of everything We created a pair﴾ [Surah al-Dhariyat: 49]: "The heaven is a pair, the earth is a pair, winter is a pair, summer is a pair, night is a pair, day is a pair, until the matter returns to Allah, the One who is not like anything."

* *

His words: ﴿and your family, except those against whom the word has already gone forth﴾ mean: "And load your family also into the ark." By "family" is meant his offspring, his wives, and his spouses [[See the explanation of "family" in earlier passages: 8:192.]] = ﴿except those against whom the word has already gone forth﴾ means: except those of whom I have said that I will destroy them along with those of your people whom I destroy.

* *

Then they differed regarding those whom Allah excepted from his family.

Some of them said: he was some of Noah's wives.

Those who said this:

18172. al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, he said: Ibn Jurayj said: ﴿and your family, except those against whom the word has already gone forth﴾, he said: "The punishment. She was his wife, who was among those who remained behind in the punishment." [[In the printed edition: "among those who remained behind," differing from the manuscript, and the manuscript is correct without doubt.]]

* *

Others said: rather, it was his son who drowned.

Those who said this:

18173. It was narrated to me on the authority of al-Musayyab, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, regarding His words: ﴿and your family, except those against whom the word has already gone forth﴾, he said: "His son, who drowned among those who drowned."

* *

His words: ﴿and those who believe﴾ mean: "And load with them those who believed you and followed you from your people" = Allah says: ﴿And none believed with him except a few﴾, meaning: and none of his people acknowledged the oneness of Allah along with Noah except a few.

* *

They differed regarding the number of those who had believed with him, whom he carried with him in the ark. Some of them said regarding that: they were eight persons.

Those who said this:

18174. Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, his words: ﴿and your family, except those against whom the word has already gone forth, and those who believe, and none believed with him except a few﴾, he said: "We were told that none in the ship were complete except Noah, his wife, his three sons, and their wives, so they were eight in all."

18175. Ibn Waki' and al-Hasan ibn Arafa narrated to us, they both said: Yahya ibn Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Ghaniya narrated to us, from his father, from al-Hakam: ﴿And none believed with him except a few﴾, he said: "Noah, his three sons, and four of his daughters-in-law."

18176. al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, he said: Ibn Jurayj said: "I was told that Noah carried with him his three sons, three wives of his sons, and the wife of Noah, so they were eight with their spouses. The names of his sons were Yafith, Sam, and Ham. Ham had relations with his wife in the ship, so Noah prayed that his semen be changed, and so he produced the Sudanese (black people)."

* *

Others said: rather, they were seven persons.

Those who said this:

18177. al-Harith narrated to me, he said: Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, he said: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash: ﴿And none believed with him except a few﴾, he said: "They were seven: Noah, three of his wives, and three sons."

* *

Others said: they were ten besides their wives.

Those who said this:

18178. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, he said: "When the tannur boiled over, Noah was carried in the ship, by the command of Allah, and they were few, as Allah said. So he carried his three sons: Sam, Ham, and Yafith, and their wives, and six people who had believed, so they were ten persons, including Noah, his sons, and their wives." [[The report 18178 was summarized earlier under number 14792, and see the commentary there.]]

* *

Others said: rather, they were eighty persons.

Those who said this:

18179. al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, he said: Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Abbas said: "Noah carried with him in the ship eighty people."

18180. al-Harith narrated to me, he said: Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, he said: Sufyan narrated to us, some of them used to say: "They were eighty," meaning the "few" that Allah mentioned: ﴿And none believed with him except a few﴾.

18181. Musa ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Masruqi narrated to me, he said: Zayd ibn al-Habbab narrated to me, he said: Husayn ibn Waqid al-Khurasani narrated to me, he said: Abu Nuhayk narrated to me, he said: I heard Ibn Abbas say: "In the ship of Noah were eighty men, one of whom was from Jurhum."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct statement regarding this is to say as Allah said: ﴿And none believed with him except a few﴾, describing them as being few, and not specifying their number by any quantity. No authentic report from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has been transmitted, so one should not go beyond the limit of Allah in this matter, since there is no limit to the exact number from the Book of Allah or from a report from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 11, verses 39–40:

**On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Whoever will receive a punishment that disgraces him, and upon whom will descend a lasting punishment﴾ (39) ﴿until when Our command came and the tannur (oven) boiled over, We said: Load into it two of every kind, a pair, and your family, except those against whom the word has already gone forth, and those who believe.﴾ And none believed with him except a few (40).**

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: Almighty Allah, mentioning the words of Noah to his people, says: ﴿So you will know﴾, O people, when the command of Allah comes, who is destroyed. ﴿Whoever will receive a punishment that disgraces him﴾ means: the one upon whom the punishment of Allah, from us and from you, comes, will be humiliated and debased [[See the explanation of "al-khizy (disgrace)" in the earlier lexical indices (kh-z-y).]] = ﴿and upon whom will descend a lasting punishment﴾ means: in addition to that, in the Hereafter, a punishment that is continuous and has no end will descend upon him, remaining upon him forever. [[See the explanation of "a lasting punishment" in earlier passages: 10:293 / 14:174, 340.]]

* *

His words: ﴿until when Our command came﴾ mean: "And Noah was making the ark" (until when Our command came), which We had promised, that his people would be overtaken by the flood that would drown them.

* *

His words: ﴿and the tannur boiled over﴾. The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of this.

18146. Zakariya ibn Yahya ibn Abi Za'ida and Sufyan ibn Waki' narrated to us, they both said: Ibn Idris narrated to us, from al-Shaybani, from Ikrimah: ﴿and the tannur boiled over﴾, he said: "The surface of the earth."
