This is because He, majestic is His praise, addressed them only with what He addressed them with, to make its meaning understood by them.

* *

= ﴿We said﴾ to Noah, when Our punishment came to his people, the punishment with which We had promised Noah to punish them, and the tannur, whose boiling over with water We made a sign of the arrival of Our punishment between Us and him, for the destruction of his people = ﴿Load into it﴾, meaning into the ark, ﴿two of every kind, a pair﴾, meaning: a male and a female of every kind, as:

18165. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, he said: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿two of every kind, a pair﴾, he said: "A male and a female of every species."

18166. Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu Asim narrated to us, he said: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

18167. al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, he said: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿two of every kind, a pair﴾, "the single one is a 'zawj (mate)', and 'al-zawjayn (the pair)' is a male and a female of every species."

18168. ... he said: Ishaq narrated to us, he said: Abd Allah narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, his words: ﴿two of every kind, a pair﴾, he said: "A male and a female of every species."

18169. ... he said: al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the same.

18170. Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿We said: Load into it two of every kind, a pair﴾, he means: "two of every species."

18171. It was narrated to me on the authority of al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, he said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words: ﴿two of every kind, a pair﴾, he means by "the pair": "a male or a female."

* *

Some scholars of the Arabic language among the Kufans said: "al-zawjan (the pair)," in the speech of the Arabs, means "the two." He said: It is said: "He has two pairs of sandals (zawja n'al)" when he has two sandals on, and one does not say "he has a pair (zawj) of sandals"; and likewise: "he has two pairs of pigeons (zawja hamam)," and "he has two pairs of shackles (zawja qayd)." He said: Do you not hear His words: ﴿And that He created the pair, the male and the female﴾ [Surah al-Najm: 45], which means two. [[See the explanation of "al-zawjayn" in earlier passages: 12:183, 184.]]

* *

Some of the Basran grammarians said regarding His words: ﴿We said: Load into it two of every kind, a pair﴾: He made "al-zawjayn" mean "the two kinds (al-darbayn)," the males and the females. He said: Yunus claimed that the verse of the poet: [[I do not know who said it.]]

"You are a man who goes out on every heedless occasion, and so you err in it once and hit once,"

he meant by it the wolf. He said: This is even more anomalous than that.

* *

Another of them said: "al-zawj" means a color. He said: Every kind is called a "color," and he cited the verse of al-A'sha in this regard:

"And every zawj of brocade that he wears, Abu Qudama, adorned with it together."

[[Diwan: 86, al-Lisan (z-w-j), from his poem about "Hawdha ibn Ali al-Hanafi," and "Abu Qudama" is him. Before it: "Whoever meets Hawdha will prostrate, not refraining, when he wraps (the turban) above the crown or sets it down. For him are crowns of rubies, decorated by its goldsmiths, which you see without flaw or defect."]]

And Labid says:

"And one of brightness, whose herds covered its voice, and adorned it, the zawj (pairs) of a tinted blossom."

[[Diwan: poem 9, verse 25, describing a rain by which the earth became radiant. Before it he says: "And a rain that adorns its valleys with plants like a variegated embroidered garment." "Its clouds rained upon it, the dark-colored, heavy-rained ones, and when their downpour is exhausted, they pour..." (The Diwan's reading; the verse continues the description.) This is the Diwan's version; another narration reads: "colors of tinted light." "Al-dakdak" is what rises and levels off in the land, "al-wuhad" is what is low, "al-mukhallab" is the striped, describing the plant and its flower as if they were striped cloths spread over the hills and valleys. "Arabat" means remained, "al-wat'a" is the cloud close to the ground, "al-jawna" is the black, because of the abundance of its water, "hatuf" is one whose thunder calls out. "Anzafa al-shay'" means removed it. He says: this abundant cloud remained over it thundering; when the heavy rain was gone, it brought a pouring rain. "Al-bahja" is the splendor of plants, "kanna" means withheld and concealed, "al-maqanib" is groups of horses, "al-sawb" is rain, "mushrab" means tinted with colors of redness, yellowness and greenness. He says: the rain came and they took shelter in it because of its length and height. As for Abu Ja'far's version, its meaning is that the mounted groups prevented anyone other than themselves from grazing it, so no sound was heard from it.]]

* *

It was mentioned that al-Hasan said regarding His words: ﴿And of everything We created a pair﴾ [Surah al-Dhariyat: 49]: "The heaven is a pair, the earth is a pair, winter is a pair, summer is a pair, night is a pair, day is a pair, until the matter returns to Allah, the One who is not like anything."

* *

His words: ﴿and your family, except those against whom the word has already gone forth﴾ mean: "And load your family also into the ark." By "family" is meant his offspring, his wives, and his spouses [[See the explanation of "family" in earlier passages: 8:192.]] = ﴿except those against whom the word has already gone forth﴾ means: except those of whom I have said that I will destroy them along with those of your people whom I destroy.

* *

Then they differed regarding those whom Allah excepted from his family.

Some of them said: he was some of Noah's wives.

Those who said this:

18172. al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, he said: Ibn Jurayj said: ﴿and your family, except those against whom the word has already gone forth﴾, he said: "The punishment. She was his wife, who was among those who remained behind in the punishment." [[In the printed edition: "among those who remained behind," differing from the manuscript, and the manuscript is correct without doubt.]]

* *

Others said: rather, it was his son who drowned.

Those who said this:

18173. It was narrated to me on the authority of al-Musayyab, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, regarding His words: ﴿and your family, except those against whom the word has already gone forth﴾, he said: "His son, who drowned among those who drowned."

* *

His words: ﴿and those who believe﴾ mean: "And load with them those who believed you and followed you from your people" = Allah says: ﴿And none believed with him except a few﴾, meaning: and none of his people acknowledged the oneness of Allah along with Noah except a few.

* *

They differed regarding the number of those who had believed with him, whom he carried with him in the ark. Some of them said regarding that: they were eight persons.

Those who said this:

18174. Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, his words: ﴿and your family, except those against whom the word has already gone forth, and those who believe, and none believed with him except a few﴾, he said: "We were told that none in the ship were complete except Noah, his wife, his three sons, and their wives, so they were eight in all."

18175. Ibn Waki' and al-Hasan ibn Arafa narrated to us, they both said: Yahya ibn Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Ghaniya narrated to us, from his father, from al-Hakam: ﴿And none believed with him except a few﴾, he said: "Noah, his three sons, and four of his daughters-in-law."

18176. al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, he said: Ibn Jurayj said: "I was told that Noah carried with him his three sons, three wives of his sons, and the wife of Noah, so they were eight with their spouses. The names of his sons were Yafith, Sam, and Ham. Ham had relations with his wife in the ship, so Noah prayed that his semen be changed, and so he produced the Sudanese (black people)."

* *

Others said: rather, they were seven persons.

Those who said this:

18177. al-Harith narrated to me, he said: Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, he said: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash: ﴿And none believed with him except a few﴾, he said: "They were seven: Noah, three of his wives, and three sons."

* *

Others said: they were ten besides their wives.

Those who said this:

18178. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, he said: "When the tannur boiled over, Noah was carried in the ship, by the command of Allah, and they were few, as Allah said. So he carried his three sons: Sam, Ham, and Yafith, and their wives, and six people who had believed, so they were ten persons, including Noah, his sons, and their wives." [[The report 18178 was summarized earlier under number 14792, and see the commentary there.]]

* *

Others said: rather, they were eighty persons.

Those who said this:

18179. al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, he said: Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Abbas said: "Noah carried with him in the ship eighty people."

18180. al-Harith narrated to me, he said: Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, he said: Sufyan narrated to us, some of them used to say: "They were eighty," meaning the "few" that Allah mentioned: ﴿And none believed with him except a few﴾.

18181. Musa ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Masruqi narrated to me, he said: Zayd ibn al-Habbab narrated to me, he said: Husayn ibn Waqid al-Khurasani narrated to me, he said: Abu Nuhayk narrated to me, he said: I heard Ibn Abbas say: "In the ship of Noah were eighty men, one of whom was from Jurhum."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct statement regarding this is to say as Allah said: ﴿And none believed with him except a few﴾, describing them as being few, and not specifying their number by any quantity. No authentic report from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has been transmitted, so one should not go beyond the limit of Allah in this matter, since there is no limit to the exact number from the Book of Allah or from a report from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

The Interpretation of His Words, the Exalted: "And he said, 'Embark upon it; in the name of God is its course and its mooring. Indeed my Lord is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.'" (11:41)

Abu Ja'far said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Noah said, "Embark upon the ship, 'in the name of God is its course and its mooring.'"

* *

In the speech there is an omitted element, for which the indication given by the report already mentioned suffices, and that is His words: "We said, 'Load into it two of every kind, and your family, except those against whom the word has already gone forth, and those who believe.' And none believed with him except a few" (11:40). So Noah carried them in it, and "he said" to them, "Embark upon it." The indication of His words, "And he said, 'Embark upon it,'" made the mention of his carrying them in it unnecessary, so it was left out.

* *

The readers differed regarding the recitation of His words, "In the name of God is its course and its mooring." The majority of the readers of Medina and Basra, and some of the Kufans, recited it: "bismi-llahi mujrāhā wa-mursāhā" (بِسْمِ اللهِ مُجْرَاهَا وَمُرْسَاهَا), with a damma on the mīm in both words. When it is recited this way, the words derive from *ajrā* (to cause to run) and *arsā* (to cause to anchor), and there are two grammatical possibilities in it:

The first: the nominative, meaning: "In the name of God is its causing-to-run and its causing-to-anchor." In this case *al-mujrā* and *al-mursā* are nominative by the preposition *bi* in His words, "in the name of God."

The second: the accusative, meaning: "In the name of God at its running and its anchoring," or "at the time of its running and its anchoring." In this case His words, "in the name of God," form a self-contained utterance, like the speaker's saying at the beginning of an act he is performing, "In the name of God," and then *al-mujrā* and *al-mursā* are accusative in the manner in which the Arabs put in the accusative their saying: "Praise be to God, from its crescent to its waning" (*sirārak wa-ihlālak*), meaning the moon's beginning and its end, as though they said, "Praise be to God, the first of the moon and its last." And there is also heard from them: "Praise be to God, from its beginning to its end" (*mā ihlālak ilā sirārak*). [[Al-Farra' said in his Ma'ani al-Qur'an after this: "They mean: what is between its beginning to its waning."]]

* *

Others of the Kufan readers recited it: "mujrāhā wa-mursāhā" (مَجْرَاهَا وَمُرْسَاهَا), with a fatḥa on the mīm in "mujrāhā" and a ḍamma on the mīm in "mursāhā," making "mujrāhā" a verbal noun from *jarā yajrī majrā*, and "mursāhā" from *arsā yursī irsā'*. [[See the explanation of *al-irsā'* above, 13:293.]]

When it is recited this way, its grammatical analysis has the two aspects, like what applies to them when both are recited as *mujrāhā wa-mursāhā* with a ḍamma on the mīm in both, as I have explained.

* *

It is related from Abu Raja' al-'Utaridi that he used to recite it: "bismi-llahi mujriyhā wa-mursīhā" (بِسْمِ اللهِ مُجْرِيهَا وَمُرْسِيهَا), with a ḍamma on the mīm in both, making them descriptions of God. When recited this way, there are also two grammatical possibilities in them, except that the more prevalent of the two aspects is the genitive, because the meaning of the utterance in this reading is: "In the name of God, the Causer-to-run of the ship and its Causer-to-anchor," so *al-mujrī* is an attribute of the name of God. It may also be accusative, which is the second possibility, because it is good to add the definite article to *al-mujrī* and *al-mursī*, as when you say, "In the name of God, the One who causes it to run and the One who causes it to anchor." When they are stripped of the article, they become accusative as circumstantial qualifiers, since they carry the sense of an indefinite, even though they are annexed to a definite noun.

* *

It has been mentioned that some of the Kufans recited it: "majrāhā wa-marsāhā" (مَجْرَاهَا وَمَرْسَاهَا), with a fatḥa on the mīm in both, from *jarā* and *rasā*, as though he directed it to mean that it is in the state of its running and the state of its settling, making both attributes belong to the ship, as 'Antarah said:

*So I bore my soul at that moment, free and patient, / it settles when the coward's breath rises in alarm.* [[From his Diwan, p. 89, among verses in which he speaks of the crow and considers it an omen of ill: "Those from whom you cawed to me in separation have kept the night of full moon sleepless and have caused pain. And I know that if my death comes to me, the swiftest flight will not save me from it. So I bore, aware of that, free..." *Nafs 'arifah* means a soul that bears hardships patiently when it is burdened with a matter, from its long struggle with the terrors of this life. *Tarsū* means it stays firm. *Tatallu'* means it leaps about looking for a place of escape or a helper, out of fear and terror.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The recitation we choose in this matter is the recitation of him who recites: "bismi-llahi mujrāhā" (بِسْمِ اللهِ مَجْرَاهَا), with a fatḥa on the mīm, and "wa-mursāhā" (وَمُرْسَاهَا), with a ḍamma on the mīm, meaning: "In the name of God when it runs and when it anchors."

I chose the fatḥa in the mīm of "mujrāhā" because it is closer to His words, "And it runs with them through waves like mountains" (11:42), and He did not say "tujrā bihim" (it is made to run with them). Whoever recites "bismi-llahi mujrāhā," the correct reading in his recitation would be "wa-hiya tujrā bihim." The consensus of the readers on reciting "tajrī" with a fatḥa on the tā' is clear evidence that the correct form of "mujrāhā" is with a fatḥa on the mīm. I chose the ḍamma in "mursāhā" because the authoritative readers unanimously agree on its ḍamma.

The meaning of His words "mujrāhā" is its course, and "mursāhā" is its halting, from "God halted it and anchored it" (*awqafahā* and *arsāhā*).

* *

Mujāhid used to recite it with a ḍamma on the mīm in both words.

18182- Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa told us, saying: Shibl told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid.

18183- ... saying: Ishaq told us, saying: 'Abd Allah told us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding "bismi-llahi mujrāhā wa-mursāhā": he said, "When they embark and when they run and anchor."

18184- Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim told us, saying: 'Isa told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "In the name of God when they embark, run, and anchor."

18185- Ibn Wakī' told us, saying: Ibn Numayr told us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding "bismi-llahi mujrāhā wa-mursāhā": he said, "In the name of God when they run and when they anchor."

18186- Abu Kurayb told us, saying: Jabir ibn Nuh told us, saying: Abu Rawq told us, from al-Dahhak, regarding His words, "Embark upon it; in the name of God is its course and its mooring": he said, "When He wished it to anchor, he said, 'In the name of God,' and it anchored; and when He wished it to run, he said, 'In the name of God,' and it ran."

* *

As for His words, "Indeed my Lord is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful," it means: Indeed my Lord is a Veiler of the sins of those who repent and turn back to Him, and Merciful to them by not punishing them after repentance. [[See the explanation of *ghafūr* and *raḥīm* above in the linguistic indexes under (ghafara) and (raḥima).]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 42–43:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And it sailed with them through waves like mountains, and Noah called to his son, and he was apart: "O my son, board with us and do not be with the disbelievers."﴾ (42)

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, exalted is His remembrance: ﴿And it sailed with them﴾, the ship was sailing with Noah and those with him in it, ﴿through waves like mountains. And Noah called to his son﴾, [calling] to him, ﴿and he was apart﴾, from him, not having boarded the ship with him: ﴿"O my son, board with us﴾, the ship ﴿and do not be with the disbelievers."﴾

* *

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He said, "I will take refuge on a mountain that will protect me from the water." [Noah] said, "There is no protector today from the decree of Allah, except for whom He has mercy." And the waves came between them, and he was among the drowned.﴾ (43)

Abu Ja'far said: His saying, exalted is His remembrance, means: Noah's son said, when Noah called him to board the ship with him, out of fear for him of drowning: ﴿"I will take refuge on a mountain that will protect me from the water"﴾, meaning: "I will go to a mountain to shelter myself from the water,"[[See the explanation of "awa" (to take refuge) above, 13:477, note 2, and the references there.]] so that it will prevent it from drowning me.

* *

By His saying, ﴿yaʿṣimunī﴾ (will protect me), he means: will prevent me, like the ʿiṣām (tie) of a waterskin, with which its head is bound so that the water does not flow out of it.[[See the explanation of "yaʿṣim" above, 10:472, note 2 / 15:73.]]

* *

As for His saying, ﴿There is no protector today from the decree of Allah, except for whom He has mercy﴾, it means: there is no preventer today from the decree of Allah that has descended upon the creation, of drowning and destruction, except for those whom We have mercy upon and rescue from it, for He is the One who prevents whomever He wills of His creation and protects.

* *

[The word] "man" (whom) here is in the nominative position, because the meaning of the speech is: there is no protector today that protects from the decree of Allah except Allah.

* *

The grammarians have differed about the position of "man" in this place.

Some of the Kufan grammarians said: it is in the accusative position, because the one protected is the opposite of the protector, and the one shown mercy is protected. He said: its accusative is like His saying: ﴿They have no knowledge of it except the following of assumption﴾ [Surah an-Nisa: 157]. He said: whoever permits it [reads] ﴿ittibāʿa al-ẓann﴾ (the following of assumption) in the accusative, and the nominative in His saying:

"And a land in which there is no companion, except the yaʿāfīr (wild oxen) and except the ʿīs (white camels)" [[It is "jirān al-ʿawd" (the old camel's companion).]]

[[The verse has been cited and its takhrij given earlier, 9:203.]]

He did not permit the nominative in "man", because the one who said "except the yaʿāfīr" made the companions of the wilderness the yaʿāfīr and what resembles them. Likewise His saying ﴿except the following of assumption﴾: it means their knowledge is assumption. He said: You are not permitted in any way to say that "the protected" is "the protector" in one state, but if you make "the protector" [carry the sense of] "the protected," [as if you said:] "there is no protected today from the decree of Allah," [[The addition between the brackets is from Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra', and it is his exact words.]] then the nominative of "man" would be permitted. He said: and there is no denying that the object ("maf'ul") may come out in the form of the subject ("fa'il"); do you not see His saying ﴿from a gushing water﴾ [Surah at-Tariq: 6], its meaning, and Allah knows best, is "mudfuq" (gushed forth)? And His saying ﴿in a pleasing life﴾, its meaning is "mardiyya" (pleasing)? The poet said: [[It is al-Hutay'a.]]

"Leave generosity, do not travel in pursuit of it, and sit, for you are the one who eats and is clothed."

[[His Diwan: 54; Tabaqat Fuhul al-Shu'ara': 98; Lisan (ṭ-ʿ-m), (k-s-w); Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra' and others, in his well-known report when he blamed al-Zibriqan and complained against him to ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, and ʿUmar said to Hassan: Did he satirize him? He said: No, but he defecated on him! I have explained it as "al-ṭāʿim" and "al-kāsī" in the relational sense, meaning: one who has food, who craves it and seeks out the best of it out of greed; and one who has clothing, who chooses it and dresses finely, with no concern for generosity. For this reason al-Zibriqan said to ʿUmar: Does my honor reach no further than that I eat and wear clothes! Similar to this is the saying of ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Hassan: "I have seen enough of generosity in you, that you wear the finest garments and are satisfied."]]

Its meaning is: the one who is clothed.

* *

Some of the grammarians of Basra said: "There is no protector today from the decree of Allah except for whom He has mercy" is [to be read as] "but whoever He has mercy upon," and it is permissible that it be read as: "no one possessing protection," meaning "protected," and "except whom He has mercy" is in the nominative as a substitute for "protector."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: There is no basis for these opinions we have related from them, because the speech of Allah, exalted is He, is only directed toward the most eloquent and most well-known usage of the speech of the people in whose tongue it was revealed, wherever a way to that can be found.

Nothing has compelled us to make "ʿāṣim" mean "maʿṣūm," nor to make "illā" mean "lākin" (but), since we find for it, in its well-known meaning in the common speech of the Arabs, a correct interpretation, which is what we have said: the meaning is: Noah said, "There is no protector today from the decree of Allah, except for whom He has mercy upon us and saves us from His punishment," just as one says, "There is no savior today from the punishment of Allah except Allah," and "There is no one who feeds today from the food of Zayd except Zayd."

This is the well-known speech and the understood meaning.

* *

As for His saying, ﴿And the waves came between them, and he was among the drowned﴾, it means: the surging water came between Noah and his son, and he drowned, [[See the explanation of "ḥāla" above, 13:472.]] so he was among those whom Allah destroyed by drowning from the people of Noah, peace be upon him.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 42–43:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And it sailed with them through waves like mountains, and Noah called to his son, and he was apart: "O my son, board with us and do not be with the disbelievers."﴾ (42)

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, exalted is His remembrance: ﴿And it sailed with them﴾, the ship was sailing with Noah and those with him in it, ﴿through waves like mountains. And Noah called to his son﴾, [calling] to him, ﴿and he was apart﴾, from him, not having boarded the ship with him: ﴿"O my son, board with us﴾, the ship ﴿and do not be with the disbelievers."﴾

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He said, "I will take refuge on a mountain that will protect me from the water." [Noah] said, "There is no protector today from the decree of Allah, except for whom He has mercy." And the waves came between them, and he was among the drowned.﴾ (43)

Abu Ja'far said: His saying, exalted is His remembrance, means: Noah's son said, when Noah called him to board the ship with him, out of fear for him of drowning: ﴿"I will take refuge on a mountain that will protect me from the water"﴾, meaning: "I will go to a mountain to shelter myself from the water,"[[See the explanation of "awa" (to take refuge) above, 13:477, note 2, and the references there.]] so that it will prevent it from drowning me.

* *

By His saying, ﴿yaʿṣimunī﴾ (will protect me), he means: will prevent me, like the ʿiṣām (tie) of a waterskin, with which its head is bound so that the water does not flow out of it.[[See the explanation of "yaʿṣim" above, 10:472, note 2 / 15:73.]]

* *

As for His saying, ﴿There is no protector today from the decree of Allah, except for whom He has mercy﴾, it means: there is no preventer today from the decree of Allah that has descended upon the creation, of drowning and destruction, except for those whom We have mercy upon and rescue from it, for He is the One who prevents whomever He wills of His creation and protects.

* *

[The word] "man" (whom) here is in the nominative position, because the meaning of the speech is: there is no protector today that protects from the decree of Allah except Allah.

* *

The grammarians have differed about the position of "man" in this place.

Some of the Kufan grammarians said: it is in the accusative position, because the one protected is the opposite of the protector, and the one shown mercy is protected. He said: its accusative is like His saying: ﴿They have no knowledge of it except the following of assumption﴾ [Surah an-Nisa: 157]. He said: whoever permits it [reads] ﴿ittibāʿa al-ẓann﴾ (the following of assumption) in the accusative, and the nominative in His saying:

"And a land in which there is no companion, except the yaʿāfīr (wild oxen) and except the ʿīs (white camels)" [[It is "jirān al-ʿawd" (the old camel's companion).]]

[[The verse has been cited and its takhrij given earlier, 9:203.]]

He did not permit the nominative in "man", because the one who said "except the yaʿāfīr" made the companions of the wilderness the yaʿāfīr and what resembles them. Likewise His saying ﴿except the following of assumption﴾: it means their knowledge is assumption. He said: You are not permitted in any way to say that "the protected" is "the protector" in one state, but if you make "the protector" [carry the sense of] "the protected," [as if you said:] "there is no protected today from the decree of Allah," [[The addition between the brackets is from Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra', and it is his exact words.]] then the nominative of "man" would be permitted. He said: and there is no denying that the object ("maf'ul") may come out in the form of the subject ("fa'il"); do you not see His saying ﴿from a gushing water﴾ [Surah at-Tariq: 6], its meaning, and Allah knows best, is "mudfuq" (gushed forth)? And His saying ﴿in a pleasing life﴾, its meaning is "mardiyya" (pleasing)? The poet said: [[It is al-Hutay'a.]]

"Leave generosity, do not travel in pursuit of it, and sit, for you are the one who eats and is clothed."

[[His Diwan: 54; Tabaqat Fuhul al-Shu'ara': 98; Lisan (ṭ-ʿ-m), (k-s-w); Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra' and others, in his well-known report when he blamed al-Zibriqan and complained against him to ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, and ʿUmar said to Hassan: Did he satirize him? He said: No, but he defecated on him! I have explained it as "al-ṭāʿim" and "al-kāsī" in the relational sense, meaning: one who has food, who craves it and seeks out the best of it out of greed; and one who has clothing, who chooses it and dresses finely, with no concern for generosity. For this reason al-Zibriqan said to ʿUmar: Does my honor reach no further than that I eat and wear clothes! Similar to this is the saying of ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Hassan: "I have seen enough of generosity in you, that you wear the finest garments and are satisfied."]]

Its meaning is: the one who is clothed.

* *

Some of the grammarians of Basra said: "There is no protector today from the decree of Allah except for whom He has mercy" is [to be read as] "but whoever He has mercy upon," and it is permissible that it be read as: "no one possessing protection," meaning "protected," and "except whom He has mercy" is in the nominative as a substitute for "protector."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: There is no basis for these opinions we have related from them, because the speech of Allah, exalted is He, is only directed toward the most eloquent and most well-known usage of the speech of the people in whose tongue it was revealed, wherever a way to that can be found.

Nothing has compelled us to make "ʿāṣim" mean "maʿṣūm," nor to make "illā" mean "lākin" (but), since we find for it, in its well-known meaning in the common speech of the Arabs, a correct interpretation, which is what we have said: the meaning is: Noah said, "There is no protector today from the decree of Allah, except for whom He has mercy upon us and saves us from His punishment," just as one says, "There is no savior today from the punishment of Allah except Allah," and "There is no one who feeds today from the food of Zayd except Zayd."

This is the well-known speech and the understood meaning.

* *

As for His saying, ﴿And the waves came between them, and he was among the drowned﴾, it means: the surging water came between Noah and his son, and he drowned, [[See the explanation of "ḥāla" above, 13:472.]] so he was among those whom Allah destroyed by drowning from the people of Noah, peace be upon him.

**The Interpretation of His Words, the Exalted:** ﴿And it was said: "O earth, swallow your water, and O sky, withhold," and the water subsided, and the matter was decreed, and it (the ark) came to rest upon al-Judi. And it was said: "Away with the wrongdoing people."﴾ (11:44)

Abu Ja'far said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: God said to the earth, after His command concerning the destruction of Noah's people by the drowning with which He destroyed them had been carried out: ﴿O earth, swallow your water﴾, that is, absorb it.

* *

It derives from the saying of the speaker: "Fulan swallowed such-and-such, yabla'uhu (he swallows it)," or "balaʿahu yabla'uhu," when he gulped it down. [[What is in the lexicons is "bala'a" (with a fatha and then a kasra). As for "bala'a" (with two fathas), Ibn al-Qutta'iyya mentioned it in his book al-Af'al, vol. 1, p. 85, and distinguished between them, saying: "Bala'a al-ta'am bal'an, and balaʿa al-ma' wal-rabq bal'an." Ibn al-Qutiyya also mentioned the same in his book al-Af'al, p. 281.]]

* *

﴿And O sky, withhold﴾, he says: withhold from the rain, hold back. ﴿And the water subsided﴾, the earth carried it away and soaked it up. ﴿And the matter was decreed﴾, he says: the command of God was carried out, and so the destruction of Noah's people was accomplished. [[See the explanation of "qadā" (decreed) in the preceding word-indexes of language (qḍy).]] ﴿And it came to rest upon al-Judi﴾, meaning the ship. "Istawat" means "arsat" (came to rest, anchored). ﴿Upon al-Judi﴾, which is a mountain, said to be in the region of Mosul or al-Jazira. ﴿And it was said: "Away with the wrongdoing people,"﴾ he says: God said: May God remove far away the wrongdoing people, those among Noah's people who disbelieved in God. [[See the explanation of "istawa" in what preceded, p. 18, note 2, and the references there.]]

18226. Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, who said: "'Ikrimah used to say: he was his son, but he opposed him in intention and deed, and therefore it was said to him: ﴿Indeed he is not of your family﴾."

18227. Al-Hasan related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri and Ibn 'Uyaynah informed us, from Musa ibn Abi 'A'ishah, from Sulayman ibn Qitah, who said: "I heard Ibn 'Abbas being asked, while he was beside the Ka'bah, about the saying of God, ﴿but they betrayed them both﴾ [Surah al-Tahrim: 10]. He said: 'As for it, it was not by fornication, but this one used to tell people that he was mad, and this one used to guide the guests (to him).'" Then he recited: ﴿Indeed, his deed was other than righteous, [a] good righteous [deed]﴾. Ibn 'Uyaynah said: "'Ammar al-Duhni informed me that he asked Sa'id ibn Jubayr about that, and he said: 'He was the son of Noah. Indeed God does not lie!'" He said: ﴿Noah called out to his son﴾. He said: "Some scholars said: 'No wife of a prophet ever committed fornication.'"

18228. Ibn Wakī' related to us, saying: Ibn 'Uyaynah related to us, from 'Ammar al-Duhni, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: "God said, and He is the Truthful, and he is His son: ﴿Noah called out to his son﴾."

18229. Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Ibn Yaman related to us, from Sa'id, from Musa ibn Abi 'A'ishah, from 'Abd Allah ibn Shaddad, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "No wife of a prophet ever committed adultery."

18230. Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to us, saying: Hushaym related to us, who said: "I asked Abu Bishr about His saying, ﴿Indeed he is not of your family﴾, and he said: 'He is not of the people of your religion, and he is not of those whom you were promised that I would save.'" Ya'qub said: Hushaym said: "Most of what Abu Bishr used to narrate to us was from Sa'id ibn Jubayr."

18231. Ibn Wakī' related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd related to us, from Ya'qub ibn Qays, who said: "A man came to Sa'id ibn Jubayr and said: 'O Abu 'Abd Allah, the one whom God mentioned in His Book as "the son of Noah," is he his son?' He said: 'Yes, by God. Indeed the Prophet of God commanded him to ride with him in the ark, but he disobeyed, and said: ﴿I will take refuge on a mountain that will protect me from the water﴾ [11:43]. He said: ﴿O Noah, indeed he is not of your family; indeed his deed is other than righteous﴾,' because of the disobedience of the Prophet of God."

18232. Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Abu Sakhr informed me, from Abu Mu'awiyah al-Bajali, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, that a man came to him and asked him. He said: "Do you think that the son of Noah was his son?" He glorified God for a long time, then said: "There is no god but God. God tells Muhammad: ﴿Noah called out to his son﴾, and you say he is not his son? Rather, he opposed him in deed, and whoever does not believe is not of him."

18233. Ya'qub and Ibn Wakī' related to me, both saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, from Abu Harun al-Ghanawi, from 'Ikrimah, concerning His saying, ﴿Noah called out to his son﴾, he said: "I testify that he was his son. God said: ﴿Noah called out to his son﴾."

18234. Ibn Wakī' related to us, saying: My father related to us, from Isra'il, from Jabir, from Mujahid and 'Ikrimah, who both said: "He was his son."

18235. Fudalah ibn al-Fadl al-Kufi related to me, saying: Bazi' said: "A man asked al-Dahhak about the son of Noah, and he said: 'Do you not marvel at this fool! He asks me about the son of Noah, and he is the son of Noah, as God said: Noah said to his son.'" [[Report 18235: Fudalah ibn al-Fadl ibn Fudalah al-Tamimi al-Tuhawi al-Kufi, a teacher of al-Tabari, truthful but sometimes erred; he is biographed in al-Tahdhib and Ibn Abi Hatim 3/2/79. "Bazi'" is al-Lahham, Abu Hazim, namely Bazi' ibn 'Abd Allah, who heard al-Dahhak. Abu Nu'aym used to speak about him, and al-Nasa'i and others declared him weak. Ibn 'Adi said: "They only objected to what he related from al-Dahhak of tafsir, and no one follows him in it." He is biographed in al-Kabir 1/2/130, Ibn Abi Hatim 1/1/420, Lisan al-Mizan 2:12, and Mizan al-I'tidal 1:143. Likewise, in both the manuscript and the printed edition at the end of the report it reads: "as God said, Noah said to his son," while the verse is: "Noah called out to his son." I fear that he meant: "Noah said to his son: O my son, board with us."]]

18236. Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih related to us, saying: 'Ubayd related to us, from al-Dahhak, that he recited: ﴿Noah called out to his son﴾, and His saying: ﴿not of your family﴾, he said: "He means: he is not of your family." He said: "He means: he is not of the family of your guardianship, nor of those whom you were promised that I would save from your family." ﴿Indeed he, his deed is other than righteous﴾, he said: "He means: his deed was in polytheism."

18237. Ibn Wakī' related to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah related to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, who said: "He, by God, is his son, of his own loins."

18238. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: 'Amr ibn 'Awn related to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, concerning His saying, ﴿not of your family﴾, he said: "Not of the people of your religion, nor of those whom you were promised that I would save him. He was his son of his own loins."

18239. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying, ﴿He said: "O Noah, indeed he is not of your family"﴾, he means: "Not of those whom We promised salvation."

18240. Reported to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His saying, ﴿Indeed he is not of your family﴾, he means: "Not of the people of your guardianship, nor of those whom you were promised that I would save from your family." ﴿Indeed his deed is other than righteous﴾, he means: "His deed was in polytheism."

18241. Ibn Wakī' related to us, saying: Khalid ibn Hayyan related to us, from Ja'far ibn Burqan, from Maymun and Thabit ibn al-Hajjaj, who both said: "He was his son, born on his bed."
* *
Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the two views is the view of the one who said: the interpretation of that is: ﴿indeed he is not of your family﴾, those whom you were promised that I would save, because he was opposed to your religion and an unbeliever toward Me. And he was his son, because God, may His remembrance be exalted, has informed His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ that he was his son, when He said: ﴿Noah called out to his son﴾. It is not permissible that He inform that he is his son and then it be contrary to what He informed. And there is no indication in His saying, ﴿Indeed he is not of your family﴾, that he is not his son, since His saying, ﴿not of your family﴾, is capable of the meanings we have mentioned, and capable of meaning: "not of the people of your religion," and then "religion" is omitted, so it is said: ﴿Indeed he is not of your family﴾, just as it is said: ﴿and ask the town in which we were﴾ [Surah Yusuf: 82].
* *
As for His saying, ﴿Indeed, his deed is other than righteous﴾, the reciters differed concerning its recitation.

The majority of the readers of the major regions (qurra' al-amsar) recited it: ﴿Indeed, his deed is other than righteous﴾, with tanwin on "'amal" and with the nominative on "ghayr."
* *
Those who recited it that way differed concerning its interpretation.

Some of them said: its meaning is: indeed your asking Me this is an other-than-righteous deed.

Mention of those who said that:

18242. Ibn Wakī' related to us, saying: Jarir related to us, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim: ﴿Indeed, he is an other-than-righteous deed﴾, he said: "Indeed your asking Me this is an other-than-righteous deed."

18243. Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿Indeed, his deed is other than righteous﴾, that is, "evil" [[I fear that the correct reading is: "that is, your asking Me," but this is how it is in the manuscript and the printed edition.]] = ﴿So do not ask Me about that of which you have no knowledge﴾.

18244. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: 'Abd Allah related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, His saying: ﴿Indeed, his deed is other than righteous﴾, he means: "Your asking Me about that of which you have no knowledge."

18245. Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Hamzah al-Zayyat, from al-A'mash, from Mujahid, His saying: ﴿Indeed, his deed is other than righteous﴾, he said: "Your asking Me is an other-than-righteous deed" = ﴿So do not ask Me about that of which you have no knowledge﴾.
* *
Others said: rather, its meaning is: indeed that which you mentioned as being your son, and asked Me to save him, is an other-than-righteous deed, that is: he is of illegitimate birth. They said: the "hā'" in His saying "innahu" refers to "the son."

Mention of those who said that:

18246. Ibn Wakī' related to us, saying: Ibn Numayr related to us, from Ibn Abi 'Urwah, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, that he recited: ﴿an other-than-righteous deed﴾, and said: "He was not, by God, his son." [[Report 18246: See what has passed, number 18212.]]
* *
It was narrated from a group of the early Muslims (al-salaf) that they recited it: ﴿Indeed, he did an other-than-righteous deed﴾, as a past-tense verb, with "ghayr" in the accusative. Among those from whom it is reported that he recited it this way is Ibn 'Abbas.

18247. Ibn Wakī' related to us, saying: Ibn 'Uyaynah related to us, from Musa ibn Abi 'A'ishah, from Sulayman ibn Qitah, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he recited: ﴿he did an other-than-righteous deed﴾.
* *
They directed the interpretation of that toward:

18248. Ibn Wakī' narrated it to us, saying: Ghundar related to us, from Ibn Abi 'Urwah, from Qatadah, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Indeed he did an other-than-righteous deed﴾, he said: "He was opposed in intention and deed."
* *
Abu Ja'far said: We do not know that this reading was recited by anyone among the readers of the major regions, except some later scholars, who argued for it on the basis of a report narrated from the Messenger of God ﷺ that he recited it that way, which is not sound in its chain. It is a hadith narrated from Shahr ibn Hawshab, sometimes saying: "from Umm Salamah," and sometimes saying: "from Asma' bint Yazid." We do not know whether [he means] "bint Yazid" [yurīd]?[[In the printed edition: "We do not know for the daughter of Yazid, nor do we know for Shahr..." and in the manuscript likewise, except that it has "ibn Yarid," and I saw that Abu Ja'far meant what I have set down, with this addition between the brackets. It seems he is saying: he says once "Umm Salamah" and once "Asma' bint Yazid," and we do not know whether the one he means by "Umm Salamah" is this one or another. See the following note.]] Nor do we know of any hearing of Shahr from Umm Salamah that is sound.

[[... The hadith of Shahr ibn Hawshab from Asma' bint Yazid, or from "Umm Salamah," Abu Ja'far did not mention its chain, and I will clarify the matter at this point, for Abu Ja'far did not give the matter its due and did not explain it sufficiently.

1. This hadith was narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad in three places (6:454, 459, 460), all through the route of Hammad ibn Salamah, from Thabit al-Bunani, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from "Asma' bint Yazid." The first and third routes are lengthy, and contain the recitation of the verse of Surah al-Zumar (39:53):
﴿O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of God. Indeed God forgives all sins; indeed He is the Forgiving, the Merciful.﴾

2. From this same route, Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi narrated it in his Musnad, p. 226, no. 1631, limited to the first verse: "Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Asma' bint Yazid al-Ansariyyah."

3. Abu Dawud narrated it in his Sunan 4:47 through two routes, no. 3982 and 3983. The first: Hammad, from Thabit, from Shahr, from Asma' bint Yazid.

Second hadith in the chain: Abd al-Aziz ibn al-Mukhtar, from Thabit, from Shahr, who said: "I asked Umm Salamah: How did the Messenger of God recite this verse?"

4. Al-Tirmidhi also narrated it in *al-Qira'at* (the Readings), through Abd Allah ibn Hafs, from Thabit al-Bunani, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Umm Salamah. He said: "This hadith has also been narrated from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Asma bint Yazid."

5. Abu Nu'aym narrated it in *al-Hilyah* 8:301, through Muhammad ibn Thabit al-Bunani, from Thabit al-Bunani, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Umm Salamah. He said: "It is a well-known hadith from the hadith of Thabit." See no. (8), for al-Tayalisi made it a hadith of Umm Salamah, the Mother of the Believers.

6. Al-Hakim narrated it in *al-Mustadrak* 2:249, restricting it to the verse of *Surat al-Zumar* that I mentioned in no. 1, through Hammad ibn Salamah, from Thabit, from Shahr, from Asma bint Yazid. Then he said: "This is a strange (gharib) and high (ali) chain, and in this book I have not cited from Shahr anything other than this single hadith."

7. Ahmad narrated it in his *Musnad* 6:294, 322, through Harun al-Nahwi, from Thabit al-Bunani, from his father, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Umm Salamah (this is in the Musnad of Umm Salamah, the Mother of the Believers). My opinion is that Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) went to the view that Shahr engaged in tadlis (concealment of a link) in this hadith, so it is not known whether he meant Asma bint Yazid al-Ansariyyah or Umm Salamah the Mother of the Believers. This is why he said afterwards: "We do not know of any sound hearing of Shahr from Umm Salamah." There is no doubt that al-Tabari here meant Umm Salamah the Mother of the Believers. Asma bint Yazid ibn al-Sakan al-Ansariyyah was a client (mawlah) of Shahr ibn Hawshab, and her kunyah was Umm Salamah. Therefore he named her once and gave her kunyah another time, and this does no harm. Shahr ibn Hawshab was the one who narrated most from his client Umm Salamah, Asma bint Yazid. Ahmad said: "How good his hadith is," and he deemed him trustworthy (thiqah), and said: "He narrated from Asma good hadiths (ahadith hisan)." Al-Tirmidhi, after citing the report, said: "I heard Abd ibn Humayd say: Asma bint Yazid is Umm Salamah al-Ansariyyah; both hadiths are one in my view." He also said: "Shahr ibn Hawshab narrated more than one hadith from Umm Salamah al-Ansariyyah, who is Asma bint Yazid." He also narrated from Aisha, from the Prophet (ﷺ), something similar to this, and we shall mention the hadith of Aisha afterwards. Nevertheless, the narration of Shahr ibn Hawshab from "Umm Salamah" the Mother of the Believers was mentioned by al-Bukhari in *al-Kabir* 2/2/259, where he said: "He heard Umm Salamah," and he added nothing and did not mention "Asma bint Yazid." For this reason I feared that al-Bukhari may have meant "Umm Salamah" Asma bint Yazid and not the Mother of the Believers. As for Ibn Abi Hatim (2/1/382), he mentioned that he "narrated from Umm Salamah and Asma bint Yazid," distinguishing between them, and the distinction indicates that he meant Umm Salamah the Mother of the Believers. Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar, in his biography, affirmed his hearing from Umm Salamah the Mother of the Believers. His narration from the Mother of the Believers is permissible, for Umm Salamah was the wife of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and she died, according to the sound opinion, in the year 61 or 62 (AH). Shahr ibn Hawshab lived eighty years and died in the year 100, though it is said 111 or 112. So his hearing from her is not invalidated by any doubt regarding his age. As for the narration itself, the scholars have affirmed that he did narrate from her. Al-Tabari rejected his narration on the grounds that he knew of no hearing of his from the Mother of the Believers, but this does not stand on anything, since others knew it. However, Ibn Hajar, in the biography of Shahr ibn Hawshab, related from Salih ibn Muhammad, after his declaration of Shahr's trustworthiness and that no lie had been found in him, the statement: "He transmits from the Prophet (ﷺ) hadiths on the readings (al-qira'at) that no one else reports." Shahr was a reciter, as al-Tabari himself mentioned, to the point that Ayyub ibn Abi Husayn said: "I have not seen anyone more knowledgeable of the Book of God than him." So if there is anything in the hadith of Shahr, it is only the strangeness of his report, and this does no harm when the chain is sound. But a difficulty remains from another direction: the narration of Ahmad through Harun al-Nahwi, from Thabit al-Bunani himself (as in no. 7), and that which al-Tayalisi narrated in no. (8) through Muhammad ibn Thabit, from Thabit, which is joined to no. (5) from the narration of Abu Nu'aym, and joined to it the second route in no. (3), then no. (4) from the narration of al-Tirmidhi, even though he transmitted from Abd ibn Humayd that they are one, as has already passed. The transmission of all these reports revolves around "Thabit al-Bunani, from Shahr." So it seems that Thabit al-Bunani narrated it from Shahr, from: Umm Salamah Asma bint Yazid; and from him, from Umm Salamah the Mother of the Believers. These are two hadiths, undoubtedly, and not as "Abd ibn Humayd" said. But has anyone other than Shahr ibn Hawshab narrated this from Umm Salamah the Mother of the Believers? I do not know. If it is sound that Shahr alone narrated it from the Mother of the Believers, did the error occur in failing to distinguish between them, from Thabit or from the one after him? I do not know either. And if they are one hadith, how did the separation occur in the musnads, making them two hadiths? And how did this separation occur, and why? Was it merely a doubt arising from the kunyah "Umm Salamah"? This is a matter requiring careful detailed examination. And this, in my opinion, is what led Abu Ja'far al-Tabari to cast doubt on the report, because of its confusion (idtirab), but he gave as its cause something other than confusion and disorder, as you have seen.

* *

As for the hadith of Aisha, which agrees with the hadith of Umm Salamah in this reading, al-Bukhari narrated it in *al-Kabir* 1/1/286, 287, through Ibrahim ibn al-Zibriqan, from Abu Rawq, from Muhammad ibn Jahhadah, from his father, from Aisha. Then he also narrated it from the same route at 1/2/251. Al-Hakim narrated it in *al-Mustadrak* through this same route, and al-Dhahabi commented on it: "Its chain is dark (muzlim)." Al-Haythami cited it in *Majma al-Zawa'id* 7:155 and said: "Al-Tabarani narrated it in *al-Awsat*, and in it is Humayd ibn al-Azraq, whom I did not know. The rest of its narrators are trustworthy." The discussion of the hadith of Aisha is lengthy, and in the narration of Muhammad ibn Jahhadah al-Iyami, from his father, there is discussion that is not the place to investigate here.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct reading in this matter, in our view, is that of the reciters of the major cities (al-amsar), which is the nominative *'amalun* (عَمَلٌ) with tanwin, and the nominative *ghayru* (غَيْرُ). That is, your request to me regarding what you ask of me concerning your son, who opposes your religion and allies himself with the people of polytheism (shirk) against me, that I deliver him from destruction, while my answer to your supplication has already passed: "Do not leave upon the earth any of the disbelievers as a dweller" (﴿لا تَذَرْ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ مِنَ الْكَافِرِينَ دَيَّارًا﴾), without exception of any of them, is a deed (عملٌ) that is not righteous (غير صالح), because it is a request from you to me that I not do what I have already said I would do, in answer to your request of me. That is the unrighteous deed.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So do not ask Me about that of which you have no knowledge﴾, it is a prohibition from God, may He be exalted, to His Prophet Noah, that he should not ask Him about the causes of His acts, the knowledge of which He has withheld from him and from other humans. He, may He be exalted, says to him: "O Noah, I have informed you concerning your request about the cause of My destroying your son, whom I destroyed. So do not ask Me afterwards about what I have concealed from you of the causes of My acts, of which you have no knowledge. ﴿I admonish you lest you be among the ignorant﴾ in your asking Me about that."

* *

Ibn Zayd used to say concerning His saying: ﴿I admonish you lest you be among the ignorant﴾:

18249 – Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said concerning His saying: ﴿I admonish you lest you be among the ignorant﴾: that ignorance should not reach such a point with you that I would not fulfil for you the promise you were promised, until you ask Me about what you have no knowledge of. ﴿And unless You forgive me and have mercy upon me, I will be among the losers﴾.

* *

The reciters differed concerning the reading of His saying: ﴿So do not ask Me about that of which you have no knowledge﴾. The majority of the reciters of the major cities read it: ﴿فَلا تَسْأَلْنِ مَا لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِ عِلْمٌ﴾ with the kasrah on the nun and its lightening (tikhfif), and this reading points to the "ya" which is the pronominal suffix referring to God: "fa-la tas'alni" (So do not ask Me). [In the manuscript and the printed edition: "kinayah ism Allah fa-la tas'alan" with a single nun at the end. The correct reading, God willing, is what I have established, with the addition of "fi" and the addition of the ya in "tas'alni".]

Some of the Meccans and some of the people of Syria read it: ﴿فَلا تَسْأَلَنَّ﴾ with the shaddah on the nun and its fathah, meaning: "fa-la tas'allanna, O Noah, ma laysa laka bihi 'ilm" (So do not ask, O Noah, about that of which you have no knowledge).

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct reading in this matter, in our view, is the lightening of the nun and its kasrah, because that is the eloquent usage of the Arabs that is common among them.

The interpretation of His words: ﴿He said, "My Lord, I seek refuge in You from asking You about that of which I have no knowledge. And unless You forgive me and have mercy upon me, I will be among the losers."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Almighty God, informing His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) about the repentance of Noah (peace be upon him) to Him for his slip, in the request he made of his Lord concerning his son, says: ﴿"My Lord, I seek refuge in You"﴾, that is: I seek Your protection from burdening myself with asking You about what I have no knowledge of, [[See the explanation of "ʿādha" (to seek refuge) above, 13:332, note 3, and the references there.]] of that which You have reserved for Your knowledge and kept hidden from Your creation. So forgive me my slip in asking You what I asked concerning my son, and if You do not forgive me and have mercy upon me, rescuing me from Your anger, ﴿"I will be among the losers"﴾, meaning: among those who defrauded themselves of their share and perished. [[See the explanation of "al-khusran" (loss) above in the lexical indexes (kh-s-r).]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 48:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿It was said: "O Noah, descend with peace from Us and blessings upon you and upon nations (who will descend) from those with you. And there will be nations whom We will provide for (in this world), then a painful punishment from Us will touch them."﴾ (11:48)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: His saying, may He be remembered, means: O Noah, descend from the ark (al-fulk) to the earth. [See the explanation of "descent" (al-hubut) above, 12:329, note 2, and the references there.]

﴿With peace from Us﴾ means: with security from Us, you and those with you, from Our destruction. [See the explanation of "peace" (al-salam) above in the lexical indexes, under (s-l-m).] ﴿And blessings upon you﴾ means: and with blessings upon you. [In the printed and manuscript texts: "and blessings upon him" again, and he did not explain it either. If nothing has fallen out of the commentary, the correct reading is what I have set down, with the addition of the preposition bi (with), indicating its coordination with what precedes it.] ﴿And upon nations from those with you﴾ means: and upon generations that will come from the offspring of those with you from your descendants. These believers from the descendants of Noah are the ones for whom happiness had preceded from God, and He blessed them before He created them in their mothers' wombs and their fathers' loins. Then He, may He be remembered, informed Noah of what He would do with the people of wretchedness from his descendants, saying to him: ﴿And nations﴾ means: and generations and groups. [See the explanation of "nation" (al-ummah) above, p. 252, note 2, and the references there.] ﴿We will provide for them﴾ in the life of this world, meaning: We will provide them with what they enjoy in it until they reach their appointed terms. [See the explanation of "enjoyment" (al-mata') above in the lexical indexes, under (m-t-' ).] ﴿Then a painful punishment from Us will touch them﴾ means: then We will make them taste, when they come to Us, a painful, agonizing punishment. [See the explanation of "touching" (al-mass) above, p. 256, note 3, and the references there.]

* *

He said: Within that peace enters every believing man and woman until the Day of Resurrection, and within that punishment and enjoyment enters every disbelieving man and woman until the Day of Resurrection.

18251- Ibn WakI' related to us, saying: Abu Dawud al-Hafari related to us, from Sufyan, from Musa ibn Ubaydah, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi: "It was said: O Noah, descend with peace from Us and blessings upon you and upon nations from those with you." He said: Within Islam enters every believing man and woman, and within polytheism every disbelieving man and woman. [In the printed edition: "entered into peace," which differs from the manuscript, and is an error.]

18252- Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Suwayd related to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, by reading, from Ibn Jurayj: "And upon nations from those with you," meaning: from those not yet born. He has decreed blessings for whoever has been preceded by happiness in God's knowledge and decree; "and nations We will provide for," from those preceded by wretchedness in God's knowledge and decree. [In the printed edition "al-shaqawah," and I have retained what is in the manuscript, here and in all the following places.]

18253- Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, similarly, except that he said: "And nations We will provide for," the enjoyment of the life of this world, from those already preceded by wretchedness in God's knowledge and decree. He said: And God did not destroy the children on the day the people of Noah drowned for the sins of their fathers, like the birds and beasts, but their term came along with the drowning.

18254- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said concerning His saying: "Descend with peace from Us and blessings upon you and upon nations from those with you and nations We will provide for": He said: They descended, by God, with Him pleased with them; they descended with peace from God. They were people of mercy from the people of that age. Then from them He brought forth offspring afterward, nations, some of whom were shown mercy and some of whom were punished. And he recited: "And upon nations from those with you and nations We will provide for." That is, the nations only separated from that band which came out of that water and was saved.

18255- It was reported from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, saying: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His saying: "O Noah, descend with peace from Us and blessings upon you and upon nations from those with you," the verse, meaning: blessings upon you and upon nations from those with you who had not yet been born; God made blessings obligatory for them because of the happiness that had preceded for them in God's knowledge. "And nations We will provide for": meaning the enjoyment of the life of this world. "Then a painful punishment from Us will touch them": because of the wretchedness that had preceded for them in God's knowledge.

18257- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said concerning His saying: "We will provide for them, then a painful punishment from Us will touch them": He said: After mercy.

18258- Al-Abbas ibn al-Walid related to us, saying: my father informed me, saying: Abdullah ibn Shawdhab informed us, saying: I heard Dawud ibn Abi Hind narrate, from al-Hasan: that he came upon this verse: "Descend with peace from Us and blessings upon you and upon nations from those with you and nations We will provide for, then a painful punishment from Us will touch them." He said: That was when God sent 'Ad, and He sent Hud to them. Some believed him, and some denied him, until the command of God came. When the command of God came, God saved Hud and those who believed with him, and God destroyed the enjoyers. Then God sent Thamud, and He sent Salih to them. Some believed him and some denied him, until the command of God came. When the command of God came, God saved Salih and those who believed with him, and God destroyed the enjoyers. Then he went through the prophets one by one, in a similar manner.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 49:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿That is among the tidings of the unseen which We reveal to you. Neither you nor your people knew them before this. So be patient; indeed the best outcome is for the God-fearing.﴾ (11:49)

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is His remembrance, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): This story which I have related to you, of Noah, his account and the account of his people, ﴿is among the tidings of the unseen﴾, meaning: it is among the reports of the unseen which you did not witness so as to know them. ﴿We reveal it to you﴾, meaning: We reveal it to you, and We make you know it. ﴿Neither you nor your people knew it before this﴾, meaning: the revelation which We send down to you. ﴿So be patient﴾, meaning: in carrying out the command of God and conveying His message, and in bearing what you encounter from the polytheists of your people, just as Noah was patient. ﴿Indeed the best outcome is for the God-fearing﴾, meaning: indeed the good end of affairs belongs to those who fear God, so they perform His obligations and avoid His prohibitions. They are the ones who triumph with what they hope for of bliss in the Hereafter, and succeed in attaining their aims in this world, just as the outcome was for Noah when he was patient in the command of God: He saved him from destruction together with those who believed in him, gave him in the Hereafter the honour that He gave him, and drowned those who denied him, destroying them all.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 50–51:

The explanation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And to 'Ad (We sent) their brother Hud. He said, "O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. You are only inventing (falsehoods).")﴾ (50)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: We sent to the people of 'Ad their brother Hud, and he said to them, "O my people, worship Allah" alone, having no partner, apart from what you worship besides Him of deities and idols. ﴿You have no deity other than Him﴾ means: there is no object of worship deserving your worship other than Him, so devote worship sincerely to Him and single Him out as God alone. ﴿You are only inventing (falsehoods)﴾ means: in associating with Him deities and idols, you are none other than people of fabrication, lying, inventing falsehood, because there is no god besides Him. [See the explanation of "al-Iftira'" (fabrication) in the earlier language indexes under the root (f-r-y).]

* *

The explanation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O my people, I do not ask you for any reward for it. My reward is only from the One who originated me. Will you not then reason?﴾ (51)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, exalted is His remembrance, reporting the words of Hud to his people: "O my people, I do not ask you, for what I call you to of sincerely devoting worship to Allah and renouncing the idols and disavowing them, for any recompense or reward." ﴿My reward is only from the One who originated me﴾ means: my reward and recompense for my counsel to you and my calling you to Allah is only from the One who created me. [See the explanation of "fatara" (originated) in the earlier passages, 11:283, 284, 487.] ﴿Will you not then reason?﴾ means: will you not reason that if I were seeking, by calling you to Allah, anything other than giving you counsel and seeking your welfare in this world and the Hereafter, I would have asked you for some worldly benefit and requested from you a reward and recompense?

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 52:

Discussion on the interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿And O my people, ask your Lord for forgiveness and then turn to Him in repentance; He will send the sky upon you in [abundant] downpour and will add strength to your strength. And do not turn away as criminals.﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The Exalted, may His remembrance be great, is informing about the statement of Hud to his people: ﴿And O my people, ask your Lord for forgiveness﴾, meaning: believe in Him so that He will forgive you your sins.

* *

And istighfar (seeking forgiveness): in this place it means belief in God, because Hud ﷺ only called his people to the Oneness of God so that He would forgive them their sins, just as Noah said to his people: ﴿Worship God, fear Him, and obey me; He will forgive you some of your sins and defer you to a specified term﴾ [Surah Nuh 71:3–4].

* *

And His words: ﴿Then turn to Him in repentance﴾, meaning: then repent to God from your past sins and from your worship of other than Him after believing in Him. ﴿He will send the sky upon you in [abundant] downpour﴾, meaning: if you believe in God and repent from your disbelief in Him, He will send the rain of the sky upon you, pouring down rain for you at the time of your need for it, and your lands will be revived from barrenness and drought. [[See the explanation of "midrar" (abundant/downpour) above, 11:263.]]

**Commentary on the Words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿We say nothing except that some of our gods have struck you with evil. He said: "I call Allah to witness, and bear witness yourselves, that I am free from what you associate, apart from Him, so scheme against me all together, then give me no respite."﴾ (11:54–55)**

Abu Ja'far [al-Tabari] said: This is a report from Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, concerning the words of the people of Hud. When he advised them, called them to the Oneness of Allah and to believing in Him, and to renouncing idols and disavowing them, they said: "We will not abandon the worship of our gods. We say only that what has moved you to disparage them and forbid their worship is that some madness from them has struck you." Hud then said to them: "I call Allah to witness concerning myself, and I call you also to witness, O people, that I am free from what you associate with Allah in worship, of your gods and idols, apart from Him." ﴿So scheme against me all together﴾, meaning: plot together, you and your gods, to harm me and to bring me distress. [[See the explanation of "al-kayd" (scheming) above, vol. 13, p. 449, note 3, and the references there.]] ﴿Then give me no respite﴾, meaning: do not delay this for me. [[See the explanation of "al-inzar" (granting respite) above, p. 151, note 3, and the references there.]] So look and see whether you and they can reach me with the evil you claim your gods have inflicted upon me.

As for His words ﴿i'taraka﴾ (has struck you), it is of the form "if'talaka" (if'ta'ala), derived from "'araniya al-shay'u ya'run'i" (the thing came upon me), meaning: when it befell you, as the poet said: [[He is Abu Khirash al-Hudhali.]]

*"From the people, there befalls him boldness and sin."*

[[Diwan al-Hudhaliyyin 2:147; Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubayda 1:290. From his qasida in which he mentions his flight from Fa'id and his Khuza'i companions, who had a blood debt (witr) against him. When they met him he fled and ran, and he mentioned that in his poetry. Then he came to mention a man who was pursuing him while he ran, and he said:*

*"I strive to escape by swift running, and there urges me on, at my back, a man broad of forearms and strong and tall."*

*"He recalls a blood-vengeance (dhahl) against us, and he is a daring one, from the people, in whom there befalls boldness and sin."*

*He says: "I strive to escape" (awa'il), meaning: I seek deliverance through swift running. "Al-dhaliq" means sharp, swift and powerful. "Haththani la-da al-matn" means he urges me on to run, a man behind me, as if from his closeness he had mounted my back. "Mashbuh al-dhira'ayn" describes this man as broad in the forearms. "Khaljam" means tall and strong. "Tadhakkara dhahlan" means a vengeance (tha'r), so his recalling the vengeance was more of a spur to him in pursuing Abu Khirash. Then he said: he is a daring one among their bold ones, who does not fear, and what drives him to that is "ijtira'" (boldness), meaning audacity that fear does not restrain, and "ma'thamun" means seeking retribution, namely requital and punishment for my sin that had been committed against them. "Al-ma'tham" and "al-atham" are one and the same.*

*In the printed edition it read "ijtiram," and in the manuscript "ijtiraman," and both are errors; the correct reading is what is recorded here, from his Diwan.]]

"Haththani la-da al-matn" means he urges me on to run, a man behind me, as if from his closeness he had mounted my back. "Mashbuh al-dhira'ayn" describes this man as broad in the forearms. "Khaljam" means tall and strong. "Tadhakkara dhahlan" means a vengeance (tha'r), so his recalling the vengeance was more of a spur to him in pursuing Abu Khirash. Then he said: he is a daring one among their bold ones, who does not fear, and what drives him to that is "ijtira'" (boldness), meaning audacity that fear does not restrain, and "ma'thamun" means seeking retribution, namely requital and punishment for my sin that had been committed against them. "Al-ma'tham" and "al-atham" are one and the same.*

*In the printed edition it read "ijtiram," and in the manuscript "ijtiraman," and both are errors; the correct reading is what is recorded here, from his Diwan.]]

The Interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, I have relied upon Allah, my Lord and your Lord. There is no creature but that He holds its forelock. Indeed, my Lord is on a straight path.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He means: "Indeed I have put my trust in Allah, who is my Master and your Master, and the Guardian over all His creation, so that you and others among creatures cannot harm me with evil." [See the explanation of "tawakkul" (trusting reliance) in the previous lexical indexes, under (w-k-l).] For there is nothing that crawls on the earth [See the explanation of "dabbah" (creature) earlier, p. 240, note 1, and the references there.] except that Allah owns it, and it is in His grip and under His authority, subdued and submissive to Him.

* *

If someone should say: How is it said, ﴿He holds its forelock﴾, singling out the "forelock" for the seizing, rather than other parts of the body?

It is said: Because the Arabs used this expression to describe one whom they characterized as humbled and submissive. They would say: "The forelock of so-and-so is only in the hand of so-and-so," meaning that he is obedient to him and he directs him however he wishes. And when they took a captive and wished to release him and bestow favor upon him, they would shave his forelock, so as to boast of this over him during times of boasting. So God addressed them with what they knew in their speech, and the meaning is what I have mentioned.

* *

As for His saying, ﴿Indeed, my Lord is on a straight path﴾, He means: Indeed my Lord is upon the way of truth, recompensing the good-doer among His creatures for his goodness and the evildoer for his evil, not wronging any of them in anything, and accepting from them nothing but Islam and faith in Him. [See the explanation of "straight path" (sirat mustaqim) earlier in the lexical indexes, under (s-r-t) and (q-w-m).] As related:

18278. Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, he said: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿Indeed, my Lord is on a straight path﴾: "The truth."

18279. Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq narrated to us, he said: Abdullah narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

18280. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim narrated to us, he said: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

18281. Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the same.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 57:

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿But if they turn away, then I have certainly conveyed to you that with which I was sent to you, and my Lord will replace you with another people, and you will not harm Him at all. Indeed, my Lord is Guardian over all things.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is His mention, relating the words of Hud to his people: ﴿But if they turn away﴾, meaning: if they turn their backs, turning away from what I call them to, namely the Oneness of God and abandoning the worship of idols. [[The correct wording of the speech should have been: "But if you turn away from what I call you to," since this is an address from Hud to his people, i.e., "fa-in tatawallaw" (but if you turn away), with one of the two taa' elided. It seems this was an oversight on the part of Abu Ja'far, may God have mercy on him and forgive him.]] = ﴿then I have certainly conveyed to you﴾, O people, = ﴿that with which I was sent to you﴾, for the Messenger has only the duty of conveying. = ﴿and my Lord will replace you with another people﴾, meaning: my Lord will destroy you, then my Lord will substitute for you from among others a people other than you, [[See the explanation of "al-istikhlaf" (substitution) in the earlier linguistic indexes under (kh-l-f).]] who will affirm His Oneness and devote worship sincerely to Him. = ﴿and you will not harm Him at all﴾, meaning: you have no power to harm Him if He wills to destroy you or to destroy you.

* *

It has been said: His destroying you does not diminish Him when He destroys you; you do not reduce Him by anything, because it is all the same to Him whether you exist or do not exist.

* *

= ﴿Indeed, my Lord is Guardian over all things﴾, meaning: indeed my Lord is possessed of preservation and knowledge over all His creation. [[See the explanation of "hafiz" (guardian) in the earlier volumes: 8:562 / 12:25, 33.]]

He says: He is the One who protects me from your reaching me with harm.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 11, verses 58–59:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿And when Our command came, We saved Hud and those who believed with him by mercy from Us, and We saved them from a harsh punishment﴾ [11:58]

Abu Ja'far said: He, the Exalted, says: When the punishment of Hud's people came, We saved Hud and those who believed in God along with him from it. ﴿By mercy from Us﴾ means: by His grace upon them and favour. ﴿And We saved them from a harsh punishment﴾ means: We also saved them from a harsh punishment on the Day of Resurrection, just as We saved them in this world from the torment that We sent down upon 'Ad. [See the explanation of "ghilzah" (harshness) above, 14:576, note 2, and the references there.]

* *

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿And those were 'Ad; they denied the signs of their Lord, disobeyed His messengers, and followed the command of every obstinate tyrant﴾ [11:59]

Abu Ja'far said: He, the Exalted, says: These are the ones upon whom We brought Our vengeance and punishment, 'Ad, who denied the proofs and evidences of God [see the explanation of "jahd" (denial) above, 11:334 / 12:476], and disobeyed His messengers, whom He sent to them to call them to His monotheism and to following His command. ﴿And followed the command of every obstinate tyrant﴾ means: every arrogant one who is proud before God, deviating from the truth, who does not submit to it nor accept it.

* *

It is said of this: "'anada 'an al-haqq, fa-huwa ya'nid 'unudan" (he deviated from the truth, so he deviates in deviation), and "al-rajul 'a'nid wa-'anud" (the man is obstinate and stubborn). From this is said of a vein that gushes and does not stop: "'irq 'a'nid", meaning harmful. [See Abu 'Ubaydah's Majaz al-Qur'an 1:291, which contains further clarification.]

From this is the verse of an anonymous rajaz poet [I do not know who said it]:

*Innī kabīrun lā uṭīqu al-'unnadā*
(I am old, I cannot bear the stubborn ones)

[Majaz al-Qur'an 1:291; al-Batalyawsi: 415; al-Jawaliqi: 336; Lisan al-'Arab ('nd); it will come in the tafsir at 29:97 (Bulaq), and elsewhere. These are verses cited as examples of rhyme-matching (iqfa'). The poem says: "When I ride, make me the middle one... I am old, I cannot bear the stubborn ones, nor can I bear the scattered, unbroken she-camels."]

* *

Narrated to us by Bishr, who said: Yazid narrated to us, who said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿And followed the command of every obstinate tyrant﴾, that he is the polytheist.
