18341- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Ya'qub al-Qummi narrated to us, saying: Ja'far narrated to us, from Sa'id: ﴿yujadilunaa fi qawmi Lut﴾, he said: When Gabriel and those with him came, they said to Abraham: "We are indeed going to destroy the people of this town; its people were indeed wrongdoers." Abraham said to them: "Will you destroy a town in which there are four hundred believers?" They said: "No!" He said: "Will you destroy a town in which there are three hundred believers?" They said: "No!" He said: "Will you destroy a town in which there are two hundred believers?" They said: "No!" He said: "Will you destroy a town in which there are forty believers?" They said: "No!" He said: "Will you destroy a town in which there are fourteen believers?" They said: "No!" Abraham was counting them as fourteen because of Lot's wife; so he fell silent and his soul was reassured.

18342- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: al-Hammani narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from al-Minhal, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The angel said to Abraham: "If there are five in it who pray, the punishment will be lifted from them."

18343- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿yujadilunaa fi qawmi Lut﴾: it was mentioned to us that his argument with them was that he said to them: "Tell me: if there are fifty believers in it, will you punish it?" They said: "No!" until it reached ten. He said: "Tell me: if there are ten in it, will you punish them?" They said: "No!" And these were three towns, containing whatever multitude and number God willed.

18344- Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿yujadilunaa fi qawmi Lut﴾, he said: It reached us that he said to them that day: "Tell me: if there are fifty Muslims in it?" They said: "If there are fifty, we will not punish them." He said: "Forty?" They said: "And forty!" He said: "Thirty?" They said: "Thirty!" until he reached ten. They said: "And if there are ten in them!" He said: "A people in which there are not ten, in which there is goodness..." Ibn Abd al-A'la said: Muhammad ibn Thawr said: Ma'mar said: It reached us that there were four thousand thousand people in the town of Lot, or whatever number God willed.

18345- Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: Amr ibn Hammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿So when fear had left Abraham and the good tidings had come to him﴾, he said: "What is your business, O messengers?" They said: "We have been sent to the people of Lot." He argued with them concerning the people of Lot, saying: "Tell me: if there are a hundred Muslims in it, will you destroy them?" They said: "No!" He kept lowering the number until it reached ten Muslims. They said: "We will not punish them if there are ten Muslims in it." Then they said: "O Abraham, turn away from this; there is in it only one household of believers," namely Lot and his household. This is the saying of God: ﴿He argued with Us concerning the people of Lot.﴾ Then the angels said: ﴿O Abraham, turn away from this; indeed the command of your Lord has come, and indeed there will come upon them a punishment that cannot be turned back.﴾

18346- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: ﴿So when fear had left Abraham and the good tidings had come to him﴾, meaning: Abraham argued on behalf of the people of Lot to turn away the punishment from them. He said: The people of the Torah claim that Abraham's argument with them, when he disputed with them concerning the people of Lot to turn away the punishment from them, was that he said to the messengers in what he spoke to them: "Tell me: if there are a hundred believers in it, will you destroy them?" They said: "No!" He said: "Tell me: if they are ninety?" They said: "No!" He said: "Tell me: if they are eighty?" They said: "No!" He said: "Tell me: if they are seventy?" They said: "No!" He said: "Tell me: if they are sixty?" They said: "No!" He said: "Tell me: if they are fifty?" They said: "No!" He said: "Tell me: if there is one Muslim man?" They said: "No!" He said: Since they did not tell Abraham that there was one believer in it, ﴿he said: "Indeed, in it is Lot,"﴾ by which he would ward off the punishment from them. ﴿They said: "We know best who is in it; we will surely save him and his family, except his wife; she is among those who remain behind."﴾ ﴿They said: "O Abraham, turn away from this; indeed the command of your Lord has come, and indeed there will come upon them a punishment that cannot be turned back."﴾

18347- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, saying: Ibn Jurayj said: Abraham said: "Will you destroy them if you find in it a hundred believers, then ninety?" until it descended to five. He said: In the town of Lot there were four thousand thousand.

18348- Muhammad ibn Awf narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Mughirah narrated to us, saying: Safwan narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Mathna and Muslim Abu al-Habil al-Ash'ari narrated to us, both saying: "So when fear had left Abraham," to the end of the verse. Abraham said: "Will you punish a great world of Your world, in which there are a hundred men?" He said: "No, by My might, nor fifty!" He said: "Then forty? Then thirty?" until he reached five. He said: "No! By My might, I will not punish them, even if there are five in it who worship Me!" Almighty and Majestic God said: ﴿But We found in it none but one house of the Muslims﴾ [Surah al-Dhariyat: 36], that is, Lot and his two daughters. He said: Then the punishment befell them. Almighty and Majestic God said: ﴿And We left in it a sign for those who fear the painful punishment﴾ [Surah al-Dhariyat: 37], and He said: ﴿So when fear had left Abraham and the good tidings had come to him, he began to argue with Us concerning the people of Lot.﴾ [[Report 18348: "Muhammad ibn Awf ibn Sufyan al-Ta'i," the teacher of al-Tabari, who has appeared repeatedly, among them: 13108.

And "Abu al-Mughirah" is: "Abd al-Quddus ibn al-Hajjaj al-Khawlani," who has appeared repeatedly, among them: 13108.

And "Safwan" is: "Safwan ibn Amr ibn Harim al-Sakuni," who has appeared repeatedly, among them: 13108.

"Abu al-Mathna" appears to mean: Muslim ibn al-Mathna al-Kufi al-Mu'adhdhin, who narrated from Ibn Umar, biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 4/1/256, and Ibn Abi Hatim 4/1/195. As for "Abu al-Habil al-Ash'ari," I find no one named thus, and I suspect an error has occurred in this chain; its correction in my view is: "He said: Abu al-Mathna Muslim narrated to us, and al-Husayl al-Ash'ari."

"Al-Husayl al-Ash'ari," as I am inclined to think, is: "al-Husayl ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Ash'ari," also said to be "Husayn," who narrated from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, biographed in al-Tahdhib and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/2/58. Yet there is something in the soul about the reality of this chain, and God knows best.]]

* *

The Arabs hardly follow "lamma" with a past-tense verb unless it is also a past. They say: "lamma qama qumtu" (when he stood, I stood), and they hardly say "lamma qama aqumu." It may be permitted with verbs that have extension, such as "al-jidal" (argument), "al-khusumah" (dispute), and "al-qital" (fighting), so they say concerning this: "lamma laqitahu uqatiluhu," meaning: I began to fight him.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, Abraham was forbearing, grieving, and turning back in repentance﴾, Almighty God means: Indeed Abraham was slow to anger, [[See the explanation of "halim" above, 11:114, note 3, and the references there.]] humbled before his Lord, submissive to Him, obedient to His command. ﴿Turning back in repentance﴾ means returning often to His obedience. As:

18349- al-Harith narrated to me, saying: Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, saying: Isra'il narrated to us, from Abu Yahya, from Mujahid: ﴿awwah, muneeb﴾, he said: al-qanit (devout) is al-raja' (one who returns often).

* *

We have already explained the meaning of "al-awwah" earlier, with the differences of those who differ, and the proofs for what we consider correct of it, in a way that makes repeating it unnecessary. [[See the explanation of "al-awwah" above, 14:523–536.]]

**The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿O Abraham, turn away from this. Indeed, the command of your Lord has come, and indeed there is coming upon them a punishment that will not be turned back.﴾ (11:76)**

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is His remembrance, reporting the words of His messengers to Abraham: ﴿O Abraham, turn away from this﴾. This is what they said to him when he argued with them concerning the people of Lot. They said: Leave off arguing about their affair and disputing over it.[[See the explanation of "i'rad" (turning away) in the earlier volume 14: 425, note 4, and the references there.]] ﴿Indeed, the command of your Lord has come﴾, meaning: the command of your Lord has come concerning their punishment. The word of punishment has been fulfilled against them, and the decree of their destruction has been carried out. ﴿And indeed there is coming upon them a punishment that will not be turned back﴾, meaning: a punishment from God that will not be repelled has descended upon the people of Lot.

* *

The report supporting what we have mentioned has been related from those who transmitted it.[[The words in parentheses are required by the context.]]

**The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And when Our messengers came to Lot, he was distressed for them and felt helpless because of them, and he said, "This is a trying day."﴾ (11:77)**

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is His remembrance, saying: When Our angels came to Lot, their coming distressed him. The word used is "sa'a," a verb derived from "su'" (evil/distress). ﴿And he felt helpless because of them﴾, meaning: his soul was constricted by grief at their coming. This was because he did not know that they were messengers of God at the time their coming distressed him. He knew what his people were doing, namely their committing of the abomination, and he feared for them. Therefore he felt helpless at their coming, and he knew that he would need to defend his guests. That is why he said: ﴿This is a trying day.﴾

Mention of those who said this:

18350. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas regarding His words: ﴿And when Our messengers came to Lot, he was distressed for them and felt helpless because of them﴾, he said: He thought ill of his people and felt helpless about his guests.

* *

18351. Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, from Hudhayfa, that he said: When the messengers came to Lot, they came to him while he was working on a piece of land of his. It had been said to them, and God knows best: Do not destroy them until Lot bears witness against them. He said: So they came to him and said: "We are going to be your guests tonight." So he set off with them. When he had gone a while, he turned and said: "Do you not know what the people of this town do? By God, I do not know anyone on the face of the earth more wicked than them!" He said: So he continued on with them. Then he said the same thing a second time, and he set off with them. When the wicked old woman, his wife, saw them, she went and warned them.[[Report 18351: al-Tabari related it in his History 1: 154.]]

18352. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, who said: Hudhayfa said, and he mentioned something similar.

18353. Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: al-Hakam ibn Bashir related to us, saying: Amr ibn Qays al-Mala'i related to us, from Sa'id ibn Bashir, from Qatada, who said: The angels came to Lot while he was in his field, and God said to the angels: "If Lot bears witness against them four times, then I have permitted you to destroy them." They said: "O Lot, we want to be your guests tonight." He said: "What has reached you of their affair?" They said: "And what is their affair?" He said: "I testify by God that it is the most evil town on earth in its deeds!" He said this four times, and Lot bore witness against them four times. Then they entered his house with him.[[Report 18353: al-Tabari related it in his History 1: 154.]]

18354. Musa ibn Harun related to me, saying: Amr ibn Hammad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, who said: The angels departed from Abraham's presence toward the town of Lot. They reached it at midday. When they arrived at the river of Sodom, they met Lot's daughter drawing water for her family. Lot had two daughters; the elder's name was "Rith" and the younger's was "Zaghrata."[[Thus it is in the manuscript, clearly dotted, although the dots are sparse in places. In the History it is "Ra'ziya," and verifying that requires a different time.]] They said to her: "O young woman, is there a dwelling?" She said: "Yes. Stay where you are and do not enter until I come to you!" She feared for them because of her people.[[That is, she feared for them.]] She went to her father and said: "O father, young men at the gate of the city wanted you. I have never seen faces of people more beautiful than theirs. Your people will not seize them and disgrace them!" His people had already forbidden him from hosting any man. They said: "Leave us alone; let us be guests to the men!" So he brought them in, and no one knew except the household of Lot. His wife went out and informed her people, saying: "In Lot's house there are men whose faces I have never seen the like of!" So his people came to him rushing.[[Report 18354: al-Tabari related it in his History 1: 154, with a complete chain, in a lengthy form.]]

18355. Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salama related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: The messengers set out, as the people of the Torah claim, from Abraham's presence to Lot at al-Mu'tafika. When the messengers came to Lot, he was distressed for them and felt helpless because of them. That was because of his fear for them, that his people would disgrace him regarding his guests. So he said: ﴿This is a trying day.﴾

* *

As for His words: ﴿And he said, "This is a trying day."﴾, he means: Lot said: This day is one of extreme harm and great affliction.

* *

It is said of it: "Yawmuna hadha ya'sibu ya'sibu 'asban" (this day of ours is trying). From this is the verse of Adi ibn Zayd:

"I was the fierce one against your opponent, and I did not retreat, / though they had you in a trying day."[[al-Aghani 2: 111; Majaz al-Qur'an 1: 294; Lisan al-'Arab (s-l-k); and it will come in the tafsir 14: 8 / 18: 13 (Bulaq). From a long ode of his, composed while he was imprisoned by al-Nu'man ibn al-Mundhir, in which he says to al-Nu'man before it:

"The enemies strove without ceasing to do me evil, / by the Lord of Mecca and the Cross,
They wanted you to delay concerning Adi, / so that he would be imprisoned or thrown into the well,
"And I was the fierce one against your opponent..."
I announce it to them and conceal every secret / as between the inner bark and the palm-frond stalk,
So I prevailed over them when we met, / with your crown, like the winning of the arrow of the skilled gambler."

"Dahdahahu" means he rolled it down from high to low. "Al-qalib" means the well; here he means the grave. "Lizaz al-khasm" means the fierce, stubborn one, strong in calamities. "A'radha 'an khasmihi" means he held back and recoiled. In the printed edition here it was "a'adda," and in the manuscript "a'ud," and the correct reading is what is adopted here. "Al-lihaa'" is the bark of a stick, and "al-'asib" is the palm frond; he means: your secret is like what lies between these two, that is, hidden and unseen. "Al-qadah al-arib" is one of the arrows of the game of chance, the arrow with many fletchings; "al-araab" are the parts of the feathers.]] And the verse of the reciter:

"A trying day that tests the champions, / testing the strong as it tests the tall spears."[[I have not identified its speaker; it is in Majaz al-Qur'an 1: 294.]]

And the words of another:

"And if you do not satisfy Bakr ibn Wa'il, / there will be a trying day for you in Iraq."[[I have not identified its speaker; it is in Majaz al-Qur'an 1: 294.]]

Ka'b ibn Ju'ayl said:

"Many groups, clinging to the lowland, / know from it a trying day."[[I have not found this verse elsewhere. In the printed edition it is "yulabbuna," and in the manuscript likewise, though with an error in the dotting; I believe the correct reading is what is adopted here, from the expression "alaba bil-makan," meaning he stayed with it and did not leave it. "Al-hadid" is a low part of the land at the end of a mountain. "Fi'am" means groups. This verse seems to be from his poetry in which he lamented Abd al-Rahman ibn Khalid ibn al-Walid, and al-Mus'ab al-Zubayri related some of its verses in Nasab Quraysh, p. 325. Ka'b ibn Ju'ayl used to praise him.]]

18360. Ali related to me, saying: Abdullah related to us, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿And he said, "This is a trying day."﴾, i.e., a severe day.

The discussion on the interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿And his people came rushing toward him, and before that they had been doing evil deeds. He said: "O my people, these are my daughters; they are purer for you. So fear God and do not disgrace me concerning my guests. Is there not among you a single right-minded man?"﴾ (78)

Abu Ja'far said: He, may He be exalted, says: his people came to Lot urging one another on toward him, trembling as they hurried, because of the desire for indecency that had taken hold of them.

* *

It is said: "ahra'a al-rajul" (the man was seized with trembling), from cold, anger or fever, when he shivers, and he is "muhra'" when he is hasty and eager, as the rajaz poet said: [[I have not identified the speaker.]]

"With hastening ones rushing toward him, hurrying" [[Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubayda 1: 294.]]

And from it is the saying of Muhalhil:

"They came rushing, while they were captives, led by them in spite of their noses." [[Lisan al-'Arab (h-r-'), and I have not identified the rest of the poem.]]

* *

The readers differed concerning the recitation of His words: ﴿hunna atharu lakum (they are purer for you)﴾.

The majority of readers recited it with the nominative ﴿atharu (purer)﴾, taking "hunna" as the subject and "atharu" as its predicate, as if it were said: "My daughters are purer for you than what you desire of indecency with men."

* *

It is reported that 'Isa ibn 'Umar al-Basri used to recite it: ﴿hunna athara lakum (they are purer for you)﴾, with the accusative "athara". [[See the recitation of 'Isa ibn 'Umar and what Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala said to him, in Tabaqat Fuhul al-Shu'ara', p. 18.]]

* *

Some of the grammarians of Basra used to say: This is not possible; the predicate of a verb which cannot do without a predicate is only put in the accusative when between the noun and the predicate are these pronouns.

Some of the grammarians of Kufa used to say: Whoever puts it in the accusative makes it an indefinite noun, leaving the definite, and "hunna" would be a supporting pronoun ('imad) for the verb, so it does not govern it.

* *

Another of them said: It is heard from the Arabs: "This is Zayd, himself exactly" (hadha Zayd iyyahu bi-'aynihi). He said: So he made it a predicate of "hadha," like your saying: "'Abd Allah was himself exactly." He said: The verb could not occur here because al-taqrib (proximity) is a rejection of speech, [[See the explanation of "al-taqrib" in what has passed, 7: 149, note 4, and p. 150, note 3. It is a term of the Kufans, meaning that "hadha" and "hadhihi" are like the sisters of "kana" in needing a raised noun and an accusative predicate.]] so the two cannot come together, because it is contradictory: that is information about something known, while this is information about the beginning of what one is in: "Here I am, present," or "Zayd is the scholar," so it is contradictory for the known to enter upon the present. Therefore it was not permitted.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The recitation which I do not permit to be opposed in this matter is the nominative: ﴿hunna atharu lakum﴾, because of the consensus of the authoritative readers of the cities upon it, along with its soundness in Arabic, and the accusative reading also has soundness in it.

* *

As for His words: ﴿fa-ttaqu Allah wa-la takhzuni fi dayfi (so fear God and do not disgrace me concerning my guests)﴾, meaning: fear God, O people, and beware of His punishment, in your committing the indecency which you are committing and seeking = ﴿wa-la takhzuni fi dayfi (and do not disgrace me concerning my guests)﴾, meaning: do not humiliate me by mounting upon my guests what they dislike you mounting upon them. [[See the explanation of "al-khizy" (disgrace) in what has passed in the indexes of language, under kh-z-y.]]

* *

"Al-dayf" (guest), in this place, is used in the singular with the meaning of the plural. The Arabs call one and many "dayf" with one form, as they say: "a just man" (rajul 'adl) and "a just people" (qawm 'adl).

* *

As for His words: ﴿a-laysa minkum rajul rashid (Is there not among you a single right-minded man?)﴾, meaning: Is there not among you a man possessing right guidance (rushd), who forbids anyone who intends to commit indecency with my guests, and prevents them from it? [[See the explanation of "al-rushd" in what has passed, 13: 114, note 5, and the references there.]] As:

18384 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salama related to us, from Ibn Ishaq: ﴿fa-ttaqu Allah wa-la takhzuni fi dayfi a-laysa minkum rajul rashid﴾, that is: Is there not a man who knows the truth and forbids the wrong?

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 79:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿They said: You certainly know that we have no claim on your daughters, and you certainly know what we want﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: the people of Lot said to Lot: ﴿You certainly know﴾, O Lot, ﴿that we have no claim on your daughters﴾, because they are not wives for us, [In the printed and manuscript texts: "ليس لنا أزواجا" ("they are not wives for us"), and the correct reading is what I have established.] as:

18385. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, who said: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: ﴿They said: You certainly know that we have no claim on your daughters﴾, that is, no wives; ﴿and you certainly know what we want﴾.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and you certainly know what we want﴾, it means: they said, "And you, O Lot, certainly know that our need lies elsewhere than your daughters, and that what we desire is what you forbid us."

* *

The people of interpretation have said in agreement with what we have said on this.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He said: "If only I had power against you, or could take refuge in a strong support!"﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Lot said to his people when they refused except to proceed with what they had come for, seeking the abomination, and he despaired of their responding to him regarding anything that he had proposed to them: ﴿If only I had power against you﴾, with helpers who would support me against you and assistants who would aid me, ﴿or could take refuge in a strong support﴾, meaning: or could join a protecting clan that would shield me from you. [See the explanation of "awā" (to take refuge) above, p. 331, footnote 1, and the references there; then see what follows at p. 422.] It would have prevented you from what you came seeking from me regarding my guests. The answer to "law" (if) has been omitted because the context indicates it, and its meaning is understood.

It is said: from ﴿a strong support﴾ comes "I took refuge in you" (awaytu ilayka), "I take refuge in you, awyan", meaning: I came to you and joined you, [See the explanation of "awā" above, p. 418, footnote 1, and the references there; this is an addition in clarification not previously given.] as the rajaz poet said:

He takes refuge in a support among the supports... in a multitude of Tays and a glorious Ban [Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubaydah 1: 294; "'adad Tays" is numerous.] [The author of the verse is unknown.]

It is also said: when Lot spoke this statement, the messengers became angry with him because of it.

[Report 18406: part of a long report narrated by Abu Ja'far in his Tarikh 1: 156, 157, and it will come as number 18415.]

The Exegesis of His Words, the Exalted: ﴿They said, "O Lut, we are messengers of your Lord; they shall never reach you. So travel with your family in a part of the night, and let none of you look back, except your wife. Indeed, what strikes them will strike her. Indeed, their appointment is the morning. Is not the morning near?"﴾ [11:81]

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, the Exalted, says: The angels said to Lut, when Lut said to his people, ﴿If only I had power over you, or could take refuge in a strong support﴾ [11:80], and they saw what distress he suffered on their account: ﴿O Lut, we are messengers of your Lord﴾, sent to destroy them, and they shall never reach you or your guest with harm, so ease your mind about the matter. ﴿So travel with your family in a part of the night﴾, meaning: Leave among them, you and your family, while part of the night remains. [[See the explanation of "al-qit'" (a part) above, p. 76.]]

* *

It is said: "asra" and "sara," both meaning to travel by night. ﴿And let none of you look back, except your wife.﴾

* *

The readings differ regarding the word ﴿fa-asri﴾.

The majority of the readers of Mecca and Medina read it "fa-sri" (فَاسْرِ), with a connecting alif and without a hamzah, from "sara."

The majority of the readers of Kufa and Basra read it ﴿fa-asri﴾ (فَأَسْرِ), with a hamzah on the alif, from "asra."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: My view on this is that both are valid readings. Each has been recited by authorities in recitation, and they are two well-known dialects of the Arabs with the same meaning. Whichever of them the reciter uses, he is correct.

* *

As for His words ﴿except your wife (imra'ataka)﴾, most readers of the Hijaz and Kufa, and some of the people of Basra, read it in the accusative, "imra'ataka" (امْرَأَتَكَ), with the interpretation: "So travel with your family, except your wife," meaning that Lut was ordered to travel with his family excluding his wife, for he was forbidden to take her along and was ordered to leave her with her people.

* *

Some of the people of Basra read it in the nominative, "imra'atuka" (امْرَأَتُكَ), meaning: "And let none of you look back, except your wife," since Lut had taken her out with him. Lut and those with him who traveled with him were forbidden to look back, except for his wife, and she looked back and perished for that reason.

* *

As for His words ﴿Indeed, what strikes them will strike her﴾, meaning: What befalls your people of punishment will befall your wife. ﴿Indeed, their appointment is the morning﴾, meaning: The appointed time for the destruction of your people is the morning. Lut found their delay strange and said to them: "Yes, hasten their destruction!" They said: ﴿Is not the morning near?﴾, meaning: At dawn the punishment will descend upon them, as related by:

18407: Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, regarding ﴿Is not the morning near?﴾: That is, it will descend upon them at the dawn of this very night of yours, so proceed as you have been commanded.

* *

What we have said on this matter is also the view of the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil, the exegetes).

Those who said so:

18408: Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Ya'qub related to us, from Ja'far, from Sa'id, who said: The messengers went from Abraham to Lut. When they came to Lut, and what happened between them occurred as God mentioned, Gabriel said to Lut: "O Lut, we are going to destroy the people of this town, for its people have been wrongdoers." Lut said to them: "Destroy them right now!" Gabriel, peace be upon him, said to him: ﴿Indeed, their appointment is the morning. Is not the morning near?﴾ So God sent down to Lut: ﴿Is not the morning near?﴾ He said: So He commanded him to travel with his family in a part of the night, and that none of them should look back except his wife. He said: So he traveled. When the hour came in which they were destroyed, Gabriel put his wing beneath them and lifted them up, until the people of heaven heard the crowing of roosters and the barking of dogs. Then he turned its upper part to its lower part and rained down upon them stones of baked clay. He said: Lut's wife heard the crash and cried: "Oh, my people!" A stone struck her and killed her. [[The report 18408: Abu Ja'far narrated it in his History, 1:155.]]

18409: Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Ya'qub related to us, from Hafs ibn Humayd, from Shamir ibn 'Atiyyah, who said: Lut had taken an oath from his wife that she would not disclose any secret of his guests. He said: When Gabriel and those with him entered upon him, she saw them in a form she had never seen before, so she hurried to her people. She came to the assembly and gestured with her hand like this, and they came rushing toward him, running between a walk and a run. When they reached Lut, Lut said to them what God had said in His Book. Gabriel said: ﴿O Lut, we are messengers of your Lord; they shall never reach you﴾. He said: Then he gestured with his hand [[Qala biyadihi: he pointed with his hand and motioned.]] and He obliterated their eyes, and they began to search for them, feeling the walls, while they could not see. [[The report 18409: Abu Ja'far narrated it in his History, 1:155.]]

18410: Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, from Hudhayfah, who said: When the wicked old woman, his wife, saw them, meaning the messengers, she went and warned them, saying: "Some people have been guests of Lut, and I have never seen people with more beautiful faces!" He said: I do not think he said anything but: "And none whiter or sweeter-smelling!" He said: So they came to him rushing, as God said. Lut then slammed the door shut. He said: They began to try to break in. He said: Gabriel asked his Lord for permission to punish them, and it was granted. He struck them with his wing, leaving them blind, wandering about on the most wicked night that ever came upon them. [[In the printed edition: "on the most wicked night that ever came upon them..." seems to be an attempted correction that spoiled it. The correct reading is that of the manuscript and the History.]]

They informed him: "We are messengers of your Lord, so travel with your family in a part of the night." He said: We have been told that Lut's wife was with him when he left the town. Then she heard the sound, turned around, and God sent a stone upon her and destroyed her. As for His words ﴿Indeed, their appointment is the morning. Is not the morning near?﴾, the Prophet of God wanted something quicker than that, and they said: ﴿Is not the morning near?﴾ [[The report 18410: Abu Ja'far narrated it in his History, 1:155, but the last sentence of the report does not appear in it.]]

18411: Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: al-Hakam ibn Bashir related to us, saying: 'Amr ibn Qays al-Mala'i related to us, from Sa'id ibn Bashir, from Qatadah, who said: His wife, meaning Lut's wife, went to her people when she saw them, meaning when she saw the messengers, and said: "Some people have been Lut's guests tonight, the likes of whom I have never seen: more beautiful faces and sweeter smell!" They came rushing to him, but Lut hastened to hold them back at the door, [[In the printed edition: "yuzjahum" (push them); the correct reading is that of the manuscript and the History.]] and said: ﴿These are my daughters, if you are going to act﴾ [15:71]. They said: ﴿Have we not forbidden you from the people of the worlds?﴾ [15:70] [[An embedding of the verses of Surat al-Hijr, 15:70–71.]]. They entered upon the angels, who seized them, and their eyes were obliterated. They said: "O Lut, you have brought us people who are sorcerers who have bewitched us! Stay as you are until morning!" He said: Gabriel gathered up the four towns of Lut, a hundred thousand in each town, and lifted them on his wing between heaven and earth, until the people of the lowest heaven heard the sounds of their roosters. Then he overturned them, and God turned its upper part to its lower part. [[The report 18411: Abu Ja'far narrated it in his History, 1:155–156.]]

18412: Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, who said: Hudhayfah said: When they entered upon him, his old woman, the wicked old woman, went and told her people: "Some people have been Lut's guests tonight, and I have never seen people with more beautiful faces than them!" He said: They came rushing [[In the History: "they came rushing to him."]] and overtook him at Lut's [[In the printed edition: "Lut overtook them"; I have the manuscript reading, though I am uncertain about it, because Abu Ja'far did not narrate this sentence in his History, and I do not know why. I did not want to change it, because of the next report, which in the History combines both chains and gives this whole sentence in a different form.]] place. An angel stood and barred the door [meaning he sealed it shut], and Gabriel asked permission to punish them. It was granted, and Gabriel struck them with his wing, leaving them blind. They spent the night in the worst of nights. Then ﴿They said: "We are messengers of your Lord, so travel with your family in a part of the night, and let none of you look back, except your wife."﴾ He said: We were told that she heard a sound, turned around, and a stone struck her, while she was separated from the people, and her place was known. [[The report 18412: Abu Ja'far narrated it in his History, 1:156. He combined this chain with the one that follows, saying: "...Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us; and al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, all of them from Ma'mar..."]]

18413: al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to me, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, from Hudhayfah, similarly, except that he said: "Lut overtook them." [[The report 18413: See the previous note, although this sentence did not appear in the wording of his report in the History.]]

18414: Musa ibn Harun related to me, saying: 'Amr ibn Hammad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, who said: When Lut said: ﴿If only I had power over you, or could take refuge in a strong support﴾, then Gabriel, peace be upon him, spread his two wings, gouged out their eyes, and they went out, trampling one another in their backs, blind, saying: "Escape, escape! In the house of Lut are the greatest sorcerers on earth!" This is His words: ﴿They had sought to seduce him from his guests, so We obliterated their eyes﴾ [54:37]. They said to Lut: ﴿We are messengers of your Lord; they shall never reach you. So travel with your family in a part of the night, and let none of you look back, except your wife. Indeed, what strikes them will strike her﴾, and follow behind your family [[This is an embedding of verses from this surah and from Surat al-Hijr, 15:65.]], meaning: Drive them on, ﴿and go where you are commanded﴾ [15:65], so God brought them out toward Syria. Lut said: Destroy them now! They said: We were only commanded for the dawn. Is not the morning near? When the pre-dawn came, Lut went out with his family, with his wife, [[In the History: "and his family with him, except his wife."]] which is God's words: ﴿Except the family of Lut; We saved them at dawn﴾ [54:34]. [[The report 18414: Abu Ja'far narrated it in his History, 1:157, with differences I have mentioned above. He mentioned its full chain, not abridged, going back to Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn Mas'ud, and some companions of the Prophet (ﷺ). It is a chain that recurs in the exegesis, in its beginning, and Abu Ja'far later abridged it.]]

18415: al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Isma'il ibn 'Abd al-Karim related to us, from 'Abd al-Samad, that he heard Wahb ibn Munabbih say: The people of Sodom, among whom Lut lived, were a people who had dispensed with women in favor of men. When God saw that [[The words in parentheses are from the History.]], He sent the angels to punish them. They came to Abraham, and what happened between him and them is what God mentioned in His Book. When they gave Sarah the good news of a son, they stood up and Abraham stood with them, walking. He said: Tell me, why have you been sent, and what is your business? They said: We have been sent to Sodom to destroy it, for its people are an evil people who have dispensed with women in favor of men. Abraham said: [Do you see] if there are fifty righteous men among them? [[The words in parentheses are from the History.]] They said: Then we will not punish them! He kept reducing the number until he said: "A household?" [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "the household"; the correct reading is from the History.]] They said: If there is a righteous household in it! He said: What about Lut and his household? They said: His wife's desire is with them! When Abraham despaired, he turned back. They went to the people of Sodom and entered upon Lut. When his wife saw them, she admired their beauty and attractiveness, and she sent word to the people of the town: "Some people have come to us whose like has never been seen, neither more beautiful nor more attractive!" [[In the History: "a people..."]] They heard of this and surrounded Lut's house from every side, scaling the walls over them. [[In the History: "the walls"; in the manuscript: "the walls"; the reading in the History is correct.]] Lut met them and said: "O people, do not disgrace me regarding my guest. I will marry you to my daughters, for they are purer for you!" They said: If we wanted your daughters, we already know where they are! He said: ﴿If only I had power over you, or could take refuge in a strong support﴾! The messengers were displeased with him and said: "Your support is indeed strong, but a punishment that cannot be repelled is coming to them!" One of them wiped their eyes with his wings, obliterating their sight, and they said: "We have been bewitched! Let us go back and return to him!" So what happened to them was what God Most High related in the Qur'an. [[In the printed edition alone: "in writing"; the correct reading is "in the Qur'an."]] Michael, who is the one in charge of the punishment, put his wing beneath it until it reached the bottom of the earth. He overturned it, and stones came down from heaven, and they pursued those of them who were not in the town wherever they were, and God destroyed them and saved Lut and his family, except his wife. [[The report 18415: Abu Ja'far narrated it in his History, 1:156–157. See the note on number 18406.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 81 (part 2 of 2):

18416 – Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, and from Abu Bakr ibn Abd Allah [and] Abu Sufyan, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, from Hudhayfah, that some of their reports entered into one another. He said: Ibrahim (peace be upon him) used to come to them and say: "Woe to you! I forbid you from [provoking] Allah's punishment!" But they did not obey, until the Book reached its appointed term, for the place of their punishment and the Lord's seizures upon them. He said: The angels came to Lut, who was working on a piece of land of his, and he invited them to hospitality. They said: "Indeed, we are going to be your guests tonight!" Allah the Exalted had charged Jibril (peace be upon him) not to punish them until Lut bore three testimonies against them. So when Lut set out with them toward his home, he mentioned what his people did of evil and great calamities. He walked with them for a while, then turned to them and said: "Do you not know what the people of this town do? I know of no one on the face of the earth more evil than them! Where shall I take you? To my people, and they are the worst of Allah's creation!" [In the printed edition: "the worst of Allah's creation," and I have kept what is in the manuscript.] Jibril turned to the angels and said: "Remember this, one!" Then he walked for a while, and when he reached the middle of the town, and he pitied them and felt shame before them, he said: "Do you not know what the people of this town do? I know of no one on the face of the earth more evil than them. Indeed my people are the worst of Allah's creation!" Jibril turned to the angels and said: "Remember, these are two!" When he reached the door of the house, he wept out of shame before them and pity for them, and said: "Indeed my people are the worst of Allah's creation. Do you not know what the people of this town do? I know of no town on the face of the earth worse than them!" Jibril said to the angels: "Remember this, three! The punishment is now due!" When they entered, his wife, the evil old woman, went off, climbed up and waved her garment. The debauchers came running swiftly, and said: "What do you have?" She said: "Lut has hosted tonight people whose faces I have never seen more beautiful, nor more fragrant than them!" So they hurried, racing to the door, and Lut was overtaken at the door. They pushed against him for a long time, he being inside while they were outside, appealing to them by Allah and saying: ﴿These are my daughters; they are purer for you﴾. Then the angel rose and bolted the door, meaning he sealed it. Jibril asked permission to punish them, and Allah permitted him. He stood in the form in which he appears in heaven, spread his wing—Jibril has two wings—and he wore a sash of strung pearls. He had bright teeth and a clear forehead, and his hair was in curls like coral, [This is as in the printed edition, meaning "the curls of hair," which is the crisped, curled part of it; in the manuscript it reads "habl habl" undotted, as if "habl, habl," meaning that which is strung in pearls like a crown. Or it may be read "jathl, jathl," which is abundant, thick hair. And Allah knows best.] that is, pearls, like snow, and his feet were green-tinted. He said: "O Lut, ﴿indeed we are messengers of your Lord; they will never reach you﴾. Step aside from the door, O Lut, and leave them to me." [In the printed edition: "Go on, O Lut," differing from the manuscript, which is the pure correct reading. It is said: "māṭa 'an al-makan" and "amāṭa 'anhu," meaning to withdraw. In the hadith of Khaybar, he took the banner and shook it, and said: "Who will take it with its right?" Then so-and-so came, and he said: "I!" He said: "Amiṭ!" Then another came, and he said: "Amiṭ"—meaning: withdraw and go away.] So Lut stepped aside from the door, and he came out upon them, spread his wing and struck their faces with a blow that blinded their eyes [as in both the printed and manuscript editions: "shadakh a'yunahum," which seems derived from "shadakhat al-ghurrah," when a blaze on a horse's face extends from the root of the forelock to the nose. Otherwise I do not know what it means]. They became blind, not knowing the way nor finding their way to their homes. Then he ordered Lut to set out with his family during that night. He said: ﴿So travel with your family in a part of the night﴾.

18417 – Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: When Lut said to his people: ﴿If only I had strength against you, or could take refuge in a firm support﴾, and the messengers heard what he said and what was said to him, and saw the distress he was in because of it. When they saw what had reached him, they said: ﴿O Lut, indeed we are messengers of your Lord; they will never reach you﴾, that is, with anything you dislike. ﴿So travel with your family in a part of the night, and let none of you turn back, except your wife; indeed, what strikes them will strike her. Indeed, their appointed time is the morning. Is not the morning near?﴾, that is, the punishment will descend upon them at the dawn of this very night, so proceed as you are commanded.

18418 – ... He said: Salama narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, that he related: that the messengers at that moment slapped the faces of those from his people who came to Lut seeking to solicit his guests, [Safa'a wajhahu bi-yadihi safa'an: he struck it with his open palm.] and they returned blind. He said: Allah says: ﴿And they had sought to solicit him for his guests, so We obliterated their eyes﴾ [Surat al-Qamar: 37].

18419 – Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿in a part of the night﴾, he said: in a portion of the night.

18420 – Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada: ﴿in a part of the night﴾, in a portion of the night.

18421 – Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn Abbas said regarding His words: ﴿in a part of the night﴾, he said: the middle of the night. And His words: ﴿and follow behind them﴾, meaning: follow behind your family. ﴿And let none of you turn back﴾ [This report is from the tafsir of a verse in Surat al-Hijr: 65, and he did not mention it there.] [Surat al-Hijr: 65].

Mujahid used to say concerning this:

18422 – Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿and let none of you turn back﴾, he said: no one looks behind him. ﴿Except your wife﴾.

* *

It is related from Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud that he used to recite: ﴿So travel with your family in a part of the night, except your wife﴾.

* *

18423 – Ahmad ibn Yusuf narrated to me of that, saying: al-Qasim ibn Sallam narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Harun, who said regarding the reading of Ibn Mas'ud: ﴿So travel with your family in a part of the night, except your wife﴾.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: This indicates the soundness of the reading with the accusative (naṣb).

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 11, verses 82–83 (part 1 of 2):

The discussion of the interpretation (ta'wil) of His saying: ﴿So when Our command came, We made its highest part its lowest and rained upon it stones of hardened clay, layered, (82) marked from your Lord. And they are not far from the wrongdoers.(83)﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: When Our command came, meaning Our punishment, and Our decree against them of destruction, ﴿We made its highest part﴾, meaning the highest part of their town, ﴿its lowest﴾. ﴿And We rained upon it﴾, He says: and We sent upon it ﴿stones of sijjil﴾.

* *

The interpreters differed about the meaning of "sijjil".

Some of them said: It is Persian: sang and gil. (See what preceded at 1:14, note 2, then p. 20.)

Those who said this:

18424: Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿of sijjil﴾: In Persian, its first part is "hajar" (stone) and its last part is "tin" (clay).

18425: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, with something similar.

18426: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abdullah narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, with something similar.

18427: Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, similar.

18428: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Ya'qub narrated to us, from Ja'far, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr regarding ﴿stones of sijjil﴾, he said: It is Persian, Arabized as sang and gil.

18429: Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: "al-sijjil" is clay.

18430: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada and Ikrima regarding ﴿of sijjil﴾: they both said: of clay.

18431: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Abd al-Karim narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Samad narrated to me, from Wahb, who said: Sijjil in Persian is sang and gil.

18432: Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi regarding ﴿stones of sijjil﴾: As for sijjil, Ibn Abbas said: It is Persian: sang and jul. "Sang" is the stone, and "jul" is the clay. He means: We sent upon them stones of clay.

18433: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Suddi, from Ikrima, from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿stones of sijjil﴾, he said: Clay within stones.

* *

Ibn Zayd said regarding this:

18434: Yunus narrated this to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying ﴿stones of sijjil﴾: It is the lowest heaven. He said: The lowest heaven is named sijjil, and it is what God sent down upon the people of Lut.

* *

Some of the scholars of Arabic speech among the Basrans used to say: "Sijjil" is from hard, strong stones, and from striking, and he cites as evidence the words of the poet: [He is Tamim ibn Abi Muqbil.]

A striking that the champions enjoined with sijjil [Majaz al-Qur'an 1:296, Muntaha al-Talab: 44, al-Ma'ani al-Kabir: 991, Lisan (s-j-n), and others. Before it he says: "And among us is an early-morning drinking if you seek it, a gathering, splendid, of eighty thousand..." and "a company who strike the helmets at the sides, a striking that the champions enjoined with sijjin."]

And he said: Some of them change the lam into a nun. [He means by his saying "some of them", that some Arabs change the lam into a nun, as the saying of al-Nabigha: "With every armoured one like a lion, rising above the joints of a trailing one of Rafin," meaning rafl. This is the end of Abu Ubayda's words in Majaz al-Qur'an; I have quoted it for clarification. And the lineage of Quraysh: 90.]

* *

Another of them said: It is "fi'il" from the speaker's saying "asjaltuhu", I sent him. So it is as if it is from that, meaning sent upon them.

* *

Another of them said: Rather, it is from "sajjaltu lahu sajlan" (I gave him a bucket) from giving, so it is as if it was said: That affliction was given to them, and they were given it. And they say "asjalahu": he neglected him.

* *

Some of them said: It is from "al-sijill", because there was in it a mark like a writing.

* *

Another of them said: Rather, it is clay that is fired as bricks are fired, and he recites the verse of al-Fadl ibn al-Abbas:

"Whoever competes with me in drawing water will compete with a noble man who fills the bucket up to the knot of the rope."

[The Poets' Dictionary: 309, and Lisan (s-j-l), and others; before it: "And I am the dark-skinned one, whom people know, dark of skin in the house of the Arabs. Whoever competes with me... Indeed, Abd Manaf is a jewel, and Abd al-Muttalib adorned the jewel." He is al-Fadl ibn al-Abbas ibn Utba ibn Abi Lahab ibn Abd al-Muttalib, and his mother was Amina bint al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib. Al-Fadl was very dark-skinned and extremely swarthy, and for that reason he said "And I am the dark-skinned one". "Khudra" (greenness) among people's complexions means intense tan, and the Arabs describe their complexions as black, while they describe the non-Arabs as red. "Karb" is the rope tied around the bucket.]

So this is from "sajjaltu lahu sajlan", I gave him.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this, in our opinion, is what the commentators said, namely that they are stones of clay, and God described them that way in His Book in one place, and that is His saying: ﴿That We may send upon them stones of clay, marked at your Lord for the transgressors﴾ [Surah al-Dhariyat: 33, 34].

* *

It has been related from Sa'id ibn Jubayr that he used to say: It is Persian and Nabatean.

18435: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: Persian and Nabatean: "sajj" and "il".

* *

Sa'id ibn Jubayr went in this to the view that the Persian name of clay is "jil", not "il", and that if it were Persian it would be "sijl" not "sijjil", because stone in Persian is called "sajj" and clay is "jil", so there is no basis for the yā' being in it while it is Persian.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: We have already explained the correct view on this at the beginning of the book, in a way that makes repeating it here unnecessary. [See what preceded at 1:13–20.]

* *

It has been mentioned from al-Hasan al-Basri that he said: The origin of the stones was clay, and it was made hard.

* *

As for His saying ﴿layered﴾, Qatada and Ikrima say regarding it:

18436: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada and Ikrima: ﴿layered﴾, he says: arranged in rows.

18437: Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: ﴿layered﴾, he says: arranged in rows.

* *

Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said regarding it:

18438: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, regarding His saying ﴿layered﴾, he said: Some of it was layered upon some.

18439: Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Abu Bakr al-Hudhali ibn Abdullah: As for His saying ﴿layered﴾, they are layered in the heaven: prepared, and they are part of God's equipment that He prepared for the wrongdoers.

* *

Some of them said: "Layered" means that they follow one another upon them. He said: That is its layering.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this is what al-Rabi' ibn Anas said, because His saying ﴿layered﴾ is an attribute of "sijjil", not of "stones". God rained upon the people stones of clay, the attribute of that clay being that it was layered upon one another, and then it was made into stones; they were not rained with clay, so that it would be described as following upon the people by its coming.

Abu Ja'far said: It would have been permissible for it to be as this interpreter interprets only if the revelation had been in the accusative "manduda(tan)", which would then be an attribute of "stones".

* *

As for His saying ﴿marked at your Lord﴾, He says: marked by God, God marked them. [See the explanation of "al-musawwama" in what preceded: 6:251–257 / 7:184–190.] "Al-musawwama" is an attribute of "stones", and for that reason it was put in the accusative as an attribute. [In the printed edition: "nasabat wa nu'ita bihā", and in the manuscript: "nasabat wa in'ita", and it seems the correct reading is what I have confirmed.]

* *

The interpreters said something similar to what we have said on this.

Those who said this:

18442: ... narrated to us, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similar.

18444: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada and Ikrima: ﴿marked﴾, they both said: encircled with it, with a trace of red. 18446: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', regarding His saying ﴿marked﴾, he said: On them is a mark of lines.

As for His saying ﴿And they are not far from the wrongdoers﴾, He, exalted is His remembrance, says, threatening the polytheists of Quraysh: And these stones which I rained upon the people of Lut are not far, O Muhammad, from the polytheists of your people, that they may be rained upon, if they do not repent of their polytheism.

* *

The interpreters said something similar to what we have said on this.

* *

The heart of the angels was: "its highest part, the lowest part of the land of Sodom," as:

18458: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Jabir ibn Nuh narrated to us, saying: Al-A'mash narrated to us, from Mujahid, who said: Jibril, peace be upon him, seized the people of Lut from their pasture and their homes; he carried them with their livestock and their goods until the people of the heaven heard the barking of their dogs, then he overturned them. [Report 18458: Abu Ja'far related it in his History 1:157.]

18459: Abu Kurayb narrated it to me again, from Mujahid, who said: Jibril inserted his wing beneath the lowest earth of the people of Lut, then he seized them with the right wing, taking them from their pasture and their livestock, then he lifted them. [Report 18459: Abu Ja'far related it in his History 1:157.]

18460: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who used to say: ﴿So when Our command came, We made its highest part its lowest﴾, he said: When they awoke in the morning, Jibril came to their town, uprooted it from its corners, then inserted his wing, then carried it upon the long feathers of his wing. [Report 18460: Abu Ja'far related it in his History 1:157.]

18461: ... narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, saying: This Ibn Abi Najih narrated to me, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Bakr = he said: Ibn Abi Najih did not hear it = from Mujahid, who said: Then he carried it upon the long feathers of his wing with what was in it, then he ascended with it to the heaven until the people of the heaven heard the barking of their dogs, then he overturned it. [In the printed edition: "sharafuha", and in the manuscript and the History "sharafuha", as if it were the plural of "sharif", like "saghir" and "saghar", "kabir" and "kibar", and it seems its correct form is "ashrafuha", because "sharaf" is not mentioned among the plurals of "sharif"; but I fear it may be "shadhdhanuha" as will come in no. 18463, note 6.] Then that is God's saying: ﴿We made its highest part its lowest and rained upon it stones of sijjil﴾. [Report 18461: Abu Ja'far related it in his History 1:157, abridged, omitting Mujahid's other statement.]

18462: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, who said: We have been told that Jibril, peace be upon him, took hold of the central handle of the town, then tossed it up to the heaven, [It is said: "al-uqab tossed him", meaning it seized him and flew off with him.] until the people of the heaven heard the barking of their dogs, [The barking of dogs: plural of "dhaghiya", meaning the one which has "dhugha'", which is the sound of the humiliated and defeated when seeking help.] then he crushed some of it upon some, making its highest its lowest, then he sent the stones after them. Qatada said: And we have been told that they were four thousand thousand. [Report 18462: Abu Ja'far related it in his History 1:157.]

18463: Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, who said: We have been told that Jibril, peace be upon him, took hold of its central handle, then tossed it up to the air of the heaven until the angels heard the barking of their dogs, then he crushed some of it upon some, then he followed the scattered ones of the people with stones. [The "shudhdhan" is the plural of "shadhdh", which means one who has left the group and become separated from it.] He said: They are three towns called "Sodom", and they are between Medina and Syria. He said: We have been told that there were four thousand thousand in it. We have been told that Ibrahim, peace be upon him, used to look out [then] and say: Sodom, a day of your destruction! [The addition [then] is from al-Tabari's History. In the History: "Sodom, a day of destruction," and I fear the correct version is what is in the commentary, and that the other is an error.] [Report 18463: Abu Ja'far related it in his History 1:157.]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 82–83 (part 2 of 2):

18464 - Musa related to me, saying: 'Amr related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, who said: When it was morning, = meaning the people of Lut = Jibril descended, and uprooted the earth from the seven earths, and carried it until he reached the lowest heaven [until the people of the heavens heard the barking of their dogs and the crowing of their roosters; then he overturned it and destroyed them]. [[The text between the brackets is an addition that is necessary from the context of the discourse; I have transcribed it from the text of the report in Tarikh al-Tabari.]] This is what is meant by Allah's words: ﴿And the overturned cities He hurled down﴾ [Surah al-Najm: 53], the overturned ones, when Jibril tipped the earth over, uprooting it with his wing. Whoever among them did not die when the earth was dropped, Allah rained down stones upon him while he was beneath the earth, and whoever among them was far off in the land. This is the saying of Allah: ﴿So We made its highest part its lowest and rained down upon them stones of hard clay﴾. Then He pursued them in the towns, so a man [would be speaking], and a stone would come to him and kill him, [[In the printed and manuscript editions: "so a man would come to him"; I have adopted the text from the History.]] and this is the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And We rained upon it stones of hard clay﴾. [[The report 18464: narrated by Abu Ja'far in his History, 1:157, 158.]]

18465 - al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Abu Bakr = and Abu Sufyan, from Ma'mar =, from Qatadah, who said: It has reached us that when Jibril, peace be upon him, became morning, he spread his wing, and with it he uprooted their land along with what was in it of their palaces, their animals, their stones, their trees, and everything that was in it. He gathered it into his wing, enfolded it and folded it within the hollow of his wing, then ascended with it to the lowest heaven, until the inhabitants of the heaven heard the voices of the people and the dogs, and they numbered four thousand thousand. Then he overturned it and sent it down to the earth upside down, so some of it crushed others, and He made its highest part its lowest, then He sent after them stones of hard clay.

18466 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq related to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi related to me, saying: It was related to me that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah sent Jibril, peace be upon him, to the overturned town, the town of Lut, peace be upon him, in which Lut lived. He lifted it with his wing, then ascended with it until the people of the lowest heaven heard the barking of its dogs and the voices of its hens. Then he turned it over onto its face, then Allah sent stones after it. Allah says: ﴿We made its highest part its lowest and rained down upon it stones of hard clay﴾. So Allah destroyed it and what was around it of the overturned towns, and they were five towns: "Sun'a", "Sa'wa", "Ghathra", "Duma" and "Sadum" = and Sadum was the greatest town = and Allah saved Lut and those with him of his family, except his wife, who was among those who perished.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 11, verses 82–83 (part 1 of 2):

The discussion of the interpretation (ta'wil) of His saying: ﴿So when Our command came, We made its highest part its lowest and rained upon it stones of hardened clay, layered, (82) marked from your Lord. And they are not far from the wrongdoers.(83)﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: When Our command came, meaning Our punishment, and Our decree against them of destruction, ﴿We made its highest part﴾, meaning the highest part of their town, ﴿its lowest﴾. ﴿And We rained upon it﴾, He says: and We sent upon it ﴿stones of sijjil﴾.

* *

The interpreters differed about the meaning of "sijjil".

Some of them said: It is Persian: sang and gil. (See what preceded at 1:14, note 2, then p. 20.)

Those who said this:

18424: Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿of sijjil﴾: In Persian, its first part is "hajar" (stone) and its last part is "tin" (clay).

18425: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, with something similar.

18426: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abdullah narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, with something similar.

18427: Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, similar.

18428: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Ya'qub narrated to us, from Ja'far, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr regarding ﴿stones of sijjil﴾, he said: It is Persian, Arabized as sang and gil.

18429: Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: "al-sijjil" is clay.

18430: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada and Ikrima regarding ﴿of sijjil﴾: they both said: of clay.

18431: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Abd al-Karim narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Samad narrated to me, from Wahb, who said: Sijjil in Persian is sang and gil.

18432: Musa ibn Harun narrated to me, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi regarding ﴿stones of sijjil﴾: As for sijjil, Ibn Abbas said: It is Persian: sang and jul. "Sang" is the stone, and "jul" is the clay. He means: We sent upon them stones of clay.

18433: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Suddi, from Ikrima, from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿stones of sijjil﴾, he said: Clay within stones.

* *

Ibn Zayd said regarding this:

18434: Yunus narrated this to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying ﴿stones of sijjil﴾: It is the lowest heaven. He said: The lowest heaven is named sijjil, and it is what God sent down upon the people of Lut.

* *

Some of the scholars of Arabic speech among the Basrans used to say: "Sijjil" is from hard, strong stones, and from striking, and he cites as evidence the words of the poet: [He is Tamim ibn Abi Muqbil.]

A striking that the champions enjoined with sijjil [Majaz al-Qur'an 1:296, Muntaha al-Talab: 44, al-Ma'ani al-Kabir: 991, Lisan (s-j-n), and others. Before it he says: "And among us is an early-morning drinking if you seek it, a gathering, splendid, of eighty thousand..." and "a company who strike the helmets at the sides, a striking that the champions enjoined with sijjin."]

And he said: Some of them change the lam into a nun. [He means by his saying "some of them", that some Arabs change the lam into a nun, as the saying of al-Nabigha: "With every armoured one like a lion, rising above the joints of a trailing one of Rafin," meaning rafl. This is the end of Abu Ubayda's words in Majaz al-Qur'an; I have quoted it for clarification. And the lineage of Quraysh: 90.]

* *

Another of them said: It is "fi'il" from the speaker's saying "asjaltuhu", I sent him. So it is as if it is from that, meaning sent upon them.

* *

Another of them said: Rather, it is from "sajjaltu lahu sajlan" (I gave him a bucket) from giving, so it is as if it was said: That affliction was given to them, and they were given it. And they say "asjalahu": he neglected him.

* *

Some of them said: It is from "al-sijill", because there was in it a mark like a writing.

* *

Another of them said: Rather, it is clay that is fired as bricks are fired, and he recites the verse of al-Fadl ibn al-Abbas:

"Whoever competes with me in drawing water will compete with a noble man who fills the bucket up to the knot of the rope."

[The Poets' Dictionary: 309, and Lisan (s-j-l), and others; before it: "And I am the dark-skinned one, whom people know, dark of skin in the house of the Arabs. Whoever competes with me... Indeed, Abd Manaf is a jewel, and Abd al-Muttalib adorned the jewel." He is al-Fadl ibn al-Abbas ibn Utba ibn Abi Lahab ibn Abd al-Muttalib, and his mother was Amina bint al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib. Al-Fadl was very dark-skinned and extremely swarthy, and for that reason he said "And I am the dark-skinned one". "Khudra" (greenness) among people's complexions means intense tan, and the Arabs describe their complexions as black, while they describe the non-Arabs as red. "Karb" is the rope tied around the bucket.]

So this is from "sajjaltu lahu sajlan", I gave him.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this, in our opinion, is what the commentators said, namely that they are stones of clay, and God described them that way in His Book in one place, and that is His saying: ﴿That We may send upon them stones of clay, marked at your Lord for the transgressors﴾ [Surah al-Dhariyat: 33, 34].

* *

It has been related from Sa'id ibn Jubayr that he used to say: It is Persian and Nabatean.

18435: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: Persian and Nabatean: "sajj" and "il".

* *

Sa'id ibn Jubayr went in this to the view that the Persian name of clay is "jil", not "il", and that if it were Persian it would be "sijl" not "sijjil", because stone in Persian is called "sajj" and clay is "jil", so there is no basis for the yā' being in it while it is Persian.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: We have already explained the correct view on this at the beginning of the book, in a way that makes repeating it here unnecessary. [See what preceded at 1:13–20.]

* *

It has been mentioned from al-Hasan al-Basri that he said: The origin of the stones was clay, and it was made hard.

* *

As for His saying ﴿layered﴾, Qatada and Ikrima say regarding it:

18436: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada and Ikrima: ﴿layered﴾, he says: arranged in rows.

18437: Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: ﴿layered﴾, he says: arranged in rows.

* *

Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said regarding it:

18439: Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Abu Bakr al-Hudhali ibn Abdullah: As for His saying ﴿layered﴾, they are layered in the heaven: prepared, and they are part of God's equipment that He prepared for the wrongdoers.

* *

Some of them said: "Layered" means that they follow one another upon them. He said: That is its layering.
