18450: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abdullah narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similar.

18451: ... narrated to us, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similar.

18452: Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, similar.

18453: Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: ﴿And they are not far from the wrongdoers﴾, he says: God has not spared any wrongdoer from it after the people of Lut.

18454: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada and Ikrima: ﴿And they are not far from the wrongdoers﴾, he says: He has not left any wrongdoer from it after them. [In the printed edition: "lam yubra' minha zalim", and in the manuscript: "yabra minha zalima", and I saw its reading as I have confirmed.]

18455: Ali ibn Sahl narrated to us, saying: Damra ibn Rabi'a narrated to us, from Ibn Shu'dhub, from Qatada regarding His saying ﴿And they are not far from the wrongdoers﴾, he said: He means the wrongdoers of this nation. He said: By God, He has not spared any wrongdoer from it since!

18456: Musa ibn Harun narrated to us, saying: Hammad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿And they are not far from the wrongdoers﴾, he says: from the oppressors of the Arabs, if they do not repent, they will be punished by them.

18457: Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Abu Bakr al-Hudhali ibn Abdullah, who said: He says: ﴿And they are not far from the wrongdoers﴾, from the oppressors of your nation, is not far, so no wrongdoer among them will feel safe from it.

* *

The heart of the angels was: "its highest part, the lowest part of the land of Sodom," as:

18458: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Jabir ibn Nuh narrated to us, saying: Al-A'mash narrated to us, from Mujahid, who said: Jibril, peace be upon him, seized the people of Lut from their pasture and their homes; he carried them with their livestock and their goods until the people of the heaven heard the barking of their dogs, then he overturned them. [Report 18458: Abu Ja'far related it in his History 1:157.]

18459: Abu Kurayb narrated it to me again, from Mujahid, who said: Jibril inserted his wing beneath the lowest earth of the people of Lut, then he seized them with the right wing, taking them from their pasture and their livestock, then he lifted them. [Report 18459: Abu Ja'far related it in his History 1:157.]

18460: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who used to say: ﴿So when Our command came, We made its highest part its lowest﴾, he said: When they awoke in the morning, Jibril came to their town, uprooted it from its corners, then inserted his wing, then carried it upon the long feathers of his wing. [Report 18460: Abu Ja'far related it in his History 1:157.]

18461: ... narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, saying: This Ibn Abi Najih narrated to me, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Bakr = he said: Ibn Abi Najih did not hear it = from Mujahid, who said: Then he carried it upon the long feathers of his wing with what was in it, then he ascended with it to the heaven until the people of the heaven heard the barking of their dogs, then he overturned it. The first thing that fell from it were its sharaf (noble parts). [In the printed edition: "sharafuha", and in the manuscript and the History "sharafuha", as if it were the plural of "sharif", like "saghir" and "saghar", "kabir" and "kibar", and it seems its correct form is "ashrafuha", because "sharaf" is not mentioned among the plurals of "sharif"; but I fear it may be "shadhdhanuha" as will come in no. 18463, note 6.] Then that is God's saying: ﴿We made its highest part its lowest and rained upon it stones of sijjil﴾. Mujahid said: Thus it did not befall any people what befell them; God blinded their eyes, then overturned their town, and rained upon them stones of sijjil. [Report 18461: Abu Ja'far related it in his History 1:157, abridged, omitting Mujahid's other statement.]

18462: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, who said: We have been told that Jibril, peace be upon him, took hold of the central handle of the town, then tossed it up to the heaven, [It is said: "al-uqab tossed him", meaning it seized him and flew off with him.] until the people of the heaven heard the barking of their dogs, [The barking of dogs: plural of "dhaghiya", meaning the one which has "dhugha'", which is the sound of the humiliated and defeated when seeking help.] then he crushed some of it upon some, making its highest its lowest, then he sent the stones after them. Qatada said: And we have been told that they were four thousand thousand. [Report 18462: Abu Ja'far related it in his History 1:157.]

18463: Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, who said: We have been told that Jibril, peace be upon him, took hold of its central handle, then tossed it up to the air of the heaven until the angels heard the barking of their dogs, then he crushed some of it upon some, then he followed the scattered ones of the people with stones. [The "shudhdhan" is the plural of "shadhdh", which means one who has left the group and become separated from it.] He said: They are three towns called "Sodom", and they are between Medina and Syria. He said: We have been told that there were four thousand thousand in it. We have been told that Ibrahim, peace be upon him, used to look out [then] and say: Sodom, a day of your destruction! [The addition [then] is from al-Tabari's History. In the History: "Sodom, a day of destruction," and I fear the correct version is what is in the commentary, and that the other is an error.] [Report 18463: Abu Ja'far related it in his History 1:157.]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 82–83 (part 2 of 2):

18464 - Musa related to me, saying: 'Amr related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, who said: When it was morning, = meaning the people of Lut = Jibril descended, and uprooted the earth from the seven earths, and carried it until he reached the lowest heaven [until the people of the heavens heard the barking of their dogs and the crowing of their roosters; then he overturned it and destroyed them]. [[The text between the brackets is an addition that is necessary from the context of the discourse; I have transcribed it from the text of the report in Tarikh al-Tabari.]] This is what is meant by Allah's words: ﴿And the overturned cities He hurled down﴾ [Surah al-Najm: 53], the overturned ones, when Jibril tipped the earth over, uprooting it with his wing. Whoever among them did not die when the earth was dropped, Allah rained down stones upon him while he was beneath the earth, and whoever among them was far off in the land. This is the saying of Allah: ﴿So We made its highest part its lowest and rained down upon them stones of hard clay﴾. Then He pursued them in the towns, so a man [would be speaking], and a stone would come to him and kill him, [[In the printed and manuscript editions: "so a man would come to him"; I have adopted the text from the History.]] and this is the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And We rained upon it stones of hard clay﴾. [[The report 18464: narrated by Abu Ja'far in his History, 1:157, 158.]]

18465 - al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Abu Bakr = and Abu Sufyan, from Ma'mar =, from Qatadah, who said: It has reached us that when Jibril, peace be upon him, became morning, he spread his wing, and with it he uprooted their land along with what was in it of their palaces, their animals, their stones, their trees, and everything that was in it. He gathered it into his wing, enfolded it and folded it within the hollow of his wing, then ascended with it to the lowest heaven, until the inhabitants of the heaven heard the voices of the people and the dogs, and they numbered four thousand thousand. Then he overturned it and sent it down to the earth upside down, so some of it crushed others, and He made its highest part its lowest, then He sent after them stones of hard clay.

18466 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq related to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi related to me, saying: It was related to me that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah sent Jibril, peace be upon him, to the overturned town, the town of Lut, peace be upon him, in which Lut lived. He lifted it with his wing, then ascended with it until the people of the lowest heaven heard the barking of its dogs and the voices of its hens. Then he turned it over onto its face, then Allah sent stones after it. Allah says: ﴿We made its highest part its lowest and rained down upon it stones of hard clay﴾. So Allah destroyed it and what was around it of the overturned towns, and they were five towns: "Sun'a", "Sa'wa", "Ghathra", "Duma" and "Sadum" = and Sadum was the greatest town = and Allah saved Lut and those with him of his family, except his wife, who was among those who perished.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 84:

On the interpretation of His words, may He be exalted: ﴿And to Midian [We sent] their brother Shu'ayb. He said, "O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. And do not diminish from the measure and the scale. Indeed, I see you in prosperity, and indeed, I fear for you the punishment of an all-encompassing Day."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: May His remembrance be exalted, He says: We sent to the descendants of Midian their brother Shu'ayb, and when he came to them he said: ﴿O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him﴾, meaning: obey Him, and humble yourselves to Him in obedience to what He has commanded you and forbidden you. ﴿You have no deity other than Him﴾, meaning: you have no object of worship besides Him who deserves worship from you. ﴿And do not diminish the measure and the scale﴾, meaning: do not diminish people's rights in your measure and your scale. ﴿Indeed, I see you in prosperity﴾.

* *

The interpreters differed concerning the "prosperity" (khayr) by which Allah informed that Shu'ayb told Midian that he saw them in it.

Some of them said: It was cheapness of prices, and he warned them of their high prices.

Those who said this:

18467. Zakariyya ibn Yahya ibn Abi Za'ida told me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Dawud al-Wasiti told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Musa told us, from al-Dhayyal ibn 'Amr, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Indeed, I see you in prosperity﴾, he said: cheapness of prices. ﴿And indeed, I fear for you the punishment of an all-encompassing Day﴾, he said: high prices. [[The report: "al-Dhayyal ibn 'Amr" appears here with a dhal marked with a dot, and it has already passed at no. 14445, with my comment on it and the comment of my brother al-Sayyid Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, in vol. 12: 589, no. 7, as "al-Zaba' ibn 'Amr." In Ibn Kathir it is "al-Dayyal" with an undotted dal. We have not been able to determine who this is. The chain here is the same chain as there.]]

18468. Ahmad ibn 'Amr al-Basri told me, saying: 'Abd al-Samad ibn 'Abd al-Warith told me, saying: Salih ibn Rustum told us, from al-Hasan, and he mentioned the people of Shu'ayb, and said: ﴿Indeed, I see you in prosperity﴾, he said: cheapness of prices. [[The report: "Ahmad ibn 'Amr al-Basri": a teacher of al-Tabari, passed at no. 9875 and 13928, and what I said about him has passed. Al-Tabari transmitted from him in his History, 1: 182 / 5: 32. In the printed edition here it was "Ahmad ibn 'Ali al-Nasri," and I do not know where this change came from.]]

18469. Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn 'Ali told me, saying: 'Abd al-Samad ibn 'Abd al-Warith told us, from Abu 'Amir al-Kharraz, from al-Hasan regarding His words: ﴿Indeed, I see you in prosperity﴾, he said: wealth and cheapness of prices.

* *

Others said: He meant by that: "Indeed, I see for you wealth and adornment of the adornments of this world."

Those who said this:

18470. al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada regarding His words: ﴿Indeed, I see you in prosperity﴾, he said: He means the good of this world and its adornment.

18471. Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatada regarding His words: ﴿Indeed, I see you in prosperity﴾, he saw upon them a husk (qishr) of the husks of this world and its adornment. [[The "qishr" is originally the bark of a tree and the like, then it was borrowed for garments and all clothing that is taken off as bark is peeled, then it was borrowed for what we wear of the adornment of life and then take off, content or unwilling.]]

18472. Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: ﴿Indeed, I see you in prosperity﴾, he said: in your worldly life, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿If he leaves behind wealth (khayr)﴾. He called it "khayr" because people call wealth "khayr."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these sayings is what Allah has informed us Shu'ayb said to his people, and that is His words: ﴿Indeed, I see you in prosperity﴾, meaning, the prosperity of this world. The prosperity of this world may include wealth, the adornment of the worldly life, and cheapness of prices. There is no indication that by his saying he meant some of the worldly goods to the exclusion of others, so it applies to all the meanings of worldly goods which the scholars mentioned they had been given.

* *

Shu'ayb said this only because his people were in ease of living and cheapness of their prices, abundant in their wealth. So he said to them: Do not diminish people's rights in your measures and your weights, for Allah has widened your provision. ﴿And indeed, I fear for you﴾, because of your opposition to the command of Allah, and your depriving people of their wealth in your measures and your weights, ﴿the punishment of an all-encompassing Day﴾, meaning: that there descend upon you the punishment of a Day whose punishment encompasses you. He made "all-encompassing" (muhit) an attribute of the Day, though it is an attribute of the "punishment," since its meaning is understood and the punishment was on the Day, so it is like their saying: "Part of your robe is burned." [[See the explanation of "muhit" previously at 15: 93, comment 1, and the references there.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 85:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And O my people, give full measure and weight in justice, and do not deprive the people of their due, and do not commit corruption on the earth, causing corruption﴾ [Q 11:85].

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is His remembrance, relating the statement of Shu'ayb to his people: Give people full measure and weight [[See "Giving full measure and weight" in what has passed before, 12:224, 555.]] "in justice," meaning: with fairness, that is, by giving those who are owed things measured or weighed their rights in full, as is due to them, without diminishing or cheating. [[See the explanation of "justice" in what has passed before, 15:103, note 3, and the references there.]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and do not deprive the people of their due﴾, it means: do not diminish the people's rights, which you are obligated to render to them by measure, weight, or otherwise, [[See the explanation of "bakhs" (deprivation) in what has passed before, p. 262, note 4, and the references there.]] as related:

18473. Al-Harith related to me, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz related to us, saying: 'Ali ibn Salih ibn Hayy related to us, saying: It reached me regarding His saying: ﴿and do not deprive the people of their due﴾, he said: Do not diminish them.

18474. Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and do not deprive the people of their due﴾, he said: Do not wrong the people in their due.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and do not commit corruption on the earth, causing corruption﴾, it means: do not travel the earth doing acts of disobedience to God there, [[See the explanation of "ath'a" (commit corruption) in what has passed before, 12:542, note 1, and the references there. = And the explanation of "corruption on the earth," 12:542, note 1, and the references there.]] as related:

18475. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿and do not commit corruption on the earth, causing corruption﴾, he said: Do not travel the earth.

18476. And it was related to me from al-Musayyab, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, regarding His saying: ﴿and do not commit corruption on the earth, causing corruption﴾, he said: Do not strive on the earth causing corruption, meaning: the deficiency of measure and weight.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 86:

The exposition of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿What Allah leaves for you is better for you, if you are believers. And I am not a guardian over you﴾ (11:86)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By His, the Exalted's, words ﴿What Allah leaves for you is better for you﴾, He means: what Allah has left for you, after you give people their rights in measure and weight with justice, He has made lawful for you, is better for you than what remains for you by your diminishing people's rights in measure and weight. ﴿If you are believers﴾ means: if you are those who affirm the promise and threat of Allah, and His lawful and unlawful.

* *

This is an opinion transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas through a chain that the transmitters do not accept as sound.

* *

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have differed regarding this.

Some of them said its meaning is: obedience to Allah is better for you.

Those who said this:

18477 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us; and Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Layth, from Mujahid: ﴿What Allah leaves for you is better for you﴾, he said: obedience to Allah is better for you.

18478 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from 'Anbasa, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, from Mujahid: ﴿What Allah leaves﴾, he said: the obedience of Allah ﴿is better for you﴾.

18479 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿What Allah leaves﴾, he said: the obedience of Allah.

18480 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from Layth, from Mujahid: ﴿What Allah leaves for you is better for you﴾, he said: obedience to Allah is better for you.

18481 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿What Allah leaves for you is better for you﴾, he said: obedience to Allah.

18482 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, similarly.

* *

Others said: the meaning of that is: your portion from your Lord is better for you.

Those who said this:

18483 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada regarding his words: ﴿What Allah leaves for you is better for you, if you are believers﴾, your portion from your Lord is better for you.

18484 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada regarding His words: ﴿What Allah leaves for you is better for you﴾, he said: your portion from Allah is better for you.

* *

Others said: its meaning is: the provision of Allah is better for you.

Those who said this:

18485 - al-Harith narrated to me, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from one he mentioned, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Baqiyyat Allah﴾, he said: the provision of Allah.

* *

Ibn Zayd said regarding His words:

18486 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: ﴿What Allah leaves for you is better for you, if you are believers﴾, he said: "The destruction" is in punishment, and "what is left" is in mercy.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: I chose the view I have chosen in interpreting this because Allah, the Exalted, only preceded to them with the prohibition against diminishing people's things in measure and weight, and Shu'ayb called them to abandon cheating in measure and diminishing in weight. Therefore, following that with news of what portion they have in fulfilling (obligations) in this world and the Hereafter is more fitting, along with the fact that His words ﴿baqiyya﴾ are a verbal noun from the speaker's saying "baqiyt baqiyya min kadha" (I remained a remnant of such-and-such). So there is no way to direct the meaning of that except to: the remnant of Allah which He has left for you, from what is yours after you fulfil people's rights, is better for you than the remnant of unlawful gain which remains for you from your wronging people by diminishing for them in measure and weight.

* *

As for His words ﴿And I am not a guardian over you﴾, He says: and I am not over you, O people, a watcher who observes you at your measuring and weighing, whether you give people their rights or wrong them? [[See the explanation of "ḥafīẓ" above, p. 365, note 3, and the references there.]] Rather, it is incumbent upon me only to convey to you the message of my Lord, and I have conveyed it to you.

**The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted Is He:** ﴿They said, "O Shu'ayb, does your prayer command you that we leave what our fathers worshipped, or that we stop doing what we like with our wealth? Indeed, you are the forbearing, the rightly guided"﴾ [87]

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is His remembrance, says: The people of Shu'ayb said, "O Shu'ayb, does your prayer (*salawat*) command you to abandon the worship of what our fathers worshipped of idols and images?" [[In the printed edition at this place it reads "aslatuka" in the singular; I have restored what is in the manuscript.]] ﴿Or that we stop doing with our wealth what we wish﴾, such as clipping and cutting dirhams and cheating people in measure and weight. ﴿Indeed, you are the forbearing﴾, meaning the one whom anger does not drive to do what he would not do when content. [[See the explanation of "al-halim" (the forbearing) above, p. 406, note 1, and the references there.]] ﴿The rightly guided﴾, meaning: rightly guided in his command to them to abandon the worship of idols. [[See the explanation of "al-rashid" (the rightly guided) above, p. 417, note 1, and the references there.]] As follows:

18487. Mahmud ibn Khidash told us, saying: Hammad ibn Khalid al-Khayyat told us, saying: Dawud ibn Qays told us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, regarding the saying of God: ﴿Does your prayer command you that we abandon what our fathers worshipped, or that we do with our wealth what we wish? Indeed, you are the forbearing, the rightly guided﴾ [[The manuscript has "aslatuka" in the singular, which is one of the two readings.]]. He said: Among the things he forbade them was *hadhf* (clipping) of dirhams, or he said: cutting of dirhams, the doubt being from Hammad. [[*Hadhf al-shay'* means cutting it from its edge; from it comes *tahdhif al-sha'r* (trimming hair), when one takes from its sides and levels it.]] [[The narrator (athar) 18487: Mahmud ibn Khidash al-Talaqani, the teacher of al-Tabari, passed earlier under no. 187. Hammad ibn Khalid al-Khayyat al-Qurashi is trustworthy; he was unlettered and could not write, but he could recite hadith. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir (3/1/25), and Ibn Abi Hatim (1/2/136).]]

18488. Sahl ibn Musa al-Razi told us, saying: Ibn Abi Fudayk told us, from Abu Mawdud, who said: I heard Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi say: "It has reached me that the people of Shu'ayb were punished for cutting dirhams; I found that in the Qur'an: ﴿Does your prayer command you that we abandon what our fathers worshipped, or that we do with our wealth what we wish?﴾" [[In the printed edition here too it reads "aslatuka" in the singular; I have restored what is in the manuscript. I will return it to the manuscript wherever I find it there, and leave the singular where I find it without noting that.]]

18489. Ibn Wakic told us, saying: Zayd ibn Habbab told us, from Musa ibn Ubayda, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, who said: The people of Shu'ayb were punished for their cutting of dirhams, so they said: ﴿O Shu'ayb, does your prayer command you that we abandon what our fathers worshipped, or that we do with our wealth what we wish?﴾

18490. ... He said: Hammad ibn Khalid al-Khayyat told us, from Dawud ibn Qays, from Zayd ibn Aslam, regarding His saying: ﴿Or that we do with our wealth what we wish﴾. He said: Among the things he forbade them was *hadhf* (clipping) of dirhams.

18491. Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿They said, "O Shu'ayb, does your prayer command you that we abandon what our fathers worshipped, or that we do with our wealth what we wish?"﴾ He said: He forbade them from cutting dinars and dirhams, so they said: "They are only our wealth; we do with them what we wish. If we wish, we cut them; if we wish, we exchange them; if we wish, we throw them away!"

18492. ... He said: Ibn Wahb also informed us, and Dawud ibn Qays al-Marri informed me that he heard Zayd ibn Aslam say regarding the saying of God: ﴿They said, "O Shu'ayb, does your prayer command you that we abandon what our fathers worshipped, or that we do with our wealth what we wish?"﴾ Zayd said: Among that was cutting dirhams.

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿Aslatuka (your prayer)﴾, al-A'mash used to say about its interpretation (*ta'wil*):

18493. Al-Hasan told us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from al-A'mash, regarding His saying: ﴿Aslatuka﴾, he said: "Your recitation" (*qira'atuka*).

* * *

If someone says: How is it said: ﴿Does your prayer command you that we abandon what our fathers worshipped, or that we do with our wealth what we wish?﴾, when Shu'ayb only forbade them to do with their wealth what you have mentioned he forbade them from?

It is said: The meaning of that is other than what you imagined. The grammarians (*ahl al-'arabiyya*, the people of Arabic grammar) have differed about its meaning.

Some of the Basrans said: Its meaning is: "Does your prayer command you that we abandon what our fathers worshipped, or that we abandon doing with our wealth what we wish?" It does not mean: "does it command you that we do with our wealth what we wish," because that is not what he commanded them.

* * *

Some of the Kufans said something similar to this view. There is also another way of reading it, which makes the command like a prohibition, as if he said: "Does your prayer command you to this and forbid us from that?" In that case the first is governed by the verb "yamuruka (commands you)", and the second is governed by coordination with "ma" in His saying ﴿ma ya'budu (what is worshipped)﴾. When that is the case, the meaning of the speech is: "Does your prayer command you that we abandon what our fathers worshipped, or that we abandon doing with our wealth what we wish?"

* * *

It is reported that one of the reciters read it as ﴿ma tashā'u (what you wish)﴾.

* * *

Abu Ja'far said: Whoever reads it that way, there is no difficulty in it, and the second "an" (that) is then coordinated with the first "an".

* * *

As for their saying to Shu'ayb: ﴿Indeed, you are the forbearing, the rightly guided﴾, they were God's enemies, and they said that to him in mockery. They only made him seem foolish and ignorant by this speech.

* * *

Those who are the people of interpretation (*ahl al-ta'wil*) said things in agreement with what we have said.

Those who said that:

18494. Al-Qasim told us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj: ﴿Indeed, you are the forbearing, the rightly guided﴾, he said: "They mock him."

18495. Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, you are the forbearing, the rightly guided﴾: "The mockers, mocking: 'Indeed, you are the forbearing, the rightly guided!'" [[In the printed edition: "bi-annaka la-anta", and the sound text is what is in the manuscript.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 88:

On the interpretation of His saying, ﴿He said, "O my people, tell me, if I am upon clear evidence from my Lord and He has provided me with good provision from Himself, [then what?] And I do not intend to oppose you in that which I forbid you from. I only intend reform as much as I am able. And my success is not except through Allah. Upon Him I have relied, and to Him I turn back."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Shu'ayb said to his people: "O my people, tell me, if I am upon clarity and proof from my Lord regarding what I call you to, namely the worship of Allah and the disavowal of worshipping idols and images, and regarding what I forbid you from, namely corrupting wealth, ﴿and He has provided me with good provision from Himself﴾, meaning lawful and good provision."

* *

﴿And I do not intend to oppose you in that which I forbid you from﴾: he says, I do not intend to forbid you from a matter and then do the opposite of it; rather, I do not do except what I command you to do, and I do not refrain except from what I forbid you from. As related:

18496. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And I do not intend to oppose you in that which I forbid you from﴾, he said: "I would not forbid you from a matter that I myself commit or engage in."

* *

﴿I only intend reform, as much as I am able﴾: he says, in what I command you and forbid you from, I intend only your reform and the reform of your affairs. ﴿As much as I am able﴾: he says, as much as I have the capacity to reform it, lest there befall you from Allah a punishment that deters, because of your opposing His command and disobeying His messenger. ﴿And my success is not except through Allah﴾: he says, my reaching the truth in my endeavor to reform you and reform your affairs is not except through Allah, for He is the one who helps in that; if He does not help me in it, I do not reach the truth in it.

* *

As for His saying, ﴿Upon Him I have relied﴾: he says, to Allah I entrust my affair, for He is my trust, and upon Him is my reliance in my affairs. [Note: in the printed and manuscript editions: "for He is my trust", and the correct reading is probably what has been established.] [See the explanation of "tawakkul" in the previous language indexes (w-k-l).]

* *

As for His saying, ﴿And to Him I turn back﴾: and to Him I turn with obedience, and I return with repentance. [See the explanation of "inabah" previously, p. 406.] As related:

18497. Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And to Him I turn back﴾, he said: "I return."

18498. Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

18499. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said:

18500. ... And Ishaq narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, his saying: ﴿And to Him I turn back﴾, he said: "I return."

18501. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, his saying: ﴿And to Him I turn back﴾, he said: "I return."

**The interpretation of His words, may He be exalted: ﴿And O my people, let not my opposition bring upon you the like of what befell the people of Noah, or the people of Hud, or the people of Salih; and the people of Lot are not far from you﴾ (11:89)**

Abu Ja'far said: May He be remembered and exalted, is relating the words of Shu'ayb to his people: ﴿And O my people, let not my opposition bring upon you﴾, meaning: let not my enmity, my hatred, and my departure from the religion I follow (1) move you to persist in what you are upon of disbelief in God, worship of idols, and cheating people in measure and weight, and refusing to turn back in repentance. Then there will befall you ﴿the like of what befell the people of Noah﴾, from drowning; ﴿or the people of Hud﴾, from punishment; ﴿or the people of Salih﴾, from the earthquake; ﴿and the people of Lot, whose lands were overturned﴾, ﴿are not far from you﴾ in their destruction. Will you not then take warning from it and reflect? He means: take a lesson from these people, and beware lest what befell them befall you because of my opposition.

As for the transmitted reports:

18502. Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding His words: ﴿Let not my opposition bring you﴾, he said: it means, let not my departure from you lead you to it, ﴿that there befall you the like of what befell the people of Noah﴾, the verse.

18503. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿Let not my opposition bring you﴾, he said: let not my opposition lead you to it.

18504. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj regarding His words: ﴿Let not my opposition bring you﴾, he said: my enmity, my hatred, and my departure.

18505. Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah regarding: ﴿and the people of Lot are not far from you﴾, he said: They were only a recent generation close to them, meaning the people of Noah, 'Ad, Thamud and Salih. (2)

18506. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah regarding His words: ﴿and the people of Lot are not far from you﴾, he said: They were only recent in time, after Noah and Thamud.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: It is also possible to say that the meaning is: "and the abode of the people of Lot is not far from you."

---

(1) Shiqaq (شقاق): opposition, defiance, or dissension; see the discussion of this word earlier in this commentary, vol. 13, p. 433, note 1, and the references cited there. Jarm (جرم): to bring upon or to cause; see its explanation earlier, vols. 9, pp. 483–485, and 10, p. 95.

(2) The editors note that this wording appears in both the manuscript and the printed edition, but they consider the correct reading to be: "meaning the people of Noah, Hud, Salih, and Lot."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 90:

The Interpretation of His Words, the Exalted: ﴿And seek forgiveness from your Lord, then turn to Him in repentance. Indeed, my Lord is Merciful and Affectionate.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, the Exalted, Who is remembered, says, reporting the words of Shu'ayb to his people: ﴿Seek forgiveness from your Lord﴾, O people, for your sins between you and your Lord, in which you persist, such as the worship of gods and idols, and defrauding people of their rights in measures and weights. ﴿Then turn to Him﴾, that is: then return to obedience to Him and submit to His command and prohibition. ﴿Indeed, my Lord is Merciful﴾, that is: He is merciful to whoever repents and turns to Him, so that He does not punish him after repentance. ﴿Affectionate﴾, that is: He has love for whoever turns back and repents to Him; He loves him and cherishes him.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 91:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted be He: ﴿They said, "O Shu'ayb, we do not understand much of what you say, and indeed we see you as weak among us. And were it not for your clan, we would have stoned you, and you are not mighty against us."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, exalted be His remembrance, says: The people of Shu'ayb said to Shu'ayb: ﴿O Shu'ayb, we do not understand much of what you say﴾, meaning: we do not know the reality of much of what you say and tell us about [[See the explanation of "al-fiqh" (understanding) above, 14:582, footnote 2, and the references there.]] = ﴿and indeed we see you as weak among us﴾.

* *

It has been mentioned that he was blind, and therefore they said to him: ﴿Indeed we see you as weak among us﴾.

* *

Mention of those who said this:

18507. Abd al-A'la ibn Wasil narrated to me, saying: Asad ibn Zayd al-Jassas narrated to us, saying: Shurayk informed us, from Salim, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding His saying: ﴿And indeed we see you as weak among us﴾, he said: He was blind. [[Narration 18507: I could not find any mention of "Asad ibn Zayd al-Jassas." What is mentioned is "Usayd ibn Zayd ibn Najih al-Jammal," who narrates from Shurayk, and from whom Abu Kurayb and his generation of Abu Ja'far al-Tabari's teachers narrate. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 1/2/16, Abu Hatim 1/1/318, and Mizan al-I'tidal 1:119. But this is "al-Jammal" and that is "al-Jassas," so I do not know who this is whom Abu Ja'far mentioned.]]

18508. Abbas ibn Abi Talib narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Mahdi al-Massisi narrated to me, saying: Khalaf ibn Khalifa narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Sa'id, the like of it.

18509. Ahmad ibn al-Walid al-Ramli narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Ziyad and Ishaq ibn al-Mundhir, and Abd al-Malik ibn Zayd narrated to us, they said: Shurayk narrated to us, from Salim, from Sa'id, the like of it. [[Narration 18509: "Abd al-Malik ibn Yazid" is how it appears in the manuscript, as I have recorded it, while in the printed edition it is "Abd al-Malik ibn Zayd," differing from the manuscript. I do not know who "Abd al-Malik ibn Yazid" or "ibn Zayd" is, who narrates from Shurayk.]]

18510. ... He said: Amr ibn Awn and Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah narrated to us, they said: We heard Shurayk say regarding His saying: ﴿And indeed we see you as weak among us﴾, he said: Blind.

18511. Sa'dawayh narrated to us, saying: Abbad narrated to us, from Shurayk, from Salim, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, the like of it. [[Narration 18511: "Sa'dawayh al-Dabbi al-Wasiti" is Sa'id ibn Sulayman, a teacher of al-Tabari, who appeared under numbers 611, 2168, 11996, 13809 (vol. 12: 585, footnote 1). Sa'dawayh narrates from Shurayk, but he also narrates from Abbad ibn al-Awwam, so here he narrates from Shurayk through an intermediary.]]

18512. al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us regarding His saying: ﴿And indeed we see you as weak among us﴾, he said: He was weak of sight. Sufyan said: and he used to be called "the orator of the prophets."

18513. ... He said: al-Hammani narrated to us, saying: Abbad narrated to us, from Shurayk, from Salim, from Sa'id: ﴿And indeed we see you as weak among us﴾, he said: He was blind of sight.

* *

= And His saying: ﴿And were it not for your clan, we would have stoned you﴾, meaning: they say: were it not that you are among your tribe and your people = ﴿we would have stoned you﴾, meaning: we would have cursed you. [[In the printed and manuscript editions: "Were it not that you are among your tribe," and I incline to think the correct reading is what I have recorded.]]

* *

Some of them said: its meaning is: we would have killed you.

Mention of those who said this:

18514. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: ﴿And were it not for your clan, we would have stoned you﴾, he said: They said: Were it not that we fear your people and your clan, we would have stoned you.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And you are not mighty against us﴾, they mean: you are not one who is honored by us, so that his humiliation and disgrace would be grievous to us; rather, that is easy for us. [[See the explanation of "ʿazīz" above in the indexes of language (ʿ-z-z).]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 92:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He said, "O my people, is my clan more honored by you than Allah? And you have put Him behind your backs, [as something] discarded. Indeed, my Lord is encompassing of what you do."﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Shu'ayb said to his people: "O my people, you have made your people more honored than Allah, and you have treated your Lord lightly, so you have put Him behind your backs, not obeying His command, not fearing His punishment, and not magnifying Him as He deserves?"

* *

It is said of a man who does not fulfill another man's need: "He cast his need behind his back" (nabadha hajatahu wara'a zahrihi), [[See the explanation of "nabadhahu wara'a zahrihi" earlier: 1:403-404 / 7:458-459, 463.]] meaning he left it, not paying attention to it. And if he fulfills it, it is said: "He placed it in front of him, before his eyes." It is also said: "Zahharta bi-hajati" and "ja'altuhā zihriyyah," meaning: behind your back, as the poet said: [[He is Artah ibn Suhayyah al-Murri.]]

"We found the sons of al-Barsa'" from the offspring of the back (al-zahr)*" [[Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubaydah 1:298; and Lisan al-'Arab (zahr). Artah used to satirize Shabib ibn al-Barsa', and both were from Banu Murrah ibn Sa'd ibn Dhubyan, and the satire between them was abundant; this is from him. See al-Aghani 13:29-44 (Dar al-Kutub), biography of Artah ibn Suhayyah = and al-Aghani 12:271-281 (Sasi), biography of Shabib ibn al-Barsa'. The first half of the verse: "So who will convey to the sons of Murrah that we..."]]

Meaning: they turn their backs on people's needs and do not pay attention to them.

* *

Those of the interpreters said the same as what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

18515- Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, he said: my paternal uncle narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿He said, "O my people, is my clan more honored by you than Allah? And you have put Him behind your backs, [as something] discarded."﴾ That is because the people of Shu'ayb and his clan were more honored by them than Allah, and the matter of Allah was insignificant to them, the Mighty and Majestic is our Lord.

18516- al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, he said: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And you have put Him behind your backs, [as something] discarded.﴾ He said: qafa. [[So it is in the printed edition, and it has a meaning, but what is in the manuscript is "qusayy," and it seems he meant "qusayyan," and this is more preferable to me.]]

18517- Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿O my people, is my clan more honored by you than Allah and you have put Him behind your backs, [as something] discarded.﴾ He says: you made your people honored, and you made your Lord insignificant.

18518- Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿And you have put Him behind your backs, [as something] discarded.﴾ He said: You did not watch over Him in anything, you only watched over my people. ﴿And you have put Him behind your backs, [as something] discarded.﴾ He says: you made your people honored, and you made your Lord insignificant.

18519- Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿And you have put Him behind your backs, [as something] discarded.﴾ He said: You did not watch over Him in anything, you only watched over my people. = ﴿And you have put Him behind your backs, [as something] discarded.﴾ You do not fear Him.

18520- al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, he said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah regarding His saying: ﴿Is my clan more honored by you than Allah?﴾ He said: You made your people honored and you were deceived regarding your Lord. I heard Ishaq ibn Abi Isra'il say: Sufyan said: ﴿And you have put Him behind your backs, [as something] discarded﴾, like a man saying to another: "You have left my need behind your back," ﴿so you have put Him behind your backs, [as something] discarded﴾, you treated His command lightly. When a man wants to fulfill the need of his companion, he places it in front of him, before his hands, and does not treat it lightly.

18521- Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: ﴿And you have put Him behind your backs, [as something] discarded.﴾ He said: "al-Zihri" is the surplus, like a camel-driver who goes out with camels kept as a surplus (zahhariyyah), [[So it came in the manuscript and the printed edition: "zahhariyyah," but the language indicates that the plural of "zihri" is "zihari," so adding the taa' here is weak in its basis.]] a surplus, he does not load anything on them except when he needs them. He said: So he says: your Lord is only like this to you, if you need Him. And if you do not need Him, He is nothing.

* *

Others said: the meaning of that is: and you have put behind your backs what Shu'ayb brought, as a discarded thing. So the pronoun in His saying ﴿and you have put Him﴾ refers, according to this view, to what Shu'ayb brought.

Mention of those who said that:

18522- Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, he said: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿And you have put Him behind your backs, [as something] discarded.﴾ He said: You left what Shu'ayb brought.

18523- ... narrated to us, he said: Ja'far ibn 'Awn narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from Mujahid, he said: They cast aside his command.

18524- al-Harith narrated to me, he said: 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from Mujahid: ﴿And you have put Him behind your backs, [as something] discarded.﴾ He said: You cast aside his command.

18525- Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to us, he said: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, he said: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿And you have put Him behind your backs, [as something] discarded.﴾ He said: The clan of Shu'ayb resolved to leave what he brought behind their backs, discarded.

18526- al-Muthanna narrated to me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, he said: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, he said =

18527- ... and Ishaq narrated to us, he said: 'Abd Allah narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿And you have put Him behind your backs, [as something] discarded.﴾ He said: Their exception of the clan of Shu'ayb, and their leaving what Shu'ayb brought behind their backs, discarded.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: We chose the view we have chosen in interpreting this, because the nearness of His saying ﴿and you have put Him behind your backs, [as something] discarded﴾ to His saying ﴿Is my clan more honored by you than Allah?﴾ makes the pronoun in His saying ﴿and you have put Him﴾ more fitting and more appropriate to refer to Allah, due to the nearness of its placement to Him.

* *

As for His saying ﴿Indeed, my Lord is encompassing of what you do﴾, it means: indeed my Lord's knowledge encompasses your deeds, [[See the explanation of "muhit" earlier, p. 445, note 2, and the references there.]] so nothing of it is hidden from Him, and He will recompense you for all of it, in this world and the next.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 93:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And O my people, act according to your position; indeed, I am acting. You will soon know ... 93 who﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, reporting the words of Shu'ayb to his people: ﴿And O my people, act according to your position﴾, meaning: according to your capacity (tamakkun).

* *

It is said of this: "The man acts according to his makanah and makinah," meaning: according to his deliberate pace, and "the man became established (makuna yamkunu makanan wa makanatan wa makanan)." [[See the explanation of "al-makanah" above, pp. 12:128, 129; here there is an addition to its sources that you will not find in the lexicon books.]]

* *

Some of the interpreters said regarding the meaning of His saying ﴿according to your position﴾: according to your stations (manazil).

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The meaning of the speech, then, is: "And O my people, act according to your capacity for the work you are doing; indeed, I am acting with deliberateness in the work I am doing," ﴿You will soon know﴾ which of us is the one who brings crime upon himself, the one who errs against it, and the one who is right in his action and benefits himself.

* *

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Whoever will receive a punishment that disgraces him, and who is a liar. And watch; indeed, I am with you a watcher (93)﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is He, reporting the words of His Prophet Shu'ayb to his people: The one to whom there comes from us and from you, O people, ﴿a punishment that will disgrace him﴾, meaning: it will humiliate and degrade him [[See the explanation of "al-khizy" above in the indexes of language (kh-z-y).]]. ﴿And who is a liar﴾, meaning: and it will likewise disgrace the one who is lying in his speech and report, from us and from you. ﴿And watch﴾, meaning: wait and observe, from al-raqabah (watching).

* *

It is said of this: "I watched so-and-so, arqubuhu, with riqbah (watchfulness)."[[See the explanation of "al-tarassud" and "al-raqib" above, 7:523, 524 / 11:239.]]

* *

As for His saying ﴿Indeed, I am with you a watcher﴾, meaning: indeed, I too am one who keeps watch for that punishment with you, and observes it, as to who among us and among you will descend upon it?[[See the explanation of "al-tarassud" and "al-raqib" above, 7:523, 524 / 11:239.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 11, verses 94–95:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And when Our command came, We saved Shu'ayb and those who believed with him by a mercy from Us, and the Shout seized those who did wrong, so they became motionless corpses in their homes﴾ (94).

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: When Our decree came concerning the people of Shu'ayb, with Our punishment, "We saved Shu'ayb," Our messenger, and those who believed in him and affirmed what he brought them from their Lord along with Shu'ayb, from Our punishment which We sent upon his people, ﴿by a mercy from Us﴾ toward him and toward those who believed in him and followed him in what had come to them from their Lord. ﴿And the Shout seized those who did wrong﴾: a cry from the sky that extinguished them, destroying them for their disbelief in their Lord. [[See the explanation of "al-Sayha" (the Shout) above, p. 380.]] It has been said that Jibril, peace be upon him, cried out to them with a shout that removed their souls from their bodies. ﴿So they became motionless in their homes﴾, ﴿jathimin﴾, on their knees, and fallen upon their courtyards. [[See the explanation of "al-Jutum" (motionlessness) above, p. 380, note 2, and the references there.]]

* *

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿As though they had never prospered therein. Unquestionably, [the people of] Madyan were removed [from mercy] as Thamud were removed﴾ (95).

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: As though the people of Shu'ayb, whom Allah destroyed with His punishment when they became motionless in their homes before that, had never lived there, and had never prospered.

* *

= From their saying: "I prospered (ghaniya) in such-and-such a place," meaning I dwelt there, [[See the explanation of "ghani bi-kadha" above, 12:569–570 / 15:56, 381.]] and from the words of al-Nabigha:

* *

They prospered thereby when they were my neighbors... from it, with the bending of messages and affection [[The verse and its explanation have passed above, p. 56.]]

And as for what has been transmitted:

18528. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿As though they had never prospered therein﴾, he said: It means, as though they had never lived therein.

18529. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, the like of it.

18530. Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, the like of it.

* *

= As for His saying: ﴿Unquestionably, [the people of] Madyan were removed [from mercy] as Thamud were removed﴾, Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, means: Unquestionably, may Allah remove Madyan from His mercy by bringing down His vengeance upon them. As for His words, ﴿wretched is the gift that is given﴾, it means: wretched is the aid that is aided, the cursing that is increased, with another like it added to it. [[In the manuscript and the printed edition: "another from it" (ukhra minha), but the correct reading appears to be what I have adopted.]]

The root of "al-rifd" is aid (al-'awn). It is said: "Fulan rafada fulanan 'inda al-amir, yarfiduhu rifdan" (with a kasrah on the ra'), meaning he aided him before the ruler. When the ra' is fatha'd (rafd), it means watering in a large bowl; and "al-rafd" is a large bowl. From this is the verse of al-A'sha:

"How many a bowl (rafd) you poured out that day, and captives from a host of equals (aqtal)..."

[[From his Diwan, p. 13, from a long qasidah of his finest poetry, praising al-Aswad ibn al-Mundhir al-Lakhmi, brother of al-Nu'man ibn al-Mundhir the king. al-Aswad had raided the two allies, Asad and Dhubyan, then attacked al-Tuff, seizing camels, captives and women from Sa'd ibn Dhubay'ah (al-A'sha's kin), while al-A'sha was absent. When he returned he found the tribe plundered, so he came to al-Aswad, recited poetry to him, and asked him to grant him the captives and transport them back; he did so. The meaning: a man once had camels he milked into a bowl for himself and his family, but the camels were taken and what he used to milk was lost; in the same way, you poured out what had been milked. "Aqtal" is the plural of "qatl" (with kasrah then sukun), and "qatl" means an enemy's counterpart, and also a like or equal. al-Asma'i, explaining the verse (and I have quoted what preceded from his commentary on the Diwan), said: "aqtal" means likes, not enemies. In the printed edition and the manuscript it appeared as "aqyal," which is an error here.]]

It is also said: "Fulan rafada hā'iṭahu" (he propped up his wall), meaning he supported it with a piece of wood so that it would not fall. "Al-rafd," with the ra' fatha'd, is the verbal noun; it is said: "rafadahu yarfiduhu rafdan." "Al-rifd" is the name of the thing a person is given, and it is "al-mirfad."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 100:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿That is from the tidings of the towns which We relate to you; some of them still standing and some mown down﴾ (11:100).

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The Exalted says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): This narrative which We have related to you in this surah, and the tidings which We have informed you of therein, are from the reports of the towns whose people We destroyed because of their disbelief in God and their denial of His messengers. [[See the explanation of "tidings" (naba') in the earlier linguistic indexes, under (n-b-')]] ﴿We relate it to you﴾, meaning, We inform you of it. [[See the explanation of "narratives" (qasas) in earlier volumes: 9:402 / 11:399 / 12:120, 307, 406 / 13:7, 274.]] ﴿Some of them still standing﴾ means: of them is one whose structure still stands, but whose people have perished and been destroyed. And of them is one whose structure still stands, inhabited; and of them is one whose structure is mown down, a ruin in collapse, its traces effaced and obliterated.

* *

From the expression "a mown crop" (zar' hasid), used when its stalks have been completely cut off. Strictly, it should be "mahsud" (mown), but it has been turned into the form "fa'il" (hasid), as we have explained in similar cases. [[See the explanation of "hasid" earlier, p. 56.]] [[See the earlier linguistic indexes on Arabic grammar and related topics.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 101:

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And We did not wrong them, but they wronged themselves. So their gods, which they invoked besides Allah, did not avail them anything when the command of your Lord came, and they increased them in nothing but ruin.﴾ (11:101)

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: We did not punish the people of these towns whose news We have related to you, O Muhammad, without their deserving Our punishment, such that We would thereby have placed Our punishment in other than its proper place. ﴿But they wronged themselves﴾, meaning: rather, they made themselves deserving, through their disobedience to Allah and their disbelief in Him, of His punishment and His chastisement, so they brought upon themselves what was not theirs to bring, and made obligatory for themselves what was not theirs to make obligatory. ﴿So their gods, which they invoked besides Allah, did not avail them anything﴾, meaning: their gods which they invoked besides Allah did not repel from them, [[See the explanation of "aghna 'anhu" above, p. 215, note 1, and the references there.]] those whom they took as lords, any of the punishment of Allah and His chastisement when their Lord brought it upon them, nor did they turn away from them any of it. ﴿When the command of your Lord came﴾, O Muhammad, meaning: when the decree of your Lord came concerning their punishment, so His retribution was due upon them and His wrath descended upon them. ﴿And they increased them in nothing but ruin﴾, meaning: and their gods, at the coming of the command of your Lord, increased these polytheists in nothing but loss, destruction and annihilation by the punishment of Allah.

* *

It is said of it: "tabbabtuhu, atabbibuhu tatbiban" (I ruined him, I ruin him, ruination), and from it is their saying to a man: "tabban laka" (ruin to you). Jarir said:

"Aradah, a remnant of the people of Lot... Alas, ruin to what they did, a ruin!"

[[From his Diwan, p. 72, from his famous qasida satirizing al-Ra'i al-Numayri. Its occasion was that "Aradah al-Numayri," in one narration "al-Ra'i" was a boon companion of al-Farazdaq. Al-Ra'i came to Basra, and Aradah invited him, fed him and gave him drink, and said: "al-Farazdaq is superior to Jarir!" He refused. When drink took hold of him, he did not cease to press him until he said: "O my two companions, the journey has drawn near, so travel on... al-Farazdaq has overcome Jarir in satire." So satire flared up between them, and among what he mentioned of Aradah was his saying: "There came to me about Aradah an evil saying, but by the father of Aradah, it did not hit the mark..." and "How many an evil mother you have, O Aradah, in the land of the acacia, who gathers the locusts..." and "Wretched is the gain that Numayr gains from you, when they make you wait and await your return..." In the manuscript and the printed edition it reads "Ara'bah," which is a clear error.]]
