* *

Abu Ja'far said: This report from Allah, exalted is His remembrance, although it is a report about the nations that passed before us, is a warning from Allah, majestic is His praise, to us, O community, that if we follow the path of the nations before us in opposing Him and His Messenger, He will take us along their path in punishment. It is also an announcement from Him that He does not wrong any of His creatures, and that it is the servants who wrong themselves, as:

18558 - Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said: He excused Himself — meaning our Lord, majestic is His praise — to His creatures, saying: ﴿And We did not wrong them﴾, regarding what We have mentioned to you of the punishment of those nations whom We punished, ﴿but they wronged themselves, so their gods did not avail them﴾, until: ﴿and they increased them in nothing but ruin﴾, he said: "those whom they used to worship did not increase them in anything but ruin."

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿And such is the seizing of your Lord when He seizes the towns while they are wrongdoing. Indeed His seizing is painful and severe.﴾ (11:102)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Just as I seized, O people, the people of those towns whose accounts I have related to you, with the punishment with which I seized them, for their opposition to My command, their denial of My messengers, and their rejection of My signs, so is My seizing of the towns and their inhabitants when I seize them with My punishment while they are wrongdoers to themselves by their disbelief in God, their association of others with Him, and their denial of His messengers. ﴿Indeed His seizing is painful﴾ means: indeed the seizing of your Lord with punishment is ﴿painful﴾, meaning: afflicting. ﴿Severe﴾ means: severe in its affliction.

* *

This is a warning from God to this community that they should not follow in His disobedience the path of the wicked nations before them, lest there befall them what befell those nations of exemplary punishments, as related:

18559 – Abu Kurayb narrated to us, who said: Abu Mu'awiya narrated to us, from Buraid ibn Abi Burda, from his father, from Abu Musa, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Indeed God gives respite to the wrongdoer – or perhaps he said: gives time – until when He seizes him, He does not let him escape." Then he recited: ﴿And such is the seizing of your Lord when He seizes the towns while they are wrongdoing.﴾

[Note on the chain: "Buraid ibn Burda" is "Buraid ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Burda al-Ash'ari", who narrates from his grandfather Abu Burda, a trustworthy narrator whose reports were recorded by the group of compilers and who is mentioned in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir and Ibn Abi Hatim. His words "from his father" mean from Abu Burda ibn Abi Musa al-Ash'ari, who is his grandfather. This report is transmitted by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (al-Fath 8:267), Muslim in his Sahih, Ibn Majah in his Sunan, and al-Tirmidhi in the Book of Tafsir. The isnad of al-Bukhari and Muslim reads "Buraida ibn Abi Burda, from his father", and that of Ibn Majah "Buraid ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Burda, from Abu Burda"; al-Tirmidhi gives the same as al-Tabari's isnad. Ibn Hajar noted this, saying: "So it occurs in the version of Abu Dharr; in another it occurs as 'from Abu Burda' instead of 'from his father', which is correct, because Buraid is the son of Abdullah ibn Abi Burda, so Abu Burda is his grandfather, not his father, but calling him father is permissible figuratively" (al-Fath 8:267). Al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan sahih gharib hadith. Abu Usama also narrated from Buraid something similar, and said: 'Yu'la.' Ibrahim ibn Sa'id al-Jawhari narrated to us, from Abu Usama, from Buraid ibn Abdullah, from his grandfather Abu Burda, from Abu Musa, from the Prophet (ﷺ), something similar, and said: 'yumla,' and he did not doubt it."

In the manuscript and the printed edition there was here: "Indeed God gives respite – and perhaps He gives time, he said: gives time," adding "gives time," which I removed, as it is an addition whose error is beyond doubt. "Amlā lahu" means he granted him respite and prolonged his term, from "al-mulāwah," which is a period of time.

18560 – Yunus narrated to me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said: God warned this community of His might by His words: ﴿And such is the seizing of your Lord when He seizes the towns while they are wrongdoing. Indeed His seizing is painful and severe.﴾

* *

Asim al-Jahdari used to recite it: ﴿And such is the seizing of your Lord when He seizes the towns while they are wrongdoing﴾, [Note: In the printed edition it reads "wa-kadhalika akhdh rabbika idh akhadha al-qura," and in the manuscript "wa-kadhalika akhdh rabbika idh akhadha al-qura," and what is in the manuscript is the same recitation, which is why the editor put "idh" in place of "idha". But since I saw that al-Tabari mentioned its disagreement with the codices of the Muslims, and the manuscript had "idha", I judged that this is what he affirmed. It is an irregular reading transmitted from Asim al-Jahdari and from Nafi' (see al-Qira'at al-Shadhdha of Ibn Khalawayh: 61). Asim and Talha ibn Musarrif recited: "wa-kadhalika akhadha rabbuka idh akhadha al-qura," and Asim also recited: "wa-kadhalika akhdh rabbika idh akhadha al-qura." So there are three readings transmitted from Asim al-Jahdari, the most divergent of which from the codices of the Muslims, and from what the readers of the metropolitan cities hold, is the one I have affirmed.] and this is a reading which I do not consider permissible to recite, because it contradicts the codices of the Muslims and what the readers of the cities hold.

**The exegesis of His words, may He be exalted:** ﴿Indeed in that is a sign for whoever fears the punishment of the Hereafter. That is a Day for which mankind will be gathered, and that is a Day witnessed.﴾ (11:103)

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Indeed, in Our seizing those of the people of the towns whose account We have related to you, O people, there is a sign, meaning a lesson and an admonition [See the explanation of "āyah" in the earlier language indices (ʾ-y-y)], for whoever among His servants fears the punishment of God and His chastisement in the Hereafter, and as a proof against him before his Lord, and as a deterrent that restrains him from disobeying God and opposing Him in what He has commanded and forbidden.

* *

It has also been said: Rather, the meaning is that in it there is a lesson for whoever fears the punishment of the Hereafter, because God will fulfil His promise to him.

Those who said this:

18561. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words: ﴿Indeed in that is a sign for whoever fears the punishment of the Hereafter﴾: "Indeed, We will fulfil for them what We promised them in the Hereafter, just as We fulfilled for the Prophets that We would give them victory."

* *

As for His words: ﴿That is a Day for which mankind will be gathered﴾, He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: this Day, meaning the Day of Resurrection, is a Day "for which mankind will be gathered," meaning God will assemble mankind for it from their graves, gathering them therein for recompense, reward and punishment. ﴿And that is a Day witnessed﴾ means: it is a Day witnessed by all creation, none of them will be absent, and on it God will then take vengeance upon those who disobeyed God, opposed His command and denied His messengers.

* *

The people of ta'wil (interpretation) have said what is similar to what we have said concerning this.

Those who said this:

18562. Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, from Mujahid, concerning His words: ﴿That is a Day for which mankind will be gathered and that is a Day witnessed﴾, he said: "It is the Day of Resurrection."

18563. Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, from Ikrimah, the like of it.

18564. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us; and Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from Ali ibn Zayd, from Yusuf al-Makki, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The witness (al-shahid)" is Muhammad, and "the witnessed (al-mashhud)" is the Day of Resurrection. Then he recited: ﴿That is a Day for which mankind will be gathered and that is a Day witnessed﴾.

18565. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: al-Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal narrated to us, saying: Hammad narrated to us, from Ali ibn Zayd, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The witness" is Muhammad, and "the witnessed" is the Day of Resurrection. Then he recited this verse: ﴿That is a Day for which mankind will be gathered and that is a Day witnessed﴾.

18566. It was related to me from al-Musayyab, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, concerning His words: ﴿That is a Day for which mankind will be gathered and that is a Day witnessed﴾, he said: "That is the Day of Resurrection, on which all creation will be assembled, and the inhabitants of the heavens and the inhabitants of the earth will witness it."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 104–107:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿And We delay it only for a term already counted (104)﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "And We do not delay the Day of Resurrection from coming upon you except for it to be decreed. He has appointed for it a term, counted and enumerated, so it will not come except at its appointed time; its coming will be neither brought forward before that nor postponed."

* *

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿The Day it comes, no soul will speak except by His permission. Among them are the wretched and the blessed (105). As for those who were wretched, they will be in the Fire, for them therein is groaning and wailing (106), abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord wills. Indeed, your Lord is the Effecter of what He intends (107)﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "The Day it comes, O people, which is the Day of Resurrection, and the Hour is established, no soul will speak except by the permission of its Lord."

* *

The reciters differed regarding the recitation of His saying: ﴿yawma ya'ti﴾ (the Day it comes).

The majority of the reciters of Madinah recited it with the yā' affirmed: ﴿yawma ya'tī lā tukallamu nafs﴾.

Some of the reciters of Basra and some of the Kufans recited it with the yā' affirmed when connected, and omitted it when pausing.

* *

A group of the people of Kufa recited it with the yā' omitted both in connection and in pausing: ﴿yawma ya'ti lā tukallamu nafs illā bi-idhnihi﴾.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct recitation in this matter, in my view, is ﴿yawma ya'ti﴾, with the yā' omitted both in connection and in pausing, following the orthography of the Mushaf; and it is a well-known dialect of the Hudhayl, who say: "Mā adri mā taqūl" (I do not know what you say). From it is the saying of the poet [[I do not know who his speaker is.]]:

Your palm is a palm that does not hold a dirham ... in generosity, and the other gives blood with the sword.

* *

It has been said: ﴿lā tukallam﴾, but it is in fact "lā tatakallam", and one of the two tā' has been dropped, the remaining one indicating it.

* *

As for His saying, ﴿Among them are the wretched and the blessed﴾, it means: among these souls that will not speak on the Day of Resurrection except by the permission of their Lord, there are wretched and blessed ones. He returned the pronoun to "soul", which is singular in wording, by mentioning the plural in His saying ﴿Among them are the wretched and the blessed﴾.

* *

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: ﴿As for those who were wretched, they will be in the Fire, for them therein is groaning﴾, which is the beginning of a donkey's bray and the like, ﴿and wailing﴾, which is its last bray when he repeats it in his chest upon finishing his braying, as Ru'bah ibn al-'Ajjaj said:

He gurgled in the chest a faint sound or sobbed, until it is said: he brays, yet he has not brayed.

* *

What we have said on this matter is also what the people of interpretation have said.

Those who said so:

18567- Al-Muthanna related to me, he said: Abu Salih related to us, he said: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿For them therein is groaning and wailing﴾: he said: a loud sound and a weak sound.

18568- ... He said: Ishaq related to us, he said: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from Abu al-'Aliyah regarding His saying: ﴿For them therein is groaning and wailing﴾, he said: "The zafir" is in the throat, and "the shahiq" is in the chest.

18569- Al-Qasim related to us, he said: Al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliyah, similarly.

18570- Al-Muthanna related to me, he said: Ishaq related to us, he said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah who said: The voice of the disbeliever in the Fire is the voice of the donkey, its beginning is zafir and its end is shahiq.

18571- Abu Hisham al-Rifa'i, Muhammad ibn Ma'mar al-Bahrani, Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, and Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, they said: Abu 'Amir related to us, he said: Sulayman ibn Sufyan related to us, he said: 'Abd Allah ibn Dinar related to us, from Ibn 'Umar, from 'Umar who said: When this verse was revealed: ﴿Among them are the wretched and the blessed﴾, I asked the Prophet ﷺ and said: O Prophet of Allah, then what is our deed for? Upon something that has been finished, or upon something not yet finished? He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Upon something that has been finished, O 'Umar, and the pens have run with it; but each is made easy for what he was created for." The wording is that of the hadith of Ibn Ma'mar. [[The report 18571: Sulayman ibn Sufyan al-Tamimi is weak, munkar al-hadith, who narrates unfamiliar reports from trustworthy narrators. He is mentioned in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 2/2/18, Ibn Abi Hatim 2/1/119, and Mizan al-I'tidal 1:415. This report is weak in its chain; Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his tafsir 4:395, from Musnad Abi Ya'la, and al-Dhahabi mentioned it in al-Mizan with its chain from Abu 'Amir al-'Aqadi. But the meaning of the report has supporting evidence in the Sahih.]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord wills. Indeed, your Lord is the Effecter of what He intends﴾, He, may His remembrance be exalted, means by His saying ﴿abiding therein﴾: remaining therein [[See the explanation of "khulud" in the earlier indices of language (kh-l-d).]]; and by His saying ﴿as long as the heavens and the earth endure﴾: forever. [[See the explanation of "ma dama" at 10:185, 11:74, 11:238.]]

* *

This is because the Arabs, when they wished to describe a thing as lasting forever, said: "This is lasting as long as the heavens and the earth endure," meaning that it lasts forever. Similarly they say: "He remains as long as night and day alternate," "as long as the sons of Samir converse by night," and "as long as the wild cows wag their tails," intending by all of this "forever." So He, may His majesty be praised, addressed them with what they know among themselves, saying: ﴿abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure﴾, and the meaning is: abiding therein forever.

* *

Ibn Zayd used to say in this matter something similar to what we have said.

18572- Yunus related to us, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: ﴿abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure﴾: as long as the earth is earth and the heaven is heaven.

* *

Then He said: ﴿except what your Lord wills﴾. The people of knowledge and interpretation differed regarding the meaning of this. Some of them said: This is an exception made by God regarding the people of monotheism (tawhid), that He will bring them out of the Fire when He wills, after He had caused them to enter it.

Those who said so:

18573- Al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, he said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿As for those who were wretched, they will be in the Fire, for them therein is groaning and wailing, abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord wills﴾, he said: God knows best its exception (thunya) [[al-thunya (with a damma and then a sukun), and al-thunyah, of the pattern fa'ilah, and al-mathnawiyah, all mean "exception".]]

It has been mentioned to us that some people will be touched by a scorching of the Fire because of sins they committed, then God will admit them to Paradise.

18574- Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord wills﴾, and God knows best its exception. [[See note no. 1.]] It has been mentioned to us that some people will be touched by a scorching of the Fire because of sins that befell them, then God will admit them to Paradise by the grace of His mercy; they are called "the Jahannamiyyun".

18575- Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, he said: Shaybân ibn Farrukh related to us, he said: Abu Hilal related to us, he said: Qatadah related to us, and he recited this verse: ﴿As for those who were wretched, they will be in the Fire, for them therein is groaning and wailing﴾, up to His saying ﴿Effecter of what He intends﴾, and then said: Anas ibn Malik related to us that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "A people will come out of the Fire" — Qatadah said: We do not say what the people of Harura say. [[The "people of Harura" are the Kharijites, who say that the perpetrator of a major sin is eternally in the Fire, because they declare the people of major sins to be disbelievers.]]

18576- Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Ya'qub related to us, from Abu Malik, that is Tha'labah, from Abu Sinan regarding His saying: ﴿As for those who were wretched, they will be in the Fire, for them therein is groaning and wailing, abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord wills﴾, he said: It is an exception regarding the people of monotheism.

18577- Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim: ﴿As for those who were wretched, they will be in the Fire﴾, up to His saying ﴿abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord wills﴾, he said: A people will come out of the Fire and enter Paradise; they are the ones who were excepted for.

18578- Al-Muthanna related to me, he said: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih related to us, he said: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Amir ibn Jushayb, from Khalid ibn Ma'dan regarding His saying: ﴿remaining therein for ages﴾ [Surah al-Naba' 78:23], and His saying: ﴿abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord wills﴾, that both are regarding the people of monotheism. [[Report 18578: 'Amir ibn Jushayb al-Himsi narrated from Abu Umamah, Khalid ibn Ma'dan and others; he is trustworthy. He is in al-Tahdhib and Ibn Abi Hatim 3/1/319. In the printed edition it was "Jushab", which is an error; the manuscript is as I have given it, though unpointed. This report will come in the tafsir at 30:8, 9 (Bulaq), in the commentary on Surah al-Naba'.]]

* *

Others said: The exception in this verse concerns the people of monotheism, except that they said: the meaning of His saying ﴿except what your Lord wills﴾ is: except that your Lord wills to overlook them so that He does not cause them to enter the Fire. They directed the exception to His saying ﴿As for those who were wretched, they will be in the Fire﴾ = ﴿except what your Lord wills﴾, not to "abiding".

Those who said so:

18579- Al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, he said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Ibn al-Taymi related to us, from his father, from Abu Nadrah, from Jabir or Abu Sa'id — meaning al-Khudri — or from a man among the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, regarding His saying: ﴿except what your Lord wills; indeed your Lord is the Effecter of what He intends﴾, he said: This verse applies to the whole Qur'an; it means: wherever in the Qur'an there is ﴿abiding therein﴾, this verse applies to it. He said: I heard Abu Mijlaz say: It is its recompense, and if God wills, He will overlook its punishment.

* *

Others said: It refers to the people of the Fire and to everyone who enters it.

Those who said so:

18580- It has been related to me from al-Musayyab, from one he mentioned, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure﴾: they will not die, nor will they leave it, as long as the heavens and the earth endure; ﴿except what your Lord wills﴾: he said: the exception of God. He said: He will command the Fire to consume them. He said: And Ibn Mas'ud said: There will come upon Jahannam a time when its doors will rattle, with no one in it, and that is after they have remained therein for ages.

18581- Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Jarir related to us, from Bayan, from al-Sha'bi who said: Jahannam is the faster of the two abodes to become populated and the faster to become ruined.

* *

Others said: God informed us of His will regarding the people of Paradise, and He explained the meaning of its exception by His saying: ﴿a gift not cut off﴾ [Surah Hud 11:108], meaning that it is an addition beyond the duration of the heavens and the earth. He said: He did not inform us of His will regarding the people of the Fire. It is permissible that His will is for an addition, and it is permissible that it is for a reduction.

Those who said so:

18582- Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: ﴿abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord wills﴾, then he recited until he reached: ﴿a gift not cut off﴾, and said: He informed us of what He wills for the people of Paradise, saying ﴿a gift not cut off﴾, and did not inform us of what He wills for the people of the Fire.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these opinions regarding the interpretation of this verse is the saying we have related from Qatadah and al-Dahhak: that this is an exception regarding the people of monotheism among the people of major sins, that God will cause them to enter the Fire, abiding therein forever, except what He wills of leaving them there for less than that; then He will bring them out and admit them to Paradise, as we have already explained in another place, [[In the printed edition: "kadha qad bayyana", which is weak speech, the scribe's poor writing having caused the error.]] in a way that suffices to dispense with repeating it in this place. [[I have lost track of its location; whoever finds it, let him confirm it.]]

We said that this is the most correct of the sayings, because God, may His majesty be praised, threatened those who associate partners with Him with eternal abiding in the Fire, and reports from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ have consistently established this. It is therefore impermissible that the exception concerns the people of polytheism. And since the reports have been transmitted in mass-transmission (tawatur) from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that God will cause a people among the believers to enter the Fire because of sins they committed, then bring them out of it and admit them to Paradise, it is impermissible that this exception concerns the people of monotheism before their entry, given the soundness of the reports from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that we have mentioned. Moreover, if we made it an exception in that sense, we would have entered into the saying of one who says: "No sinner enters Paradise, and no believer enters the Fire," and that contradicts the positions of the people of knowledge and what the reports from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ have brought. When these two views are thus invalid, no saying held by the leaders among the people of knowledge remains except the third.

* *

The grammarians have a view on this other than that, which we will mention afterwards, and explain, God willing. [[See what follows, pp. 487–489.]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is the Effecter of what He intends﴾, He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Indeed your Lord, O Muhammad, is not prevented by any preventer from doing what He intends to do to those who disobey Him and oppose His command, by way of retribution against them; rather He does what He wills to do, and His action and decree pass upon them and upon whomever among His creation He wills. [[In the printed and manuscript editions: "But He does what He wills, so His action passes upon them and upon whomever among His creation He wills His action and decree", which is not sound; the fault is the copyist's, and the correct text is as I have given it, with the first "fa'luhu" placed before.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 104–107:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿And We delay it only for a term already counted (104)﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "And We do not delay the Day of Resurrection from coming upon you except for it to be decreed. He has appointed for it a term, counted and enumerated, so it will not come except at its appointed time; its coming will be neither brought forward before that nor postponed."

* *

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿The Day it comes, no soul will speak except by His permission. Among them are the wretched and the blessed (105). As for those who were wretched, they will be in the Fire, for them therein is groaning and wailing (106), abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord wills. Indeed, your Lord is the Effecter of what He intends (107)﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "The Day it comes, O people, which is the Day of Resurrection, and the Hour is established, no soul will speak except by the permission of its Lord."

* *

The reciters differed regarding the recitation of His saying: ﴿yawma ya'ti﴾ (the Day it comes).

The majority of the reciters of Madinah recited it with the yā' affirmed: ﴿yawma ya'tī lā tukallamu nafs﴾.

Some of the reciters of Basra and some of the Kufans recited it with the yā' affirmed when connected, and omitted it when pausing.

* *

A group of the people of Kufa recited it with the yā' omitted both in connection and in pausing: ﴿yawma ya'ti lā tukallamu nafs illā bi-idhnihi﴾.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct recitation in this matter, in my view, is ﴿yawma ya'ti﴾, with the yā' omitted both in connection and in pausing, following the orthography of the Mushaf; and it is a well-known dialect of the Hudhayl, who say: "Mā adri mā taqūl" (I do not know what you say). From it is the saying of the poet [[I do not know who his speaker is.]]:

Your palm is a palm that does not hold a dirham ... in generosity, and the other gives blood with the sword.

* *

It has been said: ﴿lā tukallam﴾, but it is in fact "lā tatakallam", and one of the two tā' has been dropped, the remaining one indicating it.

* *

As for His saying, ﴿Among them are the wretched and the blessed﴾, it means: among these souls that will not speak on the Day of Resurrection except by the permission of their Lord, there are wretched and blessed ones. He returned the pronoun to "soul", which is singular in wording, by mentioning the plural in His saying ﴿Among them are the wretched and the blessed﴾.

* *

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: ﴿As for those who were wretched, they will be in the Fire, for them therein is groaning﴾, which is the beginning of a donkey's bray and the like, ﴿and wailing﴾, which is its last bray when he repeats it in his chest upon finishing his braying, as Ru'bah ibn al-'Ajjaj said:

He gurgled in the chest a faint sound or sobbed, until it is said: he brays, yet he has not brayed.

* *

Your palm is a palm that does not hold a dirham ... in generosity, and the other gives blood with the sword.

* *

It has been said: ﴿lā tukallam﴾, but it is in fact "lā tatakallam", and one of the two tā' has been dropped, the remaining one indicating it.

* *

As for His saying, ﴿Among them are the wretched and the blessed﴾, it means: among these souls that will not speak on the Day of Resurrection except by the permission of their Lord, there are wretched and blessed ones. He returned the pronoun to "soul", which is singular in wording, by mentioning the plural in His saying ﴿Among them are the wretched and the blessed﴾.

* *

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: ﴿As for those who were wretched, they will be in the Fire, for them therein is groaning﴾, which is the beginning of a donkey's bray and the like, ﴿and wailing﴾, which is its last bray when he repeats it in his chest upon finishing his braying, as Ru'bah ibn al-'Ajjaj said:

He gurgled in the chest a faint sound or sobbed, until it is said: he brays, yet he has not brayed.

* *

What we have said on this matter is also what the people of interpretation have said.

Those who said so:

18567- Al-Muthanna related to me, he said: Abu Salih related to us, he said: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿For them therein is groaning and wailing﴾: he said: a loud sound and a weak sound.

18568- ... He said: Ishaq related to us, he said: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from Abu al-'Aliyah regarding His saying: ﴿For them therein is groaning and wailing﴾, he said: "The zafir" is in the throat, and "the shahiq" is in the chest.

18569- Al-Qasim related to us, he said: Al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliyah, similarly.

18570- Al-Muthanna related to me, he said: Ishaq related to us, he said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah who said: The voice of the disbeliever in the Fire is the voice of the donkey, its beginning is zafir and its end is shahiq.

18571- Abu Hisham al-Rifa'i, Muhammad ibn Ma'mar al-Bahrani, Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, and Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, they said: Abu 'Amir related to us, he said: Sulayman ibn Sufyan related to us, he said: 'Abd Allah ibn Dinar related to us, from Ibn 'Umar, from 'Umar who said: When this verse was revealed: ﴿Among them are the wretched and the blessed﴾, I asked the Prophet ﷺ and said: O Prophet of Allah, then what is our deed for? Upon something that has been finished, or upon something not yet finished? He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Upon something that has been finished, O 'Umar, and the pens have run with it; but each is made easy for what he was created for." The wording is that of the hadith of Ibn Ma'mar. [[The report 18571: Sulayman ibn Sufyan al-Tamimi is weak, munkar al-hadith, who narrates unfamiliar reports from trustworthy narrators. He is mentioned in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 2/2/18, Ibn Abi Hatim 2/1/119, and Mizan al-I'tidal 1:415. This report is weak in its chain; Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his tafsir 4:395, from Musnad Abi Ya'la, and al-Dhahabi mentioned it in al-Mizan with its chain from Abu 'Amir al-'Aqadi. But the meaning of the report has supporting evidence in the Sahih.]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord wills. Indeed, your Lord is the Effecter of what He intends﴾, He, may His remembrance be exalted, means by His saying ﴿abiding therein﴾: remaining therein [[See the explanation of "khulud" in the earlier indices of language (kh-l-d).]]; and by His saying ﴿as long as the heavens and the earth endure﴾: forever. [[See the explanation of "ma dama" at 10:185, 11:74, 11:238.]]

* *

This is because the Arabs, when they wished to describe a thing as lasting forever, said: "This is lasting as long as the heavens and the earth endure," meaning that it lasts forever. Similarly they say: "He remains as long as night and day alternate," "as long as the sons of Samir converse by night," and "as long as the wild cows wag their tails," intending by all of this "forever." So He, may His majesty be praised, addressed them with what they know among themselves, saying: ﴿abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure﴾, and the meaning is: abiding therein forever.

* *

Ibn Zayd used to say in this matter something similar to what we have said.

18572- Yunus related to us, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: ﴿abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure﴾: as long as the earth is earth and the heaven is heaven.

* *

Then He said: ﴿except what your Lord wills﴾. The people of knowledge and interpretation differed regarding the meaning of this. Some of them said: This is an exception made by God regarding the people of monotheism (tawhid), that He will bring them out of the Fire when He wills, after He had caused them to enter it.

Those who said so:

18573- Al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, he said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿As for those who were wretched, they will be in the Fire, for them therein is groaning and wailing, abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord wills﴾, he said: God knows best its exception (thunya) [[al-thunya (with a damma and then a sukun), and al-thunyah, of the pattern fa'ilah, and al-mathnawiyah, all mean "exception".]]

It has been mentioned to us that some people will be touched by a scorching of the Fire because of sins they committed, then God will admit them to Paradise.

18574- Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord wills﴾, and God knows best its exception. [[See note no. 1.]] It has been mentioned to us that some people will be touched by a scorching of the Fire because of sins that befell them, then God will admit them to Paradise by the grace of His mercy; they are called "the Jahannamiyyun".

18575- Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, he said: Shaybân ibn Farrukh related to us, he said: Abu Hilal related to us, he said: Qatadah related to us, and he recited this verse: ﴿As for those who were wretched, they will be in the Fire, for them therein is groaning and wailing﴾, up to His saying ﴿Effecter of what He intends﴾, and then said: Anas ibn Malik related to us that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "A people will come out of the Fire" — Qatadah said: We do not say what the people of Harura say. [[The "people of Harura" are the Kharijites, who say that the perpetrator of a major sin is eternally in the Fire, because they declare the people of major sins to be disbelievers.]]

18576- Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Ya'qub related to us, from Abu Malik, that is Tha'labah, from Abu Sinan regarding His saying: ﴿As for those who were wretched, they will be in the Fire, for them therein is groaning and wailing, abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord wills﴾, he said: It is an exception regarding the people of monotheism.

18577- Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim: ﴿As for those who were wretched, they will be in the Fire﴾, up to His saying ﴿abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord wills﴾, he said: A people will come out of the Fire and enter Paradise; they are the ones who were excepted for.

18578- Al-Muthanna related to me, he said: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih related to us, he said: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Amir ibn Jushayb, from Khalid ibn Ma'dan regarding His saying: ﴿remaining therein for ages﴾ [Surah al-Naba' 78:23], and His saying: ﴿abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord wills﴾, that both are regarding the people of monotheism. [[Report 18578: 'Amir ibn Jushayb al-Himsi narrated from Abu Umamah, Khalid ibn Ma'dan and others; he is trustworthy. He is in al-Tahdhib and Ibn Abi Hatim 3/1/319. In the printed edition it was "Jushab", which is an error; the manuscript is as I have given it, though unpointed. This report will come in the tafsir at 30:8, 9 (Bulaq), in the commentary on Surah al-Naba'.]]

* *

Others said: The exception in this verse concerns the people of monotheism, except that they said: the meaning of His saying ﴿except what your Lord wills﴾ is: except that your Lord wills to overlook them so that He does not cause them to enter the Fire. They directed the exception to His saying ﴿As for those who were wretched, they will be in the Fire﴾ = ﴿except what your Lord wills﴾, not to "abiding".

Those who said so:

18579- Al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, he said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Ibn al-Taymi related to us, from his father, from Abu Nadrah, from Jabir or Abu Sa'id — meaning al-Khudri — or from a man among the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, regarding His saying: ﴿except what your Lord wills; indeed your Lord is the Effecter of what He intends﴾, he said: This verse applies to the whole Qur'an; it means: wherever in the Qur'an there is ﴿abiding therein﴾, this verse applies to it. He said: I heard Abu Mijlaz say: It is its recompense, and if God wills, He will overlook its punishment.

* *

Others said: It refers to the people of the Fire and to everyone who enters it.

Those who said so:

18580- It has been related to me from al-Musayyab, from one he mentioned, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure﴾: they will not die, nor will they leave it, as long as the heavens and the earth endure; ﴿except what your Lord wills﴾: he said: the exception of God. He said: He will command the Fire to consume them. He said: And Ibn Mas'ud said: There will come upon Jahannam a time when its doors will rattle, with no one in it, and that is after they have remained therein for ages.

18581- Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Jarir related to us, from Bayan, from al-Sha'bi who said: Jahannam is the faster of the two abodes to become populated and the faster to become ruined.

* *

Others said: God informed us of His will regarding the people of Paradise, and He explained the meaning of its exception by His saying: ﴿a gift not cut off﴾ [Surah Hud 11:108], meaning that it is an addition beyond the duration of the heavens and the earth. He said: He did not inform us of His will regarding the people of the Fire. It is permissible that His will is for an addition, and it is permissible that it is for a reduction.

Those who said so:

18582- Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: ﴿abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord wills﴾, then he recited until he reached: ﴿a gift not cut off﴾, and said: He informed us of what He wills for the people of Paradise, saying ﴿a gift not cut off﴾, and did not inform us of what He wills for the people of the Fire.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these opinions regarding the interpretation of this verse is the saying we have related from Qatadah and al-Dahhak: that this is an exception regarding the people of monotheism among the people of major sins, that God will cause them to enter the Fire, abiding therein forever, except what He wills of leaving them there for less than that; then He will bring them out and admit them to Paradise, as we have already explained in another place, [[In the printed edition: "kadha qad bayyana", which is weak speech, the scribe's poor writing having caused the error.]] in a way that suffices to dispense with repeating it in this place. [[I have lost track of its location; whoever finds it, let him confirm it.]]

We said that this is the most correct of the sayings, because God, may His majesty be praised, threatened those who associate partners with Him with eternal abiding in the Fire, and reports from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ have consistently established this. It is therefore impermissible that the exception concerns the people of polytheism. And since the reports have been transmitted in mass-transmission (tawatur) from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that God will cause a people among the believers to enter the Fire because of sins they committed, then bring them out of it and admit them to Paradise, it is impermissible that this exception concerns the people of monotheism before their entry, given the soundness of the reports from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that we have mentioned. Moreover, if we made it an exception in that sense, we would have entered into the saying of one who says: "No sinner enters Paradise, and no believer enters the Fire," and that contradicts the positions of the people of knowledge and what the reports from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ have brought. When these two views are thus invalid, no saying held by the leaders among the people of knowledge remains except the third.

* *

The grammarians have a view on this other than that, which we will mention afterwards, and explain, God willing. [[See what follows, pp. 487–489.]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is the Effecter of what He intends﴾, He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Indeed your Lord, O Muhammad, is not prevented by any preventer from doing what He intends to do to those who disobey Him and oppose His command, by way of retribution against them; rather He does what He wills to do, and His action and decree pass upon them and upon whomever among His creation He wills. [[In the printed and manuscript editions: "But He does what He wills, so His action passes upon them and upon whomever among His creation He wills His action and decree", which is not sound; the fault is the copyist's, and the correct text is as I have given it, with the first "fa'luhu" placed before.]]

**Commentary on the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿As for those who were made happy, they will be in the Garden, abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord wills — a gift never cut off.﴾ (11:108)**

Abu Ja'far [al-Tabari] said: The reciters differed over how this is recited.

The majority of the reciters of Madina, the Hijaz and Basra, and some of the Kufans, recited ﴿وَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ سَعِدُوا﴾ with a fatha on the sin.

* *

A group of the Kufan reciters recited it ﴿وَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ سُعِدُوا﴾ with a damma on the sin, meaning: they were granted happiness.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct position on this is that both are well-known readings, and whichever of them the reciter reads, he is right.

* *

If someone says: "How is it said ﴿سُعِدُوا﴾ in the passive form, rather than 'asʿadū' (أسعدوا)? You do not say, in a report where the agent is named, 'saʿadahu Allah' but rather 'asʿadahu Allah'."

It is said: This is like their saying "huwa majnūn" (هو مجنون) and "maḥbūb" (محبوب) in the passive, and when they name the agent they say "ajannahu Allah" and "aḥabbahu," and the Arabs do this often. We have explained some of this earlier in this book. [[The place of it has also escaped me; whoever finds it should note it down.]]

* *

The interpretation (ta'wil) of this is: "As for those who were made happy by the mercy of Allah, they will be in the Garden, abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure," meaning: forever. ﴿Except what your Lord wills﴾.

* *

The people of ta'wil differed over the meaning of this.

Some of them said: ﴿except what your Lord wills﴾ refers to the length of time they remained in the Fire before entering the Garden. They said: this applies to the believers who are brought out of the Fire and admitted to the Garden.

Those who said this:

18583 – Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Dahhak, regarding His saying: ﴿And as for those who were made happy, they will be in the Garden, abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord wills﴾. He said: It also concerns those who come out of the Fire and enter the Garden. He means: abiding in the Garden as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord wills — meaning, except for the time they remained in the Fire until they were admitted to the Garden.

* *

Others said: The meaning of ﴿except what your Lord wills﴾ is an addition beyond the duration of the heavens and the earth. They said: that is the eternal abiding therein, forever.

Those who said this:

18584 – Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Ya'qub narrated to us, from Abu Malik — meaning Tha'laba — from Abu Sinan: regarding ﴿And as for those who were made happy, they will be in the Garden, abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord wills﴾, he said: "His will is their abiding therein," then He followed it with: ﴿a gift never cut off﴾.

* *

The grammarians (ahl al-'Arabiyya) differed over the nature of the exception (istithna') in this place.

Some of them said that there are two meanings to it:

The first: you make it an exception that is stated but not carried out, like your saying: "By Allah, I will strike you — except if I see otherwise," while your resolve is to strike him. He said: Similarly, He says: ﴿abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord wills﴾, and He does not will it. [[In al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an: "and your resolve to strike him"; this is the exact wording of al-Farra's statement.]] [He knows best.] [[The addition between the brackets is from al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an.]]

He said: The other view: when the Arabs make an exception of something large together with something similar to it, and with something even larger than it, the meaning of "illa" (إلا) and of "wa" (الواو) is the same. So whoever says ﴿abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure﴾ = apart from what Allah wills of additional abiding — then "illa" is put in the place of "siwa" (سوى, "apart from"), and it is correct, as if He said: "abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, apart from the additional abiding and eternity He gave them." A similar usage in speech is your saying: "I have a thousand dirhams from you, except two thousand which are from so-and-so." Do you not see that in meaning this is: "I have a thousand from you, apart from the two thousand"? [[In the printed and manuscript editions it reads: "except the two thousand which precede them"; it has none of the remaining text I have set down. It is an obscure statement; I have transcribed the rest and added the bracketed portion from al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an, and this is his exact wording.]] He said: This is the more preferred of the two views in my opinion, because Allah does not break His promise. [[In the printed edition: "there is no breaking of His promise"; in the manuscript: "there is no one to break His promise"; the correct form is from Ma'ani al-Qur'an.]] He has joined the exception with His saying ﴿a gift never cut off﴾, which indicates that the exception concerning them, in His saying about abiding, is not severed from them.

* *

Another of them said something similar to this view. They said: A third possibility is permissible: that He excepted from their abiding in the Garden their being held back from it between death and resurrection, which is the barzakh (the intermediate state), until they arrive at the Garden, and then it is eternal abiding. The meaning is: they were not kept away from the Garden except for the length of their stay in the barzakh.

* *

Another of them said: It is permissible that the duration of the heavens and the earth means eternity, according to what the Arabs know and use, and the exception of the will is made from their duration, because the people of the Garden and the people of the Fire were, at some time during the duration of the heavens and the earth, in the world, not in the Garden. So it is as if He said: abiding in the Garden and abiding in the Fire for the duration of the heavens and the earth, except what your Lord wills of their being kept alive in the world before that.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these views in my opinion is the one I have reported from al-Dahhak, namely ﴿And as for those who were made happy, they will be in the Garden, abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord wills﴾ refers to the length of their stay in the Fire, from the time they entered it until they were admitted to the Garden. The verse then has a specific meaning, because the most well-known usage of the Arabs with "illa" is to direct it toward the sense of exception, excluding what follows from what precedes, unless there is some indication with it that shows otherwise. There is no indication in the speech — I mean in His saying ﴿except what your Lord wills﴾ — showing that its meaning differs from the meaning of exception understood in the speech, so that it should be directed to something else.

* *

As for His saying ﴿a gift never cut off﴾, it means: a gift from Allah not cut off from them.

* *

From their saying: "jadhadhtu al-shay' ajudduhu jadhdhan" (جذذت الشيء أجذه جذًّا), meaning "I cut the thing," as al-Nabigha said:

*It cuts the Salu'i armour, its weave doubled,
and they kindle with the flint the fire of al-Habahib.* [[From his famous qasida, from his divan p. 44, and in Lisan al-'Arab (ḥbḥb, slq, ṣfḥ). In it, before this line, he describes the swords of the Ghassanids, in his praise of 'Amr ibn al-Harith al-A'raj:
"There is no fault in them, except that their swords have notches from the clashing of battalions;
they were inherited from the days of Halima until today, having been tested by every trial."
"...it cuts the Salu'i..." — the rest of this line is missing in the source. The Salu'i are armours, attributed to Salūq, a town. "al-Ṣifāḥ" are broad stones. "Nār al-Ḥabāḥib" is the spark that falls from the flint. The divan's version reads "wa-tawaqqada bi-l-ṣifāḥ," and the two are the same.]] By his saying "tajudhdh" he means: cuts.

* *

The people of ta'wil said things similar to what we have said on this.

Those who said this:

18585 – Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: al-Muharibi narrated to us, from Jawaybir, from al-Dahhak: regarding ﴿a gift never cut off﴾, he said: not severed.

18586 – Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada regarding His saying ﴿a gift never cut off﴾, he said: not ended.

18587 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿a gift never cut off﴾, he said: a gift not cut off.

18588 – Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿never cut off﴾, he said: cut off.

18589 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿a gift never cut off﴾, he said: not cut off.

18590 – ... narrated to us, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

18591 – ... narrated to us, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-'Aliya, the like of it.

18592 – al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.

18593 – ... narrated to me, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliya, regarding His saying: ﴿a gift never cut off﴾, he said: As for this, He has enacted it. He means: a gift not ended.

18594 – Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying ﴿a gift never cut off﴾: not taken away from them.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 109:

The exegesis of His words, exalted is He: ﴿So be not in doubt, [O Muhammad], about what these worship. They worship only as their fathers worshipped before. And indeed, We will give them their portion undiminished.﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: Exalted is His remembrance, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): So do not be in doubt, O Muhammad, about what these polytheists of your people worship of gods and idols [see the explanation of "al-miryah" (doubt) in the preceding indices of language, under m-r-y], that it is misguidance and falsehood, and that it is shirk with God. ﴿They worship only as their fathers worshipped before﴾, meaning: they worship only as their fathers worshipped before them, before their own worship of them. He, exalted is His remembrance, informs that they did not worship what they worshipped of idols except by following the path of their fathers and tracing their footsteps in worshipping them, not by a command from God to them to do so, nor by a proof they had clarified which would make worshipping them obligatory upon them.

Then He, exalted is His praise, informed His Prophet of what He would do with them for their worship of that, saying, exalted is His praise: ﴿And indeed, We will give them their portion undiminished﴾, meaning: their share of what I promised them, that I will pay them in full, of good or evil [see the explanation of "wafi" in the preceding volume 14: 39, footnote 3, and the references there, and the explanation of "al-nasib" (portion) in the preceding volume 12: 408, footnote 3, and the references there]. ﴿Undiminished﴾, he says: I will not diminish them from what I promised them, but I will complete that for them in full and perfection [see the explanation of "al-naqs" (diminution) in the preceding volume 14: 132], as:

18595 - Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And indeed, We will give them their portion undiminished﴾, he said: of what they were promised of good or evil.

18596 - Abu Kurayb and Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, both saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, the like of it, except that Abu Kurayb said in his narration: of good or evil.

18597 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd informed us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Shurayk, from Jabir, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And indeed, We will give them their portion undiminished﴾, he said: what was decreed for them of good and evil.

18598 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from Jabir, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas regarding His words: ﴿And indeed, We will give them their portion undiminished﴾, he said: what befalls them of good or evil.

18599 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: ﴿And indeed, We will give them their portion undiminished﴾, he said: their portion of the punishment.

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says, consoling His Prophet regarding the denial of his people's polytheists of what he brought them from Allah, by the deed of the Children of Israel toward Musa regarding what he brought them from Allah. He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to him: "Do not let grieve you, O Muhammad, the denial of these polytheists of you. Proceed with what your Lord has commanded you of conveying His message, for what these people do to you, by rejecting what you have brought them of counsel, is the deed of their counterparts among the nations before them, and a practice (sunnah) of their ways."

Then He, may His praise be exalted, informed him of what the people of Musa did to him, saying: ﴿And We certainly gave Musa the Book﴾, meaning the Torah, just as We gave you the Criterion (al-Furqan). Then the people of Musa differed concerning that Book: some of them denied it and some of them affirmed it, just as your people have done with the Criterion, some affirming part of it and denying part. ﴿Had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord﴾, He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: had it not been for a word that preceded, O Muhammad, from your Lord, that He does not hasten punishment upon His creation, but gives respite until the Book reaches its appointed term, ﴿it would have been decided between them﴾, meaning: it would have been judged between the one among them who denied it and the one who affirmed it, by the destruction of the denier among them and the deliverance of the affirmer. ﴿And indeed they are in disquieting doubt concerning it﴾, meaning: indeed the deniers among them are in doubt about its reality, whether it is from Allah. ﴿Disquieting (murib)﴾, meaning: it causes them unease, so they do not know whether it is true or false; but they are in dispute concerning it. [Editor's note: See the explanation of "murib" above, p. 370, footnote 1.]

The exegesis on the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And indeed, to all of them your Lord will surely pay in full their deeds. Indeed, He is Acquainted with what they do.﴾ (11:111)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The readers differed concerning the recitation of this.

A group of the readers of Madinah and Kufa recited it: ﴿wa-inna﴾ with the nun doubled, and ﴿kullan lamma﴾ with the mim doubled.

* *

The scholars of Arabic grammar (ahl al-'Arabiyya) differed concerning the meaning of this.

Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: its meaning, when read thus, is: "wa-inna kullan lamimma yuwaffiyannahum Rabbuka a'malahum" — but when the mims came together, one was dropped, leaving two, and one was assimilated into the other, as the poet said: [The poet's identity is unknown.]

"Indeed, I am among those who issue the affair in its proper manner, when its ways have become difficult, its outcomes..." [Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' on the verse. In the printed edition: "lamma" and "a'yā bi-l-nabil", both of which are errors; the correct form is from the manuscript and Ma'ani al-Qur'an. His saying "lamimma" here is not of the type "lamma" that he mentions, except in the coming together of the mims. That is because his saying "wa-inna kullan lamimma yuwaffiyannahum" originally was "lamman mā", "man" with fatha then sukun, a noun. As for the one in the verse, it is "lamman mā", "min" being a preposition, and its meaning is the meaning of "rubba" for multiplicity, and their witness for it is the saying of Abu Hayya al-Numayri (Sibawayh 1:477): "And indeed, among us are those who strike the ram with a blow upon its head that casts out the tongue from the mouth."]

Then it is lightened, as some readers recited: ﴿wa-l-baghyi ya'izukum﴾ [Surat al-Nahl: 90], lightening the ya' with the ya'. [In the manuscript: "takhuff"; in the printed edition: "yukhaffif"; but in Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra', his exact words are: "by deleting the ya'", which is the correct and good reading.] It is mentioned that al-Kisa'i recited to him: [The poet's identity is unknown.]

"And they made the enemies rejoice at us, so they became with me, rejoicing over what we met..." [Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' on the verse; in the printed and manuscript editions: "wa-ashmata al-a'da'", which is an error; the correct form is from Ma'ani al-Qur'an.]

He said: he means "ladayya yatabasharuna bima laqina", so he deleted a ya', because the two are of the same vowel and are together. He said: And similar to it: [The poet's identity is unknown.]

"As if from its last, the approaching, is the cleft of Najd, high in its passes..." [Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra', on the verse. In the printed edition it reads "min ahriha", "mahram", and "al-mahārim", which is an error. "Al-makhram" (with fatha, then sukun, then kasra) is a path in the mountain, its plural being "makhārim".]

He said: he meant "ila al-qadim", so he deleted the lam before the lam.

* *

Others said: its meaning, when read thus, is: "wa-inna kullan shadidan wa-haqqan, la-yuwaffiyannahum Rabbuka a'malahum." He said: what is meant, when read thus, is: "wa-inna kullan lamma" with doubled nun and tanwin. [This is the reading of al-Zuhri, as will come, p. 498.] But the reader who recited it thus dropped the tanwin from it, and pronounced it according to the form of the verb "lamma", as he did in His saying: ﴿Then We sent Our messengers in succession (tatraa)﴾ [Surat al-Mu'minun: 44], where some read "tatra" with tanwin, as one who reads "lamma" with tanwin, and others read it without tanwin, as one who reads "lamma" without tanwin. They said: its origin is from "al-lamm", from the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿and you devour the inheritance with devouring (lamman)﴾, meaning: a severe devouring.

* *

Others said: its meaning, when read thus, is: "wa-inna kullan illa layuwaffiyannahum", as the speaker says: "bi-llahi lamma qumta 'anna, wa-bi-llahi illa qumta 'anna." [In the printed and manuscript editions: "laqad qumta 'anna, wa-bi-llahi illa qumta 'anna", which is an error; there is no evidence in it, and the correct form is from Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra', on the verse.]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: I found that the general body of the scholars of Arabic reject this view, and refuse that it is permissible to direct "lamma" to the meaning of "illa", specifically in an oath. [In the printed edition, the second "illa" is omitted, which spoils the sentence.] They said: if it were permissible for it to have the meaning of "illa", it would be permissible to say "qama al-qawmu lamma akhaka", meaning: "except your brother", and its entry into every place where "illa" fits would be allowed.

Abu Ja'far said: I see that this is corrupt for a reason clearer than what those of the grammarians whose views we have related said regarding its corruption, namely that "inna" is an affirmation of a thing and its confirmation, and "illa" is also a confirmation, and it only enters as an exception to a negation that precedes it. [In the printed and manuscript editions: "wa-illa aydan tahaqqaqa aydan", the first of the two being dropped, since it is a repetition without doubt.] So when that is its meaning, it is necessary that for the one who interprets it in the manner we mentioned from him, "inna" would have the meaning of negation in his view, so that "illa" would be an exception to it. If one says that, it is a saying whose speaker's ignorance is not hidden. Unless the reader lightens "inna" and makes it mean the "inna" that carries the sense of negation. If he does that, his reading "wa-inna kullan" is corrupt in another respect too: he would then be governing "kull" by the verb "layuwaffiyannahum", and in Arabic it is not permitted for a verb after it to govern a noun that precedes "illa". The Arabs do not say "ma Zaydan illa daraabtu", so it is corrupt in this respect if read thus, unless a reader makes "kull" nominative, thereby opposing with his reading that reading of the readers and the script of the Muslims' codices, and he does not escape the fault by departing from the known speech of the Arabs. [In the printed edition: "bi-kharujihi", the correct form being from the manuscript.]

* *

Some of the readers of Kufa recited it: ﴿wa-in kullan﴾ with "in" lightened and "kullan" in the accusative, with ﴿kullan lamma﴾ doubled.

* *

Some grammarians claimed that the reader who recited it thus intended the heavy "inna" and lightened it. He related from Abu Zayd al-Basri that he heard: "ka-an thadyayhi huqqan", governing with "ka-an", the nun lightened from "ka-anna", and from it is the saying of the poet: [From the fifty verses of Sibawayh whose speaker is unknown.]

"And a face bright at the chest, as if its two breasts were two cups..." [Sibawayh 1:281, with nominative "ka-anna thadyahu", and Ibn al-Shajari in his Amali 1:237 with nominative, 2:3 with accusative; al-Khizanah 4:358; and al-'Aini (margin of al-Khizanah) 2:305.]

* *

Some of the people of Madinah recited it with "in" lightened, "kullan" in the accusative, and "lamma" lightened.

* *

It is possible that the reader who recited it thus intended the meaning we related from the Kufan reader, by lightening the nun of "in" while meaning to double it, and by "ma" in "lamma" he meant the particle that enters speech as a filler, [("silah", meaning addition; see the glossary of terms above.)] and that he intended to load the sentence with the meaning: "wa-inna kullan layuwaffiyannahum."

And it may be that his meaning in reciting it thus was: "wa-inna kullan, layuwaffiyannahum", that is, "he will fully pay kullan", so his intention in governing "kull" would be by the verb "layuwaffiyannahum". If he meant that, there is in it the ugliness I mentioned, opposing the speech of the Arabs, because they do not govern, after the oath-lam, a noun preceding it by a verb.

* *

Some of the people of the Hijaz and Basra recited it: ﴿wa-inna﴾ doubled, ﴿kullan lamma﴾ lightened, ﴿layuwaffiyannahum﴾. This reading has two meanings:

One: that its reciter meant: "wa-inna kullan lamanil layuwaffiyannahum Rabbuka a'malahum", directing the "ma" in "lamma" to the meaning of "man", as the Exalted said: ﴿So marry what seems good to you of women (ma tāba lakum mina al-nisā')﴾ [Surat al-Nisa': 3], though its most common use by the Arabs is for other than human beings; and he intends by the lam in "lamma" the lam with which "inna" is received as an answer to it, and by the lam in "layuwaffiyannahum" the lam of oath, which entered between "ma" and its complement, as the Exalted said: ﴿And indeed among you is one who will surely delay (layubatti'anna)﴾ [Surat al-Nisa': 72], and as one says: "hadha ma laghayruhu afdalu minhu."

The other meaning: that "ma" in "lamma" be taken as the "ma" that enters speech as a filler, and the lam in it is the lam by which the answer is given; and the lam in "layuwaffiyannahum" is also the lam by which the answer to "inna" is given, repeated and restated, when that is its place, and the first was something the Arabs place in a non-original position, then they repeat it afterwards in its place, as the poet said: [The poet's identity is unknown.]

"Had my people not been mighty, then truly I would have met a fall, and surely I would have had to face a fatal end..." [Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' on the verse. In the manuscript and printed edition: "masra'i", and I have established what is in Ma'ani al-Qur'an.]

Al-Zuhri recited it, as is related from him: ﴿wa-inna kullan﴾ with "inna" doubled, and ﴿lamma﴾ with tanwin, meaning: severely, truly, and all together.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most sound of these readings in terms of its grounding in the widespread speech of the Arabs is the reading of the one who recites: "wa-inna" with its nun doubled, "kullan lamma" with "ma" lightened, ﴿layuwaffiyannahum Rabbuka﴾, meaning: "And indeed all these whose stories We have related to you, O Muhammad, in this surah, surely to them your Lord will pay in full their deeds, the good of them with abundant reward, and the evil of them with severe punishment." So "ma" means "man", the lam in it is the answer to "inna", and the lam in ﴿layuwaffiyannahum﴾ is the lam of oath.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, He is Acquainted with what they do﴾, the Exalted says: Indeed your Lord, O Muhammad, is "Acquainted" with what these polytheists of your people do; nothing of their deeds is hidden from Him, rather He knows all of it, encompasses it, and will recompense them for all of it. [See the explanation of "khabir" in the preceding linguistic indexes (kh-b-r).]

**The Interpretation of His Words, the Exalted: ﴿So be steadfast as you have been commanded, and [so too] those who turn back with you, and do not transgress. Indeed, He is Seeing of what you do.﴾ (11:112)**

Abu Ja'far said: God, the Exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "So be steadfast, O Muhammad, in obeying your Lord and in the religion with which He sent you, and in calling to it, as your Lord has commanded you" [[See the explanation of "istiqamah" (steadfastness) above, p. 187.]]. ﴿And those who turn back with you﴾ means: and those who return with you to the obedience of God and to acting on what their Lord has commanded them, after their disbelief. ﴿And do not transgress﴾ means: and do not go beyond His command to what He has forbidden you. [[See the explanation of "taghā" (to transgress) above, p. 34, note 3, and the references there.]] ﴿Indeed, He is Seeing of what you do﴾ means: indeed your Lord, O people, is aware of all the deeds you do, both obedience and disobedience. "Seeing" means that He has knowledge of them, nothing of them is hidden from Him, and He observes all of them. [[See the explanation of "baṣīr" (seeing) in the linguistic indexes under the root (ب ص ر), above.]] God, the Exalted, says: So fear God, O people, lest your Lord find you acting contrary to His command, for He has knowledge of what you do, and He is watching over you.

* *

Ibn 'Uyayna used to say, concerning the meaning of His words ﴿So be steadfast as you have been commanded﴾:

18600. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr related to us, from Sufyan, concerning His words ﴿So be steadfast as you have been commanded﴾, that he said: "Be steadfast upon the Qur'an."

18601. Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words ﴿and do not transgress﴾, that he said: "Transgression (ṭughyān) is opposing God and committing His disobedience. That is 'ṭughyān'."

The exegesis (ta'wil) of His words: ﴿And do not incline toward those who have done wrong, lest the Fire touch you, and you will have no protectors other than Allah; then you will not be helped﴾ (11:113).

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Do not incline, O people, toward the words of those who have disbelieved in Allah, so that you accept from them and approve of their deeds, ﴿lest the Fire touch you﴾ by your doing that [[See the explanation of "al-mass" (touching) above, p. 353, note 6, and the references there.]], ﴿and you will have no protectors other than Allah﴾, meaning no helper who will aid you and no ally who will look after you [[See the explanation of "al-awliya'" (protectors) above in the lexical indexes, under (w-l-y).]]. ﴿Then you will not be helped﴾ means: if you do that, Allah will not help you; rather, He will leave you without His help and will give your enemy power over you.

* *

Those who engage in interpretation have said the same as what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

18602. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: 'Abd Allah related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to us, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿And do not incline toward those who have done wrong, lest the Fire touch you﴾, meaning: inclining toward polytheism.

18603. Ibn WakI' related to us, saying: Ibn Yaman related to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-'Aliyah: ﴿And do not incline toward those who have done wrong﴾, he says: do not approve of their deeds.

18604. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-'Aliyah regarding His words: ﴿And do not incline toward those who have done wrong﴾, he says: do not approve of their deeds. He says: "al-rukun" (inclination) is approval.

18605. Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-'Aliyah, regarding His words: ﴿And do not incline toward those who have done wrong﴾, he said: do not approve of their deeds, ﴿lest the Fire touch you﴾.

18606. Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj: ﴿And do not incline toward those who have done wrong﴾, he said: Ibn 'Abbas said: do not lean toward those who have done wrong.

18607. Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah regarding His words: ﴿And do not incline toward those who have done wrong, lest the Fire touch you﴾, he says: do not join the polytheists, from which you have come out.

18608. Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿And do not incline toward those who have done wrong, lest the Fire touch you﴾, he said: "al-rukun" is compromise (idhan). And he recited: ﴿They wish you would compromise, so they would compromise﴾ [Surah al-Qalam: 9]. He said: it means you incline toward them and do not denounce what they say, though they have uttered the grave statements of their disbelief in Allah, His Book and His messengers. He said: This applies only to the people of disbelief and polytheism, not to the people of Islam. As for the people of sins among the people of Islam, Allah knows best their sins and deeds. No one should make a settlement concerning any of the disobedience of Allah, nor incline toward it in that.

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 114 (part 1 of 3):

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And establish the prayer at the two ends of the day and in the first hours of the night. Indeed, good deeds remove evil deeds. That is a reminder for those who remember.﴾ (11:114)

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, exalted is His remembrance, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿And establish the prayer﴾, O Muhammad, meaning: pray. ﴿At the two ends of the day﴾, meaning the morning and the evening.

* *

The people of ta'wil (interpretation, tafsir) differed about which of the evening prayers is meant by this verse, after all of them agreed that the one meant from the morning prayer is the Fajr (dawn prayer).

Some of them said: it means the Zuhr and the 'Asr prayers. They said: both of them belong to the evening prayer.

Among those who said this:

18609. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us. And Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid: ﴿Establish the prayer at the two ends of the day﴾, he said: the Fajr, and the evening prayers, meaning the Zuhr and the 'Asr.

18610. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, similarly.

18611. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿Establish the prayer at the two ends of the day﴾, he said: the prayer of Fajr and the prayer of the evening.

18612. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Aflah ibn Sa'id, who said: I heard Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi say: ﴿Establish the prayer at the two ends of the day﴾, he said: the two ends of the day are the Fajr, the Zuhr and the 'Asr.

18613. Al-Harith narrated to me, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, saying: Abu Ma'shar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi: ﴿Establish the prayer at the two ends of the day﴾, he said: ﴿the two ends of the day﴾, he said: the Fajr, the Zuhr and the 'Asr.

18614. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mughra' narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, regarding His words: ﴿Establish the prayer at the two ends of the day﴾, he said: the Fajr, the Zuhr and the 'Asr.

* *

Others said: it means the Maghrib prayer.

Among those who said this:

18615. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿Establish the prayer at the two ends of the day﴾, he says: the morning prayer and the Maghrib prayer.

18616. Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya narrated to us, from 'Awf, from al-Hasan: ﴿Establish the prayer at the two ends of the day﴾, he said: the morning prayer and the Maghrib.

18617. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿Establish the prayer at the two ends of the day﴾: the Subh (dawn) and the Maghrib.

* *

Others said: it means the 'Asr prayer.

Among those who said this:

18618. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: 'Abda ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, regarding His words: ﴿Establish the prayer at the two ends of the day﴾, he said: the prayer of Fajr and 'Asr.

18619. ... He said: Zayd ibn Hubab narrated to us, from Aflah ibn Sa'id al-Qaba'i, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b: ﴿Establish the prayer at the two ends of the day﴾: the Fajr and the 'Asr.

18620. Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayya narrated to us, saying: Abu Raja' narrated to us, from al-Hasan, regarding His words: ﴿Establish the prayer at the two ends of the day﴾, he said: the prayer of Subh and the prayer of 'Asr.

18621. al-Husayn ibn 'Ali al-Sada'i narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to us, saying: Mubarak narrated to us, from al-Hasan, who said: Allah said to His Prophet: ﴿Establish the prayer at the two ends of the day﴾, he said: ﴿the two ends of the day﴾: the morning and the 'Asr.

18622. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His words: ﴿Establish the prayer at the two ends of the day﴾, meaning the prayer of 'Asr and Subh.

18623. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Mubarak ibn Fudala, from al-Hasan: ﴿Establish the prayer at the two ends of the day﴾: the morning and the 'Asr.

18624. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Zayd ibn Hubab narrated to us, from Aflah ibn Zayd, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b: ﴿Establish the prayer at the two ends of the day﴾: the Fajr and the 'Asr.

18625. Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Amir narrated to us, saying: Qurra narrated to us, from al-Hasan: ﴿Establish the prayer at the two ends of the day﴾, he said: the morning and the 'Asr.

* *

Some of them said: by "the two ends of the day" is meant the Zuhr and the 'Asr, and by His words ﴿and in the first hours of the night﴾ is meant the Maghrib, the 'Isha' and the Subh.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: the most correct of these opinions in my view is the statement of the one who said: "It is the Maghrib prayer," as we have mentioned from Ibn 'Abbas.

We said it is more correct because all of them agreed that the prayer of one of the two ends is the Fajr, which is prayed before sunrise. Therefore, since this is an agreement from all of them, it is necessary that the prayer of the other end be the Maghrib, because it is prayed after sunset. And if it were necessary that the prayer of one of the two ends be meant before sunset, it would be necessary that the prayer of the other end be meant after its rising; and we know of no one who has said that, except the one who said: "It means the Zuhr and the 'Asr." That is an opinion whose corruption is not unclear [[In the printed edition: "lā nuḥīlu fasādahu" ("we do not regard its corruption as dubious"), which is an incoherent statement; in the manuscript it is undotted. One says "akhāla al-shay'" meaning it became confused; "hādhā al-amr lā yukhīlu 'alā aḥad" means it is not ambiguous to anyone; and "shay' mukhayyal" means problematic. A similar usage has passed and I commented on it at the beginning of the book, in several places.]], because both of them, in that they are both from the prayer of one of the two ends, are closer than they are to being from the prayer of the two ends of the day.
