This is because the Zuhr is undoubtedly prayed after half of the day has passed, in the second half of it, so it is impossible that it be from the first end of the day when it is at the other end.

Since no scholar says that the prayer at the first end of the day means a prayer after sunrise, it must be impermissible to say that the prayer at the other end of the day means a prayer before its setting.

And since that is so, what we have said on this matter is correct, and what contradicts it is invalid.

* *

As for His words: ﴿and in the first hours of the night﴾, it means: hours of the night.

* *

It is the plural of zulfa, and zulfa means an hour, a station, and nearness. It has been said that Muzdalifa and jam' were so named from this, because it is a station after 'Arafa. It has also been said that it was named so because Adam drew near (izdilaf) to Eve there, while she was there. From this is al-'Ajjaj's verse describing a camel:

A swift one, whom weariness has folded, and who is exhausted... the folding of the nights, zulfan after zulfan.

[[Diwan: 84; Majaz al-Qur'an 1:300; Sibawayh 1:180; and Lisan (z-l-f, h-q-f, s-m-a, w-j-f) and many others; it will come in the Tafsir 19:51 (Bulaq). After it there is: "the height of the crescent until it bent."
"Al-ayn" means fatigue. "Wajafa" from "al-wajif," which is rapid travel. "Samawat al-hilal" is its figure when it rises a little on the horizon. "Ihqawqafa" means it became crooked.]]

* *

The readers differed regarding how this is recited.

The majority of the readers of Medina and Iraq recited it: ﴿wa-zulafan﴾, with a damma on the zay and a fatha on the lam.

Some of the Medinan readers recited it with a damma on the zay and the lam, as if they directed it to being singular, and that it is like "ḥulum" (a pattern of singular/plural).

Some of the Meccan readers recited: ﴿wa-zulfan﴾, with a damma on the zay and a sukun on the lam.

Abu Ja'far said: the recitation most preferred by me is to recite it: ﴿wa-zulafan﴾, with a damma on the zay and a fatha on the lam, in the sense of the plural of zulfa, just as ghurfa is pluralized as ghuraf and ḥujra as ḥujar.

I chose this recitation because the late 'Isha' prayer is only prayed after passing zulaf of the night, and that is what I believe is meant by His words: ﴿and zulafan min al-layl﴾.

* *

In agreement with what we have said regarding His words ﴿and in the first hours of the night﴾, a group of the people of ta'wil has spoken.

Among those who said this:

18626. Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the words of Allah: ﴿and zulafan min al-layl﴾, he said: the hours of the night: the 'atama prayer.

18627. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

18628. al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, similarly.

18629. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿zulafan min al-layl﴾, he says: the 'atama prayer.

18630. Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya narrated to us, from 'Awf, from al-Hasan: ﴿wa-zulafan min al-layl﴾, he said: the 'Isha'.

18631. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Adam narrated to us, from Sufyan, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Yazid, who said: Ibn 'Abbas used to like delaying the 'Isha' and would recite: ﴿wa-zulafan min al-layl﴾.

18632. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿wa-zulafan min al-layl﴾, he said: an hour of the night: the 'atama prayer.

18633. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿wa-zulafan min al-layl﴾, he said: the 'atama. I did not hear any of our jurists and shaykhs say "'Isha'"; they say only "'atama."

* *

Some people said: the prayer which the Prophet (ﷺ) was commanded to establish at the times of zulaf of the night is the Maghrib and the 'Isha'.

Among those who said this:

18634. Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim and Ibn Waki' narrated to me, and the wording is Ya'qub's, both saying: Ibn 'Ulayya narrated to us, saying: Abu Raja' narrated to us, from al-Hasan: ﴿wa-zulafan min al-layl﴾, he said: they are two zulafs of the night: the Maghrib prayer and the 'Isha' prayer.

18635. Ibn Humayd and Ibn Waki' narrated to us, both saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Ash'ath, from al-Hasan regarding His words: ﴿wa-zulafan min al-layl﴾, he said: the Maghrib and the 'Isha'.

18636. al-Hasan ibn 'Ali narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to us, saying: Mubarak narrated to us, from al-Hasan, who said: Allah said to His Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿Establish the prayer at the two ends of the day and in zulafan of the night﴾, he said: ﴿zulafan min al-layl﴾: the Maghrib and the 'Isha'. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "They are the two zulafs of the night, the Maghrib and the 'Isha'."

18637. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, and Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid: ﴿wa-zulafan min al-layl﴾, he said: the Maghrib and the 'Isha'.

18638. al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, similarly.

18639. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, similarly.

18640. ... He said: Suwayd narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from al-Mubarak ibn Fudala, from al-Hasan, who said: Allah has explained the times of prayer in the Qur'an. He said: ﴿Establish the prayer from the decline of the sun until the darkness of the night﴾ (17:78). He said: "its decline" is when it moves away from the middle of the sky and there is a shadow on the earth. And He said: ﴿Establish the prayer at the two ends of the day﴾, the morning and the 'Asr; ﴿and zulafan min al-layl﴾, the Maghrib and the 'Isha'. He said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "They are the two zulafs of the night, the Maghrib and the 'Isha'."

18641. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: ﴿wa-zulafan min al-layl﴾, he said: it means the Maghrib prayer and the 'Isha' prayer.

18642. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Aflah ibn Sa'id, who said: I heard Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi say: ﴿zulafan min al-layl﴾: the Maghrib and the 'Isha'.

18643. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Zayd ibn Hubab narrated to us, from Aflah ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b, similarly.

18644. al-Harith narrated to me, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, saying: Abu Ma'shar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi: ﴿wa-zulafan min al-layl﴾: the Maghrib and the 'Isha'.

18645. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from 'Asim ibn Sulayman, from al-Hasan, who said: the two zulafs of the night: the Maghrib and the 'Isha'.

18646. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mughra' narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak regarding His words: ﴿wa-zulafan min al-layl﴾, he said: the Maghrib and the 'Isha'.

18647. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from 'Asim, from al-Hasan: ﴿wa-zulafan min al-layl﴾, he said: the Maghrib and the 'Isha'.

18648. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: 'Abda ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak: ﴿wa-zulafan min al-layl﴾, he said: the Maghrib and the 'Isha'.

18649. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from 'Asim, from al-Hasan: ﴿zulafan min al-layl﴾, the prayer of the Maghrib and the 'Isha'.

* *

His words: ﴿Indeed, good deeds remove evil deeds﴾ mean: Allah, exalted is His remembrance, says: indeed, turning in repentance to the obedience of Allah and acting in what pleases Him removes the consequences of disobedience to Allah and expiates sins. [[Al-athām is the punishment and recompense for sin. As for al-āthām, it is the plural of ithm, which is the wolf.]]

* *

Then the people of ta'wil differed about the good deeds which Allah means in this place, which remove evil deeds. Some of them said: they are the five obligatory prayers.

Among those who said this:

18650. Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayya narrated to us, from al-Juraymi, from Abu al-Ward ibn Thumama, from Abu Muhammad ibn al-Hadrami, who said: Ka'b narrated to us in this mosque, saying: By Him in whose hand is Ka'b's soul, indeed the five prayers are the good deeds which remove evil deeds, just as water washes away dirt. [[Report 18650: "al-Juraymi" is Sa'id ibn Iyas al-Juraymi, mentioned before many times. "Abu al-Ward ibn Thumama ibn Hazn al-Qushayri," also said to be "Thumama ibn Hazn," a reliable Successor who did not meet any Companion other than one or two, and who narrated little. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, Ibn Sa'd 7/1/164, al-Kuna of al-Bukhari: 79, Ibn Abi Hatim 4/2/451 under the kunya, and under "Thumama ibn Hazn al-Qushayri" 1/1/465. He is not said to be "Abu al-Ward" there, so they seem to be two men in his view. "Abu Muhammad ibn al-Hadrami" appears this way in the manuscript and the printed edition; but in the books of biography it is "Abu Muhammad al-Hadrami," the client of Abu Ayyub al-Ansari, biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kuna of al-Bukhari: 66, and Ibn Abi Hatim 4/2/432. They do not mention a narration from Ka'b, but this report indicates that he saw him, heard from him and narrated from him.]]

18651. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Aflah, who said: I heard Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi say regarding His words: ﴿Indeed, good deeds remove evil deeds﴾: they are the five prayers.

18652. al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from 'Abd Allah ibn Muslim, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Indeed, good deeds remove evil deeds﴾, he said: the five prayers.

18653. ... He said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from Mansur, from Mujahid: ﴿Indeed, the good deeds﴾: the prayers.

18654. Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya narrated to us, and Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Abu Usama narrated to us, both from 'Awf, from al-Hasan: ﴿Indeed, good deeds remove evil deeds﴾, he said: the five prayers.

18655. Zurayq ibn al-Sakht narrated to me, saying: Qabisa narrated to us, from Sufyan, from 'Abd Allah ibn Muslim, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas: "Indeed, good deeds remove evil deeds," he said: the five prayers. [[Report 18655: "Zurayq ibn al-Sakht" is a teacher of al-Tabari, mentioned under number 10051. In the printed edition and the manuscript here it appears as "... ibn al-Shakhb," which is an error.]]

18656. al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Amr ibn 'Awn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak regarding His words: ﴿Indeed, good deeds remove evil deeds﴾, he said: the five prayers.

18657. al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Amr ibn 'Awn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from Mansur, from al-Hasan, who said: the five prayers.

18658. al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: al-Hammani narrated to us, saying: Shurayk narrated to us, from Simak, from Ibrahim, from 'Alqama, from 'Abd Allah: ﴿Indeed, good deeds remove evil deeds﴾, he said: the five prayers.

18659. ... He said: Suwayd narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Sa'id al-Juraymi, who said: Abu 'Uthman narrated to me, from Salman, who said: By Him in whose hand is my soul, indeed the good deeds by which Allah erases evil deeds are, just as water washes away dirt, the five prayers.

18660. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us, from 'Abd Allah ibn Muslim, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Indeed, good deeds remove evil deeds﴾, he said: the five prayers.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 114 (part 2 of 3):

18661. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: 'Abdullah narrated to us, from Isrā'īl, from Abū Ishāq, from Mazīdah ibn Zayd, from Masrūq, regarding ﴿Indeed, good deeds remove bad deeds﴾, that he said: "The five prayers." [[The narration 18661: "Mazīdah ibn Zayd" is as it stands in the printed edition. In the manuscript it is unpointed, and I have not found any mention of him in any of the books of biographical evaluation (rijal). I fear it may be a corruption of something I have not identified.]]

18662. Muhammad ibn 'Umārah al-Asadī and 'Abdullah ibn Abī Ziyād al-Qaṭawānī narrated to me, both saying: 'Abdullah ibn Yazīd narrated to us, saying: Ḥaywah informed us, saying: Abū 'Aqīl Zuhrah ibn Ma'bad al-Qurashī, from the Banū Taym, from the kin group (rahṭ) of Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq (may Allah be pleased with him), informed us that he heard al-Ḥārith, the client (mawlā) of 'Uthmān ibn 'Affān (may Allah have mercy on him), say: 'Uthmān sat one day and we sat with him. The muezzin came, so 'Uthmān called for water in a vessel, which I think contained about a mudd, ["al-mudd" (with a damma on the m), a type of measure. It is said that it is measured by a man stretching out his hands and filling his palms with food.] and he performed ablution. Then he said: "I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) perform ablution like this ablution of mine. Then he said: Whoever performs ablution like this ablution of mine, then stands and prays the Dhuhr prayer, will be forgiven what is between it and the Fajr prayer; then he prays 'Asr and will be forgiven what is between it and the Dhuhr prayer; then he prays Maghrib and will be forgiven what is between it and the 'Asr prayer; then he prays 'Ishā' and will be forgiven what is between it and the Maghrib prayer; then perhaps he spends his night rolling about [["al-tamarrugh", its origin is turning over in the dust. What is meant here is that he spends the night turning over on his bed, at ease and with a tranquil mind.] Then, if he rises, performs ablution and prays Fajr, he will be forgiven what is between it and the 'Ishā' prayer. And these are the good deeds that remove bad deeds." [[The narration 18662: "Ḥaywah" is Ḥaywah ibn Shurayḥ al-Miṣrī, the jurist and ascetic, a trustworthy narrator who was frequently cited. "Zuhrah ibn Ma'bad al-Qurashī al-Taymī", "Abū 'Aqīl", is a trustworthy Successor (tābi'ī); he passed with the numbers 5451 and 5457. "Al-Ḥārith" is al-Ḥārith ibn 'Ubayd, "Abū Ṣāliḥ", the client of 'Uthmān, a trustworthy narrator, whose biography is in Ta'jīl al-Manfa'ah (78) and Ibn Abī Ḥātim (1/2/95). This report has a sound chain of narration. Aḥmad narrated it in his Musnad in full, number 513, and my brother (may Allah have mercy on him) completed the discussion of it there. It was also narrated by al-Haythamī in Majma' al-Zawā'id (1:297) and Ibn Kathīr in his tafsir (4:401 / 5:289).
= The addition found in the Musnad and elsewhere:
"They said: These are the good deeds, so what are the enduring good deeds, O 'Uthmān? He said: They are: There is no god but Allah, Glory be to Allah, Praise be to Allah, Allah is greatest, and there is no power nor strength except through Allah." This addition will come separately with these chains in the tafsir of surah al-Kahf, verse 46, vol. 15: 165, 166.]]

18663. Sa'd ibn 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Ḥakam narrated to me, saying: Abū Zur'ah narrated to us, saying: Ḥaywah narrated to us, saying: Abū 'Aqīl Zuhrah ibn Ma'bad narrated to us, that he heard al-Ḥārith, the client of 'Uthmān ibn 'Affān (may Allah be pleased with him), say: 'Uthmān ibn 'Affān sat one day on the benches (al-maqā'id) ... and he mentioned something similar from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), except that he said: "And these are the good deeds: indeed, good deeds remove bad deeds." [[The narration 18663: a repetition of the previous report. "Abū Zur'ah" is Wahb Allah ibn Rāshid al-Miṣrī, who has passed many times. "Al-maqā'id" (the benches), in Madinah, near the gate of al-Aqbar; it is said they are the raised platforms around it, and it is said they are shops near the house of 'Uthmān ibn 'Affān (may Allah be pleased with him), mentioned by Yāqūt in his dictionary (Mu'jam). I also saw the mention of "al-maqā'id" in the Musnad of Aḥmad, in the Musnad of 'Uthmān, number 505.]]

18664. Ibn al-Barqī narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abī Maryam narrated to us, saying: Nāfi' ibn Yazīd and Rushdīn ibn Sa'd informed us, both saying: Zuhrah ibn Ma'bad narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Ḥārith, the client of 'Uthmān ibn 'Affān, say: 'Uthmān ibn 'Affān sat one day on the benches, then he mentioned something similar from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), except that he said: "And these are the good deeds: ﴿Indeed, good deeds remove bad deeds﴾." [[The narration 18664: a repetition of the two previous reports. "Rushdīn ibn Sa'd" is weak; he has passed many times, including numbers 19, 1938, 2176, 2195, and elsewhere. But this report has a witness from what preceded in the Ṣiḥāḥ (the authentic collections), which strengthens it despite Rushdīn's weakness.]]

18665. Muhammad ibn 'Awf narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ismā'īl narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, saying: Ḍamḍam ibn Zur'ah narrated to us, from Shurayḥ ibn 'Ubayd, from Abū Mālik al-Ash'arī, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The prayers have been made expiations for what is between them, for Allah has said: ﴿Indeed, good deeds remove bad deeds﴾." [[The narration 18665: "Muhammad ibn 'Awf ibn Sufyān al-Ṭā'ī al-Ḥimṣī" is the teacher of al-Ṭabarī, who has passed many times. "Muhammad ibn Ismā'īl ibn 'Ayyāsh al-Ḥimṣī" is weak; he narrated from his father and did not hear anything from him; he passed with number 5445. His father: "Ismā'īl ibn 'Ayyāsh al-Ḥimṣī", trustworthy but spoken of (mutakallam fīh), who has passed many times, the last being number 14212. "Ḍamḍam ibn Zur'ah ibn Thawb al-Ḥaḍramī", trustworthy, though Abū Ḥātim weakened him; he passed with numbers 5445 and 14212. "Shurayḥ ibn 'Ubayd ibn Shurayḥ al-Ḥaḍramī", a trustworthy Successor, who passed with numbers 5445, 12194 and 14212. This report is weak in its chain, due to the defect of "Muhammad ibn Ismā'īl from his father". al-Haythamī also cited it in abridged form in Majma' al-Zawā'id (1:299), and said: "In it is Muhammad ibn Ismā'īl ibn 'Ayyāsh; Abū Ḥātim said: he did not hear anything from his father." I say: this is from his narration from his father. The rest of its narrators are trustworthy.]]

18666. Ibn Sayyār al-Qazzāz narrated to us, saying: al-Ḥajjāj narrated to us, saying: Ḥammād narrated to us, from 'Alī ibn Zayd, from Abū 'Uthmān al-Nahdī, who said: I was with Salmān under a tree, and he took a branch from its branches, dry, and shook it until its leaves fell off. Then he said: Thus did the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) do. I was with him under a tree, and he took a branch from its branches, dry, and shook it until its leaves fell off. Then he said: "Will you not ask me why I did this, O Salmān?" I said: "And why did you do it?" He said: "When a Muslim performs ablution and does it well, then prays the five prayers, his sins fall away just as these leaves have fallen." Then he recited this verse: ﴿Establish prayer at the two ends of the day and in the first hours of the night﴾, to the end of the verse. [[The narration 18666: "Ḥammād" is Ḥammād ibn Salamah. "'Alī ibn Zayd ibn Jud'ān": the scholars' statements about him have passed many times, and that he had poor memory; and also my brother, Sayyid Aḥmad (may Allah have mercy on him), had passed his verification of the reliability of his narration. "Abū 'Uthmān al-Nahdī" is 'Abd al-Raḥmān ibn Mull, a trustworthy Successor. This report was narrated by Aḥmad in his Musnad (5:437, 438), through 'Affān from Ḥammād in a wording close to Abū Ja'far's version, and through Yazīd from Ḥammād with a different wording. Abū Ja'far will narrate it again later, through Qabīṣah from Ḥammād, number 18677. al-Haythamī cited it in Majma' al-Zawā'id (1:297, 298) and said: "Aḥmad narrated it, and al-Ṭabarānī in al-Awsaṭ and al-Kabīr. In Aḥmad's chain is 'Alī ibn Zayd, whose use as evidence is disputed. The rest of its narrators are the narrators of the Ṣaḥīḥ."]]

* *

Others said: It is the statement: "Glory be to Allah, praise be to Allah, there is no god but Allah, Allah is greatest."

Mention of those who said this:

18667. al-Muthannā narrated to me, saying: al-Ḥammānī narrated to us, saying: Sharīk narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Mujāhid, regarding ﴿Indeed, good deeds remove bad deeds﴾, that he said: "Glory be to Allah, praise be to Allah, there is no god but Allah, Allah is greatest."

* *

Abū Ja'far said: The most correct of the two interpretations is the statement of the one who said: "They are the five prayers." This is because of the soundness of the reports from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and their mass transmission (tawātur) from him, that he said: "The example of the five prayers is the example of a flowing river at the door of one of you, in which he bathes five times every day. What dirt would remain on him?" [[This report Abū Ja'far narrated without a chain. Mālik narrated a similar wording in al-Muwaṭṭa' p. 174, from the hadith of Sa'd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ. al-Bukhārī narrated something similar from the hadith of Abū Hurayrah (al-Fatḥ 2:9), and Muslim in his Ṣaḥīḥ (5:169, 170).] And because this (the mention of the prayers) is in the context of Allah's command to establish the prayers, and the promise of great reward for establishing them immediately following it, is more fitting than a promise about the good deeds of all other acts of worship not mentioned, when the intention is specifically directed to some and not others.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿That is a reminder for those who remember﴾, He, may He be exalted, means: this which I have promised for abandoning oneself to wrongdoing, and about which I have warned, and what I have promised in establishing the prayers which remove bad deeds, is a reminder with which I have admonished a people who remember the promise of Allah, so they hope for His reward and fear His punishment, not those whose hearts have been sealed so that they answer no caller and hear no admonisher.

* *

It is mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning a man who had obtained, from other than his wife or his right hand's possession, some of what was forbidden to him, and then repented of that sin.

Mention of the narration regarding that:

18668. Hannād ibn al-Sarī narrated to us, saying: Abū al-Aḥwaṣ narrated to us, from Simāk, from Ibrāhīm, from 'Alqamah and al-Aswad, who both said: 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ūd said: A man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "I was intimate with a woman in some outskirts of Madinah [""'Ālajtu imra'ah", meaning he took her and enjoyed her, from "al-mu'ālajah", which means handling. This is a eloquent and concise expression.] and I did with her what is less than touching her. Here I am, so judge me as you wish!" 'Umar said: Allah would have covered you if you had covered yourself! He said: The Prophet (ﷺ) did not answer him with anything. The man rose and went away, so the Prophet (ﷺ) sent a man after him and called him. When he came, he recited to him: ﴿Establish prayer at the two ends of the day and in the first hours of the night. Indeed, good deeds remove bad deeds. That is a reminder for those who remember.﴾ A man among the people said: "Is this for him alone, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "No, rather for all of mankind." [[The narration 18668: the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ūd, which Abū Ja'far narrated through two routes: 1 - through 'Alqamah and al-Aswad, from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ūd, numbers 18668 to 18674; 2 - through Abū 'Uthmān al-Nahdī, from Ibn Mas'ūd, number 18676. I will explain them all, one by one, and all of them are sound routes. "Ibrāhīm" is Ibrāhīm ibn Yazīd al-Nakha'ī, whom the group narrated from, and he has passed many times. "Al-Aswad ibn Yazīd al-Nakha'ī", whom the group narrated from, and he is the maternal uncle of Ibrāhīm ibn Yazīd al-Nakha'ī, has passed many times. "'Alqamah" is 'Alqamah ibn Qays ibn 'Abdullah al-Nakha'ī, and he is the maternal uncle of Ibrāhīm al-Nakha'ī, because he is the paternal uncle of his two maternal uncles, al-Aswad and 'Abd al-Raḥmān; the group narrated from him, and he has passed many times. Through Abū al-Aḥwaṣ, from Simāk, from Ibrāhīm, Muslim narrated it in his Ṣaḥīḥ (17:80), Abū Dāwūd in his Sunan (4:223, number 4468), and al-Tirmidhī in the Book of Tafsir. See the commentary on the following routes. Then see the commentary on number 18675, regarding the naming of the "man" who did that.]]

18669. Abū Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Wakī' narrated to us, and Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Isrā'īl, from Simāk ibn Ḥarb, from Ibrāhīm, from 'Alqamah and al-Aswad, from 'Abdullah, who said: A man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I met a woman in an orchard, and I embraced her, touched her, kissed her, and did everything with her except that I did not have intercourse with her." The Prophet (ﷺ) remained silent about him, and then this verse was revealed: ﴿Indeed, good deeds remove bad deeds. That is a reminder for those who remember.﴾ The Prophet (ﷺ) called him and recited it to him. 'Umar said: "O Messenger of Allah, is it for him alone, or for all of mankind?" He said: "No, rather for all of mankind." The wording of the hadith is that of Ibn Wakī'. [[The narration 18669: a repetition of the previous one. Through Wakī', from Isrā'īl, from Simāk, Aḥmad narrated it in his Musnad, number 4250.]]

18670. al-Ḥasan ibn Yaḥyā narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzāq informed us, saying: Isrā'īl informed us, from Simāk ibn Ḥarb, that he heard Ibrāhīm ibn Yazīd narrate from 'Alqamah and al-Aswad, from Ibn Mas'ūd, who said: A man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I found a woman in an orchard, and I did everything with her except that I did not have intercourse with her. I kissed her and embraced her, and I did nothing other than that, so do to me what you wish!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said nothing to him. The man left, and 'Umar said: "Allah would have covered him if he had covered himself!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) followed him with his gaze, and said: "Bring him back to me!" They brought him back, and he recited to him: ﴿Establish prayer at the two ends of the day and in the first hours of the night. Indeed, good deeds remove bad deeds. That is a reminder for those who remember.﴾ He said: Then Mu'ādh ibn Jabal said: "Is it for him alone, O Prophet of Allah, or for all of mankind?" He said: "No, rather for all of mankind." [[The narration 18670: a repetition of the previous one. Through 'Abd al-Razzāq, from Isrā'īl, from Simāk, Aḥmad narrated it in his Musnad, number 4290.]]

18671. al-Muthannā narrated to me, saying: al-Ḥammānī narrated to us, saying: Abū 'Awānah narrated to us, from Simāk, from Ibrāhīm, from 'Alqamah and al-Aswad, from 'Abdullah, who said: A man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I took a woman in the orchard and did everything with her except that I did not marry her, so do with me as you wish!" The Prophet (ﷺ) was silent. When he left, he called him back and recited to him this verse: ﴿Establish prayer at the two ends of the day and in the first hours of the night﴾, the verse. [[The narration 18671: a repetition of the previous one. Through Abū 'Awānah, from Simāk, Aḥmad narrated it in his Musnad, number 4291, but he referred it to the previous one. Abū Dāwūd al-Ṭayālisī also narrated it in his Musnad, p. 37, number 285.]]

18672. Muhammad ibn al-Muthannā narrated to us, saying: Abū al-Nu'mān al-Ḥakam ibn 'Abdullah al-'Ijlī narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Simāk ibn Ḥarb, who said: I heard Ibrāhīm narrate from his maternal uncle al-Aswad, from 'Abdullah: that a man met a woman on some of the roads of Madinah, and touched her short of intercourse. He came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and told him about that, so this was revealed: ﴿Establish prayer at the two ends of the day and in the first hours of the night. Indeed, good deeds remove bad deeds. That is a reminder for those who remember.﴾ Mu'ādh ibn Jabal said: "O Messenger of Allah, is this specific to him, or general to us?" He said: "No, rather general to you." [[The narration 18672: "al-Ḥakam ibn 'Abdullah al-'Ijlī", "Abū al-Nu'mān", a trustworthy and retentive narrator, who passed with numbers 10185, 17013 and 18033. Through this route, Muslim narrated it in his Ṣaḥīḥ (17:80, 81).]]

18673. Ibn al-Muthannā narrated to us, saying: Abū Dāwūd narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, saying: Simāk informed me, saying: I heard Ibrāhīm narrate from his maternal uncle, from Ibn Mas'ūd: that a man said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "I met a woman in a ḥushsh in Madinah, [""Al-ḥushsh", the orchard, among the people of Madinah; see what has passed, number 3086.] and I did with her what is less than intercourse," similarly. [[The narration 18673: I have not found it in the Musnad of Abū Dāwūd al-Ṭayālisī, and it is known that the printed version of this Musnad is incomplete and not whole. See the following note. In the printed and manuscript editions: "Abū al-Muthannā", and the correct form is "Ibn al-Muthannā", who is Muhammad ibn al-Muthannā, the teacher of al-Ṭabarī.]]

18674. Ibn al-Muthannā narrated to us, saying: Abū Qaṭan 'Amr ibn al-Haytham al-Baghdādī narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Simāk, from Ibrāhīm, from his maternal uncle, from Ibn Mas'ūd, from the Prophet (ﷺ), similar to it. [[The narration 18674: "'Amr ibn al-Haytham al-Baghdādī", "Abū Qaṭan", trustworthy, one of the trustworthy companions of Shu'bah. He is in al-Tahdhīb and Ibn Abī Ḥātim (3/1/268). Through this route, Aḥmad narrated it in his Musnad, number 4325. My brother Sayyid Aḥmad said: "His maternal uncle is either al-Aswad ibn Yazīd al-Nakha'ī, or 'Abd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd al-Nakha'ī, for both are his maternal uncles, or 'Alqamah ibn Qays al-Nakha'ī, the paternal uncle of al-Aswad and 'Abd al-Raḥmān. Ibrāhīm narrated the hadith from all three of them, in full and abridged form, as has passed with chains numbered 3854, 4250, 4290, and 4291." It was narrated by Aḥmad under number 3584 through Sufyān al-Thawrī, from Simāk, from Ibrāhīm, from 'Abd al-Raḥmān ibn Yazīd, from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ūd, and narrated by al-Tirmidhī in the Book of Tafsir.]]

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 114 (part 3 of 3):**

18675. Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, saying: Abu Mu'awiya narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, who said: A man named Fulan ibn Mu'attib, a man of the Ansar, came and said: "O Messenger of Allah, a woman came to me and I did with her what a man does with his wife, except that I did not have intercourse with her." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not know how to answer him, until this verse was revealed: ﴿Establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approaches of the night. Indeed, good deeds remove evil deeds﴾, [the verse] to its end. So he called him and recited it to him. [[Report 18675: The Hafiz Ibn Hajar, in al-Fath (8:268-269), discussed the name of this man. He mentioned this report and then said: "Ibn Abi Khaythama also narrated it, but he said: 'A man of the Ansar called Mu'attib…'" It has also come that his name was Ka'b ibn 'Amr, and [he is] Abu al-Yusr (with a fatha on the ya' and the unpointed letter) al-Ansari. Al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and al-Bazzar narrated it through Musa ibn Talha, from Abu al-Yusr ibn 'Amr, that a woman came to him while her husband had been sent by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on an expedition," [and so on, the hadith], and it will come under numbers 18684 and 18685.]]

18676. Ya'qub and Ibn Wakī' narrated to me, both saying: Ibn 'Ulayya narrated to us. And Humayd ibn Mas'ada said: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us. And Ibn 'Abd al-A'la said: al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, all of them from Sulayman al-Taymi, from Abu 'Uthman, from Ibn Mas'ud: that a man had touched a woman in some way, I do not know how far it went, except that it was less than fornication. He came to the Prophet ﷺ and mentioned that to him, and this was revealed: ﴿Establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approaches of the night. Indeed, good deeds remove evil deeds﴾. The man said: "Is this for me, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "It is for whoever of my community acts upon it" — or: "for whoever does it." [[Report 18676: This is the second route for the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, as I indicated in the note on number 18668. "Abu 'Uthman" is 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mill al-Nahdi, as has passed many times. This is a sound hadith. Through this route al-Bukhari narrated it in his Sahih (al-Fath 2:7), from Yazid ibn Zuray', from Sulayman al-Taymi. He also narrated it again (al-Fath 8:268-269) through the same route with a slightly different wording. Muslim narrated it in his Sahih (17:79-80) through Yazid ibn Zuray' from Sulayman al-Taymi, and then through Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la from al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman from Sulayman al-Taymi, which is one of Abu Ja'far's routes for this report, with different wording. Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad under number 3653 from Yahya from Sulayman al-Taymi, and again under number 4094 through the same route. Ibn Maja narrated it in his Sunan, p. 447, number 1398, and p. 1421, number 4254. Al-Tirmidhi narrated it in the Book of Tafsir.]]

18677. Abu Kurayb and Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, both saying: Qabisa narrated to us, from Hammad ibn Salama, from 'Ali ibn Zayd, from Abu 'Uthman, who said: I was with Salman, when he took a branch of a dry tree and shook it, and said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: Whoever performs ablution and does it well, his sins fall away just as these leaves fall away!" Then he recited: ﴿Establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approaches of the night﴾, to the end of the verse. [[Report 18677: This is another route for the report that passed as number 18666, and its takhrij and explanation were given there.]]

18678. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Usama and Husayn al-Ju'fi narrated to us, from Za'ida, who said: 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from Mu'adh, who said: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, what do you think of a man who met a woman he did not know, and he did with her everything a man does with his wife, except that he did not have intercourse with her?" [[In the printed edition: "ghayr annahu lam yujami'uha" ("except that he did not have intercourse with her"), which differs from the manuscript, and the manuscript reading is the sound and good one.]] So Allah revealed this verse: ﴿Establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approaches of the night. Indeed, good deeds remove evil deeds. That is a reminder for those who remember﴾. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "Perform ablution and then pray." Mu'adh said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, is this specific to him, or is it general for the believers?" He said: "Rather, it is general for the believers." [[Report 18678: This is the hadith of Mu'adh, which will also come under number 18682. "Abu Usama" is Hammad ibn Usama, a trustworthy narrator whom the group (of compilers) narrated from, and who has passed many times. "Husayn al-Ju'fi" is Husayn ibn 'Ali al-Ju'fi, trustworthy, whom the group narrated from, and who has passed many times. "Za'ida" is Za'ida ibn Qudama, trustworthy, who has passed many times. "'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr al-Lakhmi," known as al-Nabti, is trustworthy, whom the group narrated from, and has passed under number 12573. "'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla al-Ansari" is trustworthy, whom the group narrated from, and has passed many times, including numbers 33, 2156 and 2937. This is a sound chain. Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad 5:244 through 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi and Abu Sa'id, from Za'ida, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr, and in it is the narration of Abu Sa'id directly from 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr. "Abu Sa'id" is 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Abd Allah, client of the Banu Hashim, trustworthy. Ibn Kathir cited it in his tafsir 4:404 from the Hafiz al-Daraqutni, and it will come in the note on number 18682. Al-Tirmidhi narrated it in the Book of Tafsir. Then this report will come as a mawquf report (ending with a Companion) through 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla under numbers 18679 and 18680.]]

18679. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla: that a man touched a woman in a way short of intercourse, and came to the Prophet ﷺ asking him about that. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited — or: it was revealed — ﴿Establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approaches of the night﴾, the verse. Mu'adh said: "O Messenger of Allah, is this specific to him, or is it general for the people?" He said: "It is general for the people."

18680. Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abu Dawud narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Malik ibn 'Umayr, who said: I heard 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla say: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ, and he mentioned something similar.

18681. 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Shabuwayh narrated to me, saying: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: 'Amr ibn al-Harith narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salim narrated to me, from al-Zubaydi, who said: Sulaym ibn 'Amir narrated to us, that he heard Abu Umama say: A man came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, establish upon me the hadd (prescribed punishment) of Allah" — twice. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned away from him. Then the prayer was called, and when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ finished the prayer, he said: "Where is the one who said: 'Establish upon me the hadd of Allah'?" He said: "Here I am!" He said: "Did you complete the ablution and pray with us just now?" He said: "Yes!" He said: "Then you are, from your sin, as on the day your mother bore you. So do not return!" Then Allah revealed to His Messenger at that time: ﴿Establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approaches of the night﴾, the verse. [[Report 18681: "'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Shabuwayh al-Khuza'i," the teacher of al-Tabari, has passed many times, the last under number 15379. "Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn al-'Ala al-Zubaydi," is Ibn Zabrayq, trustworthy; people spoke against him out of envy. Has passed under number 15379. "'Amr ibn al-Harith ibn al-Nu'man al-Zubaydi," was mentioned by Ibn Hibban in al-Thiqat, and al-Dhahabi said: his uprightness is not known. Has passed under number 15379. "'Abd Allah ibn Salim al-Ash'ari al-Wahzazi," Ibn Hibban declared him trustworthy. Has passed under number 15379. "Al-Zubaydi" is Muhammad ibn al-Walid ibn 'Amir al-Zubaydi, trustworthy, whom the two Shaykhs narrated from, has passed many times, the last under number 15377. "Sulaym ibn 'Amir al-Kala'i al-Himsi," is a trustworthy Successor, and has passed under number 12807. This is a good chain. I did not find the hadith of Abu Umama narrated through this route, but the imams narrated it through other routes. Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad through two routes, 5:251 and 262, through 'Ikrima ibn 'Ammar al-Yamami, from Shaddad ibn 'Abd Allah, from Abu Umama. Then he narrated it on p. 265 through al-Awza'i, from Abu 'Ammar Shaddad, from Abu Umama. Muslim narrated it through the first route in his Sahih 17:81-82. Abu Dawud narrated it through the second route in his Sunan 4:191, number 4381.]]

18682. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to me, from 'Abd al-Malik, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from Mu'adh ibn Jabal: that he was sitting with the Prophet ﷺ, when a man came and said: "O Messenger of Allah, a man touched a woman in a way that is not lawful for him. He left nothing that a man does with his wife except that he did it, except that he did not have intercourse with her?" He said: "Let him perform ablution well and then pray." So Allah revealed this verse: (﴿Establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approaches of the night﴾), the verse. Mu'adh said: "Is it for him specifically, O Messenger of Allah, or for the Muslims in general?" He said: "Rather, for the Muslims in general." [[Report 18682: This is a repetition of the report that passed as 18678; see its takhrij there.]]

18683. al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Muslim informed us, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from Yahya ibn Ja'da: that a man among the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ mentioned a woman while he was sitting with the Prophet ﷺ, so he asked his permission for a need, and he gave him permission. He went to seek her but did not find her. Then the man came back, wanting to give the Prophet ﷺ the good news of rain, and found the woman sitting by a pool. He pushed her in the chest and sat between her legs, and his penis became like a hudba (a small shrub or tuft), so he stood up regretful, until he came to the Prophet ﷺ and informed him of what he had done. The Prophet ﷺ said to him: "Ask forgiveness of your Lord and pray four rak'at." He said: And he recited to him: ﴿Establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approaches of the night﴾, the verse. [[Report 18683: "Yahya ibn Ja'da ibn Hubayra ibn Abi Wahb al-Qurashi," a trustworthy Successor, has passed under number 7472.]]

18684. al-Harith narrated to me, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated to us, saying: Qays ibn al-Rabi' narrated to us, from 'Uthman ibn Wahb, from Musa ibn Talha, from Abu al-Yusr ibn 'Amr al-Ansari, who said: A woman came to me to buy dates from me for a dirham. I said: "In the house there are dates better than these!" So she entered, and I leaned toward her and kissed her. I came to Abu Bakr and asked him, and he said: "Conceal yourself, repent, and ask Allah's forgiveness!" Then I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: "You left a man who was fighting in the way of Allah, to his family, with the like of this!!" until I thought I was among the people of the Fire, until I wished that I had become Muslim at that very hour! He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ lowered his head for a while, and then Gabriel descended and said: "Where is Abu al-Yusr?" So I came, and he recited to me: ﴿Establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approaches of the night﴾, up to: ﴿That is a reminder for those who remember﴾. Someone said: "Is it for him specifically, O Messenger of Allah, or for the people in general?" He said: "For the people in general." [[Report 18684: This is the hadith of Abu al-Yusr al-Ansari, which will come after this one with roughly the same chain. See what al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar wrote about his name, which passed in the note on number 18675. "Qays ibn al-Rabi' al-Asadi," has passed many times, the last under number 16369; a group declared him trustworthy and others declared him weak. "'Uthman ibn Mawhab," is "'Uthman ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Mawhab al-Tamimi," who is attributed to his grandfather, trustworthy. Has passed under number 17567. "Musa ibn Talha ibn 'Ubayd Allah al-Qurashi," a trustworthy Successor, whom the group narrated from, has passed under numbers 17567-17571. This report was narrated by al-Tirmidhi in the Book of Tafsir, who said: "This is a good, gharib (singular) hadith. Qays ibn al-Rabi' was declared weak by Waki' and others. Shurayk narrated this hadith from 'Uthman ibn 'Abd Allah, like the narration of Qays ibn al-Rabi'."]]

18685. al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: al-Hammani narrated to us, saying: Qays ibn al-Rabi' narrated to us, from 'Uthman ibn Mawhab, from Musa ibn Talha, from Abu al-Yusr, who said: I met a woman and embraced her, except that I did not have intercourse with her. I came to 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah have mercy on him, and he said: "Fear Allah, conceal yourself, and do not inform anyone!" I could not restrain myself until I came to Abu Bakr, may Allah have mercy on him, and I asked him, and he said: "Fear Allah, conceal yourself, and do not inform anyone!" He said: I could not restrain myself until I came to the Prophet ﷺ and informed him. He said to me: "Did you equip a fighter in his family?" I said: "No." He said: "Did you leave a fighter in his family?" I said: "No." Then he said to me, until I wished that I had entered Islam at that very hour! He said: When I turned to leave, he called me, and recited to me: ﴿Establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approaches of the night﴾. His companions said to him: "Is this specific to him, or for the people in general?" He said: "Rather, for the people in general." [[Report 18685: This is a repetition of the report that passed.]]

18686. Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to me, from Qatada: that a man touched a woman with a kiss, then came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "O Prophet of Allah, I am ruined!" So Allah revealed: ﴿Indeed, good deeds remove evil deeds. That is a reminder for those who remember﴾.

18687. Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Sulayman al-Taymi, who said: A man struck the buttock of a woman, then came to Abu Bakr and 'Umar, may Allah have mercy on them both. Whenever he asked one of them about the expiation for that, he said: "Is she a woman whose husband is away on a raid?" [mada]. [[In the manuscript there is this which I have placed in brackets, and I have not succeeded in reading it or clarifying its meaning, but whatever it is, the question is clear. As for his saying: "mughziyya," al-mughziyya is the woman whose husband went on a raid and she remained alone in the house, and from it is the hadith of 'Umar: "What is the matter with men, one of whom never stops leaning on his cushion beside a mughziyya, talking to her and she talking to him! Keep to the janba (distance), for it is chastity. People are only flesh upon a fire-pit, except what is defended from it."]] He said: "Yes." He said: "I do not know!" Then he came to the Prophet ﷺ and asked him about that. He said: "Is she a mughziyya?" He said: "Yes!" He said: "I do not know!" until Allah revealed: ﴿Establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approaches of the night. Indeed, good deeds remove evil deeds﴾.

18688. Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Qays ibn Sa'd, from 'Ata', regarding the words of Allah: ﴿Establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approaches of the night﴾: that a woman entered upon a man who sold flour, and he kissed her, and he was seized with regret. He came to 'Umar and mentioned that to him, and he said: "Fear Allah, and do not be the wife of a fighter!" The man said: "She is the wife of a fighter." So he went to Abu Bakr, and he said the same as 'Umar. They all went to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said to him: "Like that," then the Prophet ﷺ was silent and did not answer them, so Allah revealed: ﴿Establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approaches of the night﴾, the obligatory prayers, ﴿Indeed, good deeds remove evil deeds. That is a reminder for those who remember﴾.

18689. al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah informed me, who said: A woman came until she reached a man who sold flour, to buy from him, and he took her into the house. When he was alone with her, he kissed her. He said: He was seized with regret, so he went to Abu Bakr and mentioned that to him, and he said: "Watch yourself! Do not be the wife of a fighter!" While they were in that state, this was revealed: ﴿Establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approaches of the night﴾. It was said to 'Ata': "Is it the obligatory prayer?" He said: "Yes, it is the obligatory prayer." Ibn Jurayj said, and 'Abd Allah ibn Kathir said: "They are the obligatory prayers."

Ibn Jurayj said, from Yazid ibn Ruman: A man from the Banu Ghanm, a woman came to him and he kissed her, and he placed his hand upon her rear. He came to Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, then he came to 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, then he came to the Prophet ﷺ, and this verse was revealed: ﴿Establish prayer﴾, to His saying: ﴿That is a reminder for those who remember﴾. The man who kissed the woman kept being reminded, and that is His saying: ﴿a reminder for those who remember﴾.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 115–116:

The explanation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿So be patient, for indeed Allah does not allow to be lost the reward of the doers of good﴾ (11:115)

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, the Exalted, says: "Be patient, O Muhammad, over what you encounter from the polytheists of your people of harm and hardship for the sake of Allah, hoping for the abundant reward of Allah for that. For indeed Allah does not waste the reward of the deed of one who does good, obeying Allah and following His command, so that it is lost; rather, He gives it in full at the time he most needs it."

* *

The explanation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Why were there not among the generations before you those of remnant [who would] forbid corruption on earth, except a few of those We saved from them? But those who wronged followed what luxury they were given therein, and they were criminals.﴾ (11:116)

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, the Exalted, says: "Why was there not, among the generations about whose news I have related to you in this surah, those whom I destroyed for their disobedience to Me and their disbelief in My messengers [[See the explanation of "qarn" (generation) above, 11:263 / 15:37.]] before you? ﴿Those of remnant﴾ means: those possessing a remnant of understanding and intellect [[See the explanation of "baqiyyah" (remnant) above, pp. 447–449.]] who reflect on Allah's admonitions and ponder His proofs, so that they recognize what benefit there is for them in faith in Allah and what harm for them in disbelief in Him [[In the printed and manuscript editions: "wa-ʿalayhim" without "mā"; the reading with "mā" is better.]] = ﴿forbid corruption on earth﴾ means: they forbid the people of sin from their sins and the people of disbelief in Allah from their disbelief in Him, on His earth [[See the explanation of "corruption on earth" above in the language indexes (fasada).]] = ﴿except a few of those We saved from them﴾ means: there was not among the generations before you those of remnant who forbade corruption on earth, except a few. For they forbade corruption on earth, so Allah saved them from His punishment when His punishment seized those who persisted in disbelief in Allah. And they were the followers of the prophets and messengers."

* *

The accusative of "qalīlan" (a few) is because His saying ﴿except a few﴾ is an exceptive that is disconnected (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ) from what precedes it, as He said: ﴿except the people of Yunus, when they believed﴾ [Surah Yunus: 98]. We have explained this in more than one place, in a way that makes repeating it unnecessary. [[See the indexes of Arabic grammar and other topics.]]

* *

The exegetes said things similar to what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said so:

18690 – Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: He gave an excuse, saying: ﴿Why were there not among the generations before you﴾, until: ﴿except a few of those We saved from them﴾, so they are those who were saved when the punishment of Allah descended. And he recited: ﴿But those who wronged followed what luxury they were given therein.﴾

18691 – al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij concerning His saying: ﴿Why were there not among the generations before you those of remnant﴾, to His saying: ﴿except a few of those We saved from them﴾, he said: Allah makes them few from every people.

18692 – Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi ʿAdiyy narrated to us, from Dawud, who said: Bilal asked me about the statement of al-Hasan concerning qadar. [[In the printed edition here: "fi al-ʿudhr," the correct reading is what is given; see the following note.]] He said: I heard al-Hasan say: ﴿It was said, O Noah, descend with peace from Us and blessings upon you and upon nations from those with you; and nations We will provide for, then there will touch them from Us a painful punishment.﴾ He said: Allah sent Hud to ʿAd, so Allah saved Hud and those who believed with him, and the enjoyers were destroyed. * *

= It is as if these understood the meaning of the statement to be: those who wronged followed the thing in which their Lord granted them respite from the bounties of this world and its pleasures, preferring it over the work of the Hereafter and what would save them from the punishment of Allah.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 115–116:

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, the Exalted, says: "Be patient, O Muhammad, over what you encounter from the polytheists of your people of harm and hardship for the sake of Allah, hoping for the abundant reward of Allah for that. For indeed Allah does not waste the reward of the deed of one who does good, obeying Allah and following His command, so that it is lost; rather, He gives it in full at the time he most needs it."

* *

But those who wronged followed what luxury they were given therein, and they were criminals.﴾ (11:116)

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, the Exalted, says: "Why was there not, among the generations about whose news I have related to you in this surah, those whom I destroyed for their disobedience to Me and their disbelief in My messengers [[See the explanation of "qarn" (generation) above, 11:263 / 15:37.]] before you? ﴿Those of remnant﴾ means: those possessing a remnant of understanding and intellect [[See the explanation of "baqiyyah" (remnant) above, pp. 447–449.]] who reflect on Allah's admonitions and ponder His proofs, so that they recognize what benefit there is for them in faith in Allah and what harm for them in disbelief in Him [[In the printed and manuscript editions: "wa-ʿalayhim" without "mā"; the reading with "mā" is better.]] = ﴿forbid corruption on earth﴾ means: they forbid the people of sin from their sins and the people of disbelief in Allah from their disbelief in Him, on His earth [[See the explanation of "corruption on earth" above in the language indexes (fasada).]] = ﴿except a few of those We saved from them﴾ means: there was not among the generations before you those of remnant who forbade corruption on earth, except a few. Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 117:

The explanation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And your Lord would never destroy the towns unjustly while their people are reformers﴾.

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: And your Lord would never, O Muhammad, destroy the towns which He destroyed, whose news He related to you, unjustly while their people were reformers in their deeds, not wrongdoers, such that His destroying them along with their righteousness in their deeds and their obedience to their Lord would be unjust. Rather, He destroyed them because of the disbelief of their people in God, their persistence in their error, their denial of their messengers, and their committing of evil deeds.

* *

It has also been said: the meaning of that is: He would not have destroyed them for their polytheism (shirk) in God. His saying "unjustly" means: by shirk. ﴿While their people are reformers﴾ means: among themselves they do not wrong one another, but they deal justly with one another, even if they are polytheists; He only destroys them when they wrong one another.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 118–119:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿And had your Lord willed, He would have made mankind one community, but they continue to differ, (118) except those upon whom your Lord has mercy; and for that He created them. And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled: "I will surely fill Hell with jinn and mankind, all together."﴾ (119)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, the Exalted, says: And had your Lord willed, O Muhammad, He would have made all people one congregation upon one religion (millah) and one din, [[See the explanation of "ummah" above, p. 353, note 4, and the references there.]] as:

* *

As for His words: ﴿but they continue to differ﴾, He, the Exalted, says: and people continue to differ, ﴿except those upon whom your Lord has mercy﴾.

* *

Then the people of interpretation differed concerning the "difference" by which God described people as continuing in it.

Some of them said: It is difference in religions. So the interpretation of this, according to these scholars, is: People continue to differ in various religions, among them Jews, Christians, Magians, and the like.

Those who held this view said: God excepted from this those whom He had mercy upon, namely the people of faith.

I only said that this is the most correct interpretation because God, may His praise be majestic, followed that with His words: ﴿And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled: "I will surely fill Hell with jinn and mankind, all together."﴾ In that is clear evidence that what preceded it, the mention of His report about the differing of people, is only a report about a blameworthy difference which makes the Fire obligatory for them. Had it been a report about their differing in provision, He would not have followed it with a report of their punishment and torment.

18736- Ibn WakI' related to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah related to us, from someone he mentioned, from Thabit, from al-Dahhak: ﴿and for that He created them﴾, he said: For mercy.

18738- Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah related to me, saying: Hafs ibn 'Umar related to us, saying: al-Hakam ibn Aban related to us, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿but they continue to differ, except those upon whom your Lord has mercy, and for that﴾, he said: He created them for mercy, and He did not create them for punishment.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the two views regarding that is the view of the one who said: "And for difference, in wretchedness and happiness, He created them." This is because God, may His remembrance be exalted, mentioned two categories of His creation: one being the people of difference and falsehood, and the other the people of truth. Then He followed that with His words: ﴿and for that He created them﴾, so the words ﴿and for that He created them﴾ encompass the attribute of both categories, informing about each group that it is facilitated for what it was created for.

* *

If someone says: If the interpretation is as you have mentioned, then those who differ should not be blamed for their difference, since their Lord created them for that; and then those who enjoy (the world) would be the ones to blame?

It is said: The meaning of that is contrary to what you have understood. The meaning of the statement is: People continue to differ in falsehood regarding their religions and their creeds, ﴿except those upon whom your Lord has mercy﴾, so He guided him to the truth and to His knowledge; and by His knowledge, which was executed upon them before He created them, that there would be among them believer and disbeliever, wretched and happy, He created them. So the meaning of the lam in His words ﴿and for that He created them﴾ is in the sense of "upon", like your saying to a man: "I honored you upon your kindness to me" and "I honored you for your kindness to me."

* *

As for His words: ﴿And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled: "I will surely fill Hell with jinn and mankind, all together."﴾, it is due to His prior knowledge concerning them that they deserve its burning by their disbelief in God and their opposition to His command.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled﴾, it is an oath, like the speaker's saying: "My oath that I will surely visit you," and "It has become clear to me that I will surely come to you"; and for that reason it is preceded by the lam of oath.

* *

As for His words: ﴿from the jinn﴾, they are those concealed from the sight of the children of Adam. ﴿and mankind﴾, meaning the children of Adam.

It has been said: They were named "jinn" because they were upon the gardens (janan).

* *

As for the meaning of this statement of Abu Malik, that Iblis was among the angels and the jinn are his offspring, and that the angels are called jinn by him, this has been explained earlier in this book of ours. [[See the explanation of "jinn" above, 1: 502–508.]]

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿And had your Lord willed, He would have made mankind one community, but they continue to differ, (118) except those upon whom your Lord has mercy; and for that He created them. As for His words: ﴿but they continue to differ﴾, He, the Exalted, says: and people continue to differ, ﴿except those upon whom your Lord has mercy﴾.

* *

Some of them said: It is difference in religions. So the interpretation of this, according to these scholars, is: People continue to differ in various religions, among them Jews, Christians, Magians, and the like.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 11, verse 120:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We relate to you from the news of the messengers that with it We strengthen your heart. And there has come to you in this the truth, and an admonition and a reminder for the believers﴾ (11:120).

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: ﴿And We relate to you﴾, O Muhammad [see the explanation of "al-qasas" (narrative accounts) earlier, p. 470, footnote 2, and the references there] = ﴿from the news of the messengers﴾, who were before you [see the explanation of "al-naba'" (news) earlier in the lexical indices, root n-b-')] = ﴿that with it We strengthen your heart﴾, so that you do not grieve over the denial of those of your people who denied you and rejected what you brought them, and so that your breast does not constrict, causing you to leave some of what We have sent down to you because they said: ﴿Why has a treasure not been sent down to him, or an angel not come with him?﴾ When you know what those messengers before you met from their peoples, [see the explanation of "al-tathbit" (strengthening) earlier, vol. 5, pp. 354, 531 / vol. 7, pp. 272, 237 / vol. 8, p. 529 / vol. 13, p. 427], as:

18741 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His saying: ﴿And We relate to you from the news of the messengers that with it We strengthen your heart﴾, he said: So that you may know what the messengers before you encountered from their peoples.

* *

The people of Arabic grammar differed regarding the grammatical case of "kullan" (kullan).

Some of the grammarians of Basra said: It is in the accusative on the meaning: "And We relate to you from the news of the messengers that with it We strengthen your heart, kullan (all of it)," as if "kull" were, in his view, in the accusative as a verbal noun (masdar) of "naqussu," meaning: "And We relate to you that, all of the narratives."

* *

Some other grammarians rejected this view and said: That is not permissible. They said: "Kullan" is in the accusative only by "naqussu," because "kulla" is built (mabni) on being in an annexation (idafah), whether or not an annexation follows it. He said: The meaning is "kullahu naqussu 'alayk" (all of it We relate to you), and "ma nuthabbitu" is a restatement (radd) of "kull." I have already made clear the correct view on this matter. [See what has preceded regarding the ruling on "kull," vol. 6, p. 210, then the explanation of "kull" earlier, p. 212, and the lexical indices under the root k-l-l.]

18758 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us = and Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us = from Shu'bah, from Abu Raja', from al-Hasan, the like of it.

18759 - Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from Aban ibn Taghlib, from Mujahid, the like of it.

18760 - Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿And there has come to you in this the truth﴾, he said: in this sura.

18761 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah [the like of it]. [The addition between the brackets, I hope, is the correct one.]

18762 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Adam narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Raja', who said: I heard al-Hasan al-Basri say regarding the saying of God: ﴿And there has come to you in this the truth﴾, he said: meaning in this sura.

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is: "And there has come to you in this world the truth."

Those who said that:

18763 - Muhammad ibn Bashshar and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, both saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿And there has come to you in this the truth﴾, he said: in this world.

18764 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us = and Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us = from Shu'bah, from Qatadah: ﴿And there has come to you in this the truth﴾, he said: al-Hasan used to say: in this world.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the two interpretations concerning its meaning is the view of those who said: "And there has come to you in this sura the truth," due to the consensus of the authorities among the people of interpretation that this is its interpretation.

* *

If someone says: Did the Prophet ﷺ receive the truth from the suras of the Qur'an only in this sura, so that it is said: "And there has come to you in this sura the truth"?

It is said to him: Yes, indeed, it came to him in all of it.

If he says: Then what is the meaning of its specificity to this sura by His saying: ﴿And there has come to you in this the truth﴾? It is said: The meaning of the statement is: "And there has come to you in this sura the truth, together with what has come to you in the rest of the suras of the Qur'an," or "in addition to what has come to you of the truth in the rest of the suras of the Qur'an" — not that its meaning is: "And there has come to you in this sura the truth, to the exclusion of the rest of the suras of the Qur'an."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And an admonition﴾, He says: there has come to you an admonition that admonishes those ignorant of God and makes clear to them the lessons of those who disbelieved in Him and denied His messengers [see the explanation of "al-maw'izah" (admonition) earlier, p. 104, footnote 1, and the references there] = ﴿and a reminder for the believers﴾, He says: and a reminder that reminds the believers of God and His messengers, so that they do not neglect what is owed to God upon them.

**The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted Is He:** ﴿And say to those who do not believe: "Act according to your position; indeed we are acting. And wait; indeed we are waiting."﴾ (11:121–122)

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): And say, O Muhammad, to those who do not believe you and do not affirm the Oneness of Allah, ﴿Act according to your position﴾, meaning: act according to your condition and your firm standing, in what you are doing [[See the explanation of "al-makanah" above, p. 463, note 1, and the references there.]], for we are acting according to what we have been commanded by Allah to do. ﴿And wait﴾ for what Satan has promised you, for we are waiting for what Allah has promised us: war against you and our victory over you, as:

18765. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Juraij, regarding His words, ﴿And wait; indeed we are waiting﴾, he said: He says: wait for the promises of Satan to you in what he adorns for you. ﴿Indeed we are waiting.﴾

* *

**The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted Is He:** ﴿To Allah belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and to Him the whole matter will be returned. So worship Him and rely upon Him. And your Lord is not unaware of what you do.﴾ (11:123)

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): And to Allah, O Muhammad, belongs the dominion over everything that is hidden from you in the heavens and the earth, so that you did not witness it and did not know it, and did not know it [[See the explanation of "al-ghayb" above, vol. 14, p. 381, note 1, and the references there.]]. All of that is in His hand and by His knowledge; nothing of it is hidden from Him. He knows what the polytheists of your people do and what their affair will ultimately lead to, whether persistence in polytheism or abandoning it and repenting. ﴿And to Him the whole matter will be returned﴾, meaning: the return of every doer and his deed is to Allah, and He will recompense all of them for their deeds, as:

18766. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij: ﴿And to Him the whole matter will be returned﴾, he said: He will judge between them with His just judgment.

* *

﴿So worship Him﴾, meaning: so worship your Lord, O Muhammad. ﴿And rely upon Him﴾, meaning: entrust your affair to Him, and trust in Him and in His sufficiency, for He is sufficient for whoever relies upon Him [[See the explanation of "al-tawakkul" above, p. 168, note 1, and the references there.]].

* *

And His words, ﴿And your Lord is not unaware of what you do﴾, Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And your Lord, O Muhammad, is not heedless of what these polytheists of your people do [[See the explanation of "al-ghaflah" above, p. 198, note 2, and the references there.]], but He encompasses it, and nothing of it escapes Him, and He is watching them closely. So let not their turning away from you grieve you, nor their denial of the truth you have brought them; continue on with the command of your Lord, for you are under Our eyes.

18767. Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: Zayd ibn al-Hubab narrated to us, from Ja'far ibn Sulayman, from Abu Imran al-Joni, from Abd Allah ibn Rabah, from Ka'b, who said: The conclusion of the Torah is the conclusion of Hud. [[The report: 18767 — its full text has passed earlier under no. 13043, and another route with similar wording, no. 13042.]]

﴿End of the commentary on Surah Hud, and all praise is due to Allah alone.﴾
